records.title: Intersecting effects of social circumstances and transcendent thinking on mid-adolescents’ longitudinal functional connectome development
records.model_family: graph theory network analysis combined with machine learning on functional brain network features
records.clinical_problem: identifying social and psychological predictors of longitudinal functional brain network development in mid-adolescence
records.patient_population: mid-adolescents from low-socioeconomic-status contexts, longitudinal 2-year fMRI cohort (n=65)
records.model_description: Graph theory measures were computed from a 2-year longitudinal resting-state fMRI dataset of 65 mid-adolescents. Machine learning analysis was used to identify which factors, among parental education, community violence exposure, IQ, and a measured psychological disposition ('transcendent thinking'), best predicted changes in functional brain network organization (segregation, integration, entropy, energy) over the study period.
records.headline_result: machine learning identified transcendent thinking and community violence exposure, but not IQ, as the principal predictors of functional brain network change across groups

records.title: Distal Radial Epiphyseal Fusion Timing in Northwest Europeans and Middle Eastern Asylum Seekers: An Automated Ultrasound and Machine Learning Approach
records.clinical_problem: forensic age assessment via distal radial epiphyseal fusion timing (medico-legal age-of-majority determination)
records.patient_population: Northwest European and Middle Eastern individuals aged 13-25 years, including asylum seekers, assessed at German clinical sites and reception facilities
records.model_description: A fully automated ultrasound device assesses distal radial epiphyseal fusion status. Gradient-boosting machine learning models (LightGBM) were trained on 830 high-quality ultrasound datasets to classify fusion status against reference ages (documented birthdate or Greulich-Pyle bone age), evaluated with leave-one-out cross-validation across sex- and population-specific age thresholds, for forensic determination of whether an individual has reached a legally relevant age threshold.
records.dataset_size: 1,061 recordings; 830 high-quality ultrasound datasets analyzed, ages 13-25 years
records.headline_result: AUC approximately 0.81-1.00 near optimal thresholds; optimal discrimination thresholds ranged 17.0-18.5 years across sex/population groups

records.title: Structure-aware fine-grained instance segmentation for fetal brain ultrasound images
records.model_family: instance segmentation framework with structure-aware overlap metric, Laplacian regularization, and Stable Diffusion/LoRA augmentation
records.clinical_problem: fetal brain anatomical structure segmentation
records.patient_population: fetal brain ultrasound images across five standard planes
records.model_description: A structure-aware instance segmentation framework detects and segments 25 anatomical structures across five standard fetal brain ultrasound planes. It uses a structure-aware overlap metric and improved non-maximum suppression to better detect small structures, a fine-grained segmentation head, Laplacian-based spatial regularization for boundary consistency, and a diffusion-model-based data augmentation strategy to synthesize additional training images.

records.title: Image Quality Evaluation of Neonatal Brain MRI Using a Deep Learning Reconstruction Algorithm: A Quantitative and Multireader Study Using Variable Denoising Levels at 3 Tesla
records.clinical_problem: image quality improvement for neonatal brain MRI to support assessment of early myelinating structures
records.patient_population: 15 neonates undergoing 3D T1-weighted brain MRI at 3 Tesla
records.model_description: A deep learning image reconstruction algorithm was applied at low, medium and high denoising levels to 3D T1-weighted brain MRI scans of 15 neonates. Three radiologists rated image quality (signal-to-noise, artifacts, clarity) of eight early myelinating brain structures on a 4-point scale, and objective signal-to-noise and contrast-to-noise ratios were measured across denoising levels.
records.headline_result: overall increase in all image-quality categories and conspicuity of early myelinating structures with increasing denoising; significant increases in apparent SNR and CNR for nearly all pairwise comparisons
records.study_design: prospective single-center image quality evaluation, multireader study

records.title: High-Sensitivity Radiation-Free Triage for Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis via 3D Point Cloud Geometry
records.model_family: 3D point cloud geometric processing pipeline (segmentation plus classification)
records.clinical_problem: radiation-free triage screening for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS)
records.patient_population: adolescents screened for scoliosis, multi-center validation cohort
records.model_description: PointScol is a radiation-free triage system that processes 3D point clouds of the back surface, obtained by optical/depth scanning rather than X-ray, to screen for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis. It first segments the dorsal region of interest, then classifies spinal deformity, acting as a binary screening gate at a 10-degree Cobb angle threshold and as a 5-class severity grading tool to guide referral urgency. It was validated on a multi-center dataset.
records.headline_result: 100.00% sensitivity in the external cohort for the primary screening task (10-degree Cobb angle threshold)
records.study_design: technical development / multi-center diagnostic accuracy study

records.title: Protocol for a prospective accuracy study on an artificial intelligence-based ultrasound system for gestational age estimation among pregnant women in Ghana, Kenya and South Africa
records.model_family: AI algorithm for gestational age estimation from handheld blind-sweep ultrasound (commercial product)
records.clinical_problem: gestational age estimation for antenatal care and pre-eclampsia risk screening in low-resource settings
records.patient_population: 969 pregnant women at 13 health facilities across Kenya, Ghana and South Africa, presenting 11+0 to 13+6 weeks' gestation with follow-up to 27+6 weeks
records.model_description: This study protocol describes a prospective multi-country accuracy study of the commercial Intelligent Ultrasound ScanNav FetalCheck AI system, which estimates gestational age from handheld blind-sweep ultrasound scans performed by a trained midwife using a GE VScan Air device. Its accuracy will be compared against conventional fetal biometry (crown-rump length) performed by a trained sonographer as the reference standard, in 969 women across 13 facilities in Ghana, Kenya, and South Africa.

records.title: Automated Segmentation of Post-Surgical Resection Cavities on MRI in Focal Epilepsy: a MELD Study
records.clinical_problem: automated segmentation of the postoperative resection cavity after epilepsy surgery to quantify extent of tissue resection
records.patient_population: children and adults who underwent epilepsy surgery, from the multicentre MELD project (27 centres) and the EPISURG dataset, with a range of resection locations and pathologies
records.model_description: MELD-PostOp is a deep learning tool built on nnU-Net that automatically segments the surgical resection cavity on postoperative 3D T1-weighted brain MRI following epilepsy surgery. It was trained on 965 manually and semi-automatically segmented cases from 27 centres (children and adults, temporal and extra-temporal resections) and evaluated on stratified and independent held-out test cohorts against existing tools (Epic-CHOP, ResectVol).
records.release_evidence: "This open-source tool facilitates large-scale quantitative analysis"
records.dataset_size: 965 subjects for training across 27 centres; stratified test cohort n=50; independent test cohort n=87
records.headline_result: median Dice similarity coefficient 0.85 and HD95 3.61 on the combined test cohort, outperforming Epic-CHOP (DSC 0.68) and ResectVol (DSC 0.66); detected 99% (135/137) of resection cavities
records.study_design: retrospective multi-center technical development / segmentation validation study

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Pediatric and Fetal Echocardiography: Looking Beyond the Now
records.clinical_problem: AI applications across the pediatric and fetal echocardiography imaging pipeline for congenital and pediatric heart disease
records.patient_population: fetal, pediatric, and adult patients with congenital heart disease undergoing echocardiography
records.model_description: Narrative review synthesizing 2020-2025 literature on AI (machine learning and deep learning) applied to each step of the pediatric and fetal echocardiography imaging pipeline: image acquisition and quality enhancement, automated view classification, automated measurement and structure segmentation, disease detection/diagnosis including fetal screening, risk stratification, and clinical decision support. No single model is evaluated; the review frames AI as transitioning from a research interest to a clinical instrument in pediatric cardiology.

records.title: Parameter-Efficient Heterogeneous Ensemble with Analytic Geometry for Automated Fetal Head Descent Assessment
records.model_family: heterogeneous ensemble of a MedSAM-based vision transformer with low-rank adaptation and a self-configuring nnU-Net v2, fused via probability averaging
records.clinical_problem: automated angle of progression (AOP) measurement for intrapartum fetal head descent assessment
records.patient_population: pregnant patients undergoing transperineal ultrasound during labor for fetal head descent assessment
records.model_description: A dual-model ensemble combines a MedSAM-based vision transformer with low-rank adaptation and a self-configuring nnU-Net v2 to segment relevant structures on transperineal ultrasound images. The segmentation is used to compute the angle of progression (AOP), a measure of fetal head descent during labor, via closed-form tangent-line geometry on fitted ellipses. The model was trained on 4,000 images and evaluated on an independent set of 1,101 images.
records.dataset_size: 4,000 training images; independent validation set of 1,101 images (858 limited descent, 243 advanced descent)
records.headline_result: F1 0.865 (95% CI 0.831-0.896), AUC 0.960 (0.947-0.971), sensitivity 86.8%, specificity 96.0%; mean absolute AOP error 5.93 degrees (median 4.10)
records.study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study

records.title: Early Neurosurgical Intervention In Congenital Hydrocephalus: Predictive Biomarkers, Imaging Trends, And The Transformative Role Of Artificial Intelligence
records.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

records.clinical_problem: predicting timing of neurosurgery and prognosis in congenital hydrocephalus
records.patient_population: children with congenital hydrocephalus, with MRI, CT and CSF biomarker data
records.model_description: MRI and CT images from children with congenital hydrocephalus were segmented with 3D U-Net and attention-based CNN architectures to automate ventricular measurement. Clinical and CSF biomarker features (after KNN imputation and PCA) were combined with the imaging findings and fed into machine learning (SVM, random forest, XGBoost) and deep learning (RNN, LSTM) models to stratify risk, predict disease progression and evaluate surgical outcomes; explainable AI identified ventricular enlargement, CSF dynamics and periventricular changes as the top predictive features.
records.headline_result: test accuracy exceeding 95% with high precision, recall and F1-scores; XGBoost outperformed traditional classifiers, LSTM best predicted longitudinal progression

records.journal: Donald School Journal of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology

records.patient_population: 30 normal singleton pregnancies, 28-36 weeks of gestation

records.study_design: prospective observational study protocol (results not yet reported)

records.title: FCUFormer: A multi-view informed vision-language foundation model for interpreting fetal cardiac ultrasound abnormalities
records.model_family: Vision-language foundation model (Multi-view informed Multiple Instance Learning module and Multi-Level Vision-Language Alignment module), with an LLM-driven report standardization pipeline
records.clinical_problem: interpretation of fetal cardiac ultrasound for prenatal screening of congenital heart defects
records.patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal cardiac ultrasound screening (5,495 real-world fetal cardiac ultrasound records)
records.model_description: An LLM-driven pipeline standardizes free-text fetal cardiac ultrasound reports and multi-view images into structured training data without large-scale manual annotation. A cross-modal foundation model (FCUFormer) is then pretrained on this data, learning cross-view anatomical dependencies and fine-grained alignment between image regions and clinical text, to interpret fetal cardiac ultrasound and flag abnormalities.
records.headline_result: Average accuracy of 87.37% in diagnosis of various fetal ultrasound abnormalities on standardized downstream benchmarks
records.study_design: retrospective technical development and evaluation study

records.title: Developmental Trajectories of White Matter Geometry and Relationships With Cognitive Maturation
records.model_family: machine learning combined with canonical correlation analysis
records.body_region: white matter tracts (48 tracts, whole brain)
records.clinical_problem: relating white matter geometric development to executive function and crystallised intelligence
records.patient_population: 598 participants, ages 67-263 months (about 5.6-22 years), from the Human Connectome Project
records.model_description: Diffusion MRI from 598 participants aged 5.6-22 years was analyzed with director field analysis to quantify tract-level splay, bend, twist, and distortion across 48 white matter tracts. Canonical correlation analysis and machine learning related these geometric features to cognition, finding that patterns in the cingulum and internal capsule predicted individual differences in executive function and crystallised intelligence.
records.headline_result: Canonical correlation analysis (r = 0.60-0.64) and machine learning showed geometric patterns, particularly in the cingulum and internal capsule, predicted individual differences in executive function and crystallised intelligence.
records.study_design: cross-sectional diffusion MRI study with machine learning and canonical correlation analysis

records.title: A New communication efficient federated online distillation for Non-IID Data: Application to fetal brain ultrasound plane classification
records.model_family: Communication-efficient federated learning framework with online ensemble knowledge distillation (dual-branch student network with an attention-convolution module)
records.body_region: fetal brain (primary); also tested on brain tumor MRI and chest X-ray
records.clinical_problem: fetal brain ultrasound standard-plane classification under multi-institutional, privacy-preserving conditions
records.patient_population: fetal brain ultrasound datasets across multiple simulated institutions with non-independent and non-identically distributed (non-IID) data
records.model_description: FedFB is a federated learning framework in which multiple institutions each train a local teacher model on private fetal brain ultrasound data, then collectively distill their knowledge (via a small shared public dataset of soft labels) into a lightweight shared student classifier, without exchanging raw data or full model parameters. It was designed to remain accurate under heterogeneous (non-IID) data across sites while sharply reducing communication overhead, and was also tested for generalization on brain tumor MRI and chest X-ray datasets.
records.headline_result: 91.07% accuracy, 91.28% precision, 91.03% recall, 91.15% F1-score under non-IID conditions on fetal brain ultrasound plane classification, while reducing communication overhead by more than 85% compared with traditional federated learning methods
records.study_design: retrospective multi-institutional technical development and evaluation study

records.title: A twin-aware multimodal deep learning framework with optimized late fusion for early prediction of adolescent anxiety disorder

records.title: Bone2Gene: Next-generation Phenotyping of Rare Bone Diseases
records.model_family: deep learning image classifiers (binary and multi-class CNNs) with occlusion sensitivity mapping
records.clinical_problem: differential diagnosis of rare bone diseases from hand radiographs
records.patient_population: children undergoing hand radiographs for bone age assessment, with 45 different rare bone diseases (RBDs) compared to unaffected controls
records.model_description: Bone2Gene takes a hand radiograph as input and first classifies whether it shows a rare bone disease (RBD) versus not, then, for RBD-positive cases, a second multi-class model predicts which of ten RBD groups is most likely. It was trained and evaluated with 5-fold cross-validation on 5,623 multi-institutional hand radiographs from 2,471 patients with 45 RBDs and 1,382 controls, using occlusion sensitivity mapping and embedding analysis to visualize the features driving each prediction.
records.dataset_size: 5,623 multi-institutional hand radiographs from 2,471 patients with 45 different RBDs and 1,382 unaffected controls
records.headline_result: affected vs unaffected classifier: balanced accuracy 85.5%; ten-class classifier: balanced top-1 accuracy 76.6%, top-3 accuracy exceeding 90%

records.title: Study on clinical-MRI radiomic models for graded diagnosis of neonatal acute bilirubin encephalopathy based on machine learning

records.title: Multimodal MRI-based neuromarkers trace longitudinal changes in cognitive functioning in ADHD

records.headline_result: On the HC18 dataset: Dice similarity coefficient 98.91±0.76%, difference 0.06±1.18mm, absolute difference 1.05±1.21mm, Hausdorff distance 1.16±0.69mm, exceeding prior state-of-the-art methods; generalization confirmed on the separate FH-PS-AOP dataset

records.title: Developmental brain age gap in prematurity and postnatally emerging delay in congenital heart disease

records.patient_population: 1056 fetal and neonatal MRI scans (21-44 weeks) from six datasets at three centers, including preterm neonates (n=90 term-equivalent) and fetuses/neonates with congenital heart disease (n=50 fetal, n=110 postnatal)

records.headline_result: Preterm neonates born <28 weeks: brain age gap -0.7 to -0.8 weeks at term; CHD neonates: brain age gap -1.3 to -1.8 weeks presurgery, up to -3 weeks postsurgery (p<0.05)

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Pediatric Imaging: A Primer for Pediatric Clinicians
records.clinical_problem: overview of AI applications across pediatric radiology, for pediatric clinicians
records.model_description: Narrative review/primer aimed at pediatric clinicians surveying deep learning applications in pediatric imaging: chest radiograph models for pneumonia, tuberculosis and malpositioned tube detection; automated bone age assessment; neuroimaging tools for faster acquisition, lower contrast dose and critical-finding triage; cardiovascular AI for congenital heart disease detection and function assessment; and oncologic tumor characterization and segmentation. Discusses barriers including scarce pediatric datasets and limited prospective validation.

records.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence for Pneumonia Detection Using Lung Ultrasound Images: A Systematic Review
records.model_family: various (convolutional neural networks, hybrid frameworks, 3D video-based, segmentation-driven models)
records.clinical_problem: pneumonia detection
records.patient_population: systematic review of 10 studies, 15,868 participants across paediatric, adult, and mixed clinical populations undergoing lung ultrasound
records.model_description: Systematic review of AI-assisted lung ultrasound interpretation for pneumonia diagnosis. Included studies applied machine learning or deep learning (CNNs, hybrid frameworks, 3D video-based models, segmentation-driven systems) to lung ultrasound images to classify pneumonia versus normal lung, across paediatric and adult populations, and pooled diagnostic performance across ten eligible studies.
records.headline_result: Sensitivity 88-93%, specificity 80-100%, accuracy 86-94.5% across included studies

records.title: Brain Age Gap as a Neuroimaging Biomarker for Neurodevelopmental Alterations and Cognitive Impairment in Beta-Thalassaemia Major: A Deep Learning-Based Multicentre Study
records.model_family: 3D-SFCN-UNet deep learning framework for brain age prediction
records.clinical_problem: neurodevelopmental alteration and cognitive impairment assessment via brain age gap in beta-thalassaemia major
records.patient_population: 275 participants from two centers (139 children/adolescents with beta-thalassaemia major, 136 healthy controls), enrolled May 2020-October 2023
records.model_description: A 3D-SFCN-UNet deep learning model was applied to 3D T1-weighted brain MRI to predict brain age and derive a harmonized, corrected brain age gap (BAG) and voxel-level local BAG maps across two centers. Mediation analyses linked haematological indices and regional brain features to cognitive test scores, to evaluate BAG as an imaging biomarker of neurodevelopmental risk in beta-thalassaemia major.
records.dataset_size: 275 participants (139 with beta-thalassaemia major, 136 healthy controls)
records.headline_result: Model achieved brain age prediction MAE 0.74 years (r=0.93) in healthy controls; patients with beta-thalassaemia major had lower corrected brain age gap than controls (-0.645±1.461 vs 0.000±0.954 years; p<0.001), consistent after age-stratification and propensity matching

records.title: EF-ConsNET: Physiologically Anchored Multimodal Deep Learning for Diagnosis and Severity Grading of Pediatric Myocarditis
records.model_family: Multimodal deep learning framework integrating chest X-ray images, ECG signals, and structured clinical/lab features, with echocardiographic ejection fraction as a physiological supervision anchor
records.clinical_problem: diagnosis and severity grading of pediatric myocarditis
records.patient_population: two-center inpatient cohort: 5,147 cases (700 myocarditis, 4,447 non-myocarditis) for internal training/validation, plus 529 cases (197 myocarditis, 332 non-myocarditis) from a separate hospital for external validation
records.model_description: EF-ConsNET fuses chest X-ray images, ECG signals, and structured laboratory/demographic data to detect pediatric myocarditis and grade its severity (mild vs severe), using echocardiographic ejection fraction during training as a physiological anchor to keep the multimodal representation clinically consistent and to make the model's image attention focus on cardiopulmonary regions. It was designed to remain robust when some input modalities are missing.
records.dataset_size: 5,147 cases internal (700 myocarditis); 529 cases external (197 myocarditis)
records.headline_result: Internal AUROC 0.926 (myocarditis detection) and 0.911 (severity grading); external validation AUROC 0.812 (detection) and 0.765 (severity grading); performance remained above 0.899 AUROC with up to 20% simulated single-modality missingness
records.study_design: retrospective two-center diagnostic study with external validation

records.title: AI-Augmented Multimodal Model for Predicting Macrolide Resistance in Pediatric Mycoplasma Pneumonia: An External Validation Study
records.model_family: Multivariable logistic regression combining an automated AI-derived chest radiograph consolidation score with clinical and laboratory markers
records.clinical_problem: predicting macrolide resistance in pediatric Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia at hospital admission
records.patient_population: hospitalized children with PCR-confirmed Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia: 503 in the development cohort, 138 in an independent external validation cohort
records.model_description: An AI algorithm automatically quantifies a consolidation score from admission chest radiographs in children with confirmed Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia. This score is combined with routine clinical markers, laboratory findings and PCR cycle threshold values in a logistic regression nomogram to predict macrolide-resistant disease at admission, to guide earlier escalation to second-line therapy.
records.headline_result: Adding the AI consolidation score to the clinical model improved internal AUC from 0.819 (95% CI 0.762-0.876) to 0.860 (95% CI 0.812-0.909; P=0.004); external validation AUC 0.726 (95% CI 0.588-0.863)
records.study_design: multi-institutional retrospective diagnostic study with external validation

records.title: FSU-YOLOv12 for vertebral abnormalities detection in fetal spinal ultrasound
records.model_family: YOLOv12-based real-time object detection network, adapted for fetal spinal ultrasound
records.clinical_problem: detecting vertebral abnormalities (hemivertebrae, butterfly vertebrae, block vertebrae) on prenatal spinal ultrasound
records.patient_population: 968 images from 735 fetuses (development) and 221 images from 185 fetuses (external test) at two hospitals
records.model_description: FSU-YOLOv12 is a deep learning object detector adapted from YOLOv12 to detect vertebral abnormalities on fetal spinal ultrasound images, with targeted optimizations to handle small vertebrae, acoustic shadowing, artifacts, and low tissue contrast. It was trained and validated on images from one hospital and independently tested on an external hospital's data, running in real time (149 frames per second) with a lightweight architecture (2.6M parameters).
records.dataset_size: 968 images from 735 fetuses (development); 221 images from 185 fetuses (external test)
records.headline_result: mAP(50) 91.9%, mAP(75) 55.9%, mAP 52.3%, precision 94.2%, recall 86.3%, F1 90.1%, 149 fps inference with 2.6M parameters
records.study_design: retrospective multicenter model development with external test set

records.title: Deep learning model integrated with data augmentation strategy based on CT for detecting and classifying pediatric pancreatic tumors
records.journal: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
records.model_family: YOLOv8 object detector with CMUNeXt encoder module, plus fusion data augmentation
records.clinical_problem: detection and classification of pediatric pancreatic tumors (pancreatoblastoma vs solid pseudopapillary neoplasm)
records.patient_population: 21 children with pancreatoblastoma and 70 children with solid pseudopapillary neoplasm
records.model_description: Abdominal CT images from children with pancreatoblastoma or solid pseudopapillary neoplasm are manually annotated for tumor regions, then an 8-fold data-augmented training set is used to train a modified YOLOv8 object detector (with a CMUNeXt encoder module) to detect tumors and classify them into the two tumor types.
records.headline_result: Best model (post-augmentation YOLOv8-CMUNeXt): precision 92.53%, recall 78.64%, mAP@0.5 86.29%, mAP0.5:0.95 68.45%, accuracy 85.71%/72.86% for the two tumor types

records.title: Assessment of the accuracy of lung lesions diagnosis in adolescents with osteosarcoma using artificial intelligence
records.model_family: AI lung-nodule detection algorithm, previously trained on an adult dataset
records.clinical_problem: detecting pulmonary metastases (lung nodules) in adolescents with osteosarcoma
records.patient_population: adolescents with osteosarcoma undergoing chest CT (248 CT scans evaluated)
records.model_description: An existing AI algorithm for lung nodule detection, originally trained on an adult dataset, was applied retrospectively to chest CT scans of adolescents with osteosarcoma to detect pulmonary nodules ≥4 mm (a target finding for metastasis staging), and its accuracy was compared against the reference diagnosis, quantifying false positives and false negatives.
records.dataset_size: 248 CT scans of adolescents with osteosarcoma
records.headline_result: Diagnostic accuracy 0.843 (95% CI 0.794-0.887); false positive rate 2%, false negative rate 13.7%; using the AI algorithm would increase sensitivity from 0.805 to 0.891, an absolute false-negative reduction of 8.6% (relative 44%)

records.title: Automated assessment of neonatal internal capsule maturation on T2-weighted MRI across 7T and 3T
records.model_family: Fully automated 3D deep learning segmentation framework
records.clinical_problem: quantitative assessment of neonatal brain white-matter (internal capsule) maturation
records.patient_population: neonates (term and preterm) imaged with structural T2-weighted MRI at 7T and 3T
records.model_description: A fully automated 3D deep learning model segments internal capsule subregions and myelin-related signal on structural T2-weighted neonatal MRI, trained on both high-resolution 7T and conventional 3T datasets. Derived volumetric and intensity metrics were modeled against postmenstrual and postnatal age, with normative modeling used to flag individual deviations, particularly in preterm infants.
records.headline_result: Segmentation accuracy Dice > 0.95 and relative volume difference < 5% across both field strengths; significant postmenstrual-age-related volumetric and intensity changes; normative modeling revealed significant deviations in preterm infants, especially for myelin-related intensity measures
records.study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study

records.title: Conus Medullaris Position in 9,808 Pediatric Lumbosacral MRI Examinations: A Large-Cohort Reference Distribution and the Normally Positioned Conus in Surgically Treated Tethered Cord
records.model_family: nnU-Net deep learning segmentation with IBSI-compliant radiomics and L1-penalized logistic regression
records.clinical_problem: reference distribution of conus medullaris position and radiomic diagnosis of tethered cord syndrome
records.patient_population: 9,808 pediatric lumbosacral MRI examinations at a single center; 475 preoperative children surgically treated for tethered cord
records.model_description: Conus medullaris termination levels were extracted from a large archive of pediatric lumbosacral MRI reports to build a normative reference distribution. An nnU-Net deep learning model was separately trained to automatically segment the conus medullaris on axial T2-weighted images, from which IBSI-compliant radiomic features were extracted and tested (with cross-validated logistic regression) for their ability to distinguish children surgically treated for tethered cord from controls.
records.headline_result: Conus terminated at L1 in 85.7% and L2 in 14.3% of the reference cohort (n=9,655); low-lying conus (≥L3) in only 0.05%; among 475 children surgically treated for tethered cord, 99.6% had a normally positioned conus; automated segmentation achieved held-out Dice of 0.85; neither conus position nor radiomics distinguished tethered cord from controls
records.study_design: retrospective single-center large-cohort reference-distribution and nested case-control study

records.title: Three-phase learning framework for first-trimester fetal echocardiography plan classification via knowledge distillation and CBAM-enhanced DenseNet
records.model_family: DenseNet-201 backbone with convolutional block attention module (CBAM) and knowledge distillation, staged/progressive training
records.clinical_problem: classifying first-trimester fetal echocardiography standard views/planes to support early detection of congenital heart defects
records.patient_population: first-trimester fetuses (12-14 weeks gestation) undergoing fetal echocardiography
records.model_description: A three-phase progressive learning framework built on a DenseNet-201 backbone enhanced with a convolutional block attention module and knowledge distillation classifies first-trimester fetal echocardiography standard views/planes, addressing the challenge of underdeveloped cardiac structures and probe-movement variability at this gestational stage. Training proceeds in stages, from clear to deformed to the full image set, to progressively improve generalization on a minority, harder-to-classify view class, with the aim of supporting earlier detection of fetal heart defects.
records.headline_result: 3% and 1% overall accuracy/metric improvement over state-of-the-art baselines; approximately 5% recall and 3% F1 improvement for the minority X-sign view class
records.study_design: retrospective technical development and benchmark evaluation

records.model_family: deep neural networks vs. simple demographic models (comparative benchmarking)

records.patient_population: Youth from a large developmental clinical cohort, evaluated for diverse psychiatric and non-psychiatric phenotypes using EEG and fMRI
records.model_description: Machine learning models, including deep neural networks, were trained on EEG and fMRI data from a large youth developmental cohort to predict psychiatric and non-psychiatric phenotypes. Their performance was compared against simple models using only demographics and recording site; imaging-based models did not outperform the demographic-only models for clinical phenotypes.

records.title: Accurate Recognition of Pneumonia and COVID-19 by Geometric Shape Normalization of Lung Region Using Automatic Landmark Detection and Piecewise Affine Warping
records.model_family: ResNet-18 CNN with geometric shape normalization (landmark detection, Procrustes analysis, piecewise affine warping) and Grad-CAM interpretability
records.clinical_problem: pneumonia and COVID-19 classification on chest X-ray
records.patient_population: COVID-19 Radiography Database and a balanced adult-pediatric mixed dataset including pediatric cases from the Kermany dataset
records.model_description: A ResNet-18 landmark detector locates 15 points defining the lung contour on a chest X-ray, which are used to geometrically normalize (warp) the lung region to a standard shape and remove positioning/scale variation. A second ResNet-18 classifier then labels the normalized image as COVID-19, viral pneumonia, or normal. Grad-CAM and a cropping experiment were used to check whether classification relied on true lung pathology versus acquisition artifacts.
records.headline_result: 98.60±0.26% accuracy and 98.00% F1-Macro on the COVID-19 Radiography Database (5-fold cross-validation); geometrically normalized images outperformed non-aligned artifact-masked images, 94.67% vs 94.17%, on the balanced adult-pediatric mixed dataset
records.study_design: retrospective technical development and evaluation study

records.title: Variation in infant subcortical brain development from 6 to 12 months in Down syndrome
records.model_family: Deep-learning repeated-measures segmentation approach for harmonized multisite MRI
records.body_region: brain (subcortical structures: amygdala, caudate, hippocampus, pallidum, putamen, thalamus)
records.clinical_problem: characterizing subcortical brain development in infants with Down syndrome
records.patient_population: 44 infants with Down syndrome and 39 control infants without Down syndrome, imaged at 6 and 12 months in a multisite cohort
records.model_description: High-resolution T1- and T2-weighted MRI acquired during natural sleep in infants was harmonized across sites and passed through a deep-learning, repeated-measures segmentation approach to derive total intracranial volume and bilateral subcortical structure volumes. Hierarchical linear modeling was then used to compare longitudinal brain growth between infants with and without Down syndrome.
records.dataset_size: 44 infants with Down syndrome and 39 control infants
records.headline_result: Intracranial volume in infants with Down syndrome was 12.6% lower at 6 months and 16.3% lower at 12 months than controls (p<.001); subcortical structure volumes were 6.9-13.1% lower (p≤.003), with slower growth from 6 to 12 months except in the amygdala and putamen

records.title: Bidirectional Domain Shift Failure in Radiograph Fracture Classification Across Out-of-Distribution Pediatric and Mixed-Age Multi-Region Data
records.model_family: Two separately trained ResNet-50 CNN classifiers
records.clinical_problem: fracture detection generalizability between pediatric and adult radiographs
records.patient_population: pediatric wrist radiographs (GRAZPEDWRI-DX, n=20,327) and a mixed-age multi-region radiograph dataset (FracAtlas, n=4,083)
records.model_description: Two ResNet-50 fracture classifiers were trained separately, one on a pediatric wrist radiograph dataset and one on a mixed-age multi-region radiograph dataset, then each was tested on the other (opposing) population's data. Grad-CAM was used to visualize what each model relied on.
records.headline_result: Both models achieved acceptable internal test accuracy (82.2% and 83.7%), but cross-testing on the opposing population caused specificity to collapse to 0% in both directions while sensitivity was artificially inflated to 100%; the FracAtlas-trained model misread normal pediatric growth plates as fractures
records.study_design: retrospective cross-dataset diagnostic accuracy and generalizability study

records.title: A machine-learning model for quantitative assessment of maxillary sinus volume and involvement in children based on computed tomography
records.clinical_problem: quantitative assessment of chronic rhinosinusitis severity (sinus volume and inflammatory involvement)
records.patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing CT for chronic rhinosinusitis
records.model_description: A 3D convolutional neural network was trained to automatically segment the maxillary sinuses on pediatric CT scans, using manually annotated expert segmentations as ground truth, then compute sinus volume and the percentage of the sinus affected by inflammatory changes, giving a quantitative alternative to descriptive CT scoring of chronic rhinosinusitis in children.
records.dataset_size: 92 CT scans of the paranasal sinuses in pediatric patients
records.headline_result: mean sensitivity, precision and Dice coefficient near 90%; root-mean-square error 0.4 cm3 for sinus volume and 1.3 percentage points for inflammatory involvement
records.study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study

records.title: Accurate Gestational Age Estimation with a Deep Learning Model Using Ultrasound Images to Enhance Detection of Fetal Growth Restriction and Small-For-Gestational-Age Fetuses in Late Pregnancy: A Prospective Cohort Study​
records.model_name: GAUGE (GARBH-Ini Ultrasound image-based Gestational age Estimator)
records.model_family: Multi-task deep learning model with an image-based conformal prediction framework for out-of-distribution rejection
records.clinical_problem: gestational age estimation and detection of fetal growth restriction / small-for-gestational-age fetuses in late pregnancy
records.patient_population: 6,579 participants from the GARBH-Ini and WINGS prospective cohorts in North India (development); 1,577 internal test participants; 311 external test participants from a separate ultrasound lab
records.model_description: A multi-task deep learning model segments the fetal head in an ultrasound image and estimates gestational age directly from image features, rather than relying on standard fetal-size biometry formulas. A conformal-prediction step rejects out-of-distribution images before inference. It was trained on two prospective Indian cohorts and tested on an internal held-out set and an independent external site using a different ultrasound machine.
records.dataset_size: 46,926 head ultrasound images from 6,579 participants (development); 1,577 participants internal test set; 311 participants external test set
records.headline_result: Mean absolute error 3.5 days on internal test set (37.2% lower than Hadlock, 25.4% lower than INTERGROWTH-21st formulas); external test MAE 5.89 days; detected 77.6%, 88.7% and 89.7% of fetal growth restriction cases at 26-28, 30-32 and ≥35 weeks respectively, versus 48.6% (Hadlock) and 64.1% (INTERGROWTH-21st) at ≥35 weeks
records.study_design: prospective multi-cohort development and external validation study

records.title: Bone age assessment via joint feature learning, epiphyseal evaluation, and hybrid vision-language modeling
records.model_family: hybrid deep-learning framework: multi-scale joint detection, semi-supervised contrastive language-image pretraining for pseudo-labeling, and LDA/normalization-based global attention
records.clinical_problem: bone age assessment for diagnosing pediatric growth disorders
records.patient_population: 1,000 public RSNA bone age images and 9,577 additional clinical radiographs
records.model_description: A deep-learning bone age assessment pipeline combines a multi-scale joint-detection module for the hand and wrist, semi-supervised contrastive language-image pretraining used to generate pseudo-labels for epiphyseal maturity, and an attention-enhanced classification network, producing a continuous bone age estimate from a hand radiograph. It was validated on the public RSNA bone age dataset plus additional clinical radiographs, improving joint-detection rate over a YOLO baseline.
records.dataset_size: 1,000 public RSNA bone age images and 9,577 clinical radiographs
records.headline_result: 99.98% joint-detection rate (4.12% improvement over YOLOv10), 81.8% average classification accuracy, mean absolute error 0.25 years, RMSE 0.29 years
records.study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study

records.title: Machine Learning Applications in Pediatric Ultrasound for Appendicitis Diagnosis and Severity Stratification: A Systematic Review
records.model_family: Machine learning (tabular models combining structured ultrasound descriptors with clinical/lab features)
records.clinical_problem: appendicitis diagnosis and severity stratification on pediatric ultrasound
records.patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing ultrasound evaluation for suspected acute appendicitis, across 11 included studies (40-780 patients each)
records.model_description: Systematic review (PRISMA 2020, PROBAST-AI) of 11 studies applying machine learning to pediatric ultrasound for appendicitis diagnosis and severity stratification, most combining structured ultrasound descriptors with clinical and laboratory features. Reviews internal and the one available cross-site external validation study.
records.headline_result: Internal diagnostic AUROC up to 0.993 (range 0.91-0.96 across tabular models); one external validation study showed diagnostic AUROC decreasing from 0.96 internally to 0.85 externally

records.title: Diverse Concept Modeling (DiCoMX): Domain-specific self-supervised pre-training strategy for chest X-ray foundation models
records.model_family: self-supervised learning Vision Transformer with knowledge-distillation pseudo-labeling (domain-specific chest X-ray foundation model)
records.clinical_problem: chest X-ray foundation model for pneumonia and COVID-19 detection, multi-label disease classification, and lung segmentation
records.patient_population: adult and pediatric patients across multiple downstream chest radiograph datasets
records.model_description: DiCoMX is a self-supervised learning framework that pretrains a Vision Transformer on 600,638 unlabeled chest radiographs using pseudo-labels distilled from a teacher model at both the local (token) and global (whole-image) level. The pretrained backbone is then applied to independent downstream tasks including pneumonia and COVID-19 detection in adult and pediatric populations, multi-label disease classification, and lung segmentation, and the pre-training code is publicly released.
records.release_evidence: The code for pre-training foundation models using DiCoMX is publicly available at: https://github.com/Pediatric-Accelerated-Intelligence-Lab/DiCoMX
records.dataset_size: 600,638 chest radiographs for pretraining; multiple independent downstream datasets including adult and pediatric cohorts
records.headline_result: DiCoMX outperforms existing self-supervised learning methods on downstream pneumonia/COVID-19 detection, multi-label classification, and lung segmentation tasks (specific metric values not given in the abstract)
records.study_design: retrospective technical development and benchmark evaluation

records.title: Learning to read a second language establishes a parallel L2 representation alongside the native one in the VWFA
records.clinical_problem: classification of second-language literacy acquisition stage from fMRI activation patterns
records.patient_population: Native Mandarin-speaking children at three stages of second-language (English) literacy acquisition: pre-readers, beginning readers, and advanced readers
records.model_description: fMRI was collected while native Mandarin-speaking children at different stages of learning to read English (L2) passively viewed L1 and L2 words. A supervised machine learning classifier used visual word form area activation patterns to discriminate the three L2 literacy-acquisition groups; L2-based activation, but not L1-based activation, reliably separated the groups.

records.title: ASTAR: Automated induction of STAndardized radiology Reporting templates from large-scale clinical free-text corpora
records.model_name: ASTAR (Automated induction of STAndardized radiology Reporting templates)
records.model_family: LLM-based framework for automated radiology report template induction
records.clinical_problem: standardizing radiology reporting templates for fetal brain MRI
records.patient_population: 4,215 fetal brain MRI reports from multiple centers
records.model_description: ASTAR is a large language model framework that automatically induces a standardized structured-reporting template directly from a large corpus of free-text fetal brain MRI reports, replacing the manual, expert-consensus process of template construction. It was compared against two expert-curated templates on template coverage, information fidelity, diagnostic fidelity and expert-rated usability.
records.dataset_size: 4,215 fetal brain MRI reports from multiple centers
records.headline_result: ASTAR-induced template surpassed two expert-curated templates across template coverage, information fidelity, diagnostic fidelity, and expert-rated usability, reducing template development from weeks of committee deliberation to hours of automated processing

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Obstetrics and Prenatal Medicine: Current Evidence, Clinical Validation and Implementation
records.clinical_problem: AI-assisted prenatal ultrasound and fetal MRI interpretation, including standard-plane recognition, image quality assessment, fetal biometry, fetal cardiac screening, and prediction of growth restriction, preterm birth and preeclampsia
records.patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound and MRI
records.model_description: This narrative review (literature from 2021-2026) summarizes AI applications in prenatal medicine. The strongest evidence supports AI-assisted standard-plane recognition, image-quality assessment and fetal biometry on ultrasound, with emerging evidence for fetal cardiac screening, blind-sweep ultrasound, fetal MRI segmentation and placental phenotyping, and for predicting fetal growth restriction, preterm birth and preeclampsia. Most applications remain limited by retrospective design, enriched datasets and insufficient external validation; the authors recommend a human-in-the-loop model with prospective validation before autonomous clinical use.

records.title: Edge-Guided Deep Learning for Enhanced Pneumonia Detection in Radiographs
records.journal: Indian Journal of Radiology and Imaging
records.model_family: deep learning CNN with multiscale feature extraction, channel-wise attention, and edge-aware loss
records.clinical_problem: pneumonia detection/classification on chest radiographs
records.patient_population: children (Kermany pediatric chest X-ray dataset)
records.model_description: PMSAN classifies chest radiographs as pneumonia or normal, combining multiscale feature extraction and channel-wise attention with a novel edge-aware loss function to sharpen detection of subtle pathology. It was trained and evaluated on the public Kermany pediatric chest X-ray dataset, with interpretability supported by ROC curves, attention maps and edge maps.
records.headline_result: test-set accuracy 96.4%, precision 97.9%, recall 97.2%, F1-score 97.6%, AUC 0.988; five-fold cross-validation accuracy 96.4% +/- 0.5%, AUC 0.988 +/- 0.003, outperforming ResNet18 and VGG16 baselines
records.study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study

records.title: Unique Opportunities and Challenges of Artificial Intelligence in Pediatric Imaging
records.journal: Indian Journal of Radiology and Imaging
records.clinical_problem: AI applications across pediatric imaging, with bone age assessment and chest radiograph interpretation as the most established use cases
records.patient_population: pediatric imaging patients generally
records.model_description: This narrative review examines why pediatric imaging AI differs from adult radiology AI, citing developmental variability, different disease epidemiology, imaging constraints, and limited pediatric datasets. It finds the most mature applications are in image acquisition, dose reduction and workflow optimization, with bone age assessment and chest radiograph interpretation the most established interpretive/prognostic use cases, while adult-trained models often underperform in children. It calls for pediatric-specific design, shared data infrastructure, federated learning, and age-stratified prospective validation.

records.title: Out-of-Distribution Detection and Radiological Data Monitoring Using Statistical Process Control.
records.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
records.model_family: feature-representation drift detection with statistical process control
records.clinical_problem: knowing when a deployed model is being shown images it was not built for, including adult models being fed pediatric radiographs
records.patient_population: adult and pediatric chest radiographs, and CT images, used as drift scenarios
records.model_description: Not a diagnostic model but a guard on one: it detects when an incoming image is out of distribution for the deployed model, and monitors the data stream for gradual drift using statistical process control. One of its three demonstrations is exactly the failure mode a children's hospital should worry about — telling adult chest radiographs from pediatric ones, which it flagged within a day of the shift beginning. Modality- and model-agnostic by design.
records.headline_result: sensitivity for out-of-distribution detection 0.980 (CT), 0.984 (chest radiograph modality) and 0.854 (pediatric versus adult chest radiographs); a simulated adult-to-pediatric drift was detected within a day at a low false positive rate

records.title: Children Are Not Small Adults: Addressing Limited Generalizability of an Adult Deep Learning CT Organ Segmentation Model to the Pediatric Population.
records.journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
records.model_family: nnU-Net, evaluated and then retrained or fine-tuned on pediatric data
records.clinical_problem: whether the field's default open organ segmentation model, built on adults, is safe to use on children
records.patient_population: 300 adult and 359 pediatric abdominal CT scans from external datasets
records.model_description: The title is the finding. TotalSegmentator, trained on adults, drops from 0.81 to 0.73 mean Dice on pediatric scans, and the failure concentrates in the small structures — adrenal glands fall to 0.35-0.41 against 0.68-0.69 in adults. The paper then shows both fixes work: a pediatric-only model and an adult model fine-tuned on children each beat it on every organ. This is the cleanest available demonstration of why adult-trained tools need pediatric validation before deployment.
records.release_evidence: evaluates the openly available TotalSegmentator model
records.headline_result: mean Dice 0.73 in children versus 0.81 in adults (P < .001); adrenal gland Dice 0.35-0.41 versus 0.68-0.69; pediatric-specific training and fine-tuning both improved every organ, by over 0.2 Dice for the adrenals
records.study_design: retrospective external evaluation with model retraining

records.title: An automated pipeline for computation and analysis of functional ventilation and perfusion lung MRI with matrix pencil decomposition: TrueLung.

records.patient_population: 75 children with cystic fibrosis imaged at 1.5 T
records.model_description: An end-to-end pipeline that turns free-breathing, contrast-free lung MRI into ventilation and perfusion maps and quantified defect percentages, delivered as a short clinical report. It was feasible in every child attempted, with a six-minute scan and twenty-minute processing. The authors also report how often a human had to correct the segmentation and what difference that made to the numbers, which is the honest way to describe an automated pipeline in clinical use.
records.headline_result: feasible in all children, 6 min 20 s mean scan time; automatic whole-lung quantification satisfactory in 88% of patients and lobar quantification in 73%; manual refinement changed relative ventilation and perfusion by 0.7% and 2.0%

records.model_description: The comparison the vendors do not run: three commercially available bone age programs on one cohort, against a three-expert Greulich-Pyle ground truth, reporting dropout rates alongside accuracy. All three were reliable across the main age range and differed mainly at the edges of childhood, and the spread between the programs was smaller than the spread between the human readers. records.title: Clinical validation of explainable AI for fetal growth scans through multi-level, cross-institutional prospective end-user evaluation.
records.model_family: progressive concept bottleneck model with segmentation
records.clinical_problem: giving the sonographer usable feedback during a fetal growth scan, rather than a verdict afterwards
records.patient_population: 9,352 annotated images for development and 100 prospectively collected videos across centres
records.model_description: Explains itself in the terms clinicians already use: whether the image is optimized, whether each anatomical landmark is present, and where those landmarks are. The evaluation is the unusual part — prospective, across centres, with clinicians judging whether the explanations were correct and whether they were useful, and a check that the model can tell an experienced operator from an inexperienced one. Most explainable-AI papers stop at the method; this one tests whether the explanations help.
records.dataset_size: 9,352 images for development, 100 videos for prospective evaluation
records.headline_result: 96.3% classification accuracy; plane-quality assessment on par with clinicians; explanations judged correct in 74-83% and useful in 72-75% of cases; reliably discriminated clinician experience levels (p < 0.01)
records.study_design: prospective cross-centre validation with end-user evaluation

records.model_description: Measures glymphatic function (diffusion along the perivascular space), perivascular space volume, CSF volume and white matter anisotropy, then feeds those indices to an automated machine-learning framework to separate autistic from typically developing children. The glymphatic index also tracked autism severity and developmental delay, which is what makes this more than a classifier.
records.dataset_size: 178 children across two centers, with a separate validation cohort of 61
records.headline_result: area under the curve 0.84 for autism diagnosis; glymphatic index correlated with severity (r = -0.27) and developmental delay (r = 0.63)

records.title: Scanner-based real-time three-dimensional brain + body slice-to-volume reconstruction for T2-weighted 0.55-T low-field fetal magnetic resonance imaging.
records.model_family: deep learning slice-to-volume registration pipeline deployed through Gadgetron
records.clinical_problem: motion-corrected 3D fetal MRI has stayed a research technique because reconstruction happens offline, after the patient has gone home
records.patient_population: 12 prospective cases at 22-40 weeks gestation, plus 83 retrospective datasets
records.model_description: Puts fetal motion correction inside the scanner rather than in a research pipeline afterwards: reconstruction launches automatically during the examination and the 3D brain and body volumes appear on the console about seven minutes after the last stack, while the patient is still there. It is also the first such solution reported for a low-field 0.55-T scanner, which is the class of machine that could make fetal MRI more widely affordable.
records.headline_result: reconstructions available on the scanner console 6:42 ± 3:13 minutes after the final stack, rated good to acceptable for interpretation

records.model_description: Anonymous online survey of Society for German-speaking Pediatric Radiologists (GPR) and Swiss Society for Pediatric Radiology (SGPR) members on attitudes toward and current use of AI and teleradiology in pediatric radiology.
records.headline_result: 38.9% fully agreed AI is relevant to pediatric radiology; >80% said bone age determination is well-suited for AI, yet only 31% routinely use such a solution

records.title: Current progress in targeted pharmacotherapy to treat symptoms of major depressive disorder: moving from broad-spectrum treatments to precision psychiatry.
records.exclusion_reason: not primarily imaging-focused; pharmacotherapy review of major depressive disorder in which neuroimaging and machine learning are mentioned only as one of several precision-psychiatry approaches, not pediatric-specific

records.title: Video Clip Extraction From Fetal Ultrasound Scans Using Artificial Intelligence to Allow Remote Second Expert Review for Congenital Heart Disease.
records.clinical_problem: enabling remote second-expert review of fetal cardiac ultrasound to improve detection of congenital heart disease
records.patient_population: 48 fetuses (24 normal, 24 with congenital heart disease)
records.model_description: AI automatically extracts short video clips of the fetal heart from streamed ultrasound video; these clips, versus manually saved still images, are used by expert clinicians for remote second review to detect cardiac abnormalities.
records.headline_result: Second review with AI video clips improved CHD detection sensitivity from 0.792 to 0.975 (vs 0.892 with still images)
records.study_design: retrospective reader study using AI-extracted video clips

records.title: Harmonizing flows: Leveraging normalizing flows for unsupervised and source-free MRI harmonization.
records.model_family: normalizing flow network + shallow harmonizer network
records.clinical_problem: Harmonizing brain MRI acquired across different sites/scanners without needing paired data or source-site access, evaluated including neonatal brain segmentation and neonatal brain age estimation
records.patient_population: Adult and neonatal brain MRI datasets
records.model_description: A normalizing-flow network learns the distribution of a source imaging domain; a shallow harmonizer network is trained (and updated at inference) to make new-site images match that learned source distribution, unsupervised and without needing source-site data at inference, tested on neonatal brain segmentation and brain-age estimation as well as adult brain MRI
records.headline_result: Superior performance compared with existing harmonization methods (exact metric not given in abstract)
records.study_design: retrospective algorithm development and cross-domain validation study

records.title: AI-based non-invasive imaging technologies for early autism spectrum disorder diagnosis: A short review and future directions.
records.clinical_problem: reviewing AI applications using structural MRI (radiomics) for early diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder in infants and children
records.patient_population: infants and children (literature review)
records.model_description: Short review of AI tools applied to structural brain MRI radiomics for early ASD diagnosis, covering cortical parcellation methods and available databases.

records.title: Ultrasonic-Based Radiomics Signature With Machine Learning for Differentiating Prognostic Subsets of Pediatric Peripheral Neuroblastic Tumors: A Retrospective Study.
records.clinical_problem: Can ultrasound-based radiomics help distinguish prognostic subsets of pediatric neuroblastic tumors?
records.patient_population: 73 children with neuroblastic tumors
records.model_description: Ultrasound radiomics features are combined with clinical characteristics in machine learning models (extreme gradient boosting selected as best) to differentiate prognostic subsets of pediatric neuroblastic tumors.
records.headline_result: Validation AUC 0.941 (combined model), 0.918 (radiomics-only model)

records.title: Clinical Prospects for Artificial Intelligence in Obstetrics and Gynecology.
records.exclusion_reason: broad AI-in-obstetrics/gynecology review; fetal imaging is one incidental bullet among mostly adult gynecologic-oncology and reproduction content

records.title: BO-CLAHE enhancing neonatal chest X-ray image quality for improved lesion classification.
records.model_family: Bayesian optimization of CLAHE contrast enhancement
records.clinical_problem: improving image quality of low-quality portable neonatal chest X-rays to aid lesion classification without increasing radiation dose
records.patient_population: preterm and high-risk neonates undergoing portable chest X-ray
records.model_description: Bayesian optimization automatically selects CLAHE contrast-enhancement hyperparameters for neonatal chest radiographs, improving image quality and downstream deep-learning lesion classification such as transient tachypnea of the newborn.
records.headline_result: Improved classification performance for diagnosing transient tachypnea of the newborn

records.title: AXpert: human expert facilitated privacy-preserving large language models for abdominal X-ray report labeling.
records.model_family: large language model (Gemma-7B) with a distilled BERT-based model
records.clinical_problem: Automatically labeling pediatric abdominal X-ray radiology reports for the presence and subtype (pneumatosis, portal venous gas, free air) of necrotizing enterocolitis, to support NEC research
records.patient_population: pediatric abdominal X-ray reports from C.S. Mott Children's Hospital (exact n not stated)
records.model_description: AXpert uses a privacy-preserving, instruction-fine-tuned large language model (Gemma-7B) and a distilled BERT-based version to automatically annotate pediatric abdominal X-ray reports for necrotizing enterocolitis presence and subtype (pneumatosis, portal venous gas, free air), trained and deployed locally.
records.headline_result: Gemma-7B F1 score 0.9 ± 0.015 for detecting NEC-positive samples, a 132% improvement over the BlueBERT baseline
records.study_design: retrospective model development and evaluation against baseline BERT models

records.title: Disorganization of Small-World Functional Brain Networks in First-Episode, Treatment-Naïve Adolescents With Major Depressive Disorder.
records.clinical_problem: differentiating adolescents with first-episode major depressive disorder from healthy controls
records.patient_population: 23 adolescents with first-episode, treatment-naive major depressive disorder and 27 matched healthy controls
records.model_description: A machine-learning multivariate diagnostic model uses resting-state fMRI graph-theory network topology metrics to classify adolescents with major depressive disorder versus healthy controls.

records.title: Active search for tuberculosis in three youth detention centers in Peru.
records.journal: Revista peruana de medicina experimental y salud publica
records.clinical_problem: Can AI-assisted automated reading of chest X-rays help find active tuberculosis cases through active screening in youth detention centers?

records.model_description: AI software provided automated reading of chest X-rays as part of an active tuberculosis screening algorithm, combined with GeneXpert Ultra molecular testing and clinical evaluation.
records.headline_result: 8 of 105 GeneXpert tests (8.5%) confirmed TB; screening rate 1250 per 100,000, ten times the general-population rate

records.title: Automatic Measurement of Frontomaxillary Facial Angle in Fetal Ultrasound Images Using Deep Learning.
records.clinical_problem: Automatically measure the frontomaxillary facial angle on prenatal ultrasound for trisomy 21 screening
records.patient_population: 1,549 fetal ultrasound images
records.model_description: Trains a deep learning network to segment critical facial regions on 2D fetal ultrasound images, then uses a keypoint detection network to locate landmark points and compute the frontomaxillary facial angle automatically.
records.headline_result: Mean absolute error 2.354 degrees, outperforming typical junior-expert accuracy standards

records.title: The value of CT-based radiomics for differentiation of pleural effusions in bacterial pneumonia and Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia in children.
records.clinical_problem: Distinguishing bacterial pneumonia from Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia as the cause of pleural effusion in children using chest CT
records.patient_population: 535 hospitalized children with pleural effusion (167 bacterial, 368 Mycoplasma)
records.model_description: Radiomics features are manually extracted from non-contrast chest CT regions of pleural effusion, reduced by feature-selection methods (Select K Best, mRMR, LASSO), and input to a logistic regression model that classifies the effusion as bacterial or Mycoplasma pneumoniae-related
records.headline_result: AUC 0.942 (training set), 0.917 (test set)

records.title: An artificial intelligence model for Lhermitte's sign in patients with pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis: A follow-up study.
records.journal: Advances in clinical and experimental medicine : official organ Wroclaw Medical University
records.clinical_problem: Investigate correlation between Lhermitte's sign and AI-based radiological characteristics (upper cervical spinal cord lesions) in pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis
records.patient_population: 92 patients with pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (from 1,298 records screened)
records.model_description: Uses AI-based radiological analysis of spinal cord MRI to characterize cervical lesions (C1-4) and correlate them with the clinical sign Lhermitte's sign in pediatric-onset MS patients.
records.headline_result: Upper cervical lesion (C1-4) frequency higher in groups with current/past Lhermitte's sign vs never (p=0.017)

records.title: Routine and Advanced Neurologic Imaging at 0.55-T MRI: Opportunities and Challenges.
records.journal: Radiographics : a review publication of the Radiological Society of North America, Inc
records.exclusion_reason: general neuroradiology review of 0.55-T MRI; not pediatric-focused, AI mentioned only in passing

records.title: AI and early diagnostics: mapping fetal facial expressions through development, evolution, and 4D ultrasound.
records.clinical_problem: using AI and 4D ultrasound to analyze fetal facial expressions as a potential prenatal marker of neurodevelopmental disorders
records.patient_population: fetuses (review, no single cohort)
records.model_description: A narrative review of AI-assisted analysis of 4D ultrasound fetal facial movements, discussing their potential as diagnostic markers for prenatal neurodevelopmental disorders such as Bell's Palsy and Ramsay Hunt Syndrome.

records.title: Association between deep learning radiomics based on placental MRI and preeclampsia with fetal growth restriction: A multicenter study.
records.model_family: deep learning radiomics on semi-supervised placental segmentation
records.clinical_problem: identifying preeclampsia and, within it, the pregnancies where the fetus is growth restricted
records.patient_population: 420 pregnant women across centres: 140 with preeclampsia (65 with fetal growth restriction) and 280 normotensive
records.model_description: Segments the placenta automatically on T2-weighted MRI and derives a combined radiomic and deep-learning signature that separates preeclamptic from normotensive pregnancies, and then separates those where the fetus is growth restricted. The discrimination is markedly better for the growth-restricted subgroup than for preeclampsia without restriction, which is the clinically consequential half.
records.headline_result: AUC 0.84-0.89 across training, test, internal and external validation for preeclampsia; 0.918 for preeclampsia with fetal growth restriction versus normotensive, and 0.742 without restriction; placental segmentation Dice 0.917

records.title: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging traits associated with adverse right ventricular remodeling in repaired tetralogy of Fallot: A Single Center Outcomes Using cardiovascular magnetic resonance in Tetralogy of Fallot study.
records.journal: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
records.clinical_problem: Automate segmentation of cardiac MRI to study right ventricular remodeling and identify imaging traits associated with adverse RV remodeling in repaired tetralogy of Fallot
records.patient_population: 758 patients with repaired tetralogy of Fallot at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia; 152 with 2 analyzable CMR scans
records.model_description: Uses the nnU-Net deep learning method to automatically segment left and right ventricular blood pool and myocardium from 2D short-axis cardiac MRI, then computes volumetric remodeling rates to study risk factors for right ventricular deterioration after tetralogy of Fallot repair.
records.headline_result: Pulmonic valve replacement patients had significantly lower RV remodeling rates than natural-history patients; baseline LV measures associated with RV remodeling rates

records.title: A fully automated U-net based ROIs localization and bone age assessment method.
records.clinical_problem: skeletal maturity / bone age assessment
records.patient_population: adolescents undergoing hand-wrist radiography for bone age assessment (public RSNA dataset and an in-house dataset)
records.model_description: Given a hand-wrist radiograph, a U-Net first automatically localizes the regions of interest used in the Tanner-Whitehouse method, then an InceptionResNetV2 network extracts features from both the regions of interest and the whole image to estimate bone age, combining the region-based (TW3) and whole-image (Greulich-Pyle) approaches. It was trained and evaluated on the public RSNA bone age dataset and an in-house dataset.
records.dataset_size: public RSNA bone age dataset plus an in-house dataset (exact case counts not stated)
records.headline_result: Localization precision of 99.1% on the public RSNA dataset; mean absolute error 0.38 years (males) and 0.45 years (females) on RSNA, and 0.41 years (males) and 0.44 years (females) on the in-house dataset.
records.study_design: technical development with retrospective benchmark validation

records.title: Use of artificial intelligence for gestational age estimation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
records.clinical_problem: How accurately AI models estimate gestational age from ultrasound compared with the standard reference
records.patient_population: Pregnant women across 17 included studies
records.model_description: Systematic review and meta-analysis pooling AI models (mainly CNNs) that estimate gestational age from 2D ultrasound images or blind-sweep video against ultrasound-based reference standards
records.headline_result: Pooled mean GA error 4.32 days (2D images) and 2.55 days (blind-sweep video)

records.title: Automated pediatric TMJ articular disk identification and displacement classification in MRI with machine learning.
records.exclusion_reason: Temporomandibular joint MRI analysis published in a dental journal; TMJ disorder assessment falls within oral/maxillofacial (dental) practice, matching the 'dental' exclusion category rather than general pediatric radiology.

records.title: Enhancing pediatric congenital heart disease detection using customized 1D CNN algorithm and phonocardiogram signals.
