records.title: Forensic bone age assessment of hand and wrist joint MRI images in Chinese han male adolescents based on deep convolutional neural networks.
records.clinical_problem: Forensic bone age assessment (determining whether a person is above or below legal age thresholds of 12/14/16/18) from hand and wrist MRI in Chinese Han males
records.patient_population: 282 Chinese Han males aged 6.0-21.0 years
records.model_description: A deep learning model extracts and enhances epiphyseal features from hand and wrist MRI to classify subjects into legal age categories (12/14/16/18-year thresholds) and regress a continuous bone age estimate.
records.headline_result: Adult vs minor classification accuracy 91.1%; minor age-threshold classification accuracy 91.1-96.4%; regression MAE 1.24 years

records.title: Machine Learning Analysis in Diffusion Kurtosis Imaging for Discriminating Pediatric Posterior Fossa Tumors: A Repeatability and Accuracy Pilot Study.
records.model_family: Random Forest machine learning classifier with SMOTE balancing
records.clinical_problem: discriminating pediatric posterior fossa tumor subtype using diffusion kurtosis imaging
records.patient_population: 34 children (mean age 7.48 years) with posterior fossa tumors (medulloblastoma, pilocytic astrocytoma, ependymoma)
records.model_description: Whole-tumor and region-of-interest diffusion kurtosis imaging metrics are compared for measurement repeatability, then whole-tumor (VOI-based) DKI metrics from a SMOTE-balanced dataset are used to train a Random Forest classifier that discriminates medulloblastoma, pilocytic astrocytoma, and ependymoma.
records.headline_result: Random Forest classification accuracy 0.928

records.title: The Approach to Sensing the True Fetal Heart Rate for CTG Monitoring: An Evaluation of Effectiveness of Deep Learning with Doppler Ultrasound Signals.
records.clinical_problem: distinguishing fetal from maternal heart-rate origin in Doppler-derived CTG monitoring to avoid misinterpreting maternal heart rate as fetal
records.patient_population: 425 labor-monitoring cases
records.model_description: input Doppler ultrasound signal segments annotated by a midwife; output a classification of whether the autocorrelation-derived heart rate is of fetal or maternal origin
records.dataset_size: 425 cases (30,160 fetal and 2,160 maternal data points)
records.headline_result: AUC 0.98

records.title: Validation of an AI-Powered Automated X-ray Bone Age Analyzer in Chinese Children and Adolescents: A Comparison with the Tanner-Whitehouse 3 Method.
records.clinical_problem: Validating a commercially available AI-powered bone-age analyzer against the Tanner-Whitehouse 3 method in Chinese children and adolescents
records.patient_population: 900 Chinese children and adolescents from 30 centers
records.model_description: A commercially available AI-powered X-ray bone-age analyzer, using a deep-learning automated bone-age-assessment system, estimates TW3 radius-ulna-short-bone and carpal bone age from hand-wrist radiographs, compared with expert and resident raters
records.release_evidence: commercially available artificial intelligence (AI)-powered X-ray bone age analyzer
records.headline_result: TW3-RUS mean absolute error 0.48+/-0.42 years; TW3 carpal MAE 0.48+/-0.65 years, matching or exceeding doctor raters

records.title: Comparative analysis of deep-learning-based bone age estimation between whole lateral cephalometric and the cervical vertebral region in children.
records.journal: The Journal of clinical pediatric dentistry
records.clinical_problem: Comparing whole lateral cephalometric radiographs versus the cervical vertebral region alone for deep-learning bone age estimation in growing children
records.patient_population: 1,050 patients aged 4-18 years with same-day lateral cephalometric and hand-wrist radiographs
records.model_description: Two pretrained CNNs (InceptionResNet-v2, NASNet-Large) are trained to estimate bone age from either the whole lateral cephalometric radiograph or a cropped cervical-vertebrae region of interest, labeled using hand-wrist-radiograph-derived bone age, with Grad-CAM used to visualize model focus
records.headline_result: The whole-cephalogram-trained model outperformed the cervical-vertebrae-ROI-trained model (exact error metrics not given in abstract)

records.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of an Integrated AI Tool to Estimate Gestational Age From Blind Ultrasound Sweeps.
records.model_family: deep learning model embedded in a low-cost battery-powered ultrasound device
records.clinical_problem: dating a pregnancy where no trained sonographer and no high-specification machine is available
records.patient_population: 400 individuals with viable single first-trimester pregnancies in Lusaka, Zambia and Chapel Hill, North Carolina
records.model_description: The productized form of the blind-sweep gestational age model: the algorithm ships inside a cheap battery-powered probe, and the study puts it in the hands of novice users with no sonography training at all. Ground truth was set by transvaginal crown-rump length in the first trimester, so the comparison is against a fact rather than against another estimate. It met prespecified equivalence to credentialed sonographers doing standard biometry.
records.release_evidence: incorporated into the software of a low-cost, battery-powered device
records.headline_result: mean absolute error 3.2 days for novice users with the AI device versus 3.0 days for credentialed sonographers (difference 0.2 days, within the prespecified 2-day equivalence margin)

records.title: Bimodal machine learning model for unstable hips in infants: integration of radiographic images with automatically-generated clinical measurements.
records.model_family: bimodal model combining CNN image features with automatically-generated clinical measurements (aaCM); compared with LightGBM, XGBoost, SVM, single CNN
records.clinical_problem: diagnosing hip instability (developmental dysplasia of the hip) in infants at risk
records.patient_population: 813 radiographic hip images of infants at risk of DDH (232 unstable, 581 stable), multicenter
records.model_description: The model automatically generates clinical measurements (an automatic algorithm for clinical measurement, aaCM) from radiographic hip images of infants and integrates these with CNN image features in a bimodal model, to classify hips as stable or unstable, benchmarked against provocative-examination ground truth and specialist accuracy.
records.headline_result: aaCM accuracy equal to or higher than specialists; bimodal model outperformed LightGBM, XGBoost, SVM, single CNN

records.title: Deep learning-based automated bone age estimation for Saudi patients on hand radiograph images: a retrospective study.
records.clinical_problem: estimating pediatric bone age from left-hand radiographs to reduce inter-observer variability
records.patient_population: 473 patients
records.model_description: input left-hand radiographs; output a predicted bone age via CNN regression
records.release_evidence: The code of the developed model for predicting the bone age in this study is available publicly on GitHub.
records.headline_result: mean absolute error 2.3 years, median absolute error 2.1 years, MAPE 29%

records.title: Comparison of three artificial intelligence algorithms for automatic cobb angle measurement using teaching data specific to three disease groups.
records.model_family: three AI algorithms (architecture not specified) trained on disease-specific data
records.clinical_problem: Improving automatic Cobb angle measurement accuracy for both adolescent idiopathic scoliosis and adult spinal deformity by training AI on disease-specific radiograph data
records.patient_population: 1,612 whole-spine radiographs (1,029 AIS, 583 ASD) for training; 285 for testing (159 AIS, 126 ASD)
records.model_description: Three AI algorithms are trained to automatically measure Cobb angles on whole-spine radiographs, one trained on combined AIS+ASD cases, one on AIS-only, and one on ASD-only, compared against manual measurement by four spine experts
records.headline_result: The AIS/ASD-combined-trained AI showed the highest accuracy among the three algorithms (exact MAE/ICC not given in abstract)

records.title: Age-appropriate or delayed myelination? Scoring myelination in routine clinical MRI.
records.journal: European journal of paediatric neurology : EJPN : official journal of the European Paediatric Neurology Society
records.exclusion_reason: Development of a manual, visual semiquantitative myelination scoring system for pediatric MRI; not an AI/ML model itself (deep learning approaches are mentioned only as background/related work).

records.title: Choroidal Vascularity and Axial Length Elongation in Highly Myopic Children: A 2-Year Longitudinal Investigation.
records.exclusion_reason: optical coherence tomography of the choroid in myopic children; ophthalmic imaging is outside radiology as scoped here

records.title: Texture-based speciation of otitis media-related bacterial biofilms from optical coherence tomography images using supervised classification.
records.exclusion_reason: non-radiologic imaging (OCT of ear/otitis media biofilms)

records.title: Deep-DM: Deep-Driven Deformable Model for 3D Image Segmentation Using Limited Data.
records.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
records.model_family: CNN-driven deformable model (learned energy function + explicit deformable surface)
records.body_region: fetal head; also left ventricle, left atrium, bladder (mixed pediatric/adult tasks)
records.clinical_problem: 3D anatomical segmentation from limited training data, evaluated in part on fetal head segmentation on ultrasound
records.patient_population: mixed: includes fetal head ultrasound segmentation alongside adult left ventricle/atrium and bladder segmentation tasks
records.model_description: A CNN learns an energy function from localized anatomical image patches that drives an explicit deformable surface model to segment 3D structures with limited training data. One of several evaluation tasks is fetal head segmentation on ultrasound, alongside adult cardiac and bladder segmentation on MRI/CT.
records.dataset_size: varying numbers of training volumes per task (not specified for fetal head task)
records.headline_result: Outperformed state-of-the-art deep-learning segmentation methods across all tasks when few training samples were available (no single fetal-head-specific number given)

records.title: An All-in-One Array of Pressure Sensors and sEMG Electrodes for Scoliosis Monitoring.
records.exclusion_reason: Wearable pressure/EMG sensor engineering study for scoliosis brace monitoring; Cobb angle prediction is from sensor data, not radiologic imaging, and deep learning is a minor component.

records.title: The application of machine learning methods for predicting the progression of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: a systematic review.
records.clinical_problem: identifying at the first visit which adolescent scoliosis curves will progress, which determines who gets braced
records.patient_population: adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis, across 15 reviewed studies
records.model_description: A systematic review of the prediction half of scoliosis AI: which radiological and clinical factors have been used to forecast curve progression, and with what models. It reports that machine learning gives higher precision than the traditional progression rules, but that interpretability and data complexity keep it in the research literature; multi-centre work is what would move it.

records.title: Three-Stage Framework for Accurate Pediatric Chest X-ray Diagnosis Using Self-Supervision and Transfer Learning on Small Datasets.
records.clinical_problem: Diagnosing pediatric thoracic diseases from chest X-rays using models pretrained on adult data (knowledge transfer), given limited pediatric training data
records.patient_population: Pediatric CXR dataset (PhysioNet); population not otherwise detailed
records.model_description: A three-stage self-supervised and transfer-learning framework fine-tunes transformer (ViT) and CNN models, pretrained on adult chest X-ray datasets (e.g., CheXpert), to diagnose and localize six pediatric thoracic disease categories on a small pediatric chest X-ray dataset.
records.release_evidence: The source code is available online and the data can be obtained from PhysioNet.
records.dataset_size: Pediatric CXR dataset (PhysioNet); size not stated
records.headline_result: ViT-Base/16 fine-tuned on CheXpert: mean AUC 0.761 (95%CI 0.759-0.763) across 6 disease categories, sensitivity 0.639, specificity 0.683
records.study_design: Retrospective model development and benchmarking study

records.title: Automated Method for Growing Rod Length Measurement on Ultrasound Images in Children With Early Onset Scoliosis.
records.clinical_problem: measuring implanted growing-rod length noninvasively to guide lengthening in early-onset scoliosis
records.patient_population: 23 children with early-onset scoliosis surgeries
records.model_description: input ultrasound images of the implanted growing rod; output automatic identification of rod boundary/segments and a measured rod length via two Mask R-CNN models
records.headline_result: ICC 0.98; mean absolute difference 0.86±1.0 mm vs. manual measurement
records.study_design: pilot model development and validation study

records.title: Capability of multimodal large language models to interpret pediatric radiological images.
records.model_family: multimodal large language models (GPT-4, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Claude 3 Opus)
records.clinical_problem: interpreting pediatric radiological images and providing a diagnostic impression
records.patient_population: 30 medically significant pediatric radiology cases (90 images total)
records.model_description: Thirty pediatric radiology cases (90 images) with a short clinical history are submitted to three multimodal large language models (GPT-4, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Claude 3 Opus), which generate a diagnostic impression; responses are independently scored for accuracy by a resident and an attending physician.
records.release_evidence: GPT-4 (OpenAI), Gemini 1.5 Pro (Google) and Claude 3 Opus (Anthropic) are named commercial vendor products
records.headline_result: correctly diagnosed 27.8% of images (25/90), partially correct 13.3%, incorrect 58.9%
records.study_design: retrospective diagnostic accuracy evaluation of general-purpose multimodal LLMs

records.title: Segmentation and Estimation of Fetal Biometric Parameters using an Attention Gate Double U-Net with Guided Decoder Architecture.
records.model_name: ADU-GD (Attention Gate Double U-Net with Guided Decoder)
records.clinical_problem: Segmenting and measuring fetal biometric parameters (head circumference, abdominal circumference, femur length, biparietal diameter) from ultrasound
records.patient_population: not stated (benchmark ultrasound datasets)
records.model_description: ADU-GD, an attention-gated double U-Net with a guided decoder, segments fetal anatomical structures on ultrasound and estimates biometric parameters (head circumference, abdominal circumference, femur length, biparietal diameter), benchmarked against numerous other deep-learning segmentation models.
records.headline_result: MAE 0.99 mm overall; Dice 99.1%; parameter MAE: HC 2.2mm, AC 2.6mm, FL 0.6mm, BPD 1.2mm
records.study_design: Retrospective model development and benchmarking study

records.title: A deep learning approach to identify the fetal head position using transperineal ultrasound during labor.
records.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
records.clinical_problem: Automatically identifying fetal head position during the second stage of labor from transperineal ultrasound, to guide delivery management
records.patient_population: 2,154 transperineal ultrasound images from term, singleton, cephalic pregnancies across 16 centers
records.model_description: Three cascaded ResNet18-based CNNs classify transperineal ultrasound images of the fetal head into occiput anterior/posterior/transverse positions, using transabdominal ultrasound as the ground-truth label
records.headline_result: Overall accuracy 94.5% (95% CI 92.0-97.0), F1-score 0.92

records.title: The value of radiomics features of the spleen as surrogates for differentiating subtypes of common pediatric lymphomas.
records.journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
records.clinical_problem: Using CT radiomics features of the spleen to noninvasively differentiate Burkitt lymphoma from lymphoblastic lymphoma in children.
records.patient_population: 48 patients with lymphoblastic lymphoma, 61 with Burkitt lymphoma (109 total pediatric patients)
records.model_description: Radiomics features extracted from splenic CT images (noncontrast, arterial, venous phases) are combined via classifiers (QDA, LR, SVM) into fusion models to differentiate Burkitt lymphoma from lymphoblastic lymphoma.
records.headline_result: SVM_4 fusion model AUC 0.967 (training), 0.754 (test)

records.title: Applying machine learning in screening for Down Syndrome in both trimesters for diverse healthcare scenarios.
records.model_family: k-nearest neighbor, SVM, random forest, XGBoost
records.body_region: fetal (prenatal screening, combined with biochemical markers)
records.clinical_problem: Screening for Down syndrome in the first and second trimesters using ultrasound and biochemical testing, especially in resource-limited settings
records.patient_population: 7,076 pregnant women in Northern Vietnam (1,035 with a fetus with Down syndrome)
records.model_description: Machine learning models (k-nearest neighbor, SVM, random forest, XGBoost) combine ultrasound findings and biochemical test results to predict Down syndrome risk in the first and second trimesters.
records.dataset_size: 7,076 pregnant women, single site in Northern Vietnam
records.headline_result: Trimester 1: XGBoost 94% accuracy, 88% AUC; Trimester 2: SVM 89% accuracy, 84% AUC

records.title: The utility of Multicentre Epilepsy Lesion Detection (MELD) algorithm in identifying epileptic activity and predicting seizure freedom in MRI lesion-negative paediatric patients.
records.clinical_problem: detecting occult focal cortical dysplasia lesions on structural MRI in children with MRI-negative drug-resistant focal epilepsy
records.patient_population: 28 MRI-negative children (37 SEEG studies) with drug-resistant focal epilepsy
records.model_description: The MELD deep-learning algorithm analyzes structural brain MRI to detect subtle focal cortical dysplasia lesions not visible on conventional radiological review; applied retrospectively to MRI-negative pediatric epilepsy cases and compared against SEEG and PET findings.
records.headline_result: clusters identified in 14/28 (50%) children; 1 MELD cluster co-localized with resection cavity, associated with Engel 1A outcome

records.title: Radiomic study of antenatal prediction of severe placenta accreta spectrum from MRI.
records.clinical_problem: Antenatal MRI-based radiomic prediction of severe placenta accreta spectrum (placenta increta) to guide delivery planning.
records.patient_population: 100 women with placenta accreta spectrum (mean age 34.6±3.9), 64 with placenta increta, multi-center 2018-2023
records.model_description: Radiomic features extracted from T2-weighted antenatal MRI, combined with a clinical variable, are used in a random forest/support vector machine classifier to predict severe (increta) placenta accreta spectrum subtype.
records.headline_result: Clinical-radiomic model AUC 0.713, accuracy 0.695, sensitivity 0.843, specificity 0.447
records.study_design: multi-center retrospective radiomics model validation study

records.title: Applications of artificial intelligence for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: mapping the evidence.
records.clinical_problem: diagnosing adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, stratifying who will progress, and guiding treatment
records.patient_population: adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis, across 40 reviewed articles
records.model_description: Maps what AI has been used for in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: 62.5% of the work is imaging analysis, mostly automatic Cobb angle and vertebral rotation measurement and curve classification, and 37.5% is prediction, mostly of curve progression. The limiting finding is governance rather than accuracy — only 15 of 40 studies offered any clinical implementation guidance, and external validation and model transparency are largely absent.
records.dataset_size: 40 articles, 77.5% from the last five years
records.headline_result: average reported model accuracy 85.4% among the 52.5% of studies that reported it; only 37.5% gave clinical implementation guidance

records.title: Regional brain structural network topology mediates the associations between white matter damage and disease severity in first-episode, Treatment-naïve pubertal children with major depressive disorder.
records.model_family: neural network algorithm combining demographics, DTI, and graph-theory network metrics
records.clinical_problem: diagnosing first-episode major depressive disorder in pubertal children/adolescents from white matter and network changes
records.patient_population: 36 first-episode, treatment-naive adolescents with major depressive disorder (mean age 15.8) and 29 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (mean age 15.2)
records.model_description: Whole-brain diffusion tensor imaging and graph-theory network topology metrics are combined with demographic data and fed into a neural network model to distinguish first-episode, treatment-naive adolescents with major depressive disorder from healthy controls, identifying white matter and network hub abnormalities linked to symptom severity.
records.headline_result: Diagnostic model achieved AUROC 0.88 and F1 score 0.80

records.title: A comprehensive systematic review of fMRI studies on brain connectivity in healthy children and adolescents: Current insights and future directions.
records.exclusion_reason: systematic review of rs-fMRI connectivity methods in typical child/adolescent development; not focused on AI/ML models or a clinical radiology application

records.title: Beyond hand-crafted features for pretherapeutic molecular status identification of pediatric low-grade gliomas.
records.clinical_problem: non-invasively determining the molecular/genetic status of pediatric low-grade glioma from MRI to guide use of targeted therapy
records.patient_population: 336 patients treated for pediatric low-grade glioma (1999-2018)
records.model_description: Takes T2-FLAIR MRI tumor regions (manually segmented) as input and outputs a prediction of pLGG genetic/molecular status, combining a convolutional neural network with random-forest radiomics features.
records.headline_result: Mean AUC 0.824 (combined model) vs 0.802 (radiomics) vs 0.764 (CNN)

records.title: Neonatal nutrition and early childhood body composition in infants born extremely preterm.
records.exclusion_reason: DXA-derived body composition outcomes analyzed with Bayesian regression/gradient boosting on nutrition intake variables; not an image-analysis AI model

records.title: Subject-specific atlas for automatic brain tissue segmentation of neonatal magnetic resonance images.
records.model_family: random forest classifier atlas-based segmentation with expectation-maximization Markov random field
records.clinical_problem: segmenting gray matter, white matter and CSF on neonatal brain MRI
records.patient_population: 40 neonatal MR images, gestational age 37-44 weeks
records.model_description: A subject-specific atlas is generated using a random forest classifier, then combined with an expectation-maximization Markov random field method to segment gray matter, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid on neonatal brain MRI, using intensity- and gradient-based features.
records.headline_result: overall accuracy 94.3%, Dice 0.945 (GM), 0.947 (WM), 0.912 (CSF); up to 4% improvement over comparator methods

records.title: Artificial intelligence in fetal echocardiography: Recent advances and future prospects.
records.journal: International journal of cardiology. Heart & vasculature
records.clinical_problem: reviewing AI's role in improving prenatal detection of congenital heart disease via fetal echocardiography
records.patient_population: fetuses undergoing echocardiographic CHD screening (review)
records.model_description: A review of recent advances in AI applications for fetal echocardiography, including automating/standardizing display of diagnostic cardiac views to improve CHD detection accuracy.

records.title: Fetal-BET: Brain Extraction Tool for Fetal MRI.
records.journal: IEEE open journal of engineering in medicine and biology
records.model_family: U-Net style architecture with attention mechanism, multi-modality feature learning
records.clinical_problem: automatically extracting (skull-stripping) the fetal brain from heterogeneous fetal MRI sequences as a preprocessing step for fetal brain imaging pipelines
records.patient_population: approximately 72,000 2D fetal brain MRI images (T2-weighted, diffusion-weighted, and functional MRI), including normal and pathological brains from multiple scanners
records.model_description: Deep learning model using U-Net style architecture with attention mechanisms and cross-modality feature learning, trained on a large annotated multi-sequence fetal brain MRI dataset to automatically extract the fetal brain from T2-weighted, diffusion-weighted, and functional MRI
records.headline_result: accurate brain extraction on heterogeneous test data from different scanners, pathological brains, and various gestational stages (no single summary metric stated)
records.study_design: retrospective model development with external multi-center test data

records.title: Using machine learning to automatically measure kyphotic and lordotic angle measurements on radiographs for children with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
records.clinical_problem: automating kyphotic and lordotic angle measurement on radiographs to diagnose adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
records.patient_population: children with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (100 training, 60 test radiographs)
records.model_description: input lateral spine radiographs; output T1-L5 vertebral segmentation used to automatically compute kyphotic and lordotic angles
records.headline_result: clinical acceptance rate 98%/75%/97% and ICC 0.91/0.60/0.88 for T1-T12 KA/T5-T12 KA/L1-L5 LA; ~4±2 s per radiograph
records.study_design: retrospective single-center method development and validation study

records.title: FLUEnT: Transformer for detecting lung consolidations in videos using fused lung ultrasound encodings.
records.model_family: transformer combining variational autoencoder embeddings, ResNet-18 features, and patient metadata
records.clinical_problem: detecting lung consolidations on pediatric lung ultrasound video for pneumonia diagnosis
records.patient_population: pediatric lung ultrasound pneumonia patients (video-level dataset, size not specified in abstract)
records.model_description: FLUEnT combines frame-level embeddings from a variational autoencoder, spatial features from a ResNet-18, and encoded patient metadata into fused encodings that are passed to a transformer for binary classification of lung consolidation presence in pediatric lung ultrasound videos.
records.headline_result: mean balanced accuracy 89.3%, outperforming state-of-the-art models by an average of 8 percentage points

records.title: nnU-Net-based Segmentation of Tumor Subcompartments in Pediatric Medulloblastoma Using Multiparametric MRI: A Multi-institutional Study.
records.clinical_problem: Automatically delineating medulloblastoma tumor subcompartments (enhancing tumor, edema, cystic/non-enhancing core) on multiparametric MRI to support radiation therapy planning
records.patient_population: 78 pediatric medulloblastoma patients (ages 2-18) from three institutions
records.model_description: Input: gadolinium-enhanced T1, T2, and FLAIR MRI; output: automatic segmentation of tumor habitat and subcompartments, via nnU-Net models (one pretrained on adult glioma and fine-tuned, one trained directly on medulloblastoma data)
records.headline_result: Dice scores for tumor habitat 0.80-0.86 across three test sites
records.study_design: retrospective multi-institutional segmentation model development and cross-site evaluation

records.title: Deep learning applications for quantitative and qualitative PET in PET/MR: technical and clinical unmet needs.
records.exclusion_reason: general review of deep learning for PET/MR across all ages; pediatric PET/MR mentioned only as one of several unmet-need bullet points, not the review's focus

records.title: Deep generative model of the distal tibial classic metaphyseal lesion in infants: assessment of synthetic images.
records.model_family: mask conditional diffusion model (generative deep learning)
records.clinical_problem: generating synthetic training images of classic metaphyseal lesions, a fracture highly specific to infant abuse, to augment limited training data
records.patient_population: 39 infants (mean age 4.1 months) with distal tibia radiographs, used to derive real and synthetic test images
records.model_description: A mask conditional diffusion model (MaC-DM) generates synthetic distal tibia radiographs with and without classic metaphyseal lesions to augment a limited training dataset for automated fracture detection; three blinded radiologists then assessed whether the synthetic images correctly showed the lesion and whether they could distinguish real from synthetic images.
records.dataset_size: 100 real images tested (from 177 normal/73 CML dataset); 100 synthetic images generated
records.headline_result: radiologists diagnosed CML with kappa 0.90, accuracy 92%, but could not distinguish real from synthetic images (kappa 0.05, accuracy 53%)
records.study_design: retrospective single-center generative model development with reader study

records.title: Multimodal Model for Predicting Fetal Acidosis in Delivery Room.
records.journal: Studies in health technology and informatics
records.body_region: fetal heart / whole fetus (delivery room monitoring)
records.clinical_problem: prediction of fetal acidosis at delivery
records.patient_population: 2,266 deliveries at a tertiary hospital delivery room
records.model_description: Inputs are features extracted from electronic medical records, biosignals (cardiotocography) and imaging data (including fetal echocardiography), concatenated into a single feature vector; a classifier trained on this multimodal input outputs a predicted probability of post-delivery fetal acidosis.
records.headline_result: AUROC 0.752 on the test dataset

records.title: Remote Monitoring, AI, Machine Learning and Mobile Ultrasound Integration upon 5G Internet in the Prehospital Care to Support the Golden Hour Principle and Optimize Outcomes in Severe Trauma and Emergency Surgery.
records.journal: Studies in health technology and informatics
records.exclusion_reason: AI/ML mentioned only generically as part of a telemedicine feasibility simulation; not primarily a pediatric radiology imaging study

records.title: Data for AI in Congenital Heart Defects: Systematic Review.
records.journal: Studies in health technology and informatics
records.clinical_problem: prenatal detection of congenital heart disease
records.patient_population: fetuses screened for congenital heart disease across 28 studies included in the review
records.model_description: A PRISMA systematic review of 28 studies (from 621 screened) on AI applications for prenatal detection of congenital heart disease, finding deep learning as the predominant approach and ultrasound and MRI as the main data types used, summarizing the landscape of available data and methods.

records.title: Modelling a self-defined CNN for effectual classification of PCOS from ultrasound images.
records.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
records.exclusion_reason: CNN classification of PCOS on ultrasound; adult reproductive-age population, not pediatric

records.title: Longitudinal Changes in Choroidal Vascularity in Myopic and Non-Myopic Children.
records.exclusion_reason: optical coherence tomography (OCT) of the choroid/eye; non-radiologic imaging modality excluded per protocol

records.title: Separating group- and individual-level brain signatures in the newborn functional connectome: A deep learning approach.
records.clinical_problem: Can individual-specific brain functional connectivity patterns be identified in newborns using resting-state fMRI, similar to what is seen in adults?
records.patient_population: 464 neonates and 100 adults from public rs-fMRI datasets
records.model_description: Takes resting-state fMRI-derived functional connectivity matrices as input; a variational autoencoder outputs latent representations used to predict age and identify individual subjects across repeat scans.
records.headline_result: Individual identification accuracy ~45% with VAE vs. ~10-30% with linear models; age prediction r~0.7
records.study_design: retrospective methods development using public neonatal and adult rs-fMRI datasets

records.title: Learning from the few: Fine-grained approach to pediatric wrist pathology recognition on a limited dataset.
records.model_family: fine-grained deep convolutional neural network architecture with LION optimizer and Grad-CAM
records.clinical_problem: recognizing pediatric wrist pathologies, particularly fractures, on trauma X-rays
records.patient_population: children and adolescents with wrist trauma radiographs (limited dataset)
records.model_description: A fine-grained deep convolutional neural network automatically identifies discriminative regions in pediatric wrist X-rays to classify wrist pathologies, refined via ablation analysis and the LION optimizer, with Grad-CAM used to visualize the regions driving each prediction.
records.dataset_size: limited dataset (exact size not stated in abstract)
records.headline_result: accuracy 86% (augmented) and 84% (original) test sets; fracture sensitivity 97%

records.title: Alterations in the gut microbiota community are associated with childhood obesity and precocious puberty.
records.exclusion_reason: non-imaging study — gut microbiota sequencing, not diagnostic imaging

records.title: Identifying developmental changes in functional brain connectivity associated with cognitive functioning in children and adolescents with ADHD.
records.model_family: machine learning models on movie-watching fMRI connectivity
records.clinical_problem: predicting cognitive abilities (IQ and related measures) in children and adolescents with ADHD from functional connectivity
records.patient_population: children and adolescents aged 6-16 (373 with ADHD, 106 neurotypical) undergoing movie-watching fMRI
records.model_description: Functional connectivity patterns recorded while children and adolescents watched a short movie during fMRI were used to train machine learning models that predict IQ and other cognitive measures (visual-spatial, verbal comprehension, fluid reasoning), evaluated with out-of-sample cross-validation. The models successfully predicted these measures in younger children (6-11) with ADHD but not in adolescents (12-16) with ADHD.
records.dataset_size: 373 children/adolescents with ADHD, 106 neurotypical controls, ages 6-16
records.headline_result: Machine learning models predicted IQ and cognitive measures in early/middle childhood (ages 6-11) with ADHD but failed to generalize to adolescents (12-16)

records.title: Assessment of deep learning image reconstruction (DLIR) on image quality in pediatric cardiac CT datasets type of manuscript: Original research.
records.clinical_problem: Improving image quality of pediatric cardiac CT while managing radiation dose, comparing deep-learning reconstruction to conventional iterative reconstruction
records.patient_population: 109 pediatric cardiac CT scans, January 2020-December 2022

records.title: Construction and Validation of A Deep Learning-based Bone Age Prediction Model for Children Living in Both Plain and Highland Regions

records.headline_result: The best model (vision transformer pretrained on ImageNet, fine-tuned on ADC images with age fusion) achieved MCC 0.77±0.14 and accuracy 0.87±0.08, outperforming models trained on T2w (MCC 0.58) and T1w post-contrast (MCC 0.41) data.

records.title: A survey of Paediatric Radiology Artificial Intelligence
records.clinical_problem: landscape of AI applications across pediatric radiology
records.patient_population: pediatric patients (under 18) across studies published 2015-2021
records.model_description: This systematic review, following PRISMA and Cochrane Collaboration guidance, surveys AI research in pediatric radiology published from 2015 to 2021, covering use cases, tasks, methodologies, and underlying data. It reports the distribution of subspecialties, imaging modalities, tasks, and study designs, and highlights potential biases and data-quality issues limiting generalizability.
records.headline_result: 292 articles were included with an increasing annual publication trend; neuroradiology and musculoskeletal radiology were the most common subspecialties, MRI was the dominant modality, and segmentation and classification were the most common tasks, with retrospective cohort studies predominating.

records.title: Brain tumour edge detection using an enhanced canny edge detection algorithm
records.journal: International Journal of Computational Biology and Drug Design
records.exclusion_reason: pediatric population not specified; study uses general/benchmark brain tumor MRI datasets (BRATS, Kaggle)

records.title: From sensory motor and perceptual development to primary consciousness in the fetus: converging neural, behavioral, and imaging correlates of cognition-mediated emergent transitions
records.exclusion_reason: narrative review of fetal cognition and consciousness drawing on behavioral, animal and neuroimaging evidence broadly; not focused on an AI/ML imaging model

records.title: Computer-Aided Reading of Chest Radiographs for Pediatric Tuberculosis: Current Status and Future Directions
records.clinical_problem: computer-aided detection of tuberculosis on chest radiographs in children
records.patient_population: children evaluated for tuberculosis with chest radiography, particularly in primary health settings
records.model_description: This review summarizes the current, limited literature on computer-aided detection (CAD) algorithms for reading chest radiographs to diagnose tuberculosis and other pulmonary infections in children, noting that CAD systems approved for adult TB triage are not yet approved for pediatric use, and calling for large, diverse, well-annotated pediatric chest radiograph datasets to train or fine-tune such models.

records.title: Efficacy of lightweight Vision Transformers in diagnosis of pneumonia
records.exclusion_reason: population age is not stated; uses a general public chest X-ray pneumonia dataset without confirming a pediatric cohort

records.title: External Validation of Predictive Models for Diagnosis, Management and Severity of Pediatric Appendicitis
records.exclusion_reason: external validation of a multimodal clinical prediction model for pediatric appendicitis using demographic, clinical, laboratory and scoring data; ultrasound is only one of several non-imaging inputs, not an imaging-centric AI model

records.title: Research of intelligent model for automatically counting the number of vertebral ossification center below the end of conus medullaris
records.model_family: YOLOv8-based segmentation model with post-processing fitting/counting algorithm
records.clinical_problem: counting vertebral ossification centers to support fetal spina bifida screening
records.patient_population: fetuses undergoing sacrococcygeal spinal midsagittal ultrasound, retrospectively selected 2021-2022 from two hospitals
records.model_description: Midsagittal sacrococcygeal ultrasound images are input. A YOLOv8-based network segments the vertebral ossification centers and the spinal conus medullaris, and a post-processing step fits and automatically counts the ossification centers below the conus medullaris. It is intended to speed up and standardize prenatal screening for fetal spina bifida.
records.dataset_size: 3000 ultrasound images (2800 for segmentation training, 200 for testing)
records.headline_result: AI counting accuracy 95.00% vs attending physician 94.50% (P=0.823) and junior physician 88.50% (P=0.012); AI counting time 0.09s vs 5.00s (attending) and 7.00s (junior), P<0.001

records.title: A Graph Neural Network Approach to Investigate Brain Critical States Over Neurodevelopment
records.model_family: Graph Neural Network trained on Ising-model networks
records.clinical_problem: characterizing brain functional maturation using resting-state fMRI
records.patient_population: typically developing children and children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
records.model_description: A Graph Neural Network trained on simulated 2D Ising-model networks was used to estimate an 'Ising temperature' from resting-state fMRI functional connectivity, a marker of how close brain dynamics are to a critical state. The method was applied to children to study how this measure changes with age in typical development and in ADHD.
records.headline_result: Ising temperature correlated negatively with age in both typically developing children (r=-0.48, P<0.0001) and children with ADHD (r=-0.49, P<0.0001), suggesting the brain moves away from criticality with age.

records.title: Electrocardiogram-Based AI for Classifying Left Ventricular Dysfunction and Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction

records.title: Evaluation of Liver Fibrosis on Grayscale Ultrasound in a Pediatric Population Using a Cloud-based Transfer Learning Artificial Intelligence Platform
records.journal: Advanced Ultrasound in Diagnosis and Therapy
records.model_family: Google Vision AutoML (transfer learning image classification)
records.clinical_problem: noninvasive detection of liver fibrosis
records.patient_population: 190 pediatric patients referred for liver biopsy and ultrasound
records.model_description: B-mode ultrasound images of the liver (about 14 per patient) were used to train a supervised image-classification model on a cloud-based AI platform (Google Vision AutoML) via transfer learning, to classify liver appearance as fibrotic or non-fibrotic. The model's output was compared against biopsy-proven fibrosis status and against blinded pediatric radiologist reads on an external validation cohort.
records.release_evidence: built using a commercial cloud platform (Google Vision AutoML), but the resulting model itself is not stated to be released
records.dataset_size: 190 patients; 2,324 images (development, 154 cases) and 360 images (external validation, 36 cases)
records.headline_result: External validation: AI sensitivity 70.56% vs radiologists' mean sensitivity 42.04%; AI accuracy 57.78% vs radiologists' mean accuracy 46.11%

records.title: Artificial Intelligence for the Prenatal Ultrasound Diagnosis of Congenital Heart Disease: A Narrative Review
records.journal: Clinical and Experimental Obstetrics and Gynecology
records.clinical_problem: prenatal detection and diagnosis of congenital heart disease
records.patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal cardiac ultrasound
records.model_description: A narrative review of 28 studies applying artificial intelligence to fetal cardiac ultrasound, covering automated generation and identification of standard fetal cardiac views and automated detection of congenital heart disease lesions, and discussing training-data and image-segmentation challenges.

records.title: De-Coupling Connectivity: A Cognitive Biomarker in Pediatric Traumatic Brain Injury
records.model_family: graph-theory connectivity coupling metrics with regression models
records.clinical_problem: predicting cognitive outcome after pediatric traumatic brain injury
records.patient_population: children with traumatic brain injury (aged 9-18 years) and healthy controls
records.model_description: Structural and functional brain connectivity were derived from MRI using graph theory in children with traumatic brain injury and healthy controls, scanned in the acute and post-acute phases. A 'coupling connectivity' measure (correlation between structural and functional graph-theory metrics) was calculated, and regression models used acute-phase coupling connectivity to predict post-acute executive function test outcomes.
records.dataset_size: 45 children with TBI and 47 healthy controls, aged 9-18 years
records.headline_result: TBI patients showed disrupted structural-functional connectivity coupling versus controls, and acute-phase coupling connectivity significantly predicted post-acute executive function outcomes.

records.title: Applications of artificial intelligence in obstetrics
records.journal: Journal of the Korean Medical Association
records.exclusion_reason: review of ChatGPT/LLM chatbot applications across obstetric practice (patient education, drug counseling, administration); imaging is a brief tangential mention, not the focus

records.title: Automatic Diagnosis of Early Pregnancy Fetal Nasal Bone Development Based on Complex Mid-Sagittal Section Ultrasound Imaging
records.model_name: FNB-ADS (Fetal Nasal Bone Automated Diagnostic System)
records.model_family: YOLOv8 detection + lightweight segmentation network + ResNet34 classifier
records.clinical_problem: early prenatal screening for fetal nasal bone abnormality (chromosomal abnormality marker)
records.patient_population: fetuses undergoing early prenatal mid-sagittal ultrasound screening
records.model_description: FNB-ADS is an automated pipeline for early-pregnancy fetal nasal bone ultrasound. It uses YOLOv8 to localize the nasal bone region on mid-sagittal plane images, a lightweight segmentation network to segment the nasal bone, nasal tip and prenasal skin, and a ResNet34 classifier to diagnose developmental abnormalities from the segmented structures. The authors also released the FNB-UDV dataset of annotated images and videos used to develop and test the system.
records.release_evidence: The FNB-UDV image/video dataset is stated to be publicly released, but the abstract does not say whether the model code or weights are released.
records.dataset_size: 1,007 2D ultrasound images and 12 ultrasound videos (FNB-UDV dataset)
records.headline_result: Diagnostic accuracy was 92.37% on images (0.14 s/image) and 98.69% on video (0.37 s/frame inference speed).
records.study_design: technical development / retrospective diagnostic accuracy study

records.title: Using Convolutional Neural Networks for the Classification of Suboptimal Chest Radiographs
records.model_family: DenseNet121 and YOLOv8 convolutional neural networks
records.clinical_problem: identifying technically suboptimal chest radiographs to reduce repeat imaging
records.patient_population: patients undergoing chest radiography, median age 67 years (range 0-102), including pediatric and adult cases
records.model_description: DenseNet121 and YOLOv8 convolutional neural networks were trained to classify chest radiographs (both PA and lateral views) as optimal or suboptimal quality, a task intended to flag images likely to need repeat acquisition. Model classifications were compared with radiologists' classifications, and this was the first such study to include lateral views and pediatric cases.
records.dataset_size: 3,587 patients; 10,000 CXRs total (4,000/4,000 training, 400/400 validation, 25/25 test)
records.headline_result: DenseNet121 achieved AUROC 0.97 and YOLOv8 AUROC 0.95 for distinguishing optimal from suboptimal chest radiographs; agreement with radiologists varied but differences were not statistically significant.

records.title: Deep learning super-resolution of paediatric ultra-low-field MRI without paired high-field scans
records.clinical_problem: improving image quality of affordable ultra-low-field brain MRI for pediatric neuroimaging
records.patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing ultra-low-field brain MRI
records.model_description: A deep learning model generates a super-resolved brain MRI from a single ultra-low-field scan, without requiring paired high-field training data or the three orthogonal ultra-low-field acquisitions used by prior multi-resolution registration methods. Output quality was assessed by image quality metrics, correlation of derived tissue volumes, and Dice overlap of tissue segmentations, including an exploratory test of generalization across scanning sites.
records.headline_result: The single-scan deep learning approach significantly improved image quality metrics, tissue volume correlations, and Dice overlap of tissue segmentations compared with the single ultra-low-field input; an exploratory external site evaluation suggested site-specific retraining may be needed to address domain shift.

records.title: Pedvision: A Manual-Annotation-Free and Age Scalable Segmentation Pipeline for Bone Analysis in Hand X-Ray Images
records.model_family: segmentation pipeline: ROI detection network + foundation model instance translation + instance classifier network, with curriculum learning
records.clinical_problem: automated bone segmentation for pediatric bone analysis across ages
records.patient_population: children aged 4 to 228 months undergoing hand radiography
records.model_description: PedVision is a segmentation pipeline for hand X-rays that first localizes regions of interest, then uses a foundation model to translate each region into instance-level candidates, which an instance classifier network maps to one of 19 bones across five classes. A semi-automated, foundation-model-assisted annotation workflow with iterative human-in-the-loop review builds the training data across successive rounds, avoiding fully manual annotation, and is designed to scale across a wide pediatric age range including low-quality images.
records.release_evidence: "The project is open source at github.com/mohofar/PedVision."
records.dataset_size: hand X-ray images from children aged 4-228 months, segmenting 19 bones into 5 classes (exact image count not stated)
records.headline_result: Compared with DeepLabV3+ (ResNet34/ResNet101 backbones), the pipeline improved Dice scores by up to 6.19% in subjects over 14 years and 17.01% in subjects under 7 years, particularly in low-quality images.
records.study_design: technical development / retrospective segmentation accuracy study

records.title: Does Restrictive Anorexia Nervosa Impact Brain Aging? A Machine Learning Approach to Estimate Age Based on Brain Structure
records.model_family: machine learning brain-age estimation model (377 neuroanatomical features from structural MRI)
records.clinical_problem: brain age gap as a biomarker of anorexia nervosa's effect on brain structure
records.patient_population: female patients aged 10-40 years with acute or weight-restored anorexia nervosa and age-matched healthy controls
records.model_description: A machine learning model was trained on 3,487 healthy-control T1-weighted MRI scans (ages 5-45, ten datasets) using 377 neuroanatomical features to estimate brain age. It was then applied to structural MRI from acute anorexia nervosa, weight-restored anorexia nervosa, and matched healthy-control groups from two institutions to compute the brain-predicted age difference (brain-PAD) as a biomarker of accelerated brain aging.
records.dataset_size: acute AN n=113, weight-restored AN n=35, healthy controls n=90 (model trained on 3,487 healthy-control scans)
records.headline_result: Model mean absolute error was 2.37 years in healthy controls; brain age was overestimated by 2.25 years in acute AN, normalizing after weight restoration (difference from HC not significant, P=0.98); brain-PAD correlated with BMI in acute AN (r=-0.291, P=0.005).

records.title: Validation of Artificial Intelligence for Bone Age Assessment in Hong Kong Children
records.clinical_problem: skeletal (bone age) maturity assessment
records.patient_population: children referred for left hand and wrist radiographs for bone age assessment at a tertiary centre in Hong Kong, Jan-Dec 2019, mean chronological age 9.8 years
records.model_description: Left hand and wrist radiographs were analyzed by BoneXpert 3.0, an automated AI bone-age software using the Greulich and Pyle method, and compared against bone ages assessed manually by two experienced pediatric radiologists in 99 studies.
records.headline_result: Strong correlation between BoneXpert and manual assessment (r = 0.98, R2 = 0.97); mean difference -0.08 year (SD 0.73); accuracy 0.74 year overall

records.title: CT findings of mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia in children
records.journal: Chinese Journal of Interventional Imaging and Therapy
records.model_family: AI pneumonia CT image-assisted diagnostic analysis software
records.clinical_problem: quantification of pneumonia lesion extent on chest CT in mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia
records.patient_population: 85 children with mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia confirmed by nucleic acid test
records.model_description: AI-assisted chest CT image analysis software automatically quantified lesion volume, percentage of lesion volume relative to total lung volume, and CT attenuation value on CT scans of children with confirmed mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia. These quantitative parameters were then correlated with clinical laboratory markers of inflammation.
records.headline_result: Lesion volume and lesion volume percentage positively correlated with serum sialic acid, CRP, D-dimer, FDP and fibrinogen (r=0.232-0.439)

records.title: Prediction of Motor Developmental Outcomes Based on MRI Radiomics in Premature Infants
records.model_family: radiomics-based binary classification model (ANOVA feature selection, ten-fold cross-validation)
records.clinical_problem: prediction of motor neurodevelopmental outcome in preterm infants
records.patient_population: preterm infants imaged with brain MRI at term-equivalent age
records.model_description: Radiomic features were extracted from T1-weighted, T2-weighted and T2-FLAIR brain MRI obtained at term-equivalent age in preterm infants. A classification model combining these radiomic features with perinatal clinical variables was trained to predict motor developmental delay, defined using Bayley Scales assessment at 12-24 months corrected age, and compared to a clinical-variables-only model.
records.dataset_size: 218 preterm infants (90 with motor developmental delay)
records.headline_result: AUC for the combined radiomics + clinical model was 0.94 versus 0.87 for the clinical-only model and up to 0.85 for radiomics from combined MRI sequences alone.

records.title: Predicting Tumor Micronecrosis in Hepatocellular Carcinoma Using Pretreatment Contrast-Enhanced CT Radiomics Model: A Multi-Center Study
records.exclusion_reason: adult hepatocellular carcinoma cohort undergoing CT radiomics analysis; no pediatric population

records.title: Detection of Pneumonia in Children through Chest Radiographs using Artificial Intelligence in a Low-Resource Setting: A Pilot Study
records.model_family: deep learning classification model (architecture not specified)
records.clinical_problem: detection of childhood pneumonia on chest radiographs in a low-resource setting
records.patient_population: children in Nigeria undergoing chest radiography, prospectively sampled across two radiology departments
records.model_description: An AI model was developed on an open-source US pediatric chest radiograph dataset to classify images as normal or pneumonia, then externally tested on prospectively collected Nigerian pediatric chest radiographs read by two blinded radiologists as the reference standard, to evaluate generalizability to a low-resource clinical setting.
records.dataset_size: 5,232 open-source pediatric chest radiographs for development (1,349 normal/3,883 pneumonia training; 234/390 internal test) and 190 Nigerian radiographs for external testing (93 normal/97 pneumonia)
records.headline_result: The model achieved 86% accuracy and 0.93 AUC on the internal test set, but only 58% accuracy and 0.65 AUC on the external Nigerian test set.

records.title: NeoCLIP: A Self-Supervised Foundation Model for the Interpretation of Neonatal Radiographs
records.model_family: self-supervised deep contrastive learning foundation model
records.body_region: chest and abdomen (neonatal intensive care radiographs)
records.clinical_problem: interpretation of neonatal intensive care radiographs (multiple pathologies and device placement)
records.patient_population: infants who received a radiograph while admitted to a large neonatal intensive care unit
records.model_description: NeoCLIP is a self-supervised contrastive learning model trained on neonatal intensive care radiographs paired with findings automatically extracted from radiology reports using a large-language-model-based pipeline. It identifies 15 pathologies and 5 medical devices relevant to neonatal intensive care from a plain radiograph, with an option to incorporate patient demographics.
records.dataset_size: 20,154 radiographs and 15,795 reports from 4,629 infants (3,731 training, 419 validation, 479 test)
records.headline_result: NeoCLIP's AUROC exceeded all baseline methods for every radiographic finding except portal venous gas, and outperformed similar models developed for adult populations; adding demographics improved AUROC without reaching statistical significance.

records.title: Aperiodic parameters of the fMRI power spectrum associate with preterm birth and neonatal age
records.model_family: machine learning regression model on fMRI aperiodic power-spectrum parameters
records.clinical_problem: assessing brain maturation and effect of preterm birth using functional MRI
records.patient_population: neonates (preterm and full-term) from the Developing Human Connectome Project
records.model_description: Using task-free fMRI from the Developing Human Connectome Project, the aperiodic (non-oscillatory) parameters of the BOLD signal power spectrum were extracted from cortical/subcortical regions. A machine learning regression model using aperiodic parameters from 90 brain regions of interest was trained to predict post-menstrual age and postnatal age, and associations with preterm birth were examined.
records.dataset_size: Developing Human Connectome Project neonatal fMRI cohort (exact n not stated)
records.headline_result: The regression model predicted post-menstrual and postnatal age with mean test R² of 0.20-0.41; clear differences in aperiodic parameters were found between preterm and full-term infants and between sexes.

records.title: Imaging Clusters of Pediatric Low-Grade Glioma are Associated with Distinct Molecular Characteristics
records.model_family: K-means clustering on radiomic features with elastic net logistic regression
records.clinical_problem: linking imaging appearance to molecular subtype in pediatric low-grade glioma
records.patient_population: pediatric patients with low-grade glioma (pLGG) from the Children's Brain Tumor Network
records.model_description: 881 radiomic features plus clinical variables (age, sex, tumor location) were extracted from MRI of pediatric low-grade glioma and grouped into three imaging clusters using principal component analysis and K-means clustering. A supervised elastic net logistic regression model, informed by gene set enrichment and co-expression pathway analysis, was used to link each imaging cluster to specific molecular/transcriptomic pathways and mutation status (e.g., BRAF V600E, KIAA1549::BRAF fusion).
records.dataset_size: 201 pediatric low-grade glioma patients (Children's Brain Tumor Network)
records.headline_result: Three distinct imaging clusters were identified with model AUCs of 0.77, 0.78 and 0.70 for the three molecular subtypes; BRAF V600E mutations clustered mainly in imaging cluster 3 and KIAA1549::BRAF fusion in cluster 1.

records.title: Current status and application progresses of artificial intelligence in pediatric ultrasound
records.journal: Chinese Journal of Medical Imaging Technology
records.clinical_problem: AI-assisted diagnosis of pediatric diseases on ultrasound
records.patient_population: children undergoing ultrasound
records.model_description: A narrative review of the current status and progress of artificial intelligence applications in ultrasound-assisted diagnosis of pediatric diseases, noting that children have a disease spectrum distinct from adults.

records.title: Impact of a transient neonatal visual deprivation on the development of the ventral occipito-temporal cortex in humans
records.exclusion_reason: computational/theoretical fMRI study of visual cortex development after transient neonatal cataracts, using a deep neural network only as a modeling analogy; participant age at scanning and pediatric status are not stated

records.title: From womb to crib: How fetal activity patterns in utero reveal postnatal sleep behavior
records.exclusion_reason: uses wearable accelerometer and temperature sensor data to study fetal activity and infant sleep; not a radiology imaging study

records.title: Functional fingerprinting for the developing brain using deep metric learning: an ABCD study
records.clinical_problem: characterizing individual variability of brain functional organization during early adolescent development
records.patient_population: early adolescents from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study, followed over a four-year developmental period
records.model_description: Metric-BoIT is a deep metric learning model trained on resting-state fMRI functional connectivity data to generate individual 'brain fingerprints.' It was used to identify individuals from their fMRI scans within a single session and up to four years later, and the regions and cognitive/genetic correlates driving these fingerprints were analyzed.
records.dataset_size: resting-state fMRI from the ABCD dataset (exact n not stated)
records.headline_result: Individual identification accuracy reached 97.6% within a single session and 86.6% across a four-year developmental period; fingerprints correlated with fluid and crystallized intelligence and with genetic relatedness.

records.title: Neurodevelopmental deviations in schizophrenia: Evidences from multimodal connectome-based brain ages
records.model_family: machine learning brain-age estimation models (structural/functional/morphometric connectome features)
records.clinical_problem: brain developmental deviation (brain age gap) as a biomarker in early-onset schizophrenia
records.patient_population: antipsychotic-naive first-episode early-onset schizophrenia patients (childhood and adolescence) and typically developing controls
records.model_description: Structural (T1-weighted, diffusion) and functional resting-state MRI were used to build three connectome types (morphometric similarity, structural, functional) in youths with early-onset schizophrenia and typically developing controls. Eight brain-age estimation models were trained on the control group's connectome features, and the best model was applied to estimate each patient's brain age; the gap between estimated and chronological age was compared between groups and correlated with symptom severity.
records.dataset_size: 80 early-onset schizophrenia patients and 91 typically developing controls
records.headline_result: Structural and morphometric-similarity connectome features gave the best brain-age estimates; EOS patients had widened structural brain-age gaps that differed between childhood and adolescence and correlated positively with clinical symptom severity.

records.title: Deciphering pediatric low-grade glioma trajectories: Deep learning–based volumetrics for patients under surveillance.
records.model_family: deep learning segmentation algorithm combined with unsupervised time-series clustering (K-means, DBSCAN with dynamic time warping) and ARIMA-GARCH forecasting
records.clinical_problem: tracking and predicting growth trajectories of untreated pediatric low-grade glioma (pLGG) under surveillance
records.patient_population: 129 pLGG patients diagnosed 1992-2020, surveilled untreated for at least one year, median age 13.9 years, from Dana-Farber/Boston Children's Hospital and the Children's Brain Tumor Network
records.model_description: Longitudinal T2-weighted brain MRIs are input to a validated deep learning pLGG segmentation algorithm that computes 3D tumor volume at each timepoint. Unsupervised time-series clustering identifies volumetric phenotypes (progression, stability, regression) and a hybrid statistical time-series model forecasts future volumetric change, to characterize the natural history of tumors under surveillance.
records.headline_result: at last follow-up 33.8% progressed, 35.8% stable, 30.2% regressed; forecasting model average RMSE >1 cm3 (std >0.18 cm3)

records.title: Application of MRI-based radiomics model in predicting the tumor response in patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma after transcatheter arterial chemoembolization
records.exclusion_reason: adult hepatocellular carcinoma population, not pediatric

records.title: Multimodal Deep Learning in Early Autism Detection—Recent Advances and Challenges
records.exclusion_reason: review of recent progress in early autism detection using multimodal deep learning across neuroimaging, genetics and behavioral data; a survey rather than a model

records.title: AnyStar: Domain randomized universal star-convex 3D instance segmentation
records.journal: 2024 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
records.model_family: domain-randomized generative model synthesizing blob-like objects with randomized appearance, environment and imaging physics, used to train general-purpose star-convex instance segmentation networks
records.clinical_problem: instance segmentation networks for star-convex structures need densely labelled examples for every new dataset and modality, and must be re-engineered whenever contrast, shape, orientation, resolution or density change
records.patient_population: human fetal MRI (placental cotyledons), alongside microscopy, micro-CT and electron microscopy datasets
records.model_description: Trains entirely on synthetic data generated by randomizing appearance and imaging physics, so a single network segments across modalities it has never seen - and one of the demonstrations is placental cotyledons on human fetal MRI, alongside nuclei in fluorescence microscopy, micro-CT and electron microscopy. No retraining, finetuning or domain adaptation. For fetal and pediatric imaging, where annotated instances of anything are scarce, a model that needs no annotated images from the target dataset is a different kind of proposition. Code released.
records.headline_result: a single network trained only on synthesized data accurately 3D segments placental cotyledons in human fetal MRI and nuclei across microscopy, micro-CT and electron microscopy without any retraining or adaptation

records.title: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation of MRI Skull-stripping Trained on Adult Data to Newborns
records.journal: 2024 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
records.model_family: unsupervised domain adaptation of an adult-trained U-net skull-stripping model to newborn MRI
records.clinical_problem: skull-stripping newborn brain MRI, where no publicly available dataset carries manual segmentation masks to train on and an adult-trained model fails because of the domain shift
records.patient_population: newborn brain MRI
records.model_description: Confronts the exact structural problem of neonatal imaging AI - the labels do not exist and making them requires expertise nobody has time for - by adapting an adult model without any newborn labels at all. Reaching Dice 0.916, close to supervised state-of-the-art models, is the argument that the labels may not be needed. Ablation studies support the components and the code is released.
records.release_evidence: all the codes are available on GitHub
records.headline_result: Dice 0.916 +/- 0.032 for newborn skull-stripping without any newborn labels, close to supervised state-of-the-art models

records.title: Hybrid Inception Architecture with Residual Connection: Fine-tuned Inception-ResNet Deep Learning Model for Lung Inflammation Diagnosis from Chest Radiographs
records.exclusion_reason: Inception-ResNet-V2 compared against seven other convolutional networks for pneumonia diagnosis on a 5856-image Mendeley chest radiograph dataset; childhood mortality is cited as motivation but the abstract does not state that the imaged patients are children, so a pediatric population cannot be established from the record

records.title: BrainNet: A Deep Learning Approach for Brain Tumor Classification
records.exclusion_reason: BrainNet convolutional architecture for brain tumor classification on MRI, compared against transfer-learning baselines; malignant brain tumors are described as a leading cause of mortality in adult and pediatric populations but the abstract does not state the ages of the imaged patients, so a pediatric population cannot be established from the record

records.title: MAPSeg: Unified Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Heterogeneous Medical Image Segmentation Based on 3D Masked Autoencoding and Pseudo-Labeling
records.journal: 2024 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
records.model_family: unified unsupervised domain adaptation framework combining 3D masked autoencoding with pseudo-labeling, applicable centralized, federated and at test time
records.clinical_problem: keeping segmentation robust across large-scale, multi-center and longitudinal scans when annotations are not available in every domain
records.patient_population: a private infant brain MRI dataset and a public cardiac CT-MRI dataset
records.model_description: The federated and test-time variants are what make this practically relevant to pediatric imaging: infant MRI datasets are small, held privately at individual centres, and often cannot be pooled - so a method that adapts without moving data or labels between sites addresses the actual constraint. The infant brain dataset is the harder of the two benchmarks and shows the larger margin (10.5 Dice). Code released.
records.dataset_size: a private infant brain MRI dataset and a public cardiac CT-MRI dataset
records.headline_result: 10.5 Dice improvement on the private infant brain MRI dataset and 5.7 on the public cardiac CT-MRI dataset over previous state-of-the-art domain adaptation methods

records.title: Test-Time Adaptation with SaLIP: A Cascade of SAM and CLIP for Zero-shot Medical Image Segmentation
records.journal: 2024 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)
records.model_family: training-free cascade of the Segment Anything Model and CLIP: SAM produces part-based masks, CLIP retrieves the one matching a text-described region of interest, and SAM is re-prompted with it
records.clinical_problem: organ segmentation when only a handful of labelled examples exist, which is the normal condition in fetal and pediatric imaging
records.patient_population: brain, lung and fetal head segmentation tasks
records.model_description: Needs no training, no fine-tuning and no labelled data - only a text prompt - which is exactly the regime that matters for fetal and pediatric datasets too small to train on. Fetal head is one of the three evaluation tasks and is also the weakest (30.8% Dice improvement against 63.5% for brain), which is worth recording: general-purpose foundation models still transfer poorly to ultrasound, where the appearance is furthest from natural images.
records.release_evidence: code and text prompts are available
records.headline_result: Dice improvements over un-prompted SAM of 63.46% for brain, 50.11% for lung and 30.82% for fetal head, with no training or fine-tuning

records.title: Using Convolutional Neural Networks for Enhanced Pneumonia Detection via Chest X-Rays
records.journal: 2024 International Conference on IT and Industrial Technologies (ICIT)
records.exclusion_reason: convolutional network for pneumonia detection on chest radiographs with dropout regularization, reporting 98% recall; child mortality is the stated motivation but the abstract does not identify the dataset or state that the patients are children, so a pediatric population cannot be established from the record

records.title: Automation of a Rule-based Workflow to Estimate Age from Brain MR Imaging of Infants and Children Up to 2 Years Old Using Stacked Deep Learning.
records.journal: Magnetic resonance in medical sciences : MRMS : an official journal of Japan Society of Magnetic Resonance in Medicine
records.clinical_problem: Automating a rule-based myelination assessment workflow to estimate corrected age from brain MRI in infants and young children up to 2 years old
records.patient_population: 119 children under 2 years, imaged on two MRI systems; tested also in 13 Sturge-Weber syndrome cases
records.model_description: Input: T1- and T2-weighted brain MRI; output: estimated age based on myelination-related signal changes, via two stacked neural networks (target extraction network plus age estimation network)
records.headline_result: MAE 0.98 months, RMSE 1.27 months, CC 0.99 (internal); external MAE 1.85 months

records.title: Deep learning reconstruction in pediatric brain MRI: comparison of image quality with conventional T2-weighted MRI.

records.model_description: A straight three-way comparison on the same acquisitions - deep learning reconstruction, conventional intensity filtering, and the unfiltered original - read independently by two pediatric radiologists. The finding that matters clinically is lesion conspicuity, not noise: quieter images that hid lesions would be worse, and these did not. Truncation artifact, a specific and common nuisance on pediatric T2, fell significantly; motion and pulsation artifacts did not change, which is the honest limit of what reconstruction can fix.
records.release_evidence: a deep learning reconstruction mode available on the clinical scanner, compared against the scanner's conventional reconstruction

records.title: Generalizability and Bias in a Deep Learning Pediatric Bone Age Prediction Model Using Hand Radiographs.
records.model_name: 2017 RSNA Bone Age Challenge winning model

records.clinical_problem: whether an expert-level bone age model holds up outside its development hospitals and whether its errors fall evenly across demographic groups

It takes the challenge winner and asks the two questions a hospital would ask before deployment - does it generalize, and is it fair - and gets different answers to each. Generalization was clean, with no difference between internal and external error. Fairness was not: error differed by sex, and 16 percent of external predictions would have been clinically significant errors. A useful cautionary reference for any pediatric AI procurement discussion.

records.headline_result: mean absolute difference 6.8 months internally versus 6.9 months externally (P = .64), but 194 of 1202 external predictions (16%) would have changed the clinical diagnosis, and error was greater for girls than boys

records.title: Placenta segmentation in ultrasound imaging: Addressing sources of uncertainty and limited field-of-view.
records.model_family: multi-task convolutional network jointly classifying placental location and segmenting the placenta, with a multi-view multi-probe acquisition and fusion pipeline
records.clinical_problem: segmenting the placenta on fetal ultrasound, where appearance varies widely, image quality makes reference annotations unreliable, and at late gestation the placenta is larger than a single probe's field of view
records.patient_population: fetal ultrasound with annotations from multiple raters, covering anterior and posterior placentas
records.model_description: Three distinct obstacles are each answered with a different mechanism, which is unusually disciplined. The multi-task design lets a large weakly labelled location dataset improve segmentation trained on little data. Multi-rater annotation variability is measured rather than assumed, and the model is judged against it - reaching human-level agreement. And the field-of-view limit is solved outside the network, by acquiring with three probes and fusing, which is the only way to see a whole late-gestation placenta.
records.headline_result: Dice 0.86 for anterior and 0.83 for posterior placentas, matching intra- and inter-observer variability, with whole-placenta segmentation from a fused three-probe acquisition

records.title: Thyroid Nodules on Ultrasound in Children and Young Adults: Comparison of Diagnostic Performance of Radiologists' Impressions, ACR TI-RADS, and a Deep Learning Algorithm.
records.model_family: previously developed deep learning algorithm returning a malignancy likelihood and derived risk level
records.clinical_problem: deciding which thyroid nodules in children need fine-needle aspiration, currently judged by a radiologist's overall impression because the adult risk-stratification system was not built for children
records.patient_population: 139 patients 21 years and younger (median age 17.5 years; 119 female) with a thyroid nodule on ultrasound between January 2004 and September 2020, with fine-needle aspiration or surgical pathology as reference
records.model_description: A three-way comparison that shows the sensitivity-specificity trade being made rather than declaring a winner. Radiologists' gestalt is specific and insensitive (58% / 80%); ACR TI-RADS and the deep learning algorithm are both sensitive but far less specific, and the algorithm's 36% specificity is the lowest of the three. In a population where most nodules are benign and every false positive is a needle in a child's neck, that is the number that governs whether the tool is usable.
records.headline_result: deep learning sensitivity 87.5% with specificity 36.1%, versus ACR TI-RADS 85.1% / 50.6% and radiologists' overall impression 58.3% / 79.9%
records.study_design: retrospective diagnostic accuracy study with reader comparison

The argument is stated in departmental terms — shorter scans mean less sedation, fewer motion artifacts, more throughput.

records.title: Radiomics-based machine learning approach in differentiating fibro-adipose vascular anomaly from venous malformation.
