records.clinical_problem: Differentiating fibro-adipose vascular anomaly from common venous malformation on MRI to guide diagnosis and management
records.patient_population: 178 children, adolescents and young adults with vascular malformations (41 fibro-adipose vascular anomaly, 137 venous malformation)
records.model_description: Radiomics features extracted from T1-weighted and fat-saturated T2-weighted MRI, selected via LASSO or Boruta methods, are used to train weighted logistic regression models that classify vascular malformations as fibro-adipose vascular anomaly versus common venous malformation.
records.dataset_size: 178 patients (41 fibro-adipose vascular anomaly, 137 venous malformation)
records.headline_result: AUC 97% (sensitivity 94-95%, specificity 87-89%) for the best multi-sequence models
records.study_design: retrospective diagnostic model development with repeated 10-fold cross-validation

records.title: Learning the Hidden Signature of Fetal Arch Anatomy: a Three-Dimensional Shape Analysis in Suspected Coarctation of the Aorta.
records.model_family: statistical shape model with linear discriminant analysis
records.clinical_problem: improving antenatal diagnosis of coarctation of the aorta using three-dimensional shape analysis of the fetal aortic arch
records.patient_population: 112 fetuses with suspected coarctation of the aorta
records.model_description: A statistical shape modeling pipeline extracts 3D centerline shape features of the fetal aortic arch from cardiac MRI and uses linear discriminant analysis to classify true coarctation of the aorta versus false-positive cases.
records.dataset_size: 112 fetuses with suspected coarctation of the aorta
records.headline_result: AUC 0.907 for coarctation-of-the-aorta shape risk score classification

records.title: Random Forest Model for Labor Induction in Pregnant Women With Hypertensive Disorders Using a Cervical Double Balloon.
records.journal: Alternative therapies in health and medicine
records.exclusion_reason: labor induction prediction using clinical variables (random forest); not an imaging AI model, adult population

records.title: Prediction of chemotherapy-related complications in pediatric oncology patients: artificial intelligence and machine learning implementations.
records.exclusion_reason: review of AI/ML for predicting chemotherapy-related complications in pediatric oncology; imaging AI mentioned only in passing as broader context, not the review's focus

records.title: In vivo biodistribution and pharmacokinetics of sotrovimab, a SARS-CoV-2 monoclonal antibody, in healthy cynomolgus monkeys.
records.journal: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
records.exclusion_reason: animal (nonhuman primate) pharmacokinetics/biodistribution PET/CT imaging study of a monoclonal antibody; not pediatric, no AI/ML

records.title: Chest radiography and computed tomography imaging in cystic fibrosis: current challenges and new perspectives.
records.exclusion_reason: review of chest radiography and CT in children with cystic fibrosis, noting AI image analysis and photon-counting detector CT as new developments; no model developed

records.title: A review on deep-learning algorithms for fetal ultrasound-image analysis.
records.clinical_problem: the state of deep learning across the whole of fetal ultrasound
records.patient_population: fetuses undergoing ultrasound, as covered by 153 primary studies published after 2017
records.model_description: A survey of 153 papers, sorted into standard-plane detection, anatomical structure analysis and biometry estimation, with the limitations and open problems named for each category and summary tables comparing approaches. It also collects the publicly available datasets and the performance metrics the field uses, and closes on why so little of this work has reached clinical practice.

records.title: Automatic Segmentation of the Fetus in 3D Magnetic Resonance Images Using Deep Learning: Accurate and Fast Fetal Volume Quantification for Clinical Use.
records.clinical_problem: automatically measuring fetal volume/weight and indexed blood flow from MRI for clinical use
records.patient_population: 42 fetuses at median 36 weeks gestation (range 29-39)
records.model_description: a trained neural network takes 3D fetal MRI as input and outputs automatic fetal segmentation used to compute fetal volume/weight and, with phase-contrast MRI, indexed blood flow
records.headline_result: automatic vs. manual segmentation bias 4.5 +/- 351 mL (0.01% +/- 11%)

records.title: Identifying autism spectrum disorder in resting-state fNIRS signals based on multiscale entropy and a two-branch deep learning network.
records.exclusion_reason: functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) signal classification for autism; non-radiologic optical neuroimaging, akin to EEG signal analysis

records.title: Artificial intelligence to understand fluctuation of fetal brain activity by recognizing facial expressions.
records.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
records.clinical_problem: using AI to quantify fluctuation of fetal brain activity via facial expression recognition on 4D ultrasound
records.patient_population: singleton pregnancies, 27-37 weeks gestation
records.model_description: an AI classifier takes 4D ultrasound video of the fetal face as input and outputs confidence scores for seven facial expression categories, analyzed over time

records.title: Use of artificial intelligence in obstetrics: not quite ready for prime time.
records.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
records.exclusion_reason: narrative review of AI across obstetrics - prenatal diagnosis, fetal heart monitoring, pregnancy complications and labor - concluding the evidence is still very limited; no model developed

records.title: A Dataset Auditing Method for Collaboratively Trained Machine Learning Models.
records.exclusion_reason: Machine learning security/dataset-auditing (membership inference) methodology paper; not a clinical imaging application, a pediatric chest X-ray dataset is used only as one of several benchmark datasets

records.title: Prediction of gender from longitudinal MRI data via deep learning on adolescent data reveals unique patterns associated with brain structure and change over a two-year period.
records.clinical_problem: Identify structural brain differences by sex and their changes over a two-year period in adolescents using deep learning on structural MRI
records.patient_population: Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study cohort
records.model_description: Takes 3D structural MRI as input; a deep learning model trained over 200+ epochs predicts sex/gender and identifies brain regions most discriminative of sex-related structural change over two years.
records.headline_result: Gender prediction accuracy exceeding 97%
records.study_design: retrospective longitudinal deep learning study using the ABCD dataset

records.title: Functional connectivity strength and topology differences in social phobia adolescents with and without ADHD comorbidity.
records.clinical_problem: characterizing functional-connectivity differences in adolescent social phobia with and without ADHD comorbidity
records.patient_population: 158 subjects: 36 with social phobia (no ADHD), 60 with social phobia and ADHD, 62 healthy controls, average age 14.16
records.model_description: A linear SVM trained on resting-state fMRI functional-connectivity and topological network features distinguishes social phobia, ADHD comorbidity, and healthy-control groups.
records.headline_result: prediction accuracy significantly above chance rates (specific percentage not given)
records.study_design: retrospective case-control resting-state fMRI classification study

records.title: MRI Radiomics Signature of Pediatric Medulloblastoma Improves Risk Stratification Beyond Clinical and Conventional MR Imaging Features.
records.journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
records.clinical_problem: improving risk stratification for overall survival in pediatric medulloblastoma using MRI radiomics beyond clinical and conventional MRI features
records.patient_population: 111 children (mean age 5.82 years) with pathologically confirmed medulloblastoma
records.model_description: radiomic features extracted from contrast-enhanced T1 MRI are combined with clinical and conventional MRI features in an integrative Cox model that outputs predicted overall survival risk
records.headline_result: C-index 0.823 for integrative model vs. 0.702 for radiomics alone and 0.771 for clinical-MRI model

records.title: Microstate analysis in infancy.
records.exclusion_reason: EEG microstate analysis, not a radiologic diagnostic-imaging modality

records.title: Use of artificial intelligence and deep learning in fetal ultrasound imaging.
records.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
records.clinical_problem: operator dependence of obstetric ultrasound, the gold standard for detecting fetal malformation
records.patient_population: fetuses undergoing obstetric ultrasound
records.model_description: A review in the main obstetric ultrasound journal explaining what deep learning is and where it applies in fetal imaging: recognizing normal and abnormal fetal anatomy and measuring fetal biometry. Its framing is that ultrasound is only as good as the operator, and that these models are proposed as support for sonographers rather than replacements.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Ultrasound Diagnosis on Infant Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip Under Constrained Computational Resources.
records.journal: Journal of ultrasound in medicine : official journal of the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine
records.clinical_problem: Automatically diagnosing infant developmental dysplasia of the hip from static ultrasound images, with a lightweight design for embedding in ultrasound machines
records.patient_population: 881 patients (5-fold cross-validation); blind test of 209 patients (158 normal, 51 abnormal)
records.model_description: Input: static hip ultrasound images; output: alpha/beta angle measurements, femoral head coverage (FHC), percentage of femoral head diameter (PFD), and DDH diagnosis, via a lightweight automatic system (DDHnet) designed for embedding in ultrasound machines
records.headline_result: sensitivity 90.56%, specificity 100%, accuracy 98.64%; alpha angle ICC 0.96
records.study_design: retrospective algorithm development and blind test validation

records.title: TW-Net: Transformer Weighted Network for Neonatal Brain MRI Segmentation.
records.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
records.model_family: Transformer-Weighted Network (CNN encoder-decoder with Transformer module)
records.clinical_problem: accurate segmentation of neonatal brain structures to study brain growth patterns and neurodevelopmental disorder progression
records.patient_population: neonates, two independent public datasets
records.model_description: Input: neonatal brain MRI; output: multi-label brain structure segmentation, using a Transformer module to capture in-plane long-range dependencies missed by standard CNNs.
records.headline_result: Outperforms state-of-the-art deep learning methods on 2D and 2.5D multi-label tasks (no single summary metric reported)
records.study_design: methods development and comparison on two independent public datasets

records.title: Application of Digital Imaging and Artificial Intelligence to Pathology of the Placenta.
records.journal: Pediatric and developmental pathology : the official journal of the Society for Pediatric Pathology and the Paediatric Pathology Society
records.exclusion_reason: digital pathology/histopathology of placenta, non-radiologic imaging

records.title: A Machine Learning Method for Automated Description and Workflow Analysis of First Trimester Ultrasound Scans.
records.model_family: 2D+t convolutional neural network with transfer learning
records.clinical_problem: automatically describing anatomy and modeling operator workflow from first-trimester obstetric ultrasound scans
records.patient_population: pregnant patients undergoing first-trimester obstetric ultrasound scanning
records.model_description: Full-length first-trimester ultrasound scan videos are analyzed by a 2D+t (spatio-temporal) convolutional neural network with transfer learning that automatically partitions the video into semantically meaningful segments based on detected fetal anatomy, enabling analysis of operator clinical workflow, skill, and time spent on key tasks such as nuchal translucency measurement.
records.dataset_size: 250 unlabeled video scans analyzed; additional labeled training data not quantified in abstract
records.headline_result: cross-validation accuracy 96.10%, F1=0.95, precision=0.94, recall=0.95; correlation with expert annotation ρ=0.95 (p=0.06)
records.study_design: retrospective technical development and workflow-analysis study

records.title: Artificial Intelligence for Clinical Interpretation of Bedside Chest Radiographs.
records.model_family: neural network trained on structured semiquantitative radiologic reports rather than on binary labels
records.clinical_problem: reading the supine bedside chest radiograph, one of the most frequently ordered imaging studies in the world, in intensive care units where the person acting on it is often not a radiologist
records.patient_population: 193 566 radiographs from 45 016 children and adults in the intensive care unit of a university hospital, January 2009 to December 2020, reported by 98 radiologists using a structured template; a 100-radiograph internal test set adjudicated by six radiologists
records.model_description: Trained on twelve years of structured semiquantitative reports rather than on retrospectively assigned labels, so the network learns graded severity of cardiomegaly, congestion, effusion, opacity and atelectasis as radiologists actually record them. Two results stand out: it agreed with the six-radiologist consensus better than any individual radiologist did, and - the clinically operative finding - when it provided a preliminary reading, intensivists' own reports improved significantly. Nearly 200 000 radiographs including children.
records.headline_result: kappa 0.86 against the expert-panel majority versus 0.81-0.84 for individual radiologists; non-radiologist physicians improved from kappa 0.79 unaided to 0.87 when given the network's preliminary reading (P < .001)
records.study_design: retrospective model development with a multi-reader study

records.title: Anxiety onset in adolescents: a machine-learning prediction.
records.model_family: voting classifier (random forest, SVM, logistic regression)
records.clinical_problem: predicting future onset of clinical anxiety in non-anxious adolescents
records.patient_population: 156 participants who developed clinical anxiety by age 18-23 and 424 healthy controls, assessed at age 14
records.model_description: Gray-matter regional brain volumes and psychometric scores collected at age 14 are input to a voting classifier (random forest, SVM, logistic regression) that predicts prospective clinical anxiety onset 4-8 years later; Shapley values identify the most contributory features.
records.headline_result: AUC 0.68 for prospective prediction of pooled anxiety disorders

records.title: INDIAMAN-20 (INstant DIAgnosis of 20 Major ANomalies) protocol: application of IOTA diagnostic strategy to fetal anomalies.
records.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
records.exclusion_reason: Defines sonographic diagnostic descriptors/protocol for fetal anomalies; no AI/ML model developed, only mentions potential future incorporation into AI/deep learning protocols.

records.title: Predicting mini-tablet dissolution performance utilizing X-ray computed tomography.
records.journal: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences
records.exclusion_reason: pharmaceutical mini-tablet quality control via micro-CT; not a clinical/patient imaging study

records.title: Radiomics-based machine learning models for prediction of medulloblastoma subgroups: a systematic review and meta-analysis of the diagnostic test performance.
records.exclusion_reason: systematic review and meta-analysis of five radiomics machine learning studies predicting medulloblastoma molecular subgroups, with QUADAS-2 and CLAIM quality appraisal; a synthesis rather than a model

records.title: 3D-MASNet: 3D mixed-scale asymmetric convolutional segmentation network for 6-month-old infant brain MR images.
records.clinical_problem: Can improved CNN architectures accurately segment gray matter, white matter, and CSF on 6-month-old infant brain MRI, where low tissue contrast makes segmentation difficult?
records.patient_population: 23 6-month-old infants from the iSeg-2019 dataset
records.model_description: Takes T1- and T2-weighted infant brain MRI as input; a mixed-scale asymmetric convolution block plugged into existing CNN segmentation architectures outputs voxel-wise segmentation of gray matter, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid.
records.headline_result: Dice 0.931 (GM), 0.912 (WM), 0.961 (CSF); ranked first among 30 teams on the iSeg-2019 Grand Challenge validation set
records.study_design: retrospective challenge submission using public dataset

records.title: Stacked ensemble learning based on deep convolutional neural networks for pediatric pneumonia diagnosis using chest X-ray images.
records.model_family: stacked ensemble deep learning (Xception features + RF/KNN/LR/XGB/SVC/Nu-SVC/MLP stacking classifier)
records.clinical_problem: Can a stacked ensemble deep learning model provide instantaneous, accurate computer-aided detection of pediatric pneumonia on chest X-rays to reduce mortality from delayed diagnosis?
records.patient_population: Public pediatric pneumonia chest X-ray dataset
records.model_description: Takes chest X-ray images as input; features from a pretrained Xception CNN are dimensionality-reduced (Kernel PCA) and classified by a two-stage stacking ensemble, outputting a pneumonia classification.
records.headline_result: Accuracy 98.3%, precision 99.29%, recall 98.36%, F1 98.83%, AUC 98.24%

records.title: Machine learning approaches linking brain function to behavior in the ABCD STOP task.
records.clinical_problem: predicting individual differences in response inhibition (cognitive control) from multimodal neuroimaging in children
records.patient_population: 9- to 11-year-old children, ABCD Study cohort (n=7,298 cross-validation/lockbox)
records.model_description: Multivariate machine learning models use multimodal region-of-interest neuroimaging features (task fMRI activation, cortical structure, diffusion tensor imaging) to predict individual stop-signal reaction time, a measure of response inhibition, in children.
records.headline_result: stop-signal-task fMRI activation explained 12% of variance in stop-signal reaction time
records.study_design: retrospective multi-site cohort machine-learning prediction study (ABCD)

records.title: The uncovered biases and errors in clinical determination of bone age by using deep learning models.
records.model_family: deep learning bone age models (three models trained on Chinese, American, and combined datasets)
records.clinical_problem: evaluating bias and error in AI-based bone age assessment compared with radiologists
records.patient_population: test set of 1,246 children, labeled by ten senior pediatric radiologists
records.model_description: Input: hand/wrist radiographs; output: bone age estimate from three deep learning models trained on Chinese, American, and combined datasets, compared with radiologists' clinical determinations using Grad-CAM heatmap analysis of bias.
records.headline_result: mean absolute deviation 0.42 years; kappa 0.714 agreement between AI and radiologists

records.title: Cross-Sectional Observational Study of Typical in utero Fetal Movements Using Machine Learning.
records.clinical_problem: quantifying complex 3D fetal limb motion in utero from BOLD MRI to assess maternal, placental, and fetal factors affecting fetal movement as a potential biomarker of fetal health and neuromuscular development
records.patient_population: 76 sets of fetal (24-40 gestational weeks) BOLD MRI scans from 52 pregnant women (18-45 years old)
records.model_description: 3D convolutional neural network previously trained to track fetal key points (wrists, elbows, shoulders, ankles, knees, hips) on BOLD MRI time series, used to quantify upper and lower limb kinematics and absolute movement time across gestation and under maternal hyperoxia
records.dataset_size: 76 fetal MRI scan sets from 52 women
records.headline_result: significantly longer limb movement duration during maternal hyperoxia; centrifugal increase in movement across limbs; longer upper-extremity movement before 31 gestational weeks and lower-extremity movement after 35 gestational weeks

records.title: Development of Gestational Age-Based Fetal Brain and Intracranial Volume Reference Norms Using Deep Learning.
records.clinical_problem: Can deep learning automatically and accurately measure fetal intracranial and brain volumes across gestational age to create normative reference standards for detecting abnormal fetal brain volumes?
records.patient_population: 246 patients with singleton pregnancies, 19-38 weeks gestation (training); 200 additional MRIs for normative curve; 9 pathologic fetal brains for testing
records.model_description: Takes 2D fetal brain MRI in axial, coronal, and sagittal planes as input; two sequential 3D U-Nets segment intracranial contents and then brain tissue, outputting volumetric measurements used to build gestational age-based normative reference curves.
records.dataset_size: 246 patients (training); 200 additional for norms; 9 pathologic cases for testing
records.headline_result: Median Dice 0.95 (intracranial), 0.90 (brain); Pearson r=0.996 vs. manual volumes; 8/9 pathologic cases flagged as >2 SD from normative mean

records.title: Fetal behavior during MRI changes with age and relates to network dynamics.
records.clinical_problem: Automatically classifying fetal movement from continuous fMRI to relate fetal motor behavior to brain network dynamics and postnatal motor outcomes.
records.patient_population: 120 normal fetuses undergoing 12-minute fMRI scans
records.model_description: A deep-learning model extracts the fetal brain from 4D fMRI time-series data, from which frame-wise displacement is calculated to classify periods of fetal movement.

records.title: Unsupervised machine learning using K-means identifies radiomic subgroups of pediatric low-grade gliomas that correlate with key molecular markers.
records.model_family: K-means clustering with PCA on radiomic features (unsupervised machine learning)
records.clinical_problem: identifying imaging-based molecular subtypes of pediatric low-grade glioma from MRI radiomic features
records.patient_population: 157 patients with pediatric low-grade gliomas
records.model_description: Input is multi-parametric MRI (T1 pre/post-contrast, T2, T2 FLAIR) of the tumor region, from which 881 quantitative radiomic features are extracted; after PCA dimensionality reduction, K-means clustering identifies imaging-based tumor subtypes that are then compared to molecular and demographic data.
records.dataset_size: 157 patients with pediatric low-grade glioma; 881 radiomic features extracted
records.headline_result: three imaging-based subtypes differed in BRAF mutation frequency (p<0.05), age (p<0.05), tumor location (p<0.01) and histology (p<0.0001)
records.study_design: retrospective radiomics/unsupervised machine learning exploratory study

records.title: Multivendor Evaluation of Automated MRI Postprocessing of Biventricular Size and Function for Children With and Without Congenital Heart Defects.
records.journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
records.model_family: deep learning-based automated segmentation software (two commercial vendor suites: Medis Suite, SuiteHeart)
records.clinical_problem: automatically segmenting left/right ventricle for biventricular size and function assessment in children with and without congenital heart defects
records.patient_population: 80 children (20 each: healthy, LV-CHD, tetralogy of Fallot, univentricular CHD), ages ~8.9-16.4 years
records.model_description: Two fully automated commercial software suites (Medis Suite, SuiteHeart) segment left and right ventricles on pediatric cardiac MRI to calculate biventricular volumes and masses, compared to manual segmentation, in children with and without congenital heart defects.
records.release_evidence: two fully automated software suites (Medis Suite 3.2, Medis, Leiden, the Netherlands and SuiteHeart 5.0, Neosoft LLC, Pewaukee, USA)
records.headline_result: left ventricle ICC 0.96-0.97 (healthy children); right ventricle ICC 0.62-0.94 (larger errors)

records.title: A generalizable connectome-based marker of in-scan sustained attention in neurodiverse youth.
records.clinical_problem: predicting sustained attention performance from functional connectivity in neurodiverse youth, including autism
records.patient_population: youth including participants with autism spectrum disorder and neurotypical participants, across 5 datasets
records.model_description: Functional connectome data from youth performing an in-scan sustained attention task, including participants with neurodiverse conditions such as autism, are used to train connectome-based predictive models. The model developed in one dataset was validated in a separate neurotypical sample performing the same task, and its stability across months to years was examined via connectome-based identification in three additional longitudinal datasets.
records.headline_result: Successful prediction of in-scan sustained attention performance in the primary sample; the attention network model generalized to predict attention in an independent neurotypical sample
records.study_design: multi-dataset cross-sectional and longitudinal cohort study

records.title: A critical role of brain network architecture in a continuum model of autism spectrum disorders spanning from healthy individuals with genetic liability to individuals with ASD.
records.clinical_problem: understanding how brain network architecture relates to cortical alterations across a continuum from genetic liability for autism to autism spectrum disorder
records.patient_population: 560 male subjects (266 ASD, 294 controls, mean age 17.2) from ABIDE; 391 individuals (mean age 12.1) from the Pediatric Imaging, Neurocognition and Genetics database
records.model_description: a machine-learning prediction model takes structural connectome hub/network measures as input and outputs a predicted polygenic risk score for ASD, identifying regions acting as disease epicenters
records.headline_result: structural connectome predicted polygenic risk for ASD, r=0.30, p<0.0001
records.study_design: retrospective cross-sectional neuroimaging study using public datasets

records.title: Combined assisted bone age assessment and adult height prediction methods in Chinese girls with early puberty: analysis of three artificial intelligence systems.
records.model_family: AI-assisted bone age assessment systems (Greulich-Pyle, Tanner-Whitehouse TW3-RUS, China05 RUS-CHN)
records.clinical_problem: evaluating AI-assisted bone age assessment and adult height prediction accuracy in girls with early/precocious puberty
records.patient_population: 726 girls with early puberty, 87 of whom had reached adult height (1,663 left-hand radiographs)
records.model_description: Three AI-assisted bone age assessment methods (Greulich-Pyle, TW3-RUS, RUS-CHN) and three adult height prediction methods (CH05, TW3, Bayley-Pinneau) were compared against actual adult height in Chinese girls with early puberty using left-hand radiographs.
records.dataset_size: 1,663 left-hand radiographs from 726 girls with early puberty
records.headline_result: TW3 predicted adult height within +/-5 cm in 92.9% of cases, overestimating by 0.4+/-2.8 cm; CH05 underestimated by 2.9+/-3.6 cm

records.title: Adolescent functional network connectivity prospectively predicts adult anxiety symptoms related to perceived COVID-19 economic adversity.
records.journal: Journal of child psychology and psychiatry, and allied disciplines
records.clinical_problem: identifying adolescent brain network subtypes that predict later vulnerability to anxiety and depression under adversity
records.patient_population: 174 adolescents (fMRI collected at age 15, followed to age 21) from a population-based sample with high representation of marginalized individuals
records.model_description: Takes task-based fMRI functional connectivity among a priori anxiety/depression-related brain regions as input and outputs data-driven subgroups, identified via an unsupervised community detection algorithm, that predict later anxiety symptom trajectories under adverse experiences.
records.headline_result: Subgroup A showed greater increase in anxiety symptoms over time (β=0.138-0.194, p=0.023-0.042) and stronger adversity interaction (β=0.237-0.307, p=0.006-0.021)
records.study_design: prospective longitudinal cohort study with unsupervised network subtyping

records.title: An explainable autoencoder with multi-paradigm fMRI fusion for identifying differences in dynamic functional connectivity during brain development.
records.journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
records.exclusion_reason: explainable autoencoder method paper on dynamic functional connectivity during typical brain development (general population cohort)

records.title: General psychopathology factor (p-factor) prediction using resting-state functional connectivity and a scanner-generalization neural network.
records.clinical_problem: Predicting a general psychopathology risk factor (p-factor) in adolescents from resting-state functional MRI connectivity, while controlling for scanner-related variability
records.patient_population: 6905 adolescents from 18 sites (ABCD Study)
records.model_description: A scanner-generalization neural network is trained on resting-state functional connectivity from multi-site fMRI to predict an individual psychopathology (p-factor) score while reducing scanner-related confounding.
records.headline_result: correlation coefficient 0.163 (leave-one-site-out CV) vs. 0.150 (kernel ridge regression baseline)

records.title: Early Social Adversity, Altered Brain Functional Connectivity, and Mental Health.
records.exclusion_reason: review of functional connectivity phenotypes after early adversity; discusses candidate biomarkers but builds no model and asks no imaging diagnostic question

records.title: Development of an MRI-Based Radiomics-Clinical Model to Diagnose Liver Fibrosis Secondary to Pancreaticobiliary Maljunction in Children.
records.journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
records.clinical_problem: noninvasively diagnosing liver fibrosis in children with pancreaticobiliary maljunction to guide preoperative decision-making
records.patient_population: 136 children with pancreaticobiliary maljunction from two centers (111 center A, 25 center B)
records.model_description: A radiomics-clinical nomogram combining MRI radiomic features from segmented liver parenchyma with clinical factors noninvasively diagnoses liver fibrosis in children with pancreaticobiliary maljunction, validated against histopathology.
records.dataset_size: 136 children (111 center A: 74 training/37 internal validation; 25 center B external validation)
records.headline_result: combined nomogram AUC 0.977 (training), 0.921 (internal validation), 0.878 (external validation)

records.title: Applications of artificial intelligence in obstetrics.
records.exclusion_reason: review of artificial intelligence systems in obstetric diagnosis - cardiotocography, ultrasonography and MRI; no model developed

records.title: Automating the treatment planning process for 3D-conformal pediatric craniospinal irradiation therapy.
records.model_family: deep learning autocontouring + automated treatment planning tool
records.clinical_problem: Can craniospinal radiotherapy treatment planning for pediatric medulloblastoma be automated, to make this complex, time-consuming plan feasible in resource-constrained (low- and middle-income country) settings?
records.patient_population: 143 pediatric medulloblastoma CT scans (ages 2-19) for autocontour model training; 6 patients (ages 3-10) tested per planning approach
records.model_description: A deep learning model generates autocontours of relevant anatomy from pediatric medulloblastoma CT scans, feeding an autoplanning tool that automatically generates 3D-conformal craniospinal irradiation treatment plans, assessed for clinical acceptability by a radiation oncologist.
records.dataset_size: 143 CT scans for autocontour model (80:20 train:test); 18 plans tested across 6 patients
records.headline_result: Autocontour Dice similarity coefficient 0.65-0.98; all 18 tested plans scored clinically acceptable as-is or with minor edits; average planning time 3.5 +/- 0.4 minutes
records.study_design: retrospective single-center tool development with clinician acceptability assessment

records.title: Statistical and machine learning approaches to predict the necessity for computed tomography in children with mild traumatic brain injury.
records.exclusion_reason: clinical/demographic variable-only prediction model (predicts need for CT scan) that does not use or analyze imaging data

records.title: Development of a Machine Learning Model for Sonographic Assessment of Gestational Age.
records.model_family: three models - an image model on standard biometry planes, a video model on fly-to videos, and an ensemble of the two
records.clinical_problem: estimating gestational age, where derivation from manual head, abdomen and femur measurements is operator dependent and slow
records.patient_population: the Fetal Age Machine Learning Initiative cohort of 3842 participants across Chapel Hill, North Carolina and Lusaka, Zambia, with a test set of 404 participants
records.model_description: The novel input is the fly-to video - the five to ten seconds of sweeping that a machine can record automatically before the sonographer freezes the frame, normally discarded. Using it costs the operator nothing and gives the model the search as well as the destination. Two sites on two continents, and the model beat expert-acquired biometry overall and by a wider margin on fetuses predicted to be small, which is where dating errors do the most harm.
records.headline_result: the ensemble model's mean absolute error was 1.51 days lower than clinical standard biometry (95% CI -1.90 to -1.10 days), with all three models statistically superior to expert-acquired biometry

records.title: Cortical representations of numbers and nonsymbolic quantities expand and segregate in children from 5 to 8 years of age.
records.model_family: multivariate machine learning decoding (within- and between-format)
records.clinical_problem: decoding cortical representations of numerals and nonsymbolic quantity in children
records.patient_population: 89 children, either at the beginning of formal schooling (age 5) or four years in (age 8)
records.model_description: Multivariate fMRI adaptation data are combined with within- and between-format machine learning decoding to probe cortical representations of Arabic numerals and approximate nonsymbolic quantity in 89 children aged 5 or 8 years. The decoding approach tests whether the same neural code represents numerals and nonsymbolic quantities, finding a format-independent representation in right parietal cortex only in 5-year-olds.
records.headline_result: Format-independent neural representation of quantity found in right parietal cortex, present only in 5-year-olds

records.title: MRI-based radiomics nomogram in patients with high-risk placenta accreta spectrum: can it aid in the prenatal diagnosis of intraoperative blood loss?
records.clinical_problem: predicting massive intraoperative blood loss in high-risk placenta accreta spectrum before delivery, using prenatal MRI
records.patient_population: 152 (training, Hospital A) + 64 (validation, Hospital B) high-risk PAS patients
records.model_description: Takes radiomics features extracted from sagittal T2-weighted prenatal MRI of the placenta plus clinical features as input, and outputs a nomogram-based prediction of massive intraoperative blood loss during delivery in patients with placenta accreta spectrum.
records.headline_result: Nomogram AUC 0.866 (training), 0.876 (validation)
records.study_design: retrospective multicenter radiomics nomogram development study

records.title: Fetal MRI radiomics: non-invasive and reproducible quantification of human lung maturity.
records.exclusion_reason: assessment of the intra-class correlation of 100 radiomics features extracted from repeated in-vivo fetal lung MRI acquisitions in 30 fetuses; a feature reproducibility study that develops no predictive model

records.title: Learning to segment fetal brain tissue from noisy annotations.
records.model_family: deep learning segmentation trained on noisy multi-atlas labels, with a novel label smoothing procedure and loss function
records.clinical_problem: multi-label fetal brain tissue segmentation across gestation, where the transient structures change so fast that a model needs many training images and manual multi-label segmentation of that many 3D volumes is prohibitive
records.patient_population: 272 training images covering 19-39 gestational weeks segmented automatically and manually corrected, with 23 manually segmented test images from a separate set of fetuses
records.model_description: Trades label quality for label quantity deliberately, then handles the consequence: 272 volumes are segmented by multi-atlas registration with only the large errors fixed by hand, and a smoothing procedure plus a matched loss teaches the network to treat tissue boundaries as uncertain rather than trusting them. Testing on separately, manually segmented fetuses keeps the evaluation clean of the noisy labels. Beat nnU-Net, which is the standard that matters in segmentation.
records.dataset_size: 272 training and 23 manually segmented test images
records.headline_result: average Dice 0.893 for younger and 0.916 for older fetuses on transient structures, significantly more accurate than several state-of-the-art methods including nnU-Net

records.title: Radiomics based of deep medullary veins on susceptibility-weighted imaging in infants: predicting the severity of brain injury of neonates with perinatal asphyxia.

records.patient_population: 190 neonates with HIE (24 mild, 166 moderate-to-severe), born at 37 weeks or later
records.model_description: Radiomics features of the deep medullary veins on susceptibility-weighted MRI feed a nomogram (Rad-score plus urea nitrogen) that outputs a probability distinguishing mild from moderate-to-severe HIE.
records.headline_result: AUC 0.84 training cohort, 0.80 validation cohort (radiomics model)
records.study_design: retrospective single-center radiomics model development with internal training/validation split

records.title: Deep focus approach for accurate bone age estimation from lateral cephalogram.
records.model_family: DeepLabv3+ cervical vertebrae segmentation feeding an Inception-ResNet-v2 regression model by transfer learning, with gradient-weighted regression activation maps
records.clinical_problem: estimating skeletal maturity from the lateral cephalogram a growing child already has, so that a separate hand-wrist radiograph is not required
records.patient_population: 900 participants aged 4-18 years who had a lateral cephalogram and a hand-wrist radiograph on the same day, five-fold cross-validated
records.model_description: Same clinical idea as other cervical-vertebrae maturity work - remove a radiograph from the pathway - but executed end to end, with segmentation isolating the vertebrae before a regression network reads them, rather than measuring handcrafted ratios. Nine hundred same-day paired radiographs is a strong reference design. The reported mean absolute error of 0.300 years is far below what hand-wrist bone age methods achieve, which invites caution about how the reference age was defined.
records.headline_result: segmentation accuracy 0.956 with IoU 0.913; bone age mean absolute error 0.300 years and RMSE 0.390 years, with coefficient of determination 0.983

records.title: A Combined Region- and Pixel-Based Deep Learning Approach for Quantifying Abdominal Adipose Tissue in Adolescents Using Dixon Magnetic Resonance Imaging.

records.model_description: Takes axial fat-only Dixon MRI images as input and outputs automated segmentation of the abdominal wall region and subcutaneous/visceral adipose tissue pixel masks, using a U-Net CNN, for volumetric quantification.

records.title: Detecting pediatric wrist fractures using deep-learning-based object detection.
records.clinical_problem: subtle buckle fractures of the distal radius, which are the classic missed pediatric fracture
records.patient_population: 395 pediatric posteroanterior wrist radiographs, 65% with fracture and 30% with a distal radial buckle fracture
records.model_description: Detects and boxes wrist fractures, targeting the buckle fracture specifically because it is subtle and characteristically pediatric. Four trainees read the cases with and without the box. Both pediatric and radiology residents improved sharply, and — unusually — when reader and model disagreed after the model's prediction was shown, the residents were right nearly three times out of four, which suggests the box informed rather than overrode them.
records.dataset_size: 395 radiographs (229 train, 41 tune, 125 test), four readers
records.headline_result: AUC 0.92 and accuracy 88%, detecting 90% of buckle fractures; resident accuracy rose from 80% to 93% for any fracture and 69% to 92% for buckle fractures (both P < 0.001)

records.title: Superficial white matter analysis: An efficient point-cloud-based deep learning framework with supervised contrastive learning for consistent tractography parcellation across populations and dMRI acquisitions.
records.model_family: point-cloud network with supervised contrastive learning
records.clinical_problem: parcellating the superficial white matter, which most tract-segmentation methods avoid because of its complexity
records.patient_population: six independently acquired datasets spanning ages and health conditions, including neonates and patients with space-occupying brain tumors
records.model_description: Classifies tractography streamlines into 198 superficial white matter clusters, working on the streamline as a point cloud rather than on an image grid, with contrastive learning to separate plausible streamlines from outliers. The evidence that matters is the breadth of testing: six independently acquired datasets covering neonates through old age and including brains distorted by tumors, where registration-based parcellation typically fails.
records.dataset_size: large-scale training tractography plus six independent test datasets
records.headline_result: highly consistent and accurate parcellation across all six datasets including neonates and tumor patients, and much faster than comparators

records.title: Insult to Short-Range White Matter Connectivity in Childhood Brain Tumor Survivors.

records.patient_population: 26 childhood brain tumor (medulloblastoma) survivors and 26 typically developing children
records.model_description: Input is T1-weighted and diffusion-weighted MRI, from which short-range white matter connections are delineated by a whole-brain virtual dissection approach; a random forest classifier identifies which short-range connections show the largest microstructural (fractional anisotropy, axial diffusivity) differences between brain tumor survivors and typically developing children.
records.dataset_size: 26 brain tumor survivors and 26 typically developing children
records.headline_result: Random forest classifier distinguished patients from controls using short-range white matter microstructure with 87.5% accuracy

records.title: DeepMNF: Deep Multimodal Neuroimaging Framework for Diagnosing Autism Spectrum Disorder.
records.model_family: deep multimodal framework fusing 2D functional time series with 3D structural images
records.clinical_problem: computer-aided diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder in young children, where early intervention matters and no imaging benchmark exists
records.patient_population: the ABIDE-1 repository, including data from all available screening sites
records.model_description: Addresses the specific problem that has capped ABIDE results for years - multi-site data amplifies heterogeneity as fast as it adds subjects - by fusing functional time series and structural volumes so that the shared signal is reinforced. Reported as exceeding the best published validation performance on ABIDE-1 using every site.
records.headline_result: superior validation performance to the best previously reported result on the ABIDE-1 repository using data from all available sites
records.study_design: retrospective model development on a public dataset

records.title: Generalisability of fetal ultrasound deep learning models to low-resource imaging settings in five African countries.
records.model_family: fetal plane classifier with transfer-learning-based domain adaptation
records.clinical_problem: whether a fetal standard-plane classifier trained where imaging data, equipment and expertise are plentiful works anywhere else - specifically in Sub-Saharan Africa, where limited antenatal screening drives high perinatal mortality
records.patient_population: trained on 1792 patients in Spain, evaluated on 1008 patients in Denmark, then adapted to five African centres (Egypt, Algeria, Uganda, Ghana and Malawi) with 25 patients each
records.model_description: The first study to measure, rather than assume, how a fetal ultrasound model transfers from a high-resource centre to low-resource ones - and the design isolates the two things that change at once, since Denmark tests a distribution shift with good equipment while the African centres test both. Twenty-five patients per site is what such centres can realistically contribute, so showing that domain adaptation can lift recall from that little data is the practical finding.
records.dataset_size: 1792 Spanish, 1008 Danish, and 25 patients at each of five African centres
records.headline_result: transfer learning for domain adaptation raised recall on African populations while maintaining high precision across centres

records.title: Machine learning for accurate estimation of fetal gestational age based on ultrasound images.
records.model_family: machine learning image analysis of standard ultrasound planes, using no measurement inputs
records.clinical_problem: dating a pregnancy in the second and third trimesters, where biometry assumes an average fetal size at each gestational age and its error widens to at least two weeks as growth deviates from that average

records.model_description: Attacks the assumption rather than the measurement. Conventional dating converts size to age through a population growth curve, so any fetus off the average is mis-dated - which is exactly the growth-restricted fetus whose dating matters most. Reading the image directly, with no measurements at all, sidesteps that and the paper shows it holds up in intrauterine growth restriction. Blinded external validation against first-trimester-confirmed dates is the right standard and rarely met in this literature.
records.dataset_size: two independent datasets, sizes not stated in the abstract
records.headline_result: mean absolute error 3.0 days (95% CI 2.9-3.2) in the second trimester and 4.3 days (95% CI 4.1-4.5) in the third, better than current ultrasound-based clinical biometry at those ages

records.title: Deep learning based synthetic CT from cone beam CT generation for abdominal paediatric radiotherapy.
records.model_family: cycle-consistent generative adversarial network with global-residuals-only learning and a structural consistency term in the loss
records.clinical_problem: adaptive radiotherapy needs CT-quality images to recalculate dose, but the image taken on the treatment couch is a cone beam CT - and in children's abdomens, bowel gas moves between fractions and the patient numbers are small
records.patient_population: paediatric patients treated for thoracic, abdominal and pelvic malignancies, with a development dataset and a separate unseen evaluation dataset
records.model_description: Three adaptations, each aimed at a specific difficulty of the pediatric setting. Structural consistency is written into the loss because a cycleGAN will otherwise hallucinate anatomy - fatal when the change you are trying to capture is where the bowel gas moved. Slice selection on a common abdominal field of view turns scans from children treated for any thoracic, abdominal or pelvic malignancy into weakly paired training data, which is how a small population yields enough. Evaluation goes beyond image similarity to segmentation and proton-therapy-specific metrics, since the images exist to compute dose.
records.headline_result: mean absolute error 55.0 +/- 16.6 HU versus 58.9 +/- 16.8 HU for a baseline cycleGAN, with better structural agreement for gastrointestinal gas

records.title: Resting-state functional connectivity disruption between the left and right pallidum as a biomarker for subthreshold depression.

Positioned as a diagnostic assistant, which is the appropriate claim at this scale.

records.title: BOUNTI: Brain vOlumetry and aUtomated parcellatioN for 3D feTal MRI.
records.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
records.model_family: semi-supervised deep learning tissue parcellation trained on atlas-propagated, manually refined labels
records.clinical_problem: fetal brain volumetry has no universally accepted parcellation protocol, so published studies use different schemes and all of them need extensive manual refinement

records.title: AI aided workflow for hip dysplasia screening using ultrasound in primary care clinics.

records.clinical_problem: universal newborn screening for developmental dysplasia of the hip, which prevents premature osteoarthritis if caught in infancy but is not cost-effective when every scan needs an expert to perform and a radiologist or surgeon to read
records.patient_population: 369 scans in 306 infants, scanned by nurses or family physicians at three primary care clinics after video, slide and brief in-person training
records.model_description: The clearest example in this database of AI changing who can do a study rather than how well it is read. Nurses and family physicians with an afternoon of training, a handheld probe and real-time decision support reached follow-up and case-detection rates comparable to formal screening done by a sonographer and read by a specialist. The learning curve is quantified rather than asserted - follow-up rates fell from 40% to 14% after about 60 cases per site. All six infants referred on had confirmed dysplasia, and four had no risk factors that would have flagged them for selective screening.
records.release_evidence: the FDA-cleared MEDO-Hip AI app used with a commercial handheld ultrasound probe
records.dataset_size: 369 scans in 306 infants across three primary care clinics
records.headline_result: internal follow-up rate fell from 40% (nurses) and 20% (physicians) to 14% after about 60 cases per site; all 6 infants referred to pediatric orthopedics had confirmed dysplasia, 4 of them with no risk factors

records.title: StrainNet: Improved Myocardial Strain Analysis of Cine MRI by Deep Learning from DENSE.
records.model_family: three-dimensional (2D + time) convolutional neural network trained on DENSE displacement measurements
records.clinical_problem: measuring myocardial strain from ordinary cine MRI with the accuracy of DENSE, a specialized sequence most centres do not run
records.patient_population: 161 patients with various heart diseases, 99 healthy adults, and 45 healthy children and adolescents (mean age 12 years +/- 3), scanned with DENSE between August 2008 and January 2022 at multiple centres
records.model_description: Distills a specialized acquisition into a routine one: the network learns from displacement-encoded ground truth and then infers the same displacement from contour motion on ordinary cine. That makes accurate strain available wherever cine is available, which for pediatric cardiology is most places. The comparator is the commercial feature-tracking software departments actually use, and StrainNet beat it on both global and, more importantly, segmental strain, where feature tracking is weakest.
records.dataset_size: 305 subjects (161 patients, 99 healthy adults, 45 healthy children and adolescents)
records.headline_result: average end-point error 0.75 mm +/- 0.35 against DENSE; ICC with DENSE 0.87 for global and 0.75 for segmental circumferential strain, versus 0.72 and 0.48 for commercial feature tracking

records.title: Conquering the Cobb Angle: A Deep Learning Algorithm for Automated, Hardware-Invariant Measurement of Cobb Angle on Radiographs in Patients with Scoliosis.
records.model_family: deep learning pipeline for automated vertebral tilt detection and Cobb angle computation
records.clinical_problem: Cobb angle measurement, the definitional measurement in scoliosis, which is manual and slow enough that it limits surgical planning and postoperative monitoring
records.patient_population: 1310 anterior-posterior low-dose stereoradiographic images and radiographs from patients with suspected scoliosis across six centres (2005-2020), with internal (n = 460) and external (n = 161) hold-out test sets and ground truth from two experienced radiologists
records.model_description: The word in the title that matters is hardware-invariant. Postoperative films with rods and screws are where automated Cobb measurement usually fails, and monitoring after surgery is precisely when the measurement is needed repeatedly - so showing no significant difference with or without hardware (P = .80) is the finding. The same invariance is demonstrated across age, sex, body mass index, curve severity and image type, on an external test set. Under half a second per image, at under 2 degrees error.
records.headline_result: under 2 degrees error with intraclass correlation 0.96 against two radiologists, with no significant difference by surgical hardware, age, sex, BMI, scoliosis severity or image type
records.study_design: retrospective multicenter model development with external validation

records.model_description: A radiation-sparing substitute for the screening examination rather than for the diagnostic radiograph. The comparison is the honest one - the app's output and the radiographic ground truth were both put blind against two spine surgeons judging the same unclothed back - so the question asked is whether the model beats the clinical examination it would replace, not whether it beats the X-ray. Progression detection over six-month follow-up is the harder and more clinically valuable half.

records.title: Bone Age Assessment Using Artificial Intelligence in Korean Pediatric Population: A Comparison of Deep-Learning Models Trained With Healthy Chronological and Greulich-Pyle Ages as Labels.
records.model_family: convolutional neural network trained on chronological age as the label, compared against a commercial Greulich-Pyle-trained model
records.clinical_problem: whether bone age in a given population should be predicted against the Greulich-Pyle atlas or learned directly from the chronological ages of healthy children in that population
records.patient_population: 21 036 hand radiographs of Korean children and adolescents without bone-development-affecting conditions obtained 1998-2019 (median age 9 years), with two external test sets of 343 and 321 healthy Korean children
records.model_description: A direct head-to-head on the question the bone age literature keeps circling: population-specific chronological age labels against the mid-century American atlas, tested at two independent institutions. The locally trained model won on every metric at both sites. That is an argument for retraining rather than importing bone age models, and a caution about deploying an atlas-based commercial product outside the population it encodes - though the comparison is in healthy children, not the children a bone age is usually ordered for.
records.release_evidence: compared against VUNO Med-BoneAge version 1.1, a commercial Greulich-Pyle-based model
records.dataset_size: 21 036 training radiographs; 664 external test cases at two institutions
records.headline_result: RMSE 11.2 versus 13.8 months (P = 0.004) and mean absolute error 8.2 versus 10.5 months (P = 0.002) against the commercial Greulich-Pyle model at institution 1, with similar advantages at institution 2

records.dataset_size: large simulated fetal brain stack dataset (size not stated) plus real fetal brain stacks for testing
records.headline_result: Demonstrated state-of-the-art performance estimating more complicated and larger motions than conventional methods (no single quantitative figure given)

records.title: Accelerated two-dimensional phase-contrast for cardiovascular MRI using deep learning-based reconstruction with complex difference estimation

It takes undersampled k-space data as input and outputs reconstructed images with quantitative peak velocity and total flow measurements, evaluated against a parallel imaging/compressed sensing method and tested prospectively in pediatric patients.

records.headline_result: 9x accelerated CD-DL reconstruction was accurate and precise for peak velocity (bias 2.8 vs 3.9 for PICS) and total flow (1.8 vs 2.9 for PICS)
records.study_design: retrospective and prospective technical validation study

records.title: Motion artifact correction in fetal MRI based on a Generative Adversarial network method

records.dataset_size: synthetic motion-artifact training set (N not stated); validated on real motion-degraded fetal MRI scans

records.headline_result: highest mean average precision 82.10% at 17 frames per second (0.3 ms per frame) across nine cardiac substructures

records.title: Deep learning reconstruction for brain CT images in children
records.journal: Chinese Journal of Interventional Imaging and Therapy

records.patient_population: 61 children undergoing brain CT
records.model_description: Brain CT data from 61 children were reconstructed with six levels of adaptive statistical iterative reconstruction (ASIR-V) and three levels of deep learning reconstruction (DLR: low, middle, high). Signal-to-noise ratio, contrast-to-noise ratio, noise, and subjective 5-point image quality scores were compared to determine which reconstruction level best preserves diagnostic image quality.
records.headline_result: DLR-high noise reduction rate exceeded ASIR-V100% (supratentorial 0.62 vs 0.59, infratentorial 0.61 vs 0.59, both P<0.001); DLR-middle and DLR-high had higher subjective scores than all ASIR-V levels

records.title: Deeplasia: prior-free deep learning for pediatric bone age assessment robust to skeletal dysplasias
records.clinical_problem: bone age assessment, including in patients with skeletal dysplasia
records.patient_population: public RSNA bone age dataset (12,611 train / 1,425 validation / 200 test hand radiographs) plus a retrospectively collected cohort of 189 patients (568 x-rays) with molecularly confirmed genetic skeletal dysplasias
records.model_description: Deeplasia is an open-source ensemble of convolutional neural networks that takes a hand radiograph as input and outputs an estimated bone age. It was trained on the public RSNA bone age dataset and additionally validated on hand x-rays from children with skeletal dysplasias, a population usually excluded from prior bone-age models, including a longitudinal subset for test-retest precision.
records.release_evidence: We design and present Deeplasia, an open-source prior-free deep-learning approach for pediatric bone age assessment specifically validated on patients with skeletal dysplasias.
records.dataset_size: 12,611/1,425/200 RSNA hand radiographs (train/val/test); 568 x-rays from 189 patients with skeletal dysplasias
records.headline_result: mean absolute difference 3.87 months on the RSNA test set; 5.84 months on dysplastic hands; longitudinal test-retest precision 2.74 months, at least at human expert level
records.study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study

records.patient_population: 62 newborns, gestational age >=33+0 weeks, with early tachypnea/dyspnea/oxygen requirement, multicentre
records.model_description: Lung ultrasound scans obtained at defined early time points in newborns with respiratory distress were processed to extract regions of interest and used to train a neural network to interpret lung ultrasound and generate an AI-based score analogous to an established neonatal lung ultrasound score (nLUS). records.release_evidence: described as a research model with no stated public release

records.headline_result: AUROC 0.88 (T0) and 0.80 (T1) for predicting need for CPAP; AUROC 0.84 (T0) and 0.89 (T1) for predicting need for surfactant therapy

records.title: Estimating cortical thickness trajectories in children across different scanners using transfer learning from normative models
records.model_family: hierarchical Bayesian regression normative model with transfer learning
records.clinical_problem: charting individual cortical thickness development, including detecting abnormal development in children born preterm, across scanners
records.patient_population: reference model from N=40,435 individuals across the lifespan and dozens of sites; transferred to a longitudinal developmental cohort of children aged 6-17 years (N=5,985) with three measurement waves on two scanners
records.model_description: A large reference normative model of cortical thickness was estimated with hierarchical Bayesian regression from over 40,000 individuals across the lifespan, then transferred to a longitudinal cohort of children aged 6-17 scanned on two scanners not seen during model estimation. The model produces an individual deviation score for cortical thickness that is independent of scanner effects, and was shown to detect morphological heterogeneity in individuals born preterm.
records.dataset_size: reference model N=40,435 (all ages); transfer cohort N=5,985 children aged 6-17, three waves, two scanners
records.headline_result: a transfer set of as few as 25 samples per site gave good performance; deviation scores detected morphological heterogeneity in individuals born pre-term
records.study_design: retrospective multi-site longitudinal normative modeling study

records.title: Incremental improvements in tractometry-based brain-age modeling with deep learning

records.dataset_size: large sample of children and adolescents (exact N not stated)
records.headline_result: recurrent neural network architectures gave up to ~6% improvement in accuracy over the linear baseline

records.title: Improvement of Bone Age Assessment Using a Deep Learning Model in Young Children: Significance of Carpal Bone Analysis
records.model_family: hybrid Greulich-Pyle and modified Tanner-Whitehouse deep learning model

records.patient_population: 453 hand radiographs from a single institution (external validation), young children

records.title: Pediatric brain tumor classification using deep learning on MR-images from the children’s brain tumor network
records.model_family: off-the-shelf deep learning models and a custom shallow CNN, pretrained on adult MRI, with joint image-age fusion

records.headline_result: Best performance (custom shallow network with age fusion): MCC 0.71 (ADC) / 0.64 (T2-w) for infratentorial tumors; MCC 0.70 (ADC) / 0.57 (T2-w) for combined infra- and supratentorial tumors

records.title: How does artificial intelligence in radiology improve efficiency and health outcomes?
records.clinical_problem: whether radiology AI actually improves efficiency, dose, accuracy and outcomes
records.patient_population: not specified; the review is written for a pediatric radiology readership
records.model_description: A review, not a model. It names six clinical objectives AI is meant to serve — faster workflow, shorter reading time, less dose and contrast, earlier detection, better accuracy, more personalized diagnostics — and grades the published evidence for each against a hierarchical model of efficacy. Its conclusion is that the market is still maturing and very little is known about what AI contributes in practice, which is the argument for real-world monitoring before procurement.

records.dataset_size: not stated; prospectively enrolled across 15 maternity hospitals
records.headline_result: occiput anterior versus non-occiput anterior discrimination reported by accuracy, F1-score, precision-recall AUC and Cohen's kappa against transabdominal ultrasound

records.title: Language function following preterm birth: prediction using machine learning.

records.model_description: Neonatal white matter microstructure plus perinatal history, used to answer a question the neonatal follow-up clinic asks constantly and cannot currently answer at discharge. The imaging features are peak-width-of-skeletonized diffusion metrics rather than region-of-interest averages, and the model's risk factors read as clinically coherent - twins and an incomplete antenatal corticosteroid course raised risk, female sex and breastfeeding lowered it. records.headline_result: balanced accuracy 91%, sensitivity 86%, specificity 96% for typical versus delayed language development at 2 years

records.title: Exploring a new paradigm for the fetal anomaly ultrasound scan: Artificial intelligence in real time.
records.model_family: AI-enabled tools automating image acquisition, biometric measurement and report production during a live scan

records.patient_population: 23 subjects, each having both a standard and an AI-assisted scan, with a sonographer feedback survey
records.model_description: An end-to-end automation pilot rather than a single model, and the endpoint is the scan rather than an accuracy metric. Seven and a half minutes saved per scan with no clinically significant difference in biometry, and the sonographers reported that removing repetitive tasks let them concentrate on interpretation - which is the mechanism by which this would improve anomaly detection, if it does. The honest limitation is stated: plane detection saved a satisfactory view in 93% of cases for four core views but only 73% for the full thirteen, against 98% manually.
records.headline_result: 7.62 minutes (34.7%) saved per scan (p < 0.0001) with no clinically significant biometric differences; satisfactory views saved in 93% for four core views and 73% for all thirteen, versus 98% manually

records.title: Super-Resolution Cine Image Enhancement for Fetal Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
records.journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
records.model_family: two convolutional super-resolution networks applied to phase-encoding-undersampled cine acquisitions
records.clinical_problem: fetal cardiac MRI improves diagnosis of congenital heart defects but takes long enough that fetal motion frequently ruins it
records.patient_population: 28 fetuses at a median gestational week of 36 (IQR 33-38), imaged at 1.5 T with Doppler ultrasound-gated balanced SSFP cine
records.model_description: Attacks motion by shortening the acquisition rather than by correcting afterwards: acquire at a third of the phase-encoding resolution, then restore it. The evaluation is a blinded three-observer quality score against the fully sampled clinical acquisition, with bicubic interpolation and zero-padding as the honest comparators - and both of those degraded significantly at 33% while the networks did not. Three times faster acquisition with no measurable quality cost.
records.dataset_size: 28 fetuses; 36 training, 3 validation and 67 test cine slices
records.headline_result: no significant difference in blinded image quality from clinical images down to 33% phase-encoding resolution (three times faster), whereas bicubic interpolation and zero-padding degraded significantly

records.title: MRI-based radiomics signature and clinical factor for predicting H3K27M mutation in pediatric high-grade gliomas located in the midline of the brain.
records.model_family: MRMR and LASSO-selected radiomics signature across FLAIR, DWI, post-contrast T1 and ADC, combined with a clinical predictor in a nomogram
records.clinical_problem: predicting H3K27M mutation status before biopsy in pediatric high-grade midline gliomas, where conventional MRI features are not powerful enough to make the call and the mutation defines prognosis
records.patient_population: 107 children with midline high-grade glioma who underwent biopsy with preoperative MRI between June 2016 and June 2021, 79 of them H3K27M-mutant, randomly split into training and test sets
records.model_description: A purely pediatric counterpart to the mixed-age midline glioma radiomics work, and stronger for it - 107 children from one institution, four sequences plus ADC maps, and a two-stage feature selection that lands on nine features. Adding one visually assessed feature, ring enhancement, to the radiomic signature is a nice touch: it keeps a radiologist-legible term in the model. Training and test AUCs stay close, which the small mixed-age studies in this area do not manage.
records.headline_result: radiomics signature AUC 0.95 training and 0.92 test; the nomogram with ring enhancement 0.95 and 0.90

records.title: The augmented radiologist: artificial intelligence in the practice of radiology.
records.clinical_problem: where AI fits in the pediatric radiologist's working day, and what it cannot do
records.patient_population: children imaged in radiology practice
records.model_description: A review in Pediatric Radiology arguing for augmentation rather than replacement. It sets out what AI does better than a person (measuring size, shape, texture and kinetics; handling high-dimensional data) against what it does worse (it is only as good as its training sample and cannot reason toward a near-optimal solution), and proposes explainable AI and an assistant that frees the radiologist's attention for the generic parts of the job.

records.title: Segmentation of the Aorta and Pulmonary Arteries Based on 4D Flow MRI in the Pediatric Setting Using Fully Automated Multi-Site, Multi-Vendor, and Multi-Label Dense U-Net.
records.journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
records.model_family: 3D multi-label dense U-Net trained on single-site and pooled multi-site data
records.clinical_problem: segmenting the aorta and pulmonary arteries on 4D flow MRI to measure pulmonary and systemic flow and their ratio in congenital heart disease, which is done by hand and takes an expert
records.patient_population: 174 subjects across two sites (38 healthy controls, 136 congenital heart disease patients; 46% female), scanned at 1.5 and 3 T
records.model_description: Asks the question a consortium has to answer before pooling: does training across heterogeneous sites, field strengths and vendors degrade a segmentation network relative to a local one? The answer here is no - Dice and, more importantly, the derived flow measurements Qs, Qp and Qp/Qs were statistically indistinguishable between single-site and multi-site models at both sites. That clears the way for training on pooled data in congenital heart disease, where no single centre has enough cases.
records.headline_result: no significant difference between single-site and multi-site networks in aortic Dice (0.916 vs 0.915 and 0.906 vs 0.904) or in Qs, Qp and Qp/Qs at either site

records.title: Using chest computed tomography and unsupervised machine learning for predicting and evaluating response to lumacaftor-ivacaftor in people with cystic fibrosis.

One of the three clusters contained most of the responders. Alongside this, visual Bhalla scoring quantifies what the drug did to the airways - mucus plugging, wall thickening and consolidation all fell over a year.
records.headline_result: Bhalla score fell 1.40 +/- 1.53 points at one year (p<0.001); 54% of one radiomic cluster achieved a >= 5% FEV1 gain versus 32% and 33% in the others (p=0.02)

records.model_description: A closed loop rather than a model: the sequence sends each slice out to a network as it is acquired, gets a quality score back, and at the end of the stack reacquires only the worst slices, with no human in the loop. records.headline_result: image quality assessment accuracy 85.2% and AUC 0.899, used in real time to reacquire only the motion-degraded slices instead of the whole stack

records.model_description: The most useful deployment study in this database, and it contains no images. BoneXpert was built as an AI-replace tool; asked how they actually use it, only 18% of radiologists let it replace them, 60% still review the radiograph themselves to exclude underlying disease, and 40% have never overruled it. Reporting time fell sharply. The authors' conclusion is the general lesson: bone age rating is not the whole of reading a bone age radiograph, so a tool validated for one task cannot autonomously own the examination.

records.model_description: The model is a means to a reference standard: an existing validated pipeline is run over 2168 carefully screened normal children to produce age- and sex-based percentile curves for muscle area and index. The finding that muscle index correlates only weakly with age and BMI, while raw area correlates strongly, is what makes the normative curves necessary.
records.headline_result: age- and sex-based percentile curves for pediatric skeletal muscle area and index at L3; muscle area correlated strongly with weight, height, age and BMI (0.75-0.94) while muscle index correlated only weakly to moderately (0.25-0.57)

records.model_description: Two contributions worth separating. Methodologically, it settles a practical question - nine careful manual annotations beat many weak atlas-derived labels, reaching close to intra-observer variability - which changes how a group with limited annotation time should spend it. Substantively, applying the result to 278 healthy volumes produced ultrasound-specific second-trimester growth curves for choroid plexus, ventricle horns, cavum septum pellucidum and cerebellum, which is a normative reference that did not previously exist for this modality.

records.model_description: Larger than most pediatric radiomics studies at 253 children, with two separate held-out test sets rather than one, and the concordance index holds steady across all three - which is the main reason to trust it. The clinically actionable part is the last result: children with a low radiomics score did better after postoperative radiotherapy, which turns a prognostic score into a possible treatment-selection tool. The gain over clinicopathological factors alone is real but modest.
records.headline_result: concordance index 0.711, 0.707 and 0.717 on training and the two test sets; the nomogram reached 0.723 and 0.722 versus 0.665 and 0.677 for clinicopathological factors alone

records.title: Artificial Intelligence-Augmented Pediatric Lung POCUS: A Pilot Study of Novice Learners.
records.journal: Journal of ultrasound in medicine : official journal of the American Institute of Ultrasound in Medicine
records.model_family: AI-assisted software generating panoramic lung views from a pleural sweep
records.clinical_problem: diagnosing pneumonia with point-of-care lung ultrasound in the pediatric emergency department, where the technique beats chest radiography but depends heavily on who is holding the probe
records.patient_population: 32 previously healthy patients aged 0-17 years presenting to a pediatric emergency department with a cardiopulmonary complaint, scanned by seven novice learners after one hour of training; two POCUS-trained experts served as the criterion standard
records.model_description: The AI does not read for pneumonia so much as build the image - stitching a pleural sweep into a complete panoramic view of the lung, which is the part a novice cannot reliably produce. One hour of training and seven novices is a deliberately hard test of that idea. The result should be read as a feasibility signal only: three pneumonias among 32 patients gives a sensitivity confidence interval spanning almost the entire range, and the mean image quality rating was under 3 out of 5.
records.headline_result: novice sensitivity 66.7% (CI 9.4-99.1%), specificity 96.5% and accuracy 93.7% with AI augmentation; expert interrater kappa 0.8; median scan time 7 minutes

records.title: MRI Radiogenomics of Pediatric Medulloblastoma: A Multicenter Study.

records.headline_result: AUC 0.86 (viral), 0.88 (bacterial), 0.93 (mycoplasma) on the test cohort

records.title: Automatic detection of pneumonia in chest X-ray images using textural features.
records.model_family: three texture characterisation methods - radiomics, fractal dimension and superpixel-based histon - each feeding k-nearest neighbors, support vector machine and random forest classifiers

records.model_description: A comparison of handcrafted texture descriptors rather than an end-to-end network, which makes the features inspectable - and the superpixel-based histon, the newest of the three, performed best on the pediatric dataset. The performance gap between the two datasets (83-91% pediatric versus 95-99% COVID repository) is a reminder that accuracy figures in this literature track dataset difficulty more than method quality.
records.headline_result: on the paediatric dataset, accuracy 83.3% (radiomics), 89.9% (fractal dimension) and 91.3% (superpixel-based histon), with sensitivities of 89-93.6%

records.title: MRI-radiomics-clinical-based nomogram for prenatal prediction of the placenta accreta spectrum disorders.
records.model_family: radiomics signature combined with clinical nomogram
records.clinical_problem: prenatal prediction of placenta accreta spectrum disorders using MRI radiomics combined with clinical data
records.patient_population: 271 pregnant women (156 with pathology-proven placenta accreta spectrum, 115 without), across training (n=133), internal validation (n=57) and external validation (n=81) cohorts from two centers
records.model_description: Input is T2-weighted pelvic MRI plus prenatal clinical features; radiomic features are extracted and combined with MRI morphological findings and clinical data into a nomogram that outputs the predicted probability of placenta accreta spectrum disorder.
records.dataset_size: 271 pregnant women (156 PAS, 115 non-PAS) across three cohorts from two centers
