records.title: Predicting age and clinical risk from the neonatal connectome.
records.model_family: deep neural networks and random forests on structural connectome features, with sensitivity analysis for feature relevance
records.clinical_problem: whether the neonatal structural connectome carries a signal about later neurodevelopment, and whether a maturation index derived from it identifies preterm infants at risk
records.patient_population: 524 babies from the developing Human Connectome Project, term and preterm, scanned at term equivalent age, with motor outcome at 18 months corrected age
records.model_description: The age prediction is the instrument, not the point. Having learned what a term-born brain's maturity looks like at a given postmenstrual age, the model is applied to preterm infants and the residual - predicted minus actual age - becomes a maturation index, which correlated with motor outcome at 18 months. That last step is what separates this from the normative brain-age literature: the deviation is tied to a clinical endpoint in the children it would be used on. Feature relevance localized to frontal and temporal regions, thalami and basal ganglia.
records.headline_result: postmenstrual age at scan predicted with mean absolute error 0.72 weeks (r = 0.83) and gestational age at birth with 2.21 weeks (r = 0.82); the derived maturation index correlated significantly with motor outcome at 18 months corrected age

records.title: A pediatric wrist trauma X-ray dataset (GRAZPEDWRI-DX) for machine learning.
records.clinical_problem: the absence of an annotated public pediatric fracture dataset, which is what keeps most fracture AI adult-trained
records.patient_population: 6,091 children treated for wrist trauma at one pediatric surgery department between 2008 and 2018
records.model_description: A public dataset rather than a model, and arguably worth more than another classifier: 20,327 de-identified pediatric wrist radiographs across 10,643 studies, annotated by pediatric radiologists with lines, boxes and polygons marking fractures and periosteal reactions, plus age and sex. Given that children are under 1% of public medical imaging data, a dataset of this size in the commonest pediatric fracture is a substantive contribution.
records.release_evidence: this dataset is publicly available to encourage computer vision research
records.dataset_size: 20,327 images from 10,643 studies of 6,091 patients, with 74,459 tags and 67,771 labeled objects

records.title: A Fetal Brain magnetic resonance Acquisition Numerical phantom (FaBiAN).

records.title: Structural differences in adolescent brains can predict alcohol misuse.
records.model_family: support vector machines with RBF kernel and gradient boosting compared against linear models, on T1-weighted and diffusion features
records.clinical_problem: whether structural brain differences precede adolescent alcohol misuse rather than resulting from it, and whether they can identify at-risk adolescents before the behavior
records.patient_population: approximately 1182 adolescents from the IMAGEN dataset, imaged at ages 14, 19 and 22, with ten alcohol misuse phenotypes assessed at 22
records.model_description: The temporal design carries the argument: MRI at 14 predicts alcohol misuse at 22, so the structural differences are present before the drinking rather than after it. Ten phenotypes are predicted rather than one, and the paper reports which was most predictable (binge drinking) instead of picking the best and calling it the result. It is also candid about the methodology as a finding in itself - the choice of phenotype, model and confound correction each changed the answer materially, which is a caution for the whole field of small-effect psychiatric imaging.
records.headline_result: 73-78% accuracy predicting adolescent alcohol misuse at age 22 from brain structure, with the most informative features in ventricular CSF, corpus callosum, internal capsule and brain stem

records.title: Clinical parameters combined with radiomics features of PET/CT can predict recurrence in patients with high-risk pediatric neuroblastoma.
records.model_family: LASSO-selected PET/CT radiomics score combined with independent clinical risk factors in a nomogram
records.clinical_problem: predicting recurrence in high-risk pediatric neuroblastoma, so that follow-up intensity and management can be matched to the individual child's risk
records.patient_population: 84 high-risk pediatric neuroblastoma patients split 3:2 into training and test sets
records.model_description: Built within an already high-risk group, where the clinical variables have largely exhausted their discriminating power - which is why the radiomics score alone beat the clinical model and the combination beat both. Decision curve analysis shows net benefit rather than only AUC. Eighty-four patients across two sets is small for a seven-feature radiomics signature, and the confidence intervals reflect that.
records.headline_result: combined model AUC 0.889 training and 0.892 test, versus 0.813/0.869 for radiomics alone and 0.744/0.750 for the clinical model

records.title: Automated 3D reconstruction of the fetal thorax in the standard atlas space from motion-corrupted MRI stacks for 21-36 weeks GA range.
records.model_family: 3D CNN localisation and landmark-guided pose estimation feeding automated deformable slice-to-volume registration
records.clinical_problem: reconstructing a high-resolution 3D fetal trunk volume from motion-corrupted T2-weighted stacks, which is what makes detailed assessment of body anomalies including congenital heart defects possible
records.patient_population: T2-weighted fetal MRI datasets across the 21-36 week gestational age range
records.model_description: Extends to the trunk what had only been solved for the fetal brain. Two specific failures are targeted: existing trunk pipelines need manual input, and gradient-descent registration has too narrow a capture range for the severe motion typical at early gestational age. A 3D localisation network plus landmark-based pose estimation replaces both, and an outlier-rejection step throws out stacks ruined by motion or poor quality without a human deciding. The result lands in standard radiological space regardless of how the fetus is lying.
records.headline_result: fully automated deformable slice-to-volume reconstruction of the fetal thorax in the standard atlas space across 21-36 weeks, independent of fetal trunk position or stack coverage

records.title: Artificial intelligence for radiological paediatric fracture assessment: a systematic review.
records.clinical_problem: how well AI actually detects fractures in children, given that development has concentrated on adults

records.model_description: A systematic review with a pointed premise: missed fractures carry greater long-term clinical and medicolegal consequence in children than in adults, yet almost all research and commercial effort has been on adults. Only nine studies qualified. Nearly all used single-institution data and only two performed external validation, so the reported accuracies of 89 to 98 percent cannot be assumed to generalize. Its recommendation is multicentre real-world evaluation.
records.headline_result: reported AI accuracies 88.8-97.9%; only 2 of 9 studies performed external validation, and AI sensitivity exceeded human readers non-significantly in 2 of 3 comparative studies

records.title: Comparison of a Deep Learning-Based Reconstruction Algorithm with Filtered Back Projection and Iterative Reconstruction Algorithms for Pediatric Abdominopelvic CT.
records.model_family: vendor deep learning CT reconstruction at low, medium and high strength, compared against filtered back projection and hybrid iterative reconstruction
records.clinical_problem: image quality in pediatric abdominopelvic CT, where hybrid iterative reconstruction reduces noise but degrades spatial resolution and produces an unnatural noise texture
records.patient_population: 120 pediatric patients (mean age 8.7 +/- 5.2 years, 60 male) who had post-contrast abdominopelvic CT between May and October 2020
records.model_description: A physics-first comparison of six reconstructions of the same scans: noise power spectrum for noise magnitude and texture, edge rise distance for spatial resolution, then two pediatric radiologists reading blind. The result that matters is the trade-off it exposes - full-strength iterative reconstruction achieves lower noise magnitude than the network, but at a lower noise frequency and longer edge rise distance, meaning blotchier images with softer edges. Deep learning reconstruction gave better resolution and a more natural texture at comparable noise.
records.release_evidence: TrueFidelity, a commercial deep learning reconstruction algorithm on the clinical CT scanner, compared against the scanner's ASiR-V and filtered back projection
records.headline_result: deep learning reconstruction gave higher average noise spatial frequency and shorter edge rise distance than iterative reconstruction (p < 0.001), with better overall image quality on blinded review

records.title: Multi-site harmonization of MRI data uncovers machine-learning discrimination capability in barely separable populations: An example from the ABIDE dataset.
records.model_family: random forest classifier on brain structural features, with and without a multi-site harmonization protocol
records.clinical_problem: whether the failure of structural MRI to separate autism from typical development is biological or technical - that is, whether the batch effect of multi-site data collection is masking a real signal
records.patient_population: the ABIDE multi-site collection spanning a wide age range, analyzed overall and in child, adolescent and adult subgroups
records.model_description: The most useful kind of negative-adjacent result. Harmonizing across sites lifts autism-versus-control discrimination from an AUC of 0.58 - indistinguishable from chance - to 0.67, which is significant but still low. The honest conclusion is both that batch effects were hiding a real signal and that the signal, once uncovered, is small. Age-stratified results (0.62 children, 0.65 adolescents, 0.69 adults) and consistent anatomical patterns per subgroup make it more informative than a single pooled number.
records.headline_result: AUC rose from 0.58 +/- 0.04 to 0.67 +/- 0.03 after harmonization, with age-specific AUCs of 0.62 (children), 0.65 (adolescents) and 0.69 (adults)
records.study_design: retrospective model development on a public dataset

records.title: Comparison of Transfer Learning Models in Pelvic Tilt and Rotation Measurement in Pediatric Anteroposterior Pelvic Radiographs.

records.patient_population: 30 of 92 children who underwent 3D hip CT, used to generate digitally reconstructed radiographs

Excluding cardiomegaly and children under two lifted accuracy from 87.5% to 96.9%, which locates the failure precisely: the youngest children and the finding most dependent on age-specific normal anatomy. The conclusion, that these tools need validation in younger children, is the practical one.

records.title: Clinical workflow of sonographers performing fetal anomaly ultrasound scans: deep-learning-based analysis.
records.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
records.model_family: deep learning annotation model labelling scan events into 11 anatomical classes, applied to full-length ultrasound video
records.clinical_problem: what sonographers actually do during a second-trimester anomaly scan - guidelines fix which planes must be stored but not the order, and the resulting workflow has never been characterized
records.patient_population: 496 anomaly scans performed by 14 sonographers, recorded in full and segmented at automatically detected image freeze and save events
records.model_description: The clever part of the design is using the machine's own freeze and save events to mark where the interesting moments are, then only labelling the video around them - which is what makes 496 full-length scans tractable. The result is a genuine finding rather than a metric: no two anomaly scans in the entire series shared the same acquisition sequence, and transitions of three or more structures in a row were rare, which suggests sonographers work opportunistically around fetal position rather than following a route. That has direct consequences for anyone designing an automated or guided scan.
records.headline_result: the five UK-mandated views were detected in 86-97% of scans; scans most often began with head/brain (24.4%), spine (23.2%) or thorax/heart (22.8%), and no two scans shared an identical sequence
records.study_design: prospective observational study with retrospective video analysis

records.title: Deep Learning to Predict Neonatal and Infant Brain Age from Myelination on Brain MRI Scans.
records.model_family: three-dimensional regression convolutional neural network with layer-wise relevance propagation attention maps
records.clinical_problem: judging whether an infant's myelination is appropriate for age, which today means a radiologist visually inspecting T1 and T2 images against remembered milestones and comparing to gestationally corrected age
records.patient_population: 518 neonates and infants aged 0-25 months with reported normal myelination scanned at one academic center between January 1995 and June 2019 (mean gestationally corrected age 67 weeks +/- 33), with an external test set from the National Institutes of Health
records.model_description: Automates an assessment that is already part of every pediatric brain MRI report, rather than inventing a new biomarker - the output is the age the brain looks like, which is exactly what the radiologist is estimating by eye. The attention maps are the convincing part: the network attended to cerebellum, posterior white matter and basal ganglia in the youngest infants and to anterior white matter in the oldest, which is the known caudal-to-rostral, posterior-to-anterior order of myelination. Combining T1 and T2 beat either alone, and it held up on an external NIH set.
records.headline_result: mean absolute error 9.8 +/- 2.3 weeks (T1), 9.1 +/- 1.9 (T2) and 7.7 +/- 1.7 (both) internally; 9.1 weeks on the external NIH test set
records.study_design: retrospective model development with external validation

Both were checked, and the quantitative agreement was tight (tissue values within 0.5%, volumetry within about 1.5%), with lesion detectability unchanged.

records.headline_result: 42% scan time reduction with significantly improved image quality for all contrast weightings (P < .001), no significant difference in lesion detectability, tissue value differences under 0.5% and volumetry differences of -1.46% to 0.83%

records.model_description: Two deliverables in one paper, and the second is the interesting one. The first is a curated, preprocessed, analysis-ready pediatric diffusion MRI resource in BIDS format, openly released. The second is a way of scaling quality control: a small expert-scored subset plus a much larger set scored by community scientists trains a network that agrees with experts on held-out data, and an interpretability check confirms it keys on features that actually bear on quality. That paradigm - crowdsource the bulk, anchor with experts, learn the rest - transfers to any large pediatric imaging cohort.

records.model_description: Designed backwards from the deployment constraint rather than from the dataset. Six freehand sweeps replace the standard examination, so the operator needs no plane-finding skill; the model runs on an Android phone in under three seconds with no internet; and the accuracy claim is a formal non-inferiority test against standard biometry rather than a correlation. The most consequential result is that non-inferiority held when novices performed only two of the six sweep types, which is a statement about how little training the pathway actually requires.

records.headline_result: gestational age non-inferior to standard biometry (error difference -1.4 +/- 4.5 days, 95% CI -1.8 to -0.9); malpresentation AUC-ROC 0.977 (95% CI 0.949-1.00); under 3 s on-device

records.model_description: Pushes the question back about six years from where dyslexia is normally identified, to infants who cannot yet speak let alone read. The classification accuracy is barely above chance (0.55) and the authors report it that way, leaning on the effect size and on which connections drove it - the left fusiform gyrus, the region that later becomes the visual word form area, connected to frontal and parietal language networks. That anatomical coherence is the finding; the classifier is the instrument. Longitudinal follow-up to school-age reading is acknowledged as the necessary next step.

records.title: AI Estimation of Gestational Age from Blind Ultrasound Sweeps in Low-Resource Settings.

This is one of the clearest demonstrations in the corpus that AI can move an imaging capability to where the expertise is not.
records.headline_result: mean absolute error 3.9 days for the model versus 4.7 days for standard biometry (P < 0.001); 4.9 versus 5.4 days for sweeps collected by untrained users on low-cost devices

records.title: Deep Learning for Synthetic CT from Bone MRI in the Head and Neck.

records.clinical_problem: generating CT-equivalent images from bone MRI so that cortical bone can be visualized and processed without ionizing radiation - which matters most in the head and neck of children
records.patient_population: 39 pediatric and adult patients with both bone MRI and CT of the head and neck, four-fold cross-validation
records.model_description: The smaller network beat the larger one, which is worth noting for anyone assuming capacity is the constraint at 39 patients. The loss function choice is presented as a clinical trade rather than a technical detail: mean absolute error gives higher bone precision, mean squared error higher recall, and which you want depends on whether a missed or a hallucinated bone edge is worse downstream. Generalizability was tested by training and validating across hospitals, vendors and MRI techniques, and augmenting local data with outside data helped.
records.headline_result: Light_U-Net outperformed the VGG-16 models on Pearson correlation, error and bone precision/recall, with performance improving when local training data were augmented with data from other hospitals, vendors or MRI techniques

records.title: SVoRT: Iterative Transformer for Slice-to-Volume Registration in Fetal Brain MRI
records.model_family: iterative transformer modelling multiple stacks of MR slices as a sequence, trained on synthetically transformed data, alternating volume estimation with transformation updates
records.clinical_problem: volumetric reconstruction of the fetal brain from multiple stacks of motion-corrupted slices, which is highly sensitive to how the slice-to-volume transformations are initialized
records.patient_population: synthetic data for training and evaluation, with real-world fetal MRI for demonstration
records.model_description: Treats the stacks as a sequence and lets attention decide which slices inform which - so a slice whose own content is ambiguous can be placed using its neighbours, which is the situation that defeats pairwise registration under severe motion. Alternating between estimating the underlying volume and updating the transformations means the two problems bootstrap each other rather than one being solved first. Training on synthetic transformations sidesteps the absence of ground-truth motion in real data.
records.headline_result: lower registration error and better reconstruction quality than existing state-of-the-art methods on synthetic data, with improved 3D reconstruction under severe fetal motion on real MRI

records.patient_population: 548 fetal lung ultrasound images at the four-chamber view from 548 women delivering July 2018 to August 2019 at one hospital: 108 gestational diabetes, 71 pre-eclampsia, 25 both, 344 normal; imaged between 28 and 41 weeks

records.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology

It beat the standard nuchal-translucency-plus-maternal-age model decisively (0.979 versus a substantially lower AUC, P < 0.001), and the nomogram makes the output a patient-specific probability rather than a screen-positive flag.
records.headline_result: AUC 0.983 training, 0.979 validation and 0.997 retest, significantly higher than the nuchal translucency plus maternal age model (P < 0.001)

records.title: A regression framework to head-circumference delineation from US fetal images.
records.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine

records.title: Deep learning-based method for reducing residual motion effects in diffusion parameter estimation.

records.title: Predicting brain age with complex networks: From adolescence to adulthood.

records.title: Deep Relational Reasoning for the Prediction of Language Impairment and Postoperative Seizure Outcome Using Preoperative DWI Connectome Data of Children With Focal Epilepsy.

records.model_description: Preoperative diffusion-weighted imaging is used to build whole-brain structural connectomes. A 'dilated CNN + RN' model (a dilated convolutional network combined with a relation network) reasons about sparsely distributed axonal-connection dependencies to predict expressive and receptive language-impairment scores and to classify postoperative seizure outcome (freedom vs. recurrence) in children with focal epilepsy. records.title: Integration of brain and behavior measures for identification of data-driven groups cutting across children with ASD, ADHD, or OCD.

records.model_family: similarity network fusion across imaging and behavioral measures

records.patient_population: 176 children aged 6-16 with autism, ADHD or OCD from the POND network, all scanned on the same 3T scanner
records.model_description: Fuses cortical thickness, subcortical volume, white matter anisotropy and behavioral measures into a single similarity structure, then finds groups that cut across the three diagnoses. Scanning all children on one scanner removes the usual site confound.
records.headline_result: four transdiagnostic groups driven mainly by cortical thickness in socio-emotional and attention networks plus inattention symptoms; groups remained stable across resampling and differed significantly in adaptive functioning

records.title: Artificial intelligence for automatic cerebral ventricle segmentation and volume calculation: a clinical tool for the evaluation of pediatric hydrocephalus.

records.title: Deep learning prediction of proton and photon dose distributions for paediatric abdominal tumours.

records.title: Emergence and organization of adult brain function throughout child development.

records.title: Diagnostic Performance of a New Convolutional Neural Network Algorithm for Detecting Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip on Anteroposterior Radiographs.
records.model_family: convolutional neural network on cropped unilateral hip joint images
records.clinical_problem: detecting developmental dysplasia of the hip on anteroposterior pelvic radiographs, the study most often available outside a pediatric centre and the one most often read by someone without pediatric training
records.patient_population: 2601 hip AP radiographs yielding 5076 cropped unilateral hip joint images, split 80/10/10, labeled normal or DDH by three radiologists
records.model_description: The comparison is stratified by reader experience, and the result is the one that recurs across pediatric AI: the algorithm was statistically indistinguishable from the radiologist with pediatric experience and clearly better than the one without. Reporting the precision-recall curve alongside the ROC is the right choice for a screening problem with few positives, and it is where the gap between the model (0.973) and the weakest reader (0.618) is starkest.
records.headline_result: ROC AUC 0.988 and PRC AUC 0.973 for the algorithm versus 0.988-0.919 and 0.618-0.958 for radiologists; sensitivity 98.0%, specificity 98.1%, NPV 99.8%; no significant difference from the pediatric-experienced radiologist (p = 0.180) but significantly better than the inexperienced one (p < 0.001)

records.title: A Deep Attentive Convolutional Neural Network for Automatic Cortical Plate Segmentation in Fetal MRI.
records.model_family: fully convolutional network with deep attentive modules, mixed kernel convolutions, deep supervision and residual connections

records.title: A deep learning framework for 18F-FDG PET imaging diagnosis in pediatric patients with temporal lobe epilepsy.

records.title: Image processing and machine learning for telehealth craniosynostosis screening in newborns.
records.model_family: image processing and machine learning cranial shape classification software
records.clinical_problem: screening newborns for nonsyndromic craniosynostosis remotely, so that the diagnosis is not missed for want of access to a craniofacial specialist, an optical scanner or a CT
records.patient_population: 351 acceptable image sets from open-source (n = 40) and retrospectively collected newborn top-down cranial images with or without facial views (n = 339), collected April 2008 to February 2020, compared against blinded craniofacial specialists
records.model_description: Explicitly positioned as a substitute for CT-based and optical-scanner craniometrics in the screening step - which in this condition means avoiding a head CT in an infant. Two things are validated separately: the categorical call against blinded specialists, which was strong, and agreement with optical craniometry, which was excellent for cephalic index but only moderate for cranial vault asymmetry. The stated destination is a phone app usable in primary care or by telemedicine.
records.headline_result: accuracy 93.3% (95% CI 86.8-98.8), sensitivity 92.0%, specificity 94.3%; intraclass correlation with optical craniometry 0.95 for cephalic index and 0.67 for cranial vault asymmetry index

records.study_design: Retrospective single-center model development and validation study

records.title: Brain MRI radiomics analysis may predict poor psychomotor outcome in preterm neonates.
records.model_family: 1906 radiomic features from T1- and T2-weighted white matter, reduced by minimum redundancy maximum relevance, with eightfold cross-validation
records.clinical_problem: predicting poor psychomotor development in preterm neonates from the term-equivalent brain MRI they already receive
records.patient_population: 46 prospectively enrolled preterm neonates (median gestational age 29 weeks, 26 male) scanned at median 37 weeks corrected age, assessed at 12 months corrected age; 13 of 46 had poor outcome
records.model_description: The headline finding is what the radiomics saw that the radiologists did not: 45 of 46 neonates had no significant white matter injury on visual assessment, yet texture analysis of that apparently normal white matter predicted psychomotor outcome at an AUC of 0.925. Adding gestational age or diffusion parameters did not improve it. Forty-six neonates with 13 events is small and the model is cross-validated rather than externally tested, so the effect size should be treated as provisional - but the premise, that the injury is subvisual, is the interesting claim.
records.headline_result: AUC 0.925 from T1-weighted, 0.834 from T2-weighted and 0.902 from both, with sensitivity 84.6% and specificity 78.8%, despite 45 of 46 scans showing no significant white matter injury on visual assessment

records.title: Machine learning analysis of pregnancy data enables early identification of a subpopulation of newborns with ASD.

records.study_design: prospective five-year longitudinal cohort study with machine learning prediction

records.title: S3Reg: Superfast Spherical Surface Registration Based on Deep Learning.
records.model_family: end-to-end unsupervised spherical convolutional network learning deformation fields, with scaling-and-squaring diffeomorphic layers and three orthogonal Spherical U-Nets
records.clinical_problem: cortical surface registration, the prerequisite for any surface-based analysis and for establishing longitudinal correspondence in a brain that is changing shape
records.patient_population: two datasets covering adult and infant multimodal cortical features
records.model_description: Infant cortical surfaces are the hard case for registration because the cortex folds rapidly between scans, so longitudinal correspondence is exactly what fails. Learning the deformation directly on the sphere - with a topology-preserving diffeomorphic construction and three orthogonal U-Nets to handle polar distortion - keeps the guarantee that conventional methods provide while cutting the time from a minute to ten seconds, which is what makes large infant cohorts processable.
records.headline_result: superior or comparable performance to state-of-the-art registration methods while reducing registration time from about 1 minute to 10 seconds

records.title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging Findings Are Associated with Long-Term Global Neurological Function or Death after Traumatic Brain Injury in Critically Ill Children.
records.model_family: Random Forest (nonlinear) and linear modeling of MRI features
records.clinical_problem: predicting long-term neurological function or death after traumatic brain injury in critically ill children
records.patient_population: 42 critically ill children with TBI, prospectively recruited from 5 Canadian pediatric ICUs
records.model_description: Random Forest modeling identifies which subacute-phase MRI features (herniation, diffuse axonal injury location, contusion) most predict long-term global neurological outcome or death after pediatric TBI, combined with an MRI composite score in linear outcome models.
records.headline_result: an MRI composite score significantly improved prediction of favorable vs. unfavorable long-term outcome

records.title: A novel ultrasound-based approach to investigate extramedullary haematopoiesis in foetal spleen.
records.clinical_problem: Quantifying fetal splenic echogenicity change across gestation as a marker of extramedullary hematopoiesis
records.patient_population: 80 pregnant women (fetal spleens imaged), Mid-Pregnancy (19-23wk) vs End-Pregnancy (37-41wk)
records.model_description: A clustering-segmentation pipeline applied to fetal spleen ultrasound images that derives two new radiomic parameters (Dark Ratio and Light Ratio) reflecting splenic echogenicity, used to track hematopoiesis across gestation.
records.headline_result: Dark Ratio differed significantly between mid- and end-pregnancy (0.0631 vs 0.0483, P=0.014)

records.title: T2* placental MRI in pregnancies complicated with fetal congenital heart disease.
records.exclusion_reason: placental T2* relaxometry in 69 pregnancies with fetal congenital heart disease versus 37 controls, with Gaussian process regression used to build a gestation-matched normative reference; an imaging physiology study rather than a diagnostic or predictive model

records.title: Localization and Diagnosis of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder.
records.clinical_problem: Classify and localize ADHD-related brain regions in children using structural MRI
records.patient_population: ADHD-200 public dataset (NYU, KKI, and full datasets)
records.model_description: Takes 3D MRI volumes sliced into orthogonal 2D slices as input vectors; a random forest classifier trained per slice position/direction, with predictions intersected across three directions to classify ADHD and localize discriminative brain regions.
records.headline_result: More accurate identification of ADHD than comparison methods; a new suspected region identified (exact figures not given)

records.title: Robust Cortical Thickness Morphometry of Neonatal Brain and Systematic Evaluation Using Multi-Site MRI Datasets.
records.model_family: deep neural network tissue segmentation inside a cortical surface reconstruction pipeline, with edge-gradient CSF/GM boundary detection and sulcal skeletonization
records.clinical_problem: measuring cortical thickness in neonates, where small brains, large partial volume effects and sulci too narrow to show CSF defeat surface extraction methods built for adults
records.patient_population: three independent datasets comprising 736 pre-term and 97 term neonates
records.model_description: Notable for working from T1 alone, since the established neonatal pipelines assume T2 and many clinical or research protocols have only T1. The validation is unusually complete: qualitative rating of every surface, landmark displacement below one voxel, three sites, and a biological sanity check - measured thickness rose from 1.3 mm at 28 weeks to 1.8 mm at term, with cingulate growing fastest. A direct comparison against the T2-based dHCP pipeline is reported as inconclusive rather than spun. Publicly available through CBRAIN.
records.release_evidence: NEOCIVET 2.0 has been open to the public through CBRAIN, a web-based platform for processing brain imaging data
records.headline_result: 86.9% of reconstructed surfaces rated accurate across three sites, with mean landmark displacement 0.532 +/- 0.035 mm - less than a voxel
records.study_design: retrospective methods development with multi-site evaluation

records.title: Machine Learning-Based Multiparametric Magnetic Resonance Imaging Radiomics for Prediction of H3K27M Mutation in Midline Gliomas.
records.model_family: extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) over 651 radiomic features per MRI sequence, with feature selection
records.clinical_problem: predicting H3K27M mutation status in midline gliomas non-invasively, a molecular marker with prognostic weight that conventional MRI features do not distinguish
records.patient_population: 109 patients from three academic centers, 60 of them pediatric (55%); 50 H3K27M-mutant and 59 wild-type
records.model_description: A radiogenomics model for a tumor - diffuse midline glioma - where tissue is often not obtainable and the mutation defines the entity. The motivation is stated as a negative result from the prior literature: enhancement, necrosis and edema rates vary and none separates mutant from wild-type, so the signal, if there is one, is in texture rather than in anything a radiologist reports. Multi-institutional, majority pediatric, but a single random split of 109 patients and test performance below training, so the estimate is fragile.
records.headline_result: AUC 0.791 training and 0.737 test; test accuracy 72.7%, precision 76.5%, recall 72.2%, F1 74.3%

records.title: Machine Learning Predicts the 3D Outcomes of Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis Surgery Using Patient-Surgeon Specific Parameters.
records.model_family: ensemble learner over preoperative radiographic, clinical and surgical parameters
records.clinical_problem: predicting the three-dimensional spinal alignment two years after posterior spinal fusion for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, when current surgical guidelines are based on a two-dimensional classification of the curve
records.patient_population: 371 adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients who underwent posterior spinal fusion with two-year follow-up, multicenter, with prospectively collected radiographic, clinical and surgical data
records.model_description: The design separates what the patient brings from what the surgeon chooses, and quantifies each: preoperative factors alone predicted the outcome cluster at 64%, rising to 75% when the surgical decisions were added. Among the surgical predictors, the identity of the operating surgeon was itself important - and the paper says for which preoperative ranges that mattered, which is a candid and unusual thing to report. Aimed at setting expectations before surgery rather than at automating a measurement.
records.headline_result: 75% accuracy predicting three clusters of 3D surgical outcome using preoperative plus surgical factors, falling to 64% with preoperative factors alone

records.title: Fundamentals of the Development of Connectivity in the Human Fetal Brain in Late Gestation: From 24 Weeks Gestational Age to Term.

records.clinical_problem: differentiating spastic muscles in cerebral palsy from healthy muscle using MRI fat fraction and texture analysis
records.patient_population: 9 children with cerebral palsy (age 8-15) and 12 healthy controls (age 9-16)
records.model_description: Input: multi-echo Dixon MRI fat-fraction images of calf muscles with radiomics texture features; output: combined radiomics and fat-fraction model distinguishing cerebral-palsy-affected muscle from healthy muscle.
records.headline_result: combined model AUC 0.95/0.93/0.83 for the three muscles, better than radiomics or fat-fraction alone

records.title: Using deep learning and natural language processing models to detect child physical abuse.
records.model_family: deep learning on clinical features, extended with a fine-tuned BERT natural language processing model over radiology report text
records.clinical_problem: recognizing child physical abuse, which is difficult, usually needs a multidisciplinary assessment, and is subject to bias in who gets investigated
records.patient_population: 1312 children from a level 1 pediatric trauma centre registry, January 2010 to January 2020, of whom 737 (56.2%) were abused; matched non-abusive trauma controls
records.model_description: The design isolates what the imaging adds: Model 1 uses demographics, vital signs and laboratory values, and Model 2 adds the text of head CT, brain MRI and skeletal survey reports through BERT. Adding the reports lifted accuracy from 86% to 93% and positive predictive value to 96%, which quantifies how much of the abuse signal lives in the radiologist's words. The authors note most individual features correlated weakly with abuse, so the model is finding combinations rather than any single red flag. Intended to run live in the record and prompt the clinician.
records.headline_result: accuracy 86.3% and AUC 0.86 for the clinical model versus 93.4% and AUC 0.94 for the NLP model adding radiology report text, with PPV rising from 88.7% to 95.9%

records.title: Differences in subcortico-cortical interactions identified from connectome and microcircuit models in autism.

records.model_description: Structural connectome and microcircuit simulation features derived from MRI go in; supervised machine learning outputs an association with Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule symptom severity scores.

records.headline_result: macroscale connectome perturbations significantly associated with ADOS symptom severity scores

records.study_design: Study protocol for a multicenter cross-sectional study (model not yet developed/reported)

records.title: Deep learning model for predicting gestational age after the first trimester using fetal MRI.
records.model_family: deep learning regression on T2-weighted fetal brain MRI
records.clinical_problem: estimating gestational age after the first trimester, where ultrasound dating loses accuracy as pregnancy advances and some pregnancies were never dated early
records.patient_population: 184 T2-weighted fetal MRI acquisitions from 184 fetuses (mean gestational age 29.4 weeks) scanned January 2014 to June 2019, split 126 training, 29 validation and 29 test; reference standard from last menstruation and first-trimester ultrasound
records.model_description: The comparator is the right one - biparietal diameter measured on the same MRI - and the useful number is not the correlation but the spread: the model's upper limit of agreement was 2.45 weeks against 5.62 weeks for biparietal diameter, so the worst-case error is less than half. Both methods drifted with advancing gestation, which is the expected behaviour and worth knowing. Twenty-nine test cases is small.
records.headline_result: concordance correlation 0.964 for the model versus 0.920 for biparietal diameter, with upper limit of agreement 2.45 weeks versus 5.62 weeks

records.patient_population: children aged 1-5 years
records.model_description: Pediatric chest X-rays are classified as pneumonia or normal by four pretrained convolutional neural networks (VGG19, DenseNet121, Xception, ResNet50) fine-tuned via transfer learning; performance is compared across models using accuracy, sensitivity, precision, AUC and F1 score.

records.title: Multimodal brain predictors of current weight and weight gain in children enrolled in the ABCD study ®.
records.model_family: cross-validated elastic-net regression on multimodal imaging features
records.clinical_problem: identifying which 9-10 year olds will gain weight pathologically over the following year
records.patient_population: children aged 9-10 in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study
records.model_description: Uses structural, diffusion, resting-state and task-based MRI to model current body mass index and, separately, to predict pathological weight gain a year later. Structural features generalized to held-out data and predicted future pathological gain; functional and reward-task measures did not. The practical reading is that the cheap, routinely acquired structural sequence carried the signal and the elaborate functional paradigms did not.
records.headline_result: structural features explained 27% of held-out variance in body mass index and predicted pathological weight gain with area under the curve 0.83 in both training and test sets

records.title: Ultra-low-dose lung multidetector computed tomography in children - Approaching 0.2 millisievert.

records.patient_population: 23 size-matched pediatric patients per scanner (46 total), age 2-18 years

records.title: An automated framework for image classification and segmentation of fetal ultrasound images for gestational age estimation.
records.journal: Proceedings of SPIE--the International Society for Optical Engineering

records.dataset_size: not stated (large database of annotated obstetric US images)

records.title: Preoperative Assessment for Event-Free Survival With Hepatoblastoma in Pediatric Patients by Developing a CT-Based Radiomics Model.
records.clinical_problem: Can CT radiomics, before surgery, predict event-free survival in children with hepatoblastoma, to help inform treatment planning?

records.model_description: A radiomics signature, extracted from pretreatment portal-venous-phase CT and combined via LASSO Cox regression with clinicopathologic risk factors, produces a nomogram predicting event-free survival after hepatoblastoma treatment.
records.headline_result: Combined radiomics-clinicopathologic nomogram C-index 0.88 (95% CI 0.829-0.933), improved over the clinicopathologic model alone (C-index 0.81 vs 0.85 reported for radiomics vs clinical)
records.study_design: retrospective two-institution radiomics model development with external validation

records.title: Automated Segmentation of Abdominal Skeletal Muscle on Pediatric CT Scans Using Deep Learning.
records.model_family: paired U-Net models for level localization and muscle segmentation
records.clinical_problem: measuring skeletal muscle mass on CT, a marker of nutritional status and sarcopenia, which requires finding the L3 level and outlining muscle by hand
records.patient_population: 370 patients sampled uniformly from 0 to 18 years and across both sexes
records.model_description: Two problems in one pipeline: locating the L3 vertebral level on the sagittal reformat, then segmenting muscle on the corresponding axial slice. Sampling uniformly across ages from birth to 18 is the design choice that makes it pediatric rather than adult-with-children-included, since body habitus changes completely over that range. Level localization landed within the slice thickness.
records.headline_result: L3 localization error 3.23 ± 2.61 mm, within the reconstructed slice thickness; muscle segmentation Dice 0.93 ± 0.03

records.title: Deep reasoning neural network analysis to predict language deficits from psychometry-driven DWI connectome of young children with persistent language concerns.
records.model_family: dilated CNN combined with relational network (dilated CNN + RN)
records.clinical_problem: Can deep learning analysis of diffusion tractography connectome data, combined with psychometric data, predict expressive and receptive language scores in young children with persistent language concerns?

records.title: Performance evaluation of a deep learning image reconstruction (DLIR) algorithm in "double low" chest CTA in children: a feasibility study.
records.model_family: vendor deep learning CT reconstruction algorithm, high setting (DLIR-H)
records.clinical_problem: cutting both radiation and iodinated contrast dose in pediatric chest CT angiography, where iterative reconstruction runs out of headroom at low dose and 100 kVp gives too little enhancement at low contrast dose
records.patient_population: 46 children (mean age 5.9 +/- 4.2 years) scanned at 70 kVp with 0.8-1.2 ml/kg contrast, versus 46 age-matched controls at 100 kVp with 1.3-1.8 ml/kg
records.model_description: The clearest pediatric statement of what deep learning reconstruction actually buys: it is spent on lowering two doses at once. records.journal: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
records.model_family: automated analysis of fetal brain morphology on the standard transthalamic axial plane
records.clinical_problem: dating a pregnancy in the second and third trimesters where first-trimester crown-rump length was never obtained, which is the norm in settings with late booking or infrequent antenatal care

records.title: Deep learning-based parameter estimation in fetal diffusion-weighted MRI.
