records.title: Longitudinal Prediction of Infant MR Images With Multi-Contrast Perceptual Adversarial Learning.
records.clinical_problem: imputing missing longitudinal MRI scans in infants to complete developmental trajectory studies
records.patient_population: infants in the first year of life with longitudinal MRI (sample size not stated)
records.model_description: A 3D multi-contrast perceptual adversarial network (MPGAN) takes an infant's T1w/T2w MRI at one time point as input and predicts/imputes the structural MRI appearance at a different developmental time point using voxel-wise and perceptual losses.
records.headline_result: Imputed images improved downstream regression and classification task performance (no single accuracy figure reported)

records.title: Visual Explanation for Identification of the Brain Bases for Developmental Dyslexia on fMRI Data.
records.clinical_problem: classifying developmental dyslexia from functional MRI and visualizing the brain regions driving classification
records.patient_population: children diagnosed with developmental dyslexia and typical readers (sample size not stated)
records.model_description: A convolutional neural network classifies subjects as dyslexic or typical readers from functional brain imaging features, with network-visualization techniques used to generate interpretable maps of discriminative brain regions.
records.headline_result: 94.8% classification accuracy for developmental dyslexia
records.study_design: retrospective classification study with model-interpretability analysis

records.title: Wavelet Transform Artificial Intelligence Algorithm-Based Data Mining Technology for Norovirus Monitoring and Early Warning.
records.clinical_problem: Enhancing intestinal ultrasound images and combining with stool data to monitor and provide early warning of norovirus infection trends in young children
records.patient_population: 2,133 children with diarrhea
records.model_description: A wavelet-transform-based AI algorithm used for noise reduction/data mining of children's intestinal ultrasound images and stool specimen data, feeding an epidemiological early-warning model for norovirus infection trends.
records.headline_result: Positive norovirus detection rate 59% among children with diarrhea; noise-reduced ultrasound images were clearer
records.study_design: Retrospective observational study with AI-based image processing

records.title: Seeking diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers for childhood bacterial pneumonia in sub-Saharan Africa: study protocol for an observational study.
records.exclusion_reason: Study protocol for blood-protein biomarker discovery using machine learning; chest radiographs used only as part of clinical case definition criteria, not as AI input; protocol has no results.

records.title: Multimodal MR Images-Based Diagnosis of Early Adolescent Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Using Multiple Kernel Learning.
records.model_family: Boruta feature selection with multiple kernel learning fusing structural MRI, functional MRI and diffusion tensor features, classified by a support vector machine
records.clinical_problem: diagnosing ADHD in early adolescence, where current criteria rest on behavior analysis that is subjective and inconsistent especially in children
records.patient_population: comorbidity-free children with ADHD and covariable-matched healthy children aged 9-10 from the Adolescent Brain and Cognitive Development (ABCD) study
records.model_description: Fusion at the kernel level rather than by concatenating features, which is the point of the paper - it is compared directly against early feature fusion and against each modality alone, and wins. The cohort design is unusually clean for this literature: comorbidity-free cases, covariable-matched controls, a narrow 9-10 age band, drawn from ABCD. The resulting AUC of 0.698 is the sober number that clean design produces, and it is a useful calibration against the higher figures reported on less controlled samples.
records.dataset_size: ABCD subjects aged 9-10, size not stated in the abstract
records.headline_result: AUC 0.698 and accuracy 64.3%, significantly better than early feature fusion or any single modality
records.study_design: retrospective model development on a public cohort

records.title: Deep Learning-based Reconstruction for Lower-Dose Pediatric CT: Technical Principles, Image Characteristics, and Clinical Implementations.
records.journal: Radiographics : a review publication of the Radiological Society of North America, Inc
records.clinical_problem: getting diagnostic image quality out of low-dose CT in the population where dose matters most
records.patient_population: children undergoing CT for a range of clinical indications
records.model_description: A RadioGraphics review of deep-learning CT reconstruction for children: how the engines are trained on paired low-dose and high-dose data to tell true attenuation from noise, how the resulting images look and behave differently from filtered back projection and iterative reconstruction, and what dose reduction is achievable in practice. Written for a department deciding whether to adopt what is already a purchasable scanner option.
records.release_evidence: deep learning-based reconstruction has been introduced to overcome the limitations of the FBP and IR approaches and is currently available clinically

records.title: Automatic measurement of axial vertebral rotation in 3D vertebral models.
records.clinical_problem: Automatically measuring axial vertebral rotation, an indicator of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis severity, from 3D vertebral models
records.patient_population: Adolescents with 3D vertebral models (source imaging modality and n not stated)
records.model_description: A point-cloud segmentation neural network (Multi-Input PointNet with attention) that segments vertebral endplates in 3D vertebral models and an algorithm that locates the spinous process tip, to automatically compute axial vertebral rotation angle.
records.headline_result: Correlation coefficient 0.986 between automatic and manual AVR measurements
records.study_design: Retrospective algorithm development and validation study

records.title: A category attention instance segmentation network for four cardiac chambers segmentation in fetal echocardiography.
records.journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
records.clinical_problem: Automated segmentation of all four fetal cardiac chambers on echocardiography to assist diagnosis of fetal heart disease.
records.patient_population: 319 fetuses (four-chamber view echocardiography images)
records.model_description: A Category Attention Instance Segmentation Network with category, mask, and category-attention branches segments all four fetal cardiac chambers simultaneously from echocardiography images.
records.headline_result: Dice coefficients 0.7956/0.7619/0.8199/0.7470 for the four chambers; average precision 45.64%

records.title: Cast suppression in radiographs by generative adversarial networks.
records.journal: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
records.clinical_problem: Digitally suppress plaster cast superimposition in pediatric wrist radiographs to improve image interpretability
records.patient_population: 9,672 pediatric wrist radiographs, mean age 11 years
records.model_description: Takes pediatric wrist radiographs with cast as input; a CycleGAN model (U-Net or ResNet-based generator, tested at multiple input sizes) synthesizes a cast-suppressed version of the image.
records.dataset_size: 9,672 radiographs (4,836 with cast, 4,836 without); test set of 718 with cast
records.headline_result: U-Net 512 CycleGAN performed best of tested architectures (P≤.001)

records.title: Automated Segmentation of Visceral, Deep Subcutaneous, and Superficial Subcutaneous Adipose Tissue Volumes in MRI of Neonates and Young Children.
records.clinical_problem: Automated quantification of abdominal adipose tissue depots (visceral and subcutaneous fat) in neonates and young children using MRI.
records.patient_population: 333 neonates (<=2 weeks) and 755 children (4.5 or 6 years) from the GUSTO cohort
records.model_description: A convolutional neural network takes abdominal MRI volumes as input and outputs segmentation masks for superficial subcutaneous, deep subcutaneous, and visceral adipose tissue.
records.dataset_size: 1,088 volumes (333 neonates, 755 children); trained on 761, tested on 100 neonatal + 227 child volumes
records.headline_result: Dice scores 0.960/0.909/0.872 (neonates) and 0.944/0.851/0.960 (children) for SSAT/DSAT/VAT
records.study_design: retrospective secondary analysis of prospectively collected cohort data

records.title: Presurgical Evaluation Strategies for Intractable Epilepsy of Childhood.
records.clinical_problem: Presurgical localization of the epileptogenic zone in children with drug-resistant epilepsy using neuroimaging and emerging AI-assisted techniques
records.patient_population: Pediatric epilepsy surgery candidates (narrative review, no specific cohort)
records.model_description: Narrative review of presurgical evaluation techniques (video EEG, MRI, SPECT, PET, MEG, fMRI) in pediatric epilepsy, including discussion of emerging image post-processing and artificial intelligence methods for source localization.

records.title: Convolutional Neural Network-Processed MRI Images in the Diagnosis of Plastic Bronchitis in Children.
records.clinical_problem: diagnosis and characterization of plastic bronchitis on chest MRI in children
records.patient_population: 30 children with plastic bronchitis (19 boys, 11 girls)
records.model_description: A CNN-based algorithm segments chest MRI images of children with plastic bronchitis and was compared against an Active Appearance Model algorithm for segmentation accuracy (Dice and Jaccard coefficients); the segmented images were used to characterize associated findings such as atelectasis, pleural effusion, and pneumothorax.
records.headline_result: CNN Dice coefficient 0.946 vs Active Appearance Model 0.843; Jaccard 0.894 vs 0.758

records.title: Image quality assessment of pediatric chest and abdomen CT by deep learning reconstruction.
records.model_family: vendor deep learning CT denoising reconstruction at medium and high strength
records.clinical_problem: reducing radiation dose in pediatric body CT, where iterative reconstruction lowers noise but alters image texture in ways radiologists dislike
records.patient_population: 51 children aged 1-18 years (34 boys, 17 girls) scanned February to October 2020: 16 non-contrast chest, 12 contrast-enhanced chest and 23 contrast-enhanced abdomen CT
records.model_description: The noise power spectrum analysis on a phantom is what raises this above a subjective comparison: it shows the network lowers the magnitude of noise while preserving its texture, which is the specific complaint against iterative reconstruction at high strength. Equally useful is the negative finding, stated plainly - artifacts did not improve at any strength, so the technique buys noise and not artifact correction.
records.release_evidence: a vendor deep learning reconstruction option on the clinical CT scanner, compared against the scanner's ASIR-V
records.dataset_size: 51 children, 51 examinations, plus a phantom scan
records.headline_result: noise reduction of 33.0-39.6% versus 50% ASIR-V with CNR increases of 53-149%, better subjective image quality and noise (p < 0.001), but no significant difference in artifacts
records.study_design: retrospective image quality study with phantom analysis

records.title: Artificial intelligence applied to support medical decisions for the automatic analysis of echocardiogram images: A systematic review.
records.exclusion_reason: systematic review of AI for echocardiogram analysis in general (transthoracic/transesophageal/Doppler/stress); not specific to pediatric population, fetal echo only one of five categories covered

records.title: Application of the Artificial Neural Network in the Diagnosis of Infantile Bronchial Bridge with 64-Slice Multislice Spiral CT.
records.exclusion_reason: Retracted publication; excluded due to retraction (data reliability concerns), despite topical relevance to pediatric CT AI diagnosis.

records.title: dStripe: Slice artefact correction in diffusion MRI via constrained neural network.
records.clinical_problem: correcting inter-slice intensity artefacts in neonatal diffusion MRI to improve image quality for research and diagnosis
records.patient_population: neonates scanned as part of the developing Human Connectome Project
records.model_description: Input: reconstructed multi-shell high-angular-resolution neonatal diffusion MRI with inter-slice inconsistencies; output: a corrective multiplicative slice-intensity modulation field producing an artefact-corrected image, trained without ground-truth data.
records.study_design: methods development and evaluation on neonatal diffusion MRI (developing Human Connectome Project)

records.title: Rheumatic Heart Disease Screening Based on Phonocardiogram.
records.exclusion_reason: machine learning classification of rheumatic heart disease from phonocardiogram (heart sound) recordings; audio signal, not imaging

records.title: Unified framework for early stage status prediction of autism based on infant structural magnetic resonance imaging.
records.journal: Autism research : official journal of the International Society for Autism Research
records.clinical_problem: early prediction of autism spectrum disorder status in infants using structural brain MRI
records.patient_population: infants around 24 months of age, two datasets with different imaging protocols/scanners
records.model_description: Input: infant structural brain MRI (segmentation/parcellation maps from the iBEAT V2.0 pipeline); output: prediction of autism spectrum disorder status via CNN feature extraction and a Siamese network comparison.
records.study_design: retrospective model development and validation across two independent datasets

records.title: Doppler Ultrasound Imaging Combined with Fetal Heart Detection in Predicting Fetal Distress in Pregnancy-Induced Hypertension under the Guidance of Artificial Intelligence Algorithm.
records.model_family: unclear (described only as an 'artificial intelligence algorithm' with a diffusion filter for image denoising)
records.clinical_problem: Predicting fetal distress in pregnancies complicated by pregnancy-induced hypertension using Doppler ultrasound combined with fetal heart monitoring
records.patient_population: 120 pregnant women (88 with PIH and fetal distress, 32 healthy controls)
records.model_description: An AI-guided diffusion-filter algorithm denoises Doppler ultrasound images; combined Doppler ultrasound and fetal heart monitoring parameters (PI, RI, S/D) are compared between distressed and healthy pregnancies to flag fetal distress
records.headline_result: 73.3% of fetal distress cases detected by combined US + heart monitoring vs 26.7% by heart monitoring alone (P<0.05)
records.study_design: retrospective observational study; NOTE: this article has been formally retracted

records.title: Sleep Monitoring of Children With Nocturnal Enuresis: A Narrative Review.
records.exclusion_reason: narrative review of sleep monitoring (polysomnography/EEG) for nocturnal enuresis; deep learning is mentioned only as a future direction, not an imaging AI application

records.title: 1H-NMR-based metabolic profiling identifies non-invasive diagnostic and predictive urinary fingerprints in 5q spinal muscular atrophy.
records.exclusion_reason: urinary metabolomics via 1H-NMR spectroscopy; laboratory biomarker study, not imaging-based

records.title: Deep Multimodal Learning From MRI and Clinical Data for Early Prediction of Neurodevelopmental Deficits in Very Preterm Infants.
records.model_family: end-to-end deep multimodal networks over T2-weighted anatomical MRI, diffusion tensor imaging, resting-state fMRI and clinical data
records.clinical_problem: predicting cognitive, language and motor deficits at 2 years corrected age in very preterm infants, early enough to act inside the first-years window when intervention works best
records.patient_population: very preterm infants born at or before 32 weeks gestational age, imaged with multimodal MRI and followed to 2 years corrected age
records.model_description: Three MRI modalities and clinical data fused end to end, with the explicit hypothesis - and the demonstration - that the combination beats any modality alone. Separate models for cognitive, language and motor outcome rather than one composite, which matches how these deficits diverge. The authors label it proof of concept and call for a larger study with external validation, which is the right reading of accuracies in the high 80s on a single-site preterm cohort.
records.headline_result: 88.4% accuracy for cognitive, 87.2% for language and 86.7% for motor deficits at 2 years corrected age, significantly better than any individual data modality

records.title: Single-Input Multi-Output U-Net for Automated 2D Foetal Brain Segmentation of MR Images.
records.model_family: U-Net variant fused with holistically nested edge detection
records.clinical_problem: automated segmentation of the fetal brain on MRI, including abnormal cases
records.patient_population: 200 normal fetal brains (>11,500 images) plus 54 abnormal cases (>3,500 images)
records.model_description: Input: 2D fetal brain MR images; output: automated brain segmentation using a hybrid U-Net/holistically-nested-edge-detection architecture combining features from multiple side outputs.
records.dataset_size: 200 normal fetal brains (>11,500 images), 54 abnormal cases (>3,500 images)
records.headline_result: Dice 94.2±5.9% (normal), 91.2±6.8% (abnormal)
records.study_design: retrospective model development and validation study

records.title: Advanced Kidney Volume Measurement Method Using Ultrasonography with Artificial Intelligence-Based Hybrid Learning in Children.
records.clinical_problem: automating kidney volume measurement from ultrasound in children and deriving an expected-kidney-volume growth equation
records.patient_population: 141 subjects (282 kidneys) under 19 years old; 29 subjects (58 kidneys) with paired CT
records.model_description: a hybrid-learning image segmentation method takes kidney ultrasound images as input and outputs an automated kidney volume, compared to CT and the conventional ellipsoidal method, and used to derive a weight/height-based expected-volume equation
records.dataset_size: 141 subjects (282 kidneys); 29 subjects with paired CT (58 kidneys)

records.title: Autism spectrum disorder diagnosis using graph attention network based on spatial-constrained sparse functional brain networks.
records.model_name: PSCR-GAT (Pearson's correlation-based Spatial Constraints Representation with Graph Attention Network)
records.clinical_problem: autism spectrum disorder diagnosis
records.patient_population: participants from the public ABIDE I resting-state fMRI dataset (n=871); exact ages not stated in the abstract
records.model_description: Resting-state fMRI is used to build functional brain networks with a new construction method (Pearson's correlation-based Spatial Constraints Representation). The resulting brain graphs are fed into a graph attention network to classify autism spectrum disorder versus controls. Evaluated on the public ABIDE I dataset against other functional-brain-network construction and graph-neural-network classification methods.
records.headline_result: 72.40% classification accuracy for autism spectrum disorder, significantly outperforming competing methods

records.title: Optimal Method for Fetal Brain Age Prediction Using Multiplanar Slices From Structural Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
records.clinical_problem: predicting fetal brain age from structural MRI to help identify abnormal brain development
records.patient_population: 220 healthy fetuses (15.9-38.7 weeks gestational age); 21 healthy fetuses for external validation
records.model_description: Multiplanar 2D slices from fetal structural MRI, without interslice motion correction, are each input to a 2D single-channel CNN that predicts gestational age; the mode of multiple per-fetus slice predictions gives the final fetal brain age, validated on an external cohort.
records.headline_result: mean absolute error 0.125 weeks internally; 0.508 weeks on external validation
records.study_design: retrospective method development study with external validation

records.title: Using deep learning to classify pediatric posttraumatic stress disorder at the individual level.
records.clinical_problem: Classifying pediatric PTSD from healthy controls using resting-state fMRI functional connectome graph metrics
records.patient_population: 33 pediatric PTSD patients, 53 matched healthy controls
records.model_description: Whole-brain functional connectomes are built from resting-state fMRI using a 90-region atlas-based partial correlation matrix, graph theory topological metrics are extracted, and a deep learning classifier distinguishes pediatric PTSD patients from healthy controls.
records.headline_result: overall classification accuracy 71.2%

records.title: Exploring the NT-proBNP expression in Premature Infants with Patent Ductus Arteriosus (PDA) by Echocardiography.
records.clinical_problem: screen echocardiographic indicators using an AI convolutional neural network to aid diagnosis of symptomatic patent ductus arteriosus in premature infants, correlated with serum NT-proBNP
records.patient_population: 90 premature infants (52 non-PDA, 38 PDA: 26 symptomatic, 12 asymptomatic)
records.model_description: An artificial intelligence convolutional neural network (AI-CNN) is used to screen echocardiographic indicators in premature infants, correlating findings with serum NT-proBNP levels to aid diagnosis of symptomatic patent ductus arteriosus.
records.study_design: retrospective cohort correlation study using AI-CNN-assisted echocardiography

records.title: Improved support vector machine algorithm based on the influence of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus on the outcome of perinatal outcome by ultrasound imaging.
records.exclusion_reason: Title references an SVM algorithm, but the abstract describes only conventional statistical analysis (chi-square test, multivariate logistic regression) of clinical and Doppler ultrasound findings in gestational diabetes; no machine-learning methodology or results are reported.

records.title: Brain tissue development of neonates with Congenital Septal Defect: Study on MRI Image Evaluation of Deep Learning Algorithm.
records.exclusion_reason: Title references deep learning but the abstract describes only manual ventricular-index measurements and t-test/ROC comparison; no AI/ML model actually described

records.title: MRI Super-Resolution Through Generative Degradation Learning.
records.journal: Medical image computing and computer-assisted intervention : MICCAI ... International Conference on Medical Image Computing and Computer-Assisted Intervention
records.clinical_problem: improving spatial resolution of brain MRI without increasing scan time
records.patient_population: ten pediatric patients (clinical validation) plus simulated data
records.model_description: Input: low-resolution MRI; output: super-resolution reconstruction using a deep generative network that estimates scan-specific blur kernels via adversarial degradation learning, achieving 0.125 cubic mm isotropic resolution in six minutes.
records.headline_result: superior super-resolution results vs state-of-the-art deconvolution methods, at substantially reduced imaging time
records.study_design: retrospective single-center model development and validation study

records.title: Ultrashort Echo-Time MR Imaging of the Pediatric Head and Neck.
records.journal: Magnetic resonance imaging clinics of North America
records.exclusion_reason: Review of ultrashort/zero echo-time pediatric bone MR imaging technique and clinical applications (craniosynostosis, sinonasal/jaw imaging, trauma); deep learning is mentioned only in passing as one of three approaches to synthetic CT generation, not the review's focus.

records.title: Deep Learning Algorithms-Based CT Images in Glucocorticoid Therapy in Asthma Children with Small Airway Obstruction.
records.clinical_problem: using deep learning-processed CT images to evaluate small airway function and compare glucocorticoid treatment efficacy in children with asthma and small airway obstruction
records.patient_population: 118 children hospitalized with acute asthma exacerbation, 96 with small airway obstruction included
records.model_description: Input: chest CT images; output: reconstructed/segmented airway images (Res-Net feature extraction, Mask R-CNN reconstruction) used to quantify airway wall thickness and area for evaluating treatment response.
records.dataset_size: 118 children (96 with small airway obstruction, split into 3 groups of 32)
records.study_design: clinical cohort study comparing treatment groups using deep learning-based CT image analysis

records.title: Comparison of intracranial injury predictability between machine learning algorithms and the nomogram in pediatric traumatic brain injury.
records.exclusion_reason: machine learning predicts whether a head CT will show intracranial injury in children with traumatic brain injury, from 14 clinical parameters; the imaging finding is the label rather than the input, so no images or image-derived features are analyzed

records.title: The role of machine learning applications in diagnosing and assessing critical and non-critical CHD: a scoping review.
records.model_family: review of deep learning and support vector machine approaches
records.clinical_problem: diagnosis and assessment of congenital heart defects
records.patient_population: pediatric cardiology patients with suspected or confirmed congenital heart defects, across studies published 2015-2021
records.model_description: Scoping review of 50 full-text machine-learning studies in pediatric cardiology, of which 40% focused on optimizing diagnosis and assessment of congenital heart defects. Deep learning and support vector machines were the most commonly used algorithms, applied to auscultatory heart sounds, transthoracic echocardiograms, and cardiac MRIs, with an overall diagnostic accuracy above 0.80.
records.headline_result: overall diagnostic accuracy greater than 0.80 across the reviewed machine-learning studies for congenital heart defect diagnosis

records.title: Based on improved deep convolutional neural network model pneumonia image classification.
records.clinical_problem: Automatically diagnosing pneumonia, the leading infectious cause of death in children under five, from chest X-rays
records.patient_population: Pediatric chest X-ray dataset (children with and without pneumonia)
records.model_description: Chest X-ray images are fed through an Xception network for deep feature extraction, and the extracted features pass to an LSTM module that selects the most discriminative features to classify the image as pneumonia or normal
records.dataset_size: not stated (existing pediatric pneumonia chest X-ray dataset)
records.headline_result: Accuracy 96%, ROC-AUC 99%, precision 98%, recall 91%, F1 94%

records.title: Two decades of advances in muscle imaging in children: from pattern recognition of muscle diseases to quantification and machine learning approaches.
records.clinical_problem: using muscle imaging (pattern recognition and quantification) to diagnose pediatric neuromuscular disease
records.patient_population: children with neuromuscular disorders (review, no single cohort)
records.model_description: A historical review of two decades of pediatric muscle imaging, describing progression from qualitative pattern recognition of MRI/ultrasound 'MRI fingerprints' toward quantification and machine learning approaches for etiological diagnosis.

records.title: Brain MRI Radiomics Analysis of School-Aged Children with Tetralogy of Fallot.
records.journal: Computational and mathematical methods in medicine
records.clinical_problem: predict neurodevelopmental outcomes in school-aged children with tetralogy of Fallot using brain MRI radiomics
records.patient_population: school-aged TOF patients and healthy peer controls
records.model_description: Radiomics features extracted from brain MRI, reduced via LASSO regression, are used in a logistic regression model to predict neurodevelopmental status in school-aged children with corrected tetralogy of Fallot.
records.headline_result: model AUC 0.750
records.study_design: case-control validation study using radiomics model

records.title: Chest Computed Tomography Images in Neonatal Bronchial Pneumonia under the Adaptive Statistical Iterative Reconstruction Algorithm.
records.model_family: adaptive statistical iterative reconstruction algorithm (termed an AI algorithm by the authors)
records.clinical_problem: diagnosis of neonatal bronchial pneumonia on chest CT
records.patient_population: 85 neonates with pneumonia
records.model_description: The ASiR (adaptive statistical iterative reconstruction) algorithm, described by the authors as an artificial-intelligence algorithm, reconstructs chest CT images at different preweight/postweight settings to improve diagnostic image quality at reduced dose; diagnostic accuracy of CT was compared with and combined with blood C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate for diagnosing neonatal bronchial pneumonia.
records.release_evidence: ASiR (Adaptive Statistical iterative Reconstruction) is a named, vendor CT reconstruction algorithm
records.headline_result: Diagnostic accuracy: CT 80.7%, CRP 75.3%, ESR 75.1%, CRP+ESR 80.3%, CRP+ESR+CT 98.6%

records.title: Investigating myocardial performance in normal and sick fetuses by abdominal Doppler signal derived indices.
records.model_family: hybrid Hidden Markov Model and Support Vector Machine
records.clinical_problem: Automatically deriving fetal myocardial performance indices (Tei index and modified Tei index) from Doppler ultrasound and ECG signals to monitor fetal cardiac function and identify CHD and non-CHD abnormalities
records.patient_population: 80 fetuses (55 normal, 25 with cardiac/non-cardiac abnormalities)
records.model_description: A hybrid Hidden Markov Model/Support Vector Machine automated model that estimates cardiac time intervals (isovolumic contraction/relaxation time, ejection/filling time) from simultaneous fetal ECG and Doppler ultrasound signals, used to calculate myocardial performance indices.
records.headline_result: Modified TI (KI) significantly correlated with gestational age (r=-0.36, p<0.01) and differed between normal/abnormal groups
records.study_design: Prospective observational study with automated signal-processing model

records.title: Identification of Appendicitis Using Ultrasound with the Aid of Machine Learning.
records.journal: Journal of laparoendoscopic & advanced surgical techniques. Part A
records.clinical_problem: Assisting detection of the appendix on abdominal ultrasound video to aid diagnosis of pediatric appendicitis
records.patient_population: 70 abdominal ultrasound videos (50 for training, 20 for test); pediatric surgeons and residents/fellows evaluated
records.model_description: Input: abdominal ultrasound video frames; output: detection/localization of the appendix to assist diagnosis of pediatric appendicitis, via a trained AI neural network
records.headline_result: AI detection judged 'most' in 50% of test videos, 'none' in 30%
records.study_design: retrospective algorithm development with reader evaluation study

records.title: Automated Analysis of Choroidal Sublayer Morphologic Features in Myopic Children Using EDI-OCT by Deep Learning.
records.exclusion_reason: deep learning segmentation of choroidal sublayers on enhanced-depth-imaging OCT in 92 myopic and emmetropic children; ophthalmic imaging is outside the scope of this database

records.title: A maChine and deep Learning Approach to predict pulmoNary hyperteNsIon in newbornS with congenital diaphragmatic Hernia (CLANNISH): Protocol for a retrospective study.
records.model_family: machine learning and deep learning (planned; 3D U-Net for lung segmentation)
records.clinical_problem: predicting postnatal pulmonary hypertension and related outcomes in congenital diaphragmatic hernia from prenatal clinical and imaging data
records.patient_population: fetuses and newborns with isolated congenital diaphragmatic hernia, singleton pregnancies, born 2012-2020
records.model_description: Study protocol for machine-learning and deep-learning forecasting models that take integrated clinical and fetal MRI data as input and will output prediction of postnatal pulmonary hypertension and related outcomes, plus a planned 3D U-Net-based automatic fetal lung segmentation tool for MRI.
records.study_design: retrospective study protocol for machine-learning/deep-learning outcome-prediction models, registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04609163)

records.title: The Use of Artificial Intelligence in Automation in the Fields of Gynaecology and Obstetrics - an Assessment of the State of Play.
records.clinical_problem: Overview of AI applications automating gynecologic and obstetric imaging tasks, focused on prenatal sonographic diagnostics
records.model_description: Narrative review of AI techniques (image reconstruction, noise reduction, quality assurance, segmentation, computer-aided detection/classification, radiogenomics) applied in gynecology and obstetrics, with a focus on automated prenatal sonographic diagnostics.

records.title: [Computed tomography-based radiomics for differential of retroperitoneal neuroblastoma and ganglioneuroblastoma in children].
records.journal: Nan fang yi ke da xue xue bao = Journal of Southern Medical University
records.clinical_problem: differentiating retroperitoneal neuroblastoma from ganglioneuroblastoma in children on CT
records.patient_population: 172 children with neuroblastoma and 48 with ganglioneuroblastoma
records.model_description: CT radiomics features are extracted from non-enhanced and post-enhanced images and combined in a multivariate regression model to output the probability of neuroblastoma vs. ganglioneuroblastoma.
records.headline_result: Combined model AUC 0.861 (training), 0.827 (testing)
records.study_design: retrospective radiomics model-development study with training/testing split

records.title: DenResCov-19: A deep transfer learning network for robust automatic classification of COVID-19, pneumonia, and tuberculosis from X-rays.
records.journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
records.exclusion_reason: DenResCov-19 classifies COVID-19, pneumonia, tuberculosis and healthy chest radiographs by joining DenseNet-121 and ResNet-50; childhood pneumonia mortality is cited as motivation but the abstract does not state that the imaged patients are children, so a pediatric population cannot be established from the record

records.title: Medical Augmentation (Med-Aug) for Optimal Data Augmentation in Medical Deep Learning Networks.
records.exclusion_reason: general medical-image data-augmentation method paper; no pediatric-specific population or focus stated

records.title: A multi-modal MRI analysis of brain structure and function in relation to OXT methylation in maltreated children and adolescents.
records.clinical_problem: identifying sensitive periods and types of childhood maltreatment associated with oxytocin-gene methylation and its effects on brain structure/function
records.patient_population: 24 maltreated children and 31 non-maltreated children/adolescents
records.model_description: Input is multi-modal brain MRI (voxel-based morphometry, diffusion tensor imaging, task and resting-state fMRI) and salivary DNA methylation data; a random forest regression model identifies which maltreatment age and type most contribute to an oxytocin methylation index, which is then related to brain structure and function.
records.headline_result: sensitive period ages 5-8 and physical abuse contributed most to the oxytocin methylation index; index was negatively correlated with left superior parietal lobule gray matter volume
records.study_design: case-control multi-modal MRI study with random forest analysis

records.title: Intracranial Densitometry-Augmented Machine Learning Enhances the Prognostic Value of Brain CT in Pediatric Patients With Traumatic Brain Injury: A Retrospective Pilot Study.
records.clinical_problem: Predict outcome (Glasgow Outcome Scale, mortality, length of stay, need for surgery) in pediatric traumatic brain injury using automated CT densitometric analysis
records.patient_population: 58 pediatric TBI patients
records.model_description: Takes automated Hounsfield-unit densitometric distributions from supratentorial brain CT as input; a CatBoost gradient boosting model predicts TBI outcome measures.
records.headline_result: AUC 0.83 favorability, 0.91 in-hospital mortality, 0.83 length of stay, 0.71 need for surgery

records.title: Computer-Aided Diagnosis of Children with Cerebral Palsy under Deep Learning Convolutional Neural Network Image Segmentation Model Combined with Three-Dimensional Cranial Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
records.exclusion_reason: retracted publication

records.title: 3D Virtual Reality Imaging of Major Aortopulmonary Collateral Arteries: A Novel Diagnostic Modality.
records.journal: World journal for pediatric & congenital heart surgery
records.exclusion_reason: 3D virtual reality visualization tool for surgical planning; no AI/ML component

records.title: Automatic measurement of fetal femur length in ultrasound images: a comparison of random forest regression model and SegNet.
records.model_family: random forest regression and SegNet (deep learning, fully convolutional network)
records.clinical_problem: automated measurement of fetal femur length on ultrasound

records.title: A Deep-Learning Aided Diagnostic System in Assessing Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip on Pediatric Pelvic Radiographs.
records.model_family: three-stage pipeline: Mask R-CNN pelvic bone segmentation, HRNet landmark localization, then measurement and classification
records.clinical_problem: measuring and classifying developmental dysplasia of the hip on pediatric pelvic radiographs, where the acetabular index and centre-edge angle are drawn by hand and observers disagree
records.patient_population: 1265 pediatric pelvic radiographs for training and 133 from two other medical institutions for validation, with three orthopedic surgeons as comparators
records.model_description: The decomposition matches how the measurement is actually made - find the ilium, pubis, ischium and femoral heads, then place the landmarks, then compute the angles - which makes each stage checkable. The result that matters clinically is not accuracy but variance: intraclass consistency across surgeons was 0.79-0.98 while the model's was 1.00, because a deterministic model measuring the same film twice cannot disagree with itself. It also matched an intermediate surgeon on Tonnis and IHDI grading, in less time.
records.headline_result: Tonnis and IHDI classification accuracy 0.86-0.95 for both hips; no statistically significant difference from surgeons on the numeric indices; intraclass consistency 1.00 for the model versus 0.79-0.98 among surgeons, and significantly faster
records.study_design: retrospective model development with external validation and observer comparison

The gap between the neural network (82%) and the support vector classifier (72%) on the same features is worth noting: on data this wide, the choice of classifier is doing as much work as the features.

Instead the model detects the seven lung ultrasound features a neonatologist already names - normal, irregular and thick pleura, A-lines, separate and coalescent B-lines, consolidations - and leaves the diagnostic inference to the clinician. The authors argue explicitly that feeding images to a model for a diagnosis will not earn medical trust, and that the output must be in the operator's own vocabulary. Attention with a stacked module is used to suppress irrelevant ultrasound regions - a reasonable response to speckle and shadow. records.title: Detecting Outliers with Poisson Image Interpolation
records.model_family: self-supervised anomaly detection trained only on normal data, using Poisson rather than foreign patch interpolation
records.clinical_problem: screening, where supervised learning of every possible pathology is unrealistic - so the model learns normal appearance and flags what departs from it, tested on hypoplastic left heart syndrome in prenatal fetal cardiac ultrasound and on common lung anomalies in chest radiographs
records.patient_population: prenatal fetal cardiac ultrasound and chest radiographs
records.model_description: The framing is right for pediatric and fetal screening specifically: the abnormalities are individually rare, collectively common and impossible to enumerate for supervised training, so learning normal is the only scalable route. Choosing Poisson interpolation over the earlier foreign-patch strategy is what makes it work in a challenging data regime like fetal cardiac ultrasound, where blending artefacts would otherwise be the anomaly the model learns. Code released.
records.headline_result: outperformed state-of-the-art anomaly detection by a good margin on hypoplastic left heart syndrome in fetal cardiac ultrasound and on lung anomalies in chest radiographs

records.title: Self Context and Shape Prior for Sensorless Freehand 3D Ultrasound Reconstruction
records.model_family: online learning framework with a differentiable reconstruction algorithm, self-supervised context learning at test time, and adversarial training of an anatomical shape prior
records.clinical_problem: reconstructing a 3D volume from a freehand ultrasound sweep without a position sensor, so that the limited field of view of 3D ultrasound is overcome using an ordinary probe and a free scan path
records.patient_population: developmental dysplasia of the hip ultrasound and fetal ultrasound datasets
records.model_description: The diagnosis of what previous methods got wrong is precise: they learned from simple, uniform scanning sequences, while real clinical scans mix skills and follow complicated paths, so a model that only fits its training sequences fails in practice. Adapting at test time from the case's own context, plus an adversarially learned shape prior, is the response. Both evaluation datasets are pediatric or fetal - infant hip dysplasia and fetal ultrasound - which is where sensorless 3D would matter most.
records.headline_result: outperformed state-of-the-art methods on shift errors and path similarity for freehand 3D reconstruction on developmental dysplasia of the hip and fetal ultrasound datasets

records.model_description: A theory paper with a fetal application, and unusually the theory is a uniqueness result: there is one and only one way to convert a standard loss for fully segmented images into a proper loss that handles partial labels. That matters because partial annotation is the normal state of pediatric and fetal datasets, assembled piecemeal across studies with different labels of interest. Includes fetuses with open spina bifida rather than only normal anatomy, which is where segmentation methods usually break. Implementation released.
records.headline_result: a new state of the art in partially supervised fetal brain 3D MRI segmentation, producing a network that segments eight structures in normal fetuses and in fetuses with open spina bifida

That is close but not equal, and the per-subfeature breakdown localizes the gap to air-trapping and large lesions, which is actionable. A structured score is a good automation target precisely because its variability is what limits its use in longitudinal care.

records.title: An automated framework for localization, segmentation and super-resolution reconstruction of fetal brain MRI.
records.model_family: two-stage CNN localization and segmentation plus outlier-robust super-resolution
records.clinical_problem: producing a usable high-resolution fetal brain volume from motion-corrupted stacks, including brains malformed by open spina bifida
records.patient_population: fetuses with normal brains and with varying ventriculomegaly associated with open spina bifida
records.model_description: A four-stage pipeline that takes the motion-corrupted 2D slice stacks of a fetal brain MRI and returns a high-resolution volume in standard anatomical space with no user input. One network finds the brain, a second segments it finely, then a super-resolution step reconstructs the volume. It removes the manual brain-masking step that has kept fetal volume reconstruction out of routine practice.
records.headline_result: each stage outperformed state-of-the-art methods on segmentation and reconstruction, including expert-reader quality assessment

records.title: Modular segregation of task-dependent brain networks contributes to the development of executive function in children.
records.exclusion_reason: graph analysis of task-dependent network segregation and executive function in typically developing children; no machine-learning model and no clinical target

records.title: Prediction of sleep side effects following methylphenidate treatment in ADHD youth.
records.model_family: logistic ridge regression, SVM, J48 decision tree
records.clinical_problem: Can pre-treatment features, including brain structural connectivity, predict which children with ADHD will develop sleep problems after starting methylphenidate?
records.patient_population: 83 ADHD subjects (training cohort), 36 ADHD subjects (independent validation cohort), in an 8-week open-label methylphenidate trial
records.model_description: Machine learning classifiers combine demographic, clinical, neuropsychological, genetic and structural brain connectivity (frontostriatal circuit) features, added stepwise, to predict whether a child with ADHD will develop sleep problems after starting methylphenidate.
records.headline_result: Best model (logistic ridge regression, full feature set including structural connectivity) achieved 95.5% accuracy (AUC 0.99) in training; 86.1% accuracy (AUC 0.92) in independent validation
records.study_design: prospective open-label trial with machine-learning outcome prediction and independent validation

records.title: Deep learning, reusable and problem-based architectures for detection of consolidation on chest X-ray images.
records.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
records.model_family: problem-based CNN architecture with transfer learning and custom preprocessing
records.clinical_problem: detecting consolidation on a child's chest radiograph
records.patient_population: children in the pediatric chest X-ray dataset, with a separate dataset used to test generalization
records.model_description: Argues that networks designed to win on ImageNet are the wrong shape for radiographs, and designs an architecture around the problem instead, with preprocessing chosen to preserve the information that consolidation lives in. It checks its own reasoning with an occlusion test showing which region drove each decision, and tests generalization on a second dataset rather than a held-out split of the same one.
records.dataset_size: the pediatric chest X-ray dataset plus an external validation dataset
records.headline_result: 94.67% accuracy for consolidation detection, above the previously published architectures on the same dataset

records.title: Using a Dual-Input Convolutional Neural Network for Automated Detection of Pediatric Supracondylar Fracture on Conventional Radiography.
records.model_family: dual-input CNN merging two ResNet branches
records.clinical_problem: detecting supracondylar fracture of the humerus in children on conventional radiographs
records.patient_population: children undergoing elbow radiography; 1,266 AP and lateral pairs for development, 258 for temporal testing and 95 from a second hospital
records.model_description: Reads the anteroposterior and lateral elbow radiographs together, as a radiologist does, by merging two networks rather than judging each view alone. Tested twice on data the model had never seen: a later year at the same hospital and a different hospital entirely. Its errors are asymmetric in a clinically useful direction, with very high negative predictive value and lower specificity, meaning it over-calls rather than misses.
records.dataset_size: 1,266 radiograph pairs for development; 258 temporal and 95 geographic external test pairs
records.headline_result: AUC 0.985 (temporal) and 0.992 (geographic) external test sets, comparable to human readers; geographic sensitivity 100%, specificity 86.1%, negative predictive value 100%
records.study_design: retrospective development with temporal and geographic external validation and reader study

records.title: Multivariate models of brain volume for identification of children and adolescents with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder.

records.patient_population: training: 79 FASD (5.7-18.9y) and 81 controls (5.8-18.5y); testing: 67 FASD (6.0-19.6y) and 74 controls (5.2-19.5y), from two independent datasets
records.model_description: 87 regional brain volumes extracted from 3D T1-weighted MRI using FreeSurfer are input to a support vector machine that classifies children/adolescents as having fetal alcohol spectrum disorder or being a healthy control; separate models are also built by sex.
records.dataset_size: training: 79 FASD + 81 controls; testing: 67 FASD + 74 controls (independent dataset)
records.headline_result: test accuracy 77%, sensitivity 64%, specificity 88%
records.study_design: retrospective multicenter case-control diagnostic accuracy study with independent test dataset

records.headline_result: Prediction accuracy 82% (95% CI 0.73-0.94)

records.title: Expected-value bias in routine third-trimester growth scans.

records.title: Deep Learning for Lesion Detection, Progression, and Prediction of Musculoskeletal Disease.
records.journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
records.clinical_problem: where deep learning stands for musculoskeletal lesion detection, progression and prediction, including pediatric bone age
records.patient_population: adults and children in the reviewed literature
records.model_description: A review that sorts musculoskeletal deep learning by modality and by how close each application is to the clinic. Its judgment is that pediatric bone age and fracture detection on radiographs perform well enough to be nearly ready for practice, while CT and especially MRI applications remain harder because the abnormality has to be tracked across slices and contrasts. It closes by insisting on prospective multi-institution evaluation before deployment.

records.title: The digital surgeon: How big data, automation, and artificial intelligence will change surgical practice.
records.exclusion_reason: narrative review/commentary on AI, big data, and automation in surgical practice generally; not focused on pediatric radiology imaging AI

records.title: Deep CNN ensembles and suggestive annotations for infant brain MRI segmentation.
records.journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
records.model_family: ensemble of semi-dense 3D fully convolutional networks
records.clinical_problem: segmenting the 6-month infant brain, where gray and white matter are nearly isointense
records.patient_population: 6-month-old infants in the public MICCAI iSEG-2017 challenge data
records.model_description: An ensemble of networks segmenting infant brain tissue from paired T1 and T2 images. The useful property is that where the ensemble members disagree, the segmentation is usually wrong, so the disagreement map tells a human where to look and correct. The architecture uses an order of magnitude fewer parameters than a 3D U-Net, which matters for anyone deploying this on ordinary hardware.
records.headline_result: ranked first or second on most metrics among 21 teams; ensemble disagreement highly correlated with segmentation error
records.study_design: technical development on a public challenge

records.title: A novel hybrid atlas-free hierarchical graph-based segmentation of newborn brain MRI using wavelet filter banks.
records.model_family: hybrid wavelet filter bank + fuzzy SVM
records.clinical_problem: Segmenting newborn brain MRI into tissue types (white matter, gray matter) to assess brain growth, when similar tissue intensities make segmentation difficult
records.patient_population: Newborn infants (<28 days old), T1- and T2-weighted MRI
records.model_description: A hybrid atlas-free hierarchical graph-based segmentation method using wavelet filter banks for feature extraction and a fuzzy support vector machine for tissue classification, taking multimodal T1/T2 newborn brain MRI as input and producing tissue segmentation maps.
records.headline_result: Segmentation precision 90%, sensitivity 98%
records.study_design: Retrospective algorithm development and validation study

records.title: Altered resting-state functional network connectivity is associated with suicide attempt in young depressed patients.
records.exclusion_reason: resting-state fMRI functional network connectivity study of suicide attempt in young depressed patients; no diagnostic AI/ML model, and sample includes adults

records.title: Deep learning segmentation of orbital fat to calibrate conventional MRI for longitudinal studies.
records.model_family: deep learning segmentation of orbital fat used as an intensity reference tissue
records.clinical_problem: comparing conventional MRI intensities across scans years apart, where normalizing to brain tissue is circular in a disease that changes the brain - so a reference tissue outside the disease process is needed
records.patient_population: 1018 scans from 256 participants in a study of pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis, at 1.5 and 3 T
records.model_description: The reasoning is the contribution: in multiple sclerosis both white and gray matter are affected, so normalizing to brain tissue removes the biological change you are trying to measure. Orbital fat is always in a head T1, is unaffected by the disease, and is tedious to outline - which makes it a good automation target. Machine segmentations agreed with the adjudicating expert better than other experts did, and calibrated intensities tracked semi-quantitative magnetization transfer ratio better than the standard normalization algorithm. Half a second per scan.
records.headline_result: machine segmentations agreed with the adjudicating expert better than other expert humans did, and calibration agreed with magnetization transfer ratio imaging better than the WhiteStripe normalization algorithm, at 0.5 s per scan

records.title: EEG spectral power, but not theta/beta ratio, is a neuromarker for adult ADHD.

records.exclusion_reason: non-radiologic imaging; high-frequency skin ultrasound for atopic dermatitis is a dermatologic application, explicitly excluded category

records.title: Submillimeter MR fingerprinting using deep learning-based tissue quantification.
records.clinical_problem: rapid, high-resolution brain tissue (T1/T2) quantification via MR fingerprinting
records.patient_population: 5 adults and 2 pediatric subjects undergoing brain MR fingerprinting
records.model_description: Input is submillimeter-resolution MR fingerprinting acquisition data; output is quantitative T1 and T2 tissue maps, produced by a deep learning model that replaces standard template matching, tested on adult and pediatric subjects.
records.headline_result: high-quality 0.8 mm in-plane T1/T2 mapping achieved in 7.5 seconds per slice, a 5-fold acceleration versus standard methods
records.study_design: prospective technical development and feasibility study

records.title: Bone age determination using only the index finger: a novel approach using a convolutional neural network compared with human radiologists.
records.model_family: separate convolutional networks trained on whole-hand radiographs and on cropped index-finger images
records.clinical_problem: whether the whole hand is needed for bone age, or whether a single digit carries enough of the maturational signal
records.patient_population: the public RSNA pediatric bone age challenge dataset: 12 611 training and 200 test radiographs, with the index finger cropped to create a parallel dataset; three pediatric radiologists also read both versions
records.model_description: A clean ablation with a practical payoff. The network lost almost nothing when restricted to the index finger (5.1 versus 4.7 months), while radiologists reading the same cropped images degraded badly (8.0 months) - so the information is there and humans are not extracting it. The authors turn that into advice a radiologist can act on immediately: use the second digit as the starting point of the search pattern. It also raises the question of how little of an image these models actually need.
records.headline_result: mean absolute difference 5.1 months for the index-finger network versus 4.7 months for the whole-hand network (P = 0.14), against 8.0 months for radiologists reading the same index-finger radiographs (P < 0.0001)
records.study_design: retrospective model development with reader comparison

records.title: Deep Convolutional Neural Network-Based Automatic Classification of Neonatal Hip Ultrasound Images: A Novel Data Augmentation Approach with Speckle Noise Reduction.
records.model_family: convolutional neural network on automatically segmented image patches, with speckle-reduction-based data augmentation using an optimized Bayesian non-local means filter
records.clinical_problem: classifying neonatal hips by Graf's method, the most reproducible ultrasound system for developmental dysplasia of the hip and still highly dependent on the skill of both the sonographer and the evaluator
records.patient_population: neonatal hip ultrasound images captured in Graf's standard plane, divided into normal, mild dysplasia and severe dysplasia
records.model_description: The novelty is in the augmentation rather than the architecture: instead of geometric transforms, the training set is expanded with speckle-reduced variants produced by an optimized Bayesian non-local means filter, which teaches the network what is anatomy and what is ultrasound noise. The gain is large and cleanly attributed - accuracy rose from 92.29% to 97.70% from that change alone. A transferable idea for any ultrasound classification problem with limited data.
records.headline_result: accuracy 97.70% with speckle-reduction augmentation, up from 92.29% without it

records.title: Predictive validity of radiographic signs of complete discoid lateral meniscus in children using machine learning techniques.
records.journal: Journal of orthopaedic research : official publication of the Orthopaedic Research Society

records.clinical_problem: predicting the presence of complete discoid lateral meniscus from knee radiograph measurements
records.patient_population: 141 knees (age 7-16) with complete discoid lateral meniscus and 141 age/sex-matched normal knees
records.model_description: Input: radiographic measurements of the knee (lateral joint space, fibular head height, tibial spine height, etc.); output: prediction of presence of complete discoid lateral meniscus.
records.dataset_size: 141 knees with discoid meniscus + 141 matched normal knees
records.headline_result: Random forest model: AUC 0.909, sensitivity 86.5%, specificity 82.2%
records.study_design: retrospective diagnostic accuracy / prediction model study

records.title: Substance use initiation and the prediction of subsequent academic achievement.
records.clinical_problem: Do baseline structural brain MRI features and substance-use onset predict later academic achievement in adolescents, potentially identifying imaging biomarkers of vulnerability related to substance use?
records.patient_population: 170 physically healthy adolescents followed longitudinally (7th-12th grade)
records.model_description: A machine learning approach uses 336 baseline structural MRI-derived brain metrics (regional thickness, area, volume) together with academic and substance-use history to identify features predicting 11th/12th-grade GPA and to distinguish drinkers from non-drinkers.
records.headline_result: 16 of 336 baseline MRI features distinguished average-performing drinkers from non-drinkers; no single accuracy/AUC given
records.study_design: longitudinal cohort study with machine-learning feature selection

records.title: Using deep-learning algorithms to classify fetal brain ultrasound images as normal or abnormal.
records.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
records.model_family: deep-learning segmentation, classification and localization models
records.clinical_problem: recognizing an abnormal fetal brain on standard axial screening planes
records.patient_population: images from 10,251 normal and 2,529 abnormal pregnancies, with abnormality confirmed by neonatal ultrasound, follow-up or autopsy
records.model_description: Takes a standard axial fetal brain ultrasound image, segments the skull outline, classifies the brain as normal or abnormal, and overlays a heat map indicating where the abnormality is. Trained on a large hospital archive with outcomes confirmed after birth rather than by the reporting sonographer, and split at case rather than image level, which is the methodologically careful choice.
records.dataset_size: 15,372 normal and 14,047 abnormal images from 12,780 pregnancies
records.headline_result: classification accuracy 96.3%, sensitivity 96.9%, specificity 95.9%, AUC 0.989; lesions localized precisely in 61.6% of abnormal images and closely in a further 24.6%

records.title: Machine Learning in Fetal Cardiology: What to Expect.
records.clinical_problem: assessing fetal cardiac structure and function when the heart is small, moving, and often scanned by someone without fetal echocardiography training
records.patient_population: fetuses undergoing echocardiography
records.model_description: A short review for fetal cardiologists of where machine learning can help: improving the acquired image, extracting measurements and segmentations automatically, and supporting the prenatal diagnosis of cardiac remodeling and structural abnormality. Written as an orientation to the technology rather than an evaluation of specific models.

records.title: Early immune stimulation and childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia in Costa Rica: A comparison of statistical approaches.
records.exclusion_reason: no imaging; epidemiologic/statistical study of childhood leukemia risk factors, not radiology

records.title: Computer-aided diagnosis for World Health Organization-defined chest radiograph primary-endpoint pneumonia in children.
records.model_family: pixel-level texture classification on multi-scale Gaussian derivative features
records.clinical_problem: identifying WHO-defined primary-endpoint pneumonia on a child's chest radiograph, the definition used in vaccine efficacy and epidemiological studies
records.patient_population: 858 interpretable pediatric chest radiographs, 39% with primary-endpoint pneumonia by radiologist consensus
records.model_description: Targets a specific and consequential definition rather than pneumonia in general: the WHO primary-endpoint criterion is what vaccine trials are scored against, and it depends on three radiologists agreeing. Automating it would make large epidemiological studies tractable and remove reader variability from vaccine efficacy estimates. Three radiologists independently set the reference, and the harder task of separating primary-endpoint pneumonia from other infiltrate is reported separately.
records.headline_result: AUC 0.850 against radiologist consensus (sensitivity 76%, specificity 80%); AUC 0.810 separating primary-endpoint pneumonia from other infiltrate

records.title: Deep Learning Techniques for Automatic Detection of Embryonic Neurodevelopmental Disorders.
records.model_family: four-stage framework: transfer learning, deep feature extraction, feature reduction and classification, with feature fusion across pretrained networks
records.clinical_problem: detecting embryonic neurodevelopmental disorders on prenatal MRI, where up to three in a thousand pregnancies carry a brain defect and earlier detection changes counseling
records.patient_population: embryonic MRI images across various gestational ages
records.model_description: The argument is against the handcrafted-feature pipelines that preceded it: enhancement, segmentation and feature engineering each introduce choices, and a deep network learns from the raw image instead. Feature fusion across several pretrained backbones stands in for the training data that prenatal MRI cohorts do not have. Comparison is against prior work on embryonic images rather than a held-out external set, so the performance claim is relative.
records.headline_result: identified embryonic neurodevelopmental disorders from MRI across a range of gestational ages, performing competitively with prior work on embryonic images

records.title: Differences between children and adults in functional connectivity between the inferior frontal gyrus and extrastriate body area for gestural interaction.
records.exclusion_reason: conventional fMRI statistical analysis of gestural interaction differences between children and adults; no AI/ML component

records.title: Study of Effect of Sympathetic Nerve on Children's Brain Diseases Based on Analysis of Magnetic Resonance Imaging Kurtosis.

records.title: Toward point-of-care ultrasound estimation of fetal gestational age from the trans-cerebellar diameter using CNN-based ultrasound image analysis.
records.model_family: CNN-based pipeline for transcerebellar plane detection, transcerebellar diameter measurement and gestational age estimation
records.clinical_problem: dating a pregnancy at the point of care in low- and middle-income countries, where the two barriers are the steep learning curve for scanning and the lack of affordable portable devices
records.patient_population: conventional ultrasound data simulating the point-of-care task, with a first application to clinical video from a low-cost probe
records.model_description: Chooses the transcerebellar diameter rather than head circumference deliberately - it is a single linear measurement on one plane, which is what a short sweep from an inexperienced operator can realistically yield. The whole framework is specified around the hardware it would run on: a wireless probe, a phone or tablet, and on-device processing. Proof of concept, with the transfer to real low-cost probe video presented as the next step rather than as an achieved result.
records.headline_result: proof-of-concept accuracy for automatic transcerebellar plane detection, diameter measurement and gestational age estimation, with a first application to low-cost probe video

records.title: Functional Connectivity Fingerprints at Rest Are Similar across Youths and Adults and Vary with Genetic Similarity.
records.clinical_problem: using individual brain functional connectivity patterns to study genetic influences on network organization across development
records.patient_population: two twin datasets (adult, pediatric) and two repeat-scan datasets (adult, pediatric)
records.model_description: Input is resting-state functional connectivity MRI; support vector machine classifiers trained on one scan session are used to identify the same individual, or a co-twin, from an independent scan, to study how classification accuracy varies with genetic relatedness.
records.headline_result: 100% accuracy identifying individuals from a repeat scan; classifier accuracy decreased with decreasing genetic relatedness between twins

records.title: Prediction of Pulmonary to Systemic Flow Ratio in Patients With Congenital Heart Disease Using Deep Learning-Based Analysis of Chest Radiographs.
records.model_family: transfer-learned convolutional network regressing a continuous value from the chest radiograph
records.clinical_problem: quantifying pulmonary blood flow in congenital heart disease from the chest radiograph, which today is read subjectively and qualitatively and whose gold standard is an invasive catheterization
records.patient_population: 1031 cardiac catheterizations in 657 patients at a tertiary center from January 2005 to April 2019 (median age 3.4 years, IQR 1.2-8.6), with 78 patients / 100 catheterizations held out; mean Fick-derived pulmonary to systemic flow ratio 1.43 (SD 0.95)
records.model_description: Turns a qualitative impression - does the pulmonary vasculature look plethoric - into a number on the same scale as the catheter measurement, with the Fick-derived ratio from a simultaneous catheterization as ground truth. The comparison against three certified pediatric cardiologists reading the same films is what establishes the claim, and the clinically salient operating point (a ratio of 2.0 or more, the shunt magnitude that prompts intervention) is reported separately. A non-invasive stand-in for part of what catheterization is done to answer.
records.dataset_size: 1031 catheterizations in 657 patients; 100 held out for evaluation
records.headline_result: prediction of the pulmonary to systemic flow ratio from chest radiographs evaluated by intraclass correlation and Bland-Altman analysis, with the diagnostic concordance rate compared against three certified pediatric cardiologists
records.study_design: retrospective observational study with expert comparison

records.title: DW-Net: A cascaded convolutional neural network for apical four-chamber view segmentation in fetal echocardiography.
records.journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
records.model_family: dilated convolutional chain followed by a W-Net refinement stage
records.clinical_problem: outlining the seven key structures of the apical four-chamber view, from which congenital heart disease is judged
records.patient_population: 895 apical four-chamber views from fetal echocardiography
records.model_description: Segments seven anatomical structures in the fetal four-chamber view, contending with speckle, chambers that look alike, and boundaries that simply are not visible in places. A dilated convolution chain localizes the chambers across scales and a second stage sharpens the boundaries. The output is intended as the input to automated cardiac indices rather than as a diagnosis in itself.
records.headline_result: Dice 0.827, pixel accuracy 0.933, AUC 0.990, substantially above established segmentation methods

records.title: Ovarian torsion: developing a machine-learned algorithm for diagnosis.
records.model_family: machine-learned decision algorithm over discrete sonographic features
records.clinical_problem: diagnosing ovarian torsion quickly enough in girls with pelvic or abdominal pain, since delay causes irreversible ovarian ischemia and the ultrasound features are not pathognomonic
records.patient_population: all pediatric patients treated for surgically confirmed ovarian torsion at a quaternary pediatric hospital over 11 years, with a non-torsed control cohort of girls and young adults presenting to the emergency department between April 2015 and May 2016
records.model_description: Works on the features a radiologist already records rather than on pixels - ovarian volumes, medialized position relative to the mid-uterine line, Doppler signal, peripheral follicles, mass or cyst, free fluid - which makes the resulting algorithm something a reader can follow and argue with at the workstation. Surgical confirmation defines the cases, and the paper also reports how often each individual sonographic sign appears, which is useful on its own. Published in Pediatric Radiology and framed as an aid to the radiologist rather than a replacement.
records.dataset_size: 11 years of surgically confirmed torsion cases plus a contemporaneous non-torsed control cohort
records.headline_result: a machine-learned algorithm over sonographic features to aid radiologists in diagnosing ovarian torsion, with the frequency of each sonographic element quantified

records.title: Prediction of fetal weight at varying gestational age in the absence of ultrasound examination using ensemble learning.

records.patient_population: 15 analyzed children (of 21 enrolled), average age 5.9 years
records.model_description: In-house software automatically segments kidney parenchyma and aorta on dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI using convolutional neural network techniques, then fits a tracer kinetic model to calculate MRI-based GFR, compared against nuclear medicine 99mTc-DTPA GFR and creatinine-based eGFR.
records.headline_result: MR-GFR vs. NM-GFR Pearson r=0.98 (vs. eGFR r=0.73)

records.title: Artificial intelligence in bone age assessment: accuracy and efficiency of a novel fully automated algorithm compared to the Greulich-Pyle method.
records.model_family: fully automated AI bone age software
records.clinical_problem: bone age assessment against the Greulich-Pyle standard, in both accuracy and reading time
records.patient_population: 514 patients undergoing hand radiography for bone age
records.model_description: Compares a commercial-style automated bone age program against three blinded radiologists applying Greulich-Pyle, with a two-expert consensus as reference. The software was more accurate than the individual readers, not merely comparable, and cut reading time by 87%. Performance did not differ by sex. The design is the useful part: blinded readers, a consensus reference, and time measured alongside accuracy.
records.release_evidence: described as a novel AI software version; commercial availability not stated in the abstract
records.headline_result: mean absolute deviation from reference 0.34 years for the software versus 0.79 years for the readers (p < 0.001); reading time reduced by 87%

records.title: DeepFMRI: End-to-end deep learning for functional connectivity and classification of ADHD using fMRI.
records.model_family: end-to-end deep network (feature extractor, connectivity network, classifier)
records.clinical_problem: diagnosing ADHD, which currently rests entirely on behavioral assessment
records.patient_population: children in the public ADHD-200 dataset, contributed by several imaging sites
records.model_description: Takes preprocessed resting-state fMRI time series and outputs an ADHD diagnosis, learning the functional connectivity representation as part of the network rather than computing it beforehand. Because connectivity is learned end to end, the model can be interrogated for which regions carried the decision; here the frontal lobe dominated. Trained and tested on a public multi-site dataset, so the numbers are directly comparable with prior work.
records.headline_result: 73.1% accuracy at the New York University site (specificity 91.6%, sensitivity 65.5%), above prior state of the art
records.study_design: technical development on a public benchmark

records.title: Towards a new 3D classification for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis.
records.model_family: fuzzy c-means clustering over ten 3D parameters measured on biplanar radiograph reconstructions
records.clinical_problem: classifying adolescent idiopathic scoliosis in three dimensions, since the classifications surgeons plan from are two-dimensional and do not describe the deformity they are actually operating on
records.patient_population: patients from a multicenter adolescent idiopathic scoliosis database, all with biplanar radiographs and 3D reconstruction of the entire spine; cluster sizes 11 to 290
records.model_description: Unsupervised, and deliberately so - the point is to let the data propose subgroups rather than test an existing scheme. Eleven clusters emerged from ten 3D parameters, and the validation step is the one that matters for a taxonomy: four experienced spine surgeons from the SRS 3D Scoliosis Committee reviewed representative cases and unanimously agreed each cluster was a group current classifications do not name. Whether these subgroups predict surgical outcome is the unanswered question.
records.headline_result: eleven statistically distinct 3D subgroups, all judged by four spine surgeons to be undefined in current classifications

records.patient_population: children undergoing MRI
records.model_description: A RadioGraphics review of the commercially available ways to shorten a pediatric MRI (parallel imaging, simultaneous multislice, radial sampling, compressed sensing, automated protocol selection) and the ones still under investigation, including AI-based reconstruction and prospective motion correction. It is the practical counterpart to the model papers: it says which of these a department can buy today.
records.release_evidence: the reviewed acceleration techniques are described as commercially available products in clinical use

records.title: Distinguishing between paediatric brain tumour types using multi-parametric magnetic resonance imaging and machine learning: A multi-site study.

records.patient_population: children with brain tumours imaged at multiple centres
records.model_description: Most quantitative work in this area is single-centre and single-modality; this combines diffusion and perfusion imaging across sites. It also takes features from the whole brain as well as the tumour, and finds both contribute, which is a useful observation for a field that segments the lesion and discards everything else.
records.dataset_size: a multi-centre paediatric brain tumour cohort
records.headline_result: combining diffusion and perfusion features from tumour and whole brain gave the optimal classifier at over 80% predictive precision

records.title: Toward identifying reproducible brain signatures of obsessive-compulsive profiles: rationale and methods for a new global initiative.

records.title: Using Deep Learning Algorithms to Grade Hydronephrosis Severity: Toward a Clinical Adjunct.
records.clinical_problem: grading hydronephrosis severity on renal ultrasound, currently a subjective five-point judgment
records.patient_population: 673 patients aged 0 to 116 months (mean 16.5 months) with 2,420 sagittal renal ultrasound images across all five Society for Fetal Urology grades
records.model_description: Assigns a Society for Fetal Urology grade to a renal ultrasound image. The reported numbers are refreshingly candid: it places 94% of images correctly or within one grade, but only 51% exactly right on the five-way task, and the clinically decisive distinctions (low versus high grade, and grade II versus III) reach 78% and 71%. The authors frame it as a decision and teaching aid rather than a grader.
records.headline_result: 94% of images correct or within one grade on the five-way task (51% exactly correct); 78% accuracy for low versus high grade and 71% for grade II versus III
