records.model_description: Input: fetal echocardiography ultrasound video frames; output: classification of anatomical structures/views, using an incremental learning hierarchical network that can add new anatomy classes without forgetting prior ones.
records.headline_result: reduced accuracy depreciation over old tasks from 6.75% to 1.10% (balanced) and 6.95% to 1.89% (imbalanced) with incremental learning
records.study_design: retrospective algorithm development and internal validation

records.journal: Computational and mathematical methods in medicine

records.patient_population: 95 children with ADHD and 105 healthy controls from the ADHD-200 database
records.model_description: Dynamic features of intrinsic connectivity networks from resting-state fMRI, together with head-motion and other measures, are input to support vector regression models. The models estimate individual clinical scores of inattention and impulsivity in children with and without ADHD, with the sensorimotor network most associated with inattention and the executive control network with impulsivity.
records.dataset_size: 95 children with ADHD, 105 healthy controls (ADHD-200 database)
records.headline_result: Estimated scores correlated significantly with inattention (r = 0.4 ± 0.02, p < 0.01) and impulsivity (r = 0.31 ± 0.02, p < 0.01)

records.title: Novel Deep Learning Network Analysis of Electrical Stimulation Mapping-Driven Diffusion MRI Tractography to Improve Preoperative Evaluation of Pediatric Epilepsy.
records.model_family: deep convolutional neural network classifying diffusion MRI streamline trajectories, trained against electrical stimulation mapping findings
records.clinical_problem: identifying eloquent white matter before epilepsy surgery in children, so that resection margins spare motor, language and vision
records.patient_population: 89 children with focal epilepsy, with electrical stimulation mapping as the reference
records.model_description: The clinical validation goes well past accuracy. Three things are tested: whether the predicted pathways sit within the 1 cm spatial resolution of electrical stimulation mapping, whether respecting the predicted margins forecasts an absence of postoperative deficit (92% accurate), and whether the volume of language pathway actually removed tracks the postoperative change in language ability (R = 0.7). That last result is the one that turns a tract classifier into surgical evidence - it says the deficit follows the white matter you took, not only the cortex.
records.headline_result: 98% tract classification accuracy; preserved margins predicted absence of postoperative deficit with 92% accuracy; change in language pathway volume correlated with change in language ability (R = 0.7, p < 0.001)
records.study_design: retrospective model development with surgical outcome correlation

records.patient_population: trained on eight healthy adult volunteers and tested on eight pediatric patients
records.model_description: Segments the spine on tracked ultrasound and reconstructs a 3D volume from which the scoliosis angle is measured, offering a radiation-free substitute for the serial radiographs that scoliosis follow-up requires. The paper is honest about the adult-to-pediatric transfer: fuzzy segmentation metrics dropped when the network trained on adults was applied to children, and thresholds had to be re-optimized. Measurement error against radiography was nonetheless within 2.2 degrees.
records.dataset_size: eight adult volunteers for training, eight pediatric patients for testing
records.headline_result: maximum error 2.2 degrees against radiographic scoliosis measurement, with each measurement taking under one minute; segmentation metrics fell when translating from adults to children

records.title: Diagnostic performance of convolutional neural network-based Tanner-Whitehouse 3 bone age assessment system.
records.journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
records.model_family: convolutional neural network scoring the 13 RUS and 7 carpal bones of the Tanner-Whitehouse 3 system
records.clinical_problem: bone age assessment by the Tanner-Whitehouse 3 method, which is more granular than Greulich and Pyle but requires staging twenty individual bones and is correspondingly slow and variable
records.patient_population: 9059 clinical left hand radiographs from PACS between January 2012 and December 2016, split 8005 training / 804 validation / 250 test; the test set was also read by four endocrinologists and two radiologists
records.model_description: Automates the scoring system endocrinologists prefer but rarely use because of its cost in time, and reports agreement bone by bone rather than only in aggregate - which localizes where humans disagree with each other (capitate, hamate, middle and distal phalanges) and where they do not. Six expert readers as the comparator. One and a half seconds per image against many minutes by hand.
records.headline_result: root mean square 0.50 years against the reviewers' consensus, with accuracy better than the individual reviewers' estimates and image processing in 1.5 +/- 0.2 s
records.study_design: retrospective model development with multi-reader comparison

records.title: Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks for Neonatal Brain Image Segmentation.
records.model_family: single-modality and dual-modality 3D convolutional networks retrained for neonatal data
records.clinical_problem: segmenting gray matter, white matter and cerebrospinal fluid in the term-equivalent neonatal brain, where the tissue contrast is inverted relative to the older infant brain that existing networks were tuned on
records.patient_population: 24 pairs of neonatal T1 and T2 data from the Developing Human Connectome Project for retraining, with eight pairs for validation and eight for testing
records.model_description: Takes two networks that won on 6-month infant data and asks whether they transfer to newborns, where the contrast is inverted - a concrete test of how narrow pediatric segmentation models are. Dual-modality HyperDense-Net won, and the ablation is practically useful: single-modality LiviaNET did better on T2 than T1 across every tissue type, which tells a site with only one sequence which to acquire. Training and inference times are reported, which papers rarely do and departments need. The models are being made available through the Canadian Neonatal Brain Platform.
records.release_evidence: the networks will be continuously retrained and made available through the Canadian Neonatal Brain Platform
records.dataset_size: 40 neonatal T1/T2 pairs from the dHCP public dataset
records.headline_result: dual-modality HyperDense-Net reached Dice 0.94/0.95/0.92 for the three tissue types versus 0.90/0.90/0.88 for single-modality LiviaNET on T2

records.title: Artificial intelligence system can achieve comparable results to experts for bone age assessment of Chinese children with abnormal growth and development.
records.model_family: fully automated artificial intelligence system based on the Greulich and Pyle method, developed on Chinese children
records.clinical_problem: bone age assessment in the children it actually gets ordered for - those with abnormal growth and development - rather than in the developmentally normal children most systems are validated on
records.patient_population: developed on 8000 bone age radiographs from five medical centres across China, then tested on 745 consecutive children (360 boys, 385 girls) with abnormal growth and development from another tertiary centre in north China between January and October 2018
records.model_description: The test set is what makes this worth recording: consecutive children with abnormal growth and development, which is the referral population, evaluated at a centre separate from the five that supplied training data. Accuracy within one year was 84.6% overall, and the paper names exactly where it broke down - short stature with bone deformity, severe osteomalacia, and hands where carpals and phalanges mature at different rates. Those are precisely the children a bone age is ordered for.
records.dataset_size: 8000 development radiographs from five centres; 745 test cases from a sixth
records.headline_result: 84.60% accuracy within 1 year against a two-expert consensus reference (89.45% in the 12-18 year group), RMSE 0.76 years, mean absolute difference 0.58 years

records.title: Predicting motor outcome in preterm infants from very early brain diffusion MRI using a deep learning convolutional neural network (CNN) model.
records.model_family: patch-based convolutional neural network on fractional anisotropy maps
records.clinical_problem: identifying preterm infants headed for neuromotor delay early enough to refer them for intervention
records.patient_population: 77 infants born under 31 weeks gestation, imaged at 29-35 weeks postmenstrual age with motor outcome at 2 years corrected age
records.model_description: Predicts abnormal motor outcome at two years from diffusion MRI acquired before term, which is earlier than most preterm prediction work and therefore closer to when intervention could start. Classification is done on image patches and aggregated with a tuned threshold, and heat maps show which brain locations drove the abnormal predictions. Accuracy is moderate and the confidence intervals are wide on 77 infants.
records.dataset_size: 77 very preterm infants (48 normal, 29 abnormal outcome)
records.headline_result: sensitivity 70%, specificity 74%, AUC 0.72 for abnormal motor outcome at 2 years from MRI acquired at 29-35 weeks postmenstrual age

records.title: Neonatal Brain Microstructure and Machine-Learning-Based Prediction of Early Language Development in Children Born Very Preterm.
records.model_family: multivariate logistic models with leave-one-out cross-validation and exhaustive feature selection over diffusion tensor metrics
records.clinical_problem: identifying which very-low-birth-weight preterm infants are heading for language delay, early enough to intervene while neuroplasticity is greatest
records.patient_population: 102 very-low-birth-weight neonates (birthweight <= 1500 g, gestational age <= 32 weeks) recruited 2010-2011, of whom 92 returned for Bayley-III assessment at 18-22 months adjusted age
records.model_description: Near-term diffusion imaging used as a prognostic instrument rather than a descriptive one. Exhaustive feature selection narrows to three brain regions, which keeps the model small enough to interpret and to replicate. Separate models for composite, expressive and receptive language, with the strongest performance on expressive and receptive - and a side finding that cerebellar asymmetry tracked lower receptive scores. Nearly a third of the cohort scored below 85, so the outcome is common enough for the prediction to matter.
records.headline_result: sensitivity and specificity of 89%/86% for composite, 100%/90% for expressive and 100%/90% for receptive language risk

records.title: Deep Learning Measurement of Leg Length Discrepancy in Children Based on Radiographs.

This is the shape of the pediatric AI application most likely to pay for itself, an exact, repetitive measurement rather than a judgment call.
records.headline_result: correlation 0.99 with radiologist measurements (mean absolute error 0.45 cm for individual bones, 0.51 cm for discrepancy); 1 second versus 96 seconds per study

records.title: Ependymoma and pilocytic astrocytoma: Differentiation using radiomics approach based on machine learning.

The pediatric relevance is in the transfer step: a model pretrained on adult cohorts and fine-tuned on children reached higher performance for pneumonia than either alone, which is the practical recipe for a children's hospital with a smaller archive.

records.title: Multi-instance Deep Learning of Ultrasound Imaging Data for Pattern Classification of Congenital Abnormalities of the Kidney and Urinary Tract in Children.

Class activation mapping showed the network attending to anatomically meaningful parts of the kidney, and sensitivity (0.873) trails specificity (0.986), which is the wrong way round for a condition where a miss means renal damage.
records.headline_result: AUC 0.961 +/- 0.026 combining views with mean pooling, versus 0.796 and 0.815 for single sagittal and transverse images; specificity 0.986 and sensitivity 0.873

records.study_design: retrospective single-center technical development and evaluation study

records.title: Artificial intelligence (AI) in urology-Current use and future directions: An iTRUE study.

records.journal: Proceedings of SPIE--the International Society for Optical Engineering

records.title: Computer-aided diagnosis for fetal brain ultrasound images using deep convolutional neural networks.
records.journal: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
records.model_family: deep convolutional networks: segmentation of the craniocerebral region, then four-class classification, then class activation mapping for localization
records.clinical_problem: prenatal detection of five common fetal brain abnormalities on standard neurosonographic planes, where missed malformations change counseling and management
records.patient_population: real-world clinical fetal brain ultrasound images at the transventricular and transcerebellar standard planes
records.model_description: A three-stage design that gets weakly-supervised localization for free: the classifier is trained only on image-level labels, and lesions are then localized by class activation mapping rather than by any drawn box. That keeps the annotation burden low, and the numbers show the cost - classification is strong while localization overlap is modest. Positioned as support for junior operators, whose false negatives on fetal brain anomalies are the stated target.
records.headline_result: Dice 0.942 for craniocerebral segmentation, average F1 0.96 for classification, average mean IOU 0.497 for lesion localization

records.title: Discovering Salient Anatomical Landmarks by Predicting Human Gaze.
records.journal: Proceedings. IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging
records.clinical_problem: Automatically discovering anatomical landmarks that sonographers visually attend to during fetal neurosonography, to support image registration
records.patient_population: Fetal ultrasound scans with sonographer eye-gaze tracking
records.model_description: A CNN is trained to predict sonographer gaze-point (saliency) maps from fetal ultrasound video frames; local maxima of the predicted saliency maps become candidate anatomical landmarks, matched across images via CNN feature clustering
records.dataset_size: not stated exactly (full-length clinical fetal ultrasound scans)
records.headline_result: Landmark alignment errors of 4.1%-10.9% of fetal head long-axis length when used for affine registration

records.title: Self-Supervised Representation Learning for Ultrasound Video.
records.journal: Proceedings. IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging
records.model_family: self-supervised network trained to reorder a reshuffled video clip and predict the geometric transformation applied to it
records.clinical_problem: the annotation bottleneck in fetal ultrasound analysis, where expert labels are expensive and scarce and most methods cannot be trained without them
records.patient_population: unlabelled fetal ultrasound video
records.model_description: A pretraining recipe rather than a clinical model, and the pretext tasks are chosen with anatomy in mind: to put a shuffled clip back in order, the network has to know what the sweep is passing over, and to name the geometric transform it has to know the anatomy's orientation. No human annotation is used at any point. Representations transferred to standard plane detection and saliency prediction, which is the argument that what was learned is anatomical rather than incidental.
records.headline_result: meaningful transferable representations learned without any human annotation, transferring well to standard plane detection and saliency prediction

records.title: Healthy versus pathological learning transferability in shoulder muscle MRI segmentation using deep convolutional encoder-decoders.
records.journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
records.model_family: deep convolutional encoder-decoders with encoders pre-trained on ImageNet
records.clinical_problem: segmenting the four rotator cuff muscles on MRI in children with obstetrical brachial plexus palsy, so that muscle volume - and from it force - can be estimated without hours of manual tracing
records.patient_population: 24 shoulder examinations in children with unilateral obstetrical brachial plexus palsy, evaluated leave-one-out
records.model_description: A study framed around the two constraints that define pediatric musculoskeletal AI: very little annotated data, and pathological anatomy that looks nothing like the healthy training examples. It answers the transferability question directly by comparing learning schemes, and the winner combines healthy and pathological annotated data with ImageNet pre-training rather than choosing between them. Supraspinatus, the smallest and most atrophied muscle, is where it degrades.
records.headline_result: Dice 82.4% deltoid, 82.0% infraspinatus, 71.0% supraspinatus and 82.8% subscapularis, with surface estimation errors below 83 mm2 except supraspinatus at 134.6 mm2

records.title: Artificial intelligence for interpretation of segments of whole body MRI in CNO: pilot study comparing radiologists versus machine learning algorithm.
records.clinical_problem: assessing treatment response on whole-body MRI in chronic nonbacterial osteomyelitis (CNO)
records.patient_population: patients under age 16 with CNO treated with pamidronate at a tertiary pediatric hospital
records.model_description: Pre- and post-pamidronate whole-body MRI segments of the distal femur and proximal tibia are compared by a machine learning algorithm that classifies treatment response (improved, worsened, stable), benchmarked against a panel of pediatric radiologists as ground truth.
records.headline_result: sensitivity 100% for detecting disease improvement/worsening, but only 33.3% of samples classified correctly overall vs. radiologist ground truth
records.study_design: retrospective single-center pilot diagnostic accuracy study

records.title: Real-time diameter of the fetal aorta from ultrasound.
records.model_family: CNN with convolutional gated recurrent unit (C-GRU) and a periodicity-aware loss function
records.clinical_problem: real-time measurement of fetal aortic vascular diameter from ultrasound
records.patient_population: 25 real ultrasound sequences from third-trimester pregnancy checks, plus 1,000 synthetic sequences
records.model_description: A neural network combining CNN feature extraction, a convolutional GRU temporal module, and a periodicity-aware loss (CyclicLoss) measures the fetal abdominal aorta diameter in real time from ultrasound video.
records.dataset_size: 25 real ultrasound sequences plus 1,000 synthetic sequences
records.headline_result: MSE 0.09 mm^2 (vs. 0.31 state-of-the-art); relative error 5.3% (vs. 8.1%); 289 frames/sec

records.title: Planning stereoelectroencephalography using automated lesion detection: Retrospective feasibility study.
records.model_family: neural network classifier over cortical surface features from structural MRI
records.clinical_problem: planning stereoelectroencephalography electrode placement in children with drug-resistant epilepsy whose MRI is diagnostically complex, where getting the electrodes to the seizure onset zone is the whole point of the procedure
records.patient_population: three cohorts: 34 patients with visible focal cortical dysplasia for training and cross-validation, 20 pediatric healthy controls for specificity, and 34 sEEG patients for the implantation feasibility analysis
records.model_description: Rather than reporting lesion-detection accuracy, the study asks whether the detected lesions land where the seizures actually start, by coregistering electrode contacts with the classifier's predictions and letting clinical neurophysiologists define the onset contacts. Specificity in controls was 100%, which matters more than sensitivity for a tool that would add electrodes. The striking cases are the three patients where sEEG localized nothing and the classifier flagged abnormalities that had not been implanted.
records.dataset_size: 34 focal cortical dysplasia patients, 20 controls, 34 sEEG patients
records.headline_result: 74% sensitivity in patients with radiologically defined lesions and 100% specificity in controls; 86% of histopathologically confirmed focal cortical dysplasias detected, with 62% colocalization between classifier output and seizure onset zone contacts

records.title: Functional brain connectivity in ex utero premature infants compared to in utero fetuses.

records.title: Mimicking the radiologists' workflow: Estimating pediatric hand bone age with stacked deep neural networks.
records.model_family: two-stage system: a detector network localizing ossification areas, then sex- and region-specific regression networks estimating age from each area
records.clinical_problem: bone age estimation from the left hand radiograph, which pediatric endocrinologists order routinely and which requires substantial expertise to read
records.patient_population: pediatric hand radiographs, evaluated on the RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Challenge test set
records.model_description: Deliberately reproduces the Tanner-Whitehouse workflow - find each ossification area, score it, combine - rather than regressing an age from the whole image, and the payoff is interpretability: a radiologist can see which areas drove the estimate and disagree with one of them. The authors make the case explicitly against purely encoder-based architectures, which give a number and no account of it. Competitive on the RSNA challenge test set while remaining explainable, and the detector trains from a small annotated set.
records.dataset_size: RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Challenge data
records.headline_result: average error 4.56 months on the RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Challenge test set, with self-explanatory per-area results
records.study_design: retrospective model development on a public benchmark

records.title: Combined Denoising and Suppression of Transient Artifacts in Arterial Spin Labeling MRI Using Deep Learning.

records.title: Efficient Pneumonia Detection in Chest Xray Images Using Deep Transfer Learning.
records.model_family: weighted ensemble of ResNet18, Xception, InceptionV3, DenseNet121 and MobileNetV3

records.patient_population: children in the Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Center pneumonia dataset

records.headline_result: computational models performed similarly to human operators on common plane classification; fine-grained brain-plane categorization remained harder

records.patient_population: 142 childhood cancer patients (abdominal planning CTs) with simulated Wilms' tumor radiotherapy plans
records.model_description: An evolutionary machine-learning algorithm links anatomical features (extracted from digitally reconstructed radiographs simulating historical films) and radiotherapy plan/record features to predict 3D dose-volume metrics for organs at risk, without needing a surrogate anatomy.
records.dataset_size: 142 planning CTs, 300 artificial plans, 42,600 simulated dose distributions
records.headline_result: mean absolute error <=0.6 Gy for organs fully in/out of field; <=1.7-2.9 Gy or <=13% for organs at the field edge

records.title: Connectome mapping with edge density imaging differentiates pediatric mild traumatic brain injury from typically developing controls: proof of concept.
records.model_family: principal component analysis + support vector machine
records.clinical_problem: distinguishing pediatric mild traumatic brain injury from typically developing controls when conventional imaging is normal
records.patient_population: 24 adolescents (14 with mild TBI, 10 typically developing controls), aged 10-16 years
records.model_description: Diffusion MRI fiber tractography is used to compute edge density imaging maps of brain connectivity; PCA and an SVM classifier applied to these maps distinguish mild TBI from typically developing controls, compared against neurocognitive tests and conventional fractional anisotropy.

records.title: Achieving accurate estimates of fetal gestational age and personalised predictions of fetal growth based on data from an international prospective cohort study: a population-based machine learning study.
records.model_family: machine-learning regression on serial fetal biometry
records.clinical_problem: dating a pregnancy accurately in the second and third trimesters, and forecasting how a given fetus will grow
records.patient_population: healthy, well-nourished participants in the multicentre INTERGROWTH-21st study, with generalization tested in the more heterogeneous INTERBIO-21st cohort
records.model_description: Estimates gestational age from ultrasound biometry measured across a ten-week window, and separately forecasts a specific fetus's growth trajectory six weeks ahead. The methodological move that makes it credible is the reference standard: accuracy is judged against the exactly known intervals between a woman's own scan visits rather than her recalled last menstrual period, which is itself unreliable. Generalization was checked in a different, more heterogeneous population.
records.headline_result: gestational age between 20 and 30 weeks estimated to within 3 days with 95% confidence, a prediction interval 3-5 times narrower than previous algorithms; 6-week growth forecasts accurate to within 7 days

records.title: Temporal-plus epilepsy in children: A connectomic analysis in magnetoencephalography.

records.title: Deep white matter analysis (DeepWMA): Fast and consistent tractography segmentation.
records.model_family: CNN classifier on a 2D multi-channel fiber descriptor (FiberMap)
records.clinical_problem: identifying named white matter tracts consistently enough to quantify them across very different subjects
records.patient_population: 597 diffusion MRI scans from six independently acquired populations spanning 1 day to 82 years, including neonates and patients with brain tumors
records.model_description: Sorts the individual streamlines of a whole-brain tractogram into 54 named deep white matter tracts by classifying each fiber from an encoding of its spatial trajectory. The claim that matters clinically is consistency across subjects who look nothing alike: it identified over 99% of tracts across all subjects, including day-old neonates and brains distorted by space-occupying tumors, where registration-based methods break down.
records.dataset_size: 1 million labeled fiber samples for training; 597 diffusion MRI scans for testing
records.headline_result: 90.99% fiber classification accuracy in training; over 99% of tracts successfully identified across all test subjects including neonates and tumor patients

records.title: Spatio-temporal visual attention modelling of standard biometry plane-finding navigation.
records.model_family: multi-task network with a feature extractor, a bidirectional convolutional LSTM temporal attention module and an auxiliary video classification module, trained with a soft dynamic time warping loss
records.clinical_problem: how an experienced sonographer navigates to a standard biometry plane - abdomen, trans-ventricular head and femur - and whether that search behaviour can be learned and used to guide plane detection
records.patient_population: 280 video clips of 3-7 seconds each, one per biometry plane, with simultaneously recorded gaze tracking from an experienced sonographer
records.model_description: Trained on where an expert actually looked, frame by frame, which is a supervision signal almost nobody has. The model learns to reproduce the visual search rather than the final answer, and the clinical relevance is then tested by using the predicted attention to find the plane - an auxiliary task that validates the primary one. Adding time to a previously spatial-only model improved every saliency metric, which says the navigation is a trajectory and not a series of independent glances.
records.headline_result: best model outperforms the previous spatial model on all static and dynamic saliency metrics, with standard plane detection F1 of 83.7% (abdomen), 89.9% (head) and 81.1% (femur)

records.title: Deep Predictive Motion Tracking in Magnetic Resonance Imaging: Application to Fetal Imaging.
records.model_family: recurrent neural network with spatial and temporal encoder-decoders, predicting motion parameters from sequences of acquired slices
records.clinical_problem: fetal motion during MRI, which today is handled by an operator watching slices go by and re-acquiring stacks - operator-dependent, expensive in scanner time, and hard for a pregnant woman to tolerate

records.title: Automatic Measurements of Fetal Lateral Ventricles in 2D Ultrasound Images Using Deep Learning.
records.model_family: deep convolutional network for pixel-wise segmentation, followed by morphological pixel-per-centimeter estimation and minimum enclosing rectangle measurement
records.clinical_problem: measuring the width of the fetal lateral ventricles, the core measurement of antenatal neurosonographic assessment, which is subjective and depends on the scanner's experience

records.model_description: Deliberately broader than the single-disease pediatric models that preceded it: four disease categories plus normal, rather than pneumonia versus not. The honest conclusion in the abstract is the useful one - the scheme is strong at the normal-versus-abnormal decision and much weaker at telling the specific diseases apart, with per-class accuracies between 72% and 86%. That is the profile of a triage tool, and the authors say so.
records.headline_result: 92.47% accuracy for abnormal versus normal; per-class accuracy 71.94% bronchiolitis/bronchitis, 72.19% bronchopneumonia, 85.42% lobar pneumonia, 85.71% pneumothorax and 80.00% normal

records.journal: Medical image computing and computer-assisted intervention : MICCAI ... International Conference on Medical Image Computing and Computer-Assisted Intervention

records.title: Rethinking Greulich and Pyle: A Deep Learning Approach to Pediatric Bone Age Assessment Using Pediatric Trauma Hand Radiographs.
records.model_family: convolutional neural network trained to predict chronological age directly, compared against a Greulich and Pyle-trained deep learning model
records.clinical_problem: whether bone age assessment should still be anchored to the Greulich and Pyle atlas, built from a narrow mid-century American population, or learned from a contemporary pediatric population directly
records.patient_population: 15 129 frontal pediatric trauma hand radiographs from Children's Hospital of New York (December 2009 to May 2017) for training, and 214 trauma hand radiographs from Hasbro Children's Hospital as an independent test set
records.model_description: The premise is the interesting part: trauma hand radiographs from developmentally normal children are an enormous, unused, unbiased sample of what a modern pediatric hand looks like at a known chronological age - so the atlas can be replaced rather than automated. It beat both the Greulich and Pyle-trained network and two pediatric radiologists reading by the atlas, on an independent hospital's films. The authors flag a systematic bias toward over-predicting age in younger children.
records.headline_result: mean absolute error 11.1 months versus 12.9 for the Greulich and Pyle-trained network (P = .0005), 14.6 for radiologist 1 and 16.0 for radiologist 2 (both P < .0001)
records.study_design: retrospective model development with external validation and reader comparison

records.model_description: This review surveys ultrasound imaging features used to screen for Down syndrome in the first (11-14 weeks) and second (15-22 weeks) trimesters, such as nasal bone hypoplasia/absence, nuchal thickness, fetal heart rate, and limb-bone shortening, and introduces the use of deep-learning techniques for identifying these features, without presenting a specific model or its performance.

records.title: Automatic fetal brain extraction from 2D in utero fetal MRI slices using deep neural network
records.model_family: two-stage fully convolutional network (shallow FCN + multi-scale FCN)
records.clinical_problem: automatic extraction (segmentation) of the fetal brain for downstream MRI analysis
records.patient_population: 88 2D in-utero fetal MRI scans
records.model_description: A two-step deep-learning pipeline first uses a shallow fully convolutional network to rapidly locate and crop a region of interest around the fetal brain on 2D in-utero MRI slices, then refines the segmentation with a deeper multi-scale FCN using dilated convolutions and residual learning to produce the final brain mask. Evaluated on 88 fetal MRI scans, it located the fetal brain with 100% accuracy and processed one MRI stack in about 6 seconds.
records.headline_result: Brain localization accuracy 100%; Dice score 0.958, sensitivity 0.950, precision 0.968; ~6 seconds per MRI stack

records.model_description: MCS-CF preprocesses resting-state functional MRI, extracts functional-connectivity and amplitude-of-low-frequency-fluctuation features, and uses a Modified Cuckoo Search algorithm to select the most useful features before classifying subjects as ADHD or control with a cascade-forest (gcForest) classifier. It was evaluated on the public ADHD-200 dataset and reported using accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, intended to improve on prior fMRI-based ADHD classifiers' speed and accuracy.

records.title: Automated measurement network for accurate segmentation and parameter modification in fetal head ultrasound images

records.model_description: An end-to-end fully convolutional network segments the fetal head on 2D ultrasound images while a parallel regression branch predicts biparietal diameter (BPD) and occipitofrontal diameter (OFD); head circumference is then derived from the segmentation. The network uses a feature pyramid with an attention mechanism and a region-of-interest pooling layer tailored to the elliptical head shape, trained and evaluated on the public HC18 dataset, and is reported to outperform existing fetal head measurement methods.

records.title: Non-Local U-Nets for Biomedical Image Segmentation
records.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
records.model_family: U-Net with flexible global aggregation blocks replacing stacked local operators, usable as size-preserving, down-sampling and up-sampling layers
records.clinical_problem: biomedical image segmentation, evaluated on the 3D multimodality isointense infant brain MR segmentation task

records.model_description: An architecture paper whose chosen benchmark is the infant brain, which says something about how that task became the proving ground for segmentation methods. records.title: Segmentation of uterus and placenta in MR images using a fully convolutional neural network
records.model_family: fully convolutional network for 3D segmentation with minimal operator interaction guiding placental localization
records.clinical_problem: segmenting the uterine cavity and placenta on fetal MRI, which is needed to detect abnormalities affecting maternal and fetal health and to estimate their volumes

records.model_description: Accepts a small amount of operator interaction rather than insisting on full automation, and uses it where it helps most - localizing the placenta, whose position varies and whose boundary with the uterine wall is ambiguous. Reporting volume estimation error alongside Dice is the right endpoint, since placental volume is what clinical studies use; the gap between the two structures (2% versus 9% volume error) shows how much harder the placenta is.

records.title: ADHD Identification using Convolutional Neural Network with Seed-based Approach for fMRI Data
records.journal: Proceedings of the 2020 9th International Conference on Software and Computer Applications
records.model_family: convolutional neural network over seed-based functional connectivity maps from default mode network regions

records.title: Detection of Pediatric Pneumonia from Chest X-Ray Images using CNN and Transfer Learning
records.journal: 2020 3rd International Conference on Emerging Technologies in Computer Engineering: Machine Learning and Internet of Things (ICETCE)
records.model_family: a basic CNN plus VGG16, VGG19 and InceptionV3 by transfer learning
records.clinical_problem: detecting pneumonia on children's chest radiographs where an expert reader is unavailable or costly
records.patient_population: a pediatric pneumonia dataset of 2992 pneumonia and 2972 normal chest radiographs, tested on 854 pneumonia and 849 normal images
records.model_description: A straightforward four-architecture comparison on the standard pediatric pneumonia benchmark, with all four exceeding 97%. Its interest is as a data point on how saturated this particular benchmark is - when a basic CNN and three pretrained networks all land within a point of each other, the remaining differences are noise and the task has stopped discriminating between methods.
records.headline_result: over 97% accuracy from all four models

records.title: Multi-Branch Deformable Convolutional Neural Network with Label Distribution Learning for Fetal Brain Age Prediction
records.journal: 2020 IEEE 17th International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI)
records.model_family: multi-branch deformable convolutional network aggregating multi-view MRI stacks, trained with label distribution learning
records.clinical_problem: predicting fetal brain age from MRI for developmental analysis and early diagnosis of congenital anomalies, when the fetal brain sits at an arbitrary position and orientation among surrounding organs
records.patient_population: 289 fetal brain MRI subjects
records.model_description: Two adaptations to fetal MRI specifically. Deformable convolutions let the receptive field follow a brain that is arbitrarily rotated and partly obscured by adjacent organs, rather than assuming a canonical pose. And label distribution learning treats the age label as a distribution rather than a point, which both reflects the real uncertainty of gestational dating and helps with a 289-subject sample. Multiple views are aggregated across branches rather than one stack being chosen.
records.headline_result: promising fetal brain age prediction on a 289-subject fetal MRI dataset using deformable convolutions, label distribution learning and multi-view aggregation

records.title: Vertebra-Focused Landmark Detection for Scoliosis Assessment

records.title: Placenta Imaging Workshop 2018 report: Multiscale and multimodal approaches.

records.title: Neuroanatomical features and its usefulness in classification of patients with PANDAS.
records.model_family: multivariate pattern analysis over voxel-based morphometry, diffusion tensor and surface features
records.clinical_problem: whether pediatric autoimmune neuropsychiatric disorder associated with streptococci has a neuroanatomical signature that could serve as a biomarker, in a condition whose very existence as an entity rests on distinguishing it from ordinary early-onset OCD
records.patient_population: 14 pediatric patients with PANDAS paired with 14 healthy subjects
records.model_description: The first pattern-analysis study of this early-onset OCD subtype, and its negative results are as informative as the positive one: diffusion metrics and every cortical surface feature showed no group difference, while gray matter did, and only gray matter supported classification. The authors read that as consistent with an immune rather than a developmental origin. Fourteen pairs, so 75% accuracy is a signal that the question is worth pursuing rather than a usable test.
records.headline_result: 75% accuracy classifying PANDAS from controls using gray matter features; no significant group differences in diffusion or cortical surface measures

records.title: The developmental neural substrates of item and serial order components of verbal working memory.
records.exclusion_reason: developmental fMRI study of item versus serial order verbal working memory in 59 children aged 7-12; no machine learning model

records.title: Breathe New Life Into Your Chest CT Exams: Using Advanced Acquisition and Postprocessing Techniques.
records.exclusion_reason: general adult-focused chest CT technique review; pediatric imaging mentioned only in passing; no specific AI/ML model described

records.title: Supervised machine learning quality control for magnetic resonance artifacts in neonatal data sets.
records.clinical_problem: automated quality control detection of major artifacts (e.g., motion) in neonatal brain MRI datasets
records.patient_population: preterm newborns
records.model_description: Input: 2D transverse T2-weighted neonatal brain MRI images, represented by 70 focus/texture/noise/natural-scene-statistics features; output: automated QC Pass/Fail classification.
records.release_evidence: tested an open source method to detect major artifacts among 2D neonatal MRI via supervised machine learning
records.dataset_size: 1020 two-dimensional T2-weighted MRI images of preterm newborns
records.headline_result: Best model (RUSBoost): 85% positive predictive value, 75% sensitivity for QC Fail images

records.title: Computer-aided diagnosis of congenital abnormalities of the kidney and urinary tract in children based on ultrasound imaging data by integrating texture image features and deep transfer learning image features.
records.model_family: support vector machine on transfer-learned deep features combined with conventional texture features
records.clinical_problem: identifying congenital abnormalities of the kidney and urinary tract on the ultrasound children already receive
records.patient_population: 50 children with congenital abnormalities of the kidney and urinary tract and 50 controls, imaged during routine care
records.model_description: Combines features learned by a pretrained network with hand-computed texture features and shows the combination beats either alone, which is the useful methodological finding on a 100-child dataset where a deep model alone would overfit. Uses images from routine clinical care rather than a curated research acquisition.
records.headline_result: AUC 0.92, 0.88 and 0.92 for left, right and bilateral abnormal kidney scans, significantly better than either feature set alone (p < 0.001)

records.title: Comparative effectiveness of convolutional neural network (CNN) and recurrent neural network (RNN) architectures for radiology text report classification.
records.model_family: CNN with GloVe embeddings, and a domain-phrase attention hierarchical recurrent network
records.clinical_problem: extracting whether a CT report says there is a pulmonary embolus, at scale and across institutions
records.patient_population: adult and pediatric patients whose thoracic CT reports were collected from four healthcare centers
records.model_description: Reads a free-text thoracic CT report and decides whether it describes a pulmonary embolus. The recurrent model builds up word, sentence and document representations and weights domain-specific phrases through an attention mechanism. The finding that matters for a children's hospital is the transfer: models trained on adult reports classified pediatric reports at the same F1 of 0.99, which is not what happens with image models.
records.dataset_size: over 7,370 thoracic CT reports from four centers
records.headline_result: F1 0.99 for pulmonary embolus in adults and 0.99 in the pediatric population, beating the rule-based PEFinder on multi-institutional test sets

records.title: Beyond Human Perception: Sexual Dimorphism in Hand and Wrist Radiographs Is Discernible by a Deep Learning Model.
records.model_family: deep convolutional neural network with class activation maps
records.clinical_problem: whether hand and wrist radiographs carry a sex signal, which bears on bone age assessment (a sex-specific reference) and on forensic identification
records.patient_population: 1531 hand radiographs of children and adults aged 5 to 70 years, plus a small exploratory sample of 44 patients with sexual developmental disorders or transgender identity
records.model_description: The clearest demonstration in this database of a model doing something people cannot: 95.9% against two radiologists at 58% and 46%, and the radiologists could not find the pattern even when shown the model's heat maps. The exploratory arm is the thoughtful part - in 44 patients with sexual developmental disorders or transgender identity, agreement with phenotypic sex fell to 77.8%, which raises the question of what the model is measuring and complicates any forensic use.
records.headline_result: 95.9% accuracy (kappa 0.92) versus 58% and 46% for two radiologists; agreement with phenotypic sex fell to 77.8% in patients with sexual developmental disorders or transgender identity
records.study_design: retrospective model development with reader comparison

records.title: The RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Machine Learning Challenge.
records.clinical_problem: skeletal maturity (bone age) assessment
records.patient_population: children whose hand radiographs make up a curated 14,236-image challenge dataset
records.model_description: Not one model but a public competition: RSNA released a curated set of 14,236 pediatric hand radiographs with reference bone ages and invited teams to submit algorithms, scored on mean absolute distance in months. Almost every entry used convolutional neural networks. The paper reports what a coordinated community effort achieved and is the reference point later bone-age papers compare against.
records.release_evidence: the data set was made available to registered challenge participants; the abstract says nothing about releasing the models
records.headline_result: best five entries achieved mean absolute distance of 4.2 to 4.5 months

records.title: Using an artificial neural network to predict traumatic brain injury.
records.model_family: artificial neural network over radiologist-interpreted CT findings
records.clinical_problem: ruling in clinically relevant traumatic brain injury in children so that the rest can be discharged on an evidence-based basis rather than admitted for observation
records.patient_population: 12 902 children from the Pediatric Emergency Care Applied Research Network traumatic brain injury dataset
records.model_description: Built on PECARN, the dataset that produced the clinical decision rule pediatric emergency medicine already uses, and aimed at the same decision - who can safely go home. The inputs are the radiologist's CT findings rather than the pixels, so this is decision support layered on the report rather than image analysis. Sensitivity above 99% is the operating point the problem demands, since the cost of a missed clinically relevant injury is not symmetric with the cost of an observation stay.
records.headline_result: prediction of clinically relevant traumatic brain injury with greater than 99% sensitivity and AUC 0.99
records.study_design: retrospective secondary analysis of a multi-center cohort

records.title: Predictive connectome subnetwork extraction with anatomical and connectivity priors.
records.journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
records.clinical_problem: identifying predictive brain connectome subnetworks for developmental outcomes in preterm neonates and for autism classification
records.patient_population: 168 structural connectomes of preterm neonates; 1,013 resting-state functional connectomes from the ABIDE database
records.model_description: a sparse linear regression model with anatomical and connectivity priors takes a structural or functional connectome as input and outputs a predicted cognitive/neuromotor developmental outcome (preterm cohort) or autism spectrum category (ABIDE cohort) via a learned weighted subnetwork
records.study_design: retrospective algorithm development and validation study using two cohorts

records.title: Functional connectivity changes associated with fMRI neurofeedback of right inferior frontal cortex in adolescents with ADHD.

records.title: MR Imaging-Based Radiomic Signatures of Distinct Molecular Subgroups of Medulloblastoma.
records.clinical_problem: predicting the molecular subgroup of pediatric medulloblastoma (sonic hedgehog, group 3, group 4) from pre-treatment MRI, without tissue sampling
records.patient_population: 109 pediatric patients with medulloblastoma from 3 children's hospitals, January 2001 to January 2014
records.model_description: 590 radiomic features extracted from MRI tumor segmentations (T1- and T2-weighted) are used with feature selection and cross-validated classifiers to output a predicted molecular subgroup label for each medulloblastoma.
records.dataset_size: 109 pediatric patients (3-cohort multi-institutional dataset), 590 radiomic features
records.headline_result: AUC 0.79, 0.70, 0.83 (SHH, group 3, group 4) with double 10-fold cross-validation on combined cohort; AUC 0.70-0.73 (SHH) and 0.76-0.80 (group 4) with independent 3-dataset cross-validation
records.study_design: multi-institutional retrospective radiomics/machine-learning study with cross-cohort validation

records.title: Young children's neural processing of their mother's voice: An fMRI study.
records.exclusion_reason: basic developmental neuroscience fMRI study of children's neural processing of their mother's voice; no AI/ML model

records.title: Neural architecture supporting active emotion processing in children: A multivariate approach.
records.clinical_problem: classifying emotional condition and age group from task fMRI activation during naturalistic emotion processing
records.patient_population: 21 adults and 30 children (mean age 7.75 years) undergoing task fMRI
records.model_description: BOLD fMRI activation recorded while children and adults watched movie clips portraying positive, negative, and neutral emotions is used to train multivariate support vector machines. The models classify the emotional condition being viewed and distinguish children from adults within each condition, based on activity in sensory, socio-emotional, and emotion-regulation regions.
records.headline_result: 61.44% accuracy classifying emotional condition across all participants; adults vs. children significantly distinguished within each condition (p < 0.05)

records.title: No evidence of differences in cognitive control in children with autism spectrum disorder or obsessive-compulsive disorder: An fMRI study.
records.exclusion_reason: fMRI group-comparison study of cognitive control in autism and OCD; no trained AI/ML diagnostic model

records.title: Automated Fetal Head Detection and Circumference Estimation from Free-Hand Ultrasound Sweeps Using Deep Learning in Resource-Limited Countries.
records.model_family: VGG-inspired detection network followed by a U-net measurement network
records.clinical_problem: estimating gestational age where there is no sonographer, using a sweep protocol any health worker can learn in a day
records.patient_population: 183 pregnant women at St. Luke's Hospital, Wolisso, Ethiopia
records.model_description: Works from sweeps acquired with a fixed protocol that requires no knowledge of ultrasound, and which will usually not contain the standard plane at all. One network finds the frames containing the fetal head, a second measures head circumference in those frames, and gestational age follows from the Hadlock curve. Validated against standard-plane measurements taken by an experienced sonographer on the same women.
records.headline_result: most automatically estimated gestational ages fell within the 2.5th to 97.5th centile interval of the Hadlock curve relative to reference measurements

records.title: Feasibility study of intelligent autonomous determination of the bladder voiding need to treat bedwetting using ultrasound and smartphone ML techniques : Intelligent autonomous treatment of bedwetting.

records.title: Diagnostic performance of an artificial neural network to predict excess body fat in children.
records.exclusion_reason: predicts excess body fat from clinical/anthropometric variables (age, height, weight, waist circumference); DXA imaging used only as reference standard, not as AI model input

records.title: EEG-based age-prediction models as stable and heritable indicators of brain maturational level in children and adolescents.
records.exclusion_reason: random forest and relevance vector machine age prediction from resting-state EEG power in children and adolescents; electroencephalography, not imaging

records.clinical_problem: skeletal maturity (bone age) assessment

records.study_design: editorial / commentary on a machine-learning challenge

records.title: Unbiased age-specific structural brain atlases for Chinese pediatric population.
records.clinical_problem: whether a pediatric brain atlas built on one population is valid for children of another
records.patient_population: 328 cognitively normal Chinese children aged 6-12, with two independent validation datasets of 114 and 71 children
records.model_description: A set of age-specific brain templates built from Chinese children, made because the widely used NIH pediatric atlases are derived from Caucasian children. The comparison found substantial anatomical differences in frontal and parietal regions, and using the matched atlas gave significantly better tissue segmentation and brain-age prediction in Chinese children. It is a concrete demonstration that population mismatch in a reference dataset degrades downstream results.
records.release_evidence: released on the NITRC website at https://www.nitrc.org/projects/chn-pd
records.dataset_size: 328 children for atlas construction; 185 children across two validation datasets
records.headline_result: significantly higher accuracy than the NIH pediatric atlases for both brain-age prediction and tissue segmentation in Chinese children

records.title: Identifying lesions in paediatric epilepsy using morphometric and textural analysis of magnetic resonance images.
records.clinical_problem: identifying epileptogenic lesions (focal cortical dysplasia) in children with intractable epilepsy, including MRI-negative cases
records.patient_population: pediatric cohort with medically intractable epilepsy, MRI-positive and MRI-negative for focal cortical dysplasia
records.model_description: T1-weighted, T2-weighted and FLAIR MRI sequences are processed with morphometric and gray-level co-occurrence texture features, which are input to a 2-step Bayesian classifier that flags candidate epileptogenic lesions, evaluated separately in MRI-positive and MRI-negative epilepsy cases.
records.headline_result: combining all three sequences: 97% subjectwise sensitivity in MRI-positive cases and 70% in MRI-negative cases; 100% healthy-subject rejection

records.title: The analysis of the effects of acute rheumatic fever in childhood on cardiac disease with data mining.
records.exclusion_reason: Data mining of clinical/laboratory records (not image-based AI) to analyze the cardiac effects of childhood rheumatic fever; chest x-ray findings ('teleNormal', 'cardiomegaly') are used only as an input attribute label, not analyzed by AI.

records.title: Characterization of Autism Spectrum Disorder across the Age Span by Intrinsic Network Patterns.

records.title: White Matter Connectome Edge Density in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders: Potential Imaging Biomarkers Using Machine-Learning Models.
records.model_family: machine learning models (naive Bayes, random forest, SVM, neural networks)
records.clinical_problem: identifying autism spectrum disorder from white matter connectome imaging biomarkers
records.patient_population: 14 boys with autism spectrum disorder and 33 typically developing boys, aged 8-12 years
records.model_description: Diffusion MRI-derived edge density and tract-based connectome metrics go in; machine-learning classifiers (naive Bayes, random forest, SVM, neural network) output identification of children with autism spectrum disorder.
records.dataset_size: 14 boys with ASD, 33 typically developing boys
records.headline_result: best model (random forest, edge density metrics) accuracy 75.3%, specificity 97.0%, PPV 81.5%
records.study_design: case-control diffusion MRI connectome study comparing multiple machine-learning classifiers

records.title: A review on lung boundary detection in chest X-rays.
records.journal: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
records.clinical_problem: isolating the lungs on a chest radiograph, the step every downstream chest analysis depends on
records.patient_population: adults and children in the reviewed studies, with particular attention to pediatric and deformed-lung cases
records.model_description: A review of lung segmentation on chest radiographs from 2006 to 2017, classifying methods into rule-based, pixel-classification, model-based, hybrid and deep-learning families. Its finding for a children's hospital is a gap: almost all published algorithms are validated on adult posteroanterior films of healthy-looking lungs, while pediatric films are noisier, obstructed by whoever is holding the child, and anatomically different by developmental stage.
records.headline_result: hybrid and deep-learning methods reached inter-observer-level segmentation performance, at the cost of long training and high computational complexity

records.title: Brain Structure and Function in School-Aged Children With Sluggish Cognitive Tempo Symptoms.
records.journal: Journal of the American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry
records.exclusion_reason: cross-sectional MRI study of regional volume, white matter integrity and functional connectivity associated with sluggish cognitive tempo symptoms in 178 school-aged children; association analysis, no machine learning model

records.exclusion_reason: association between prenatal lead exposure and fetal functional connectivity; no machine-learning model

records.title: Sensory over-responsivity: parent report, direct assessment measures, and neural architecture.
records.exclusion_reason: group comparison of white matter anisotropy by sensory over-responsivity phenotype; no machine-learning model

records.title: Evaluation of an improved tool for non-invasive prediction of neonatal respiratory morbidity based on fully automated fetal lung ultrasound analysis.
records.model_family: deep learning lung delineation feeding quantitative texture analysis
records.clinical_problem: predicting neonatal respiratory morbidity from ultrasound instead of amniocentesis
records.patient_population: 790 fetal lung ultrasound images obtained between 24 and 39 weeks gestation
records.model_description: The successor version of the commercial fetal lung maturity tool, with the manual lung outlining replaced by deep learning. The comparison that makes the paper worth reading is three-way: fully automated, the same texture analysis with manual delineation, and gestational age alone. Automation cost essentially nothing in accuracy (91.5% versus 90.3%) while both beat gestational age alone (75.6%) decisively.
records.release_evidence: quantusFLM version 3.0, a commercial software tool
records.headline_result: sensitivity 71.0%, specificity 94.7%, accuracy 91.5% fully automated, against 90.3% with manual delineation and 75.6% using gestational age alone

records.title: Evaluating reinforcement learning agents for anatomical landmark detection.
records.model_family: deep Q-network reinforcement learning agents with multi-scale hierarchical search
records.body_region: fetal head, adult brain and heart
records.clinical_problem: finding anatomical landmarks automatically, the step that biometry and registration depend on
records.patient_population: fetuses in a fetal head ultrasound dataset, alongside adult brain and cardiac MRI datasets
records.model_description: Rather than scanning the whole image, an agent starts somewhere and learns to walk toward the landmark, treating the 3D scan as an environment to navigate. Searching coarse-to-fine with hierarchical step sizes speeds this up four- to fivefold and copes with the large fields of view and noisy backgrounds where fixed-scale agents fail. Evaluated on fetal head ultrasound among three datasets.
records.dataset_size: three medical imaging datasets; sizes not stated
records.headline_result: surpassed state-of-the-art supervised and reinforcement-learning landmark methods; hierarchical steps sped up search 4-5 times

records.title: Amygdala-prefrontal cortex white matter tracts are widespread, variable and implicated in amygdala modulation in adolescents.
records.exclusion_reason: developmental neuroscience: probabilistic tractography maps amygdala-prefrontal tracts in 142 adolescents and a machine-learning regression relates that connectivity to amygdala reactivity; no diagnostic or clinical imaging model

records.title: Attention gated networks: Learning to leverage salient regions in medical images.
records.model_family: attention-gated CNN module for VGG / U-Net
records.clinical_problem: identifying the correct standard views during fetal ultrasound screening
records.patient_population: fetuses undergoing mid-pregnancy screening ultrasound; the segmentation experiments use adult abdominal CT
records.model_description: A drop-in module that makes a standard CNN learn where to look, suppressing irrelevant image regions without a separate organ-localization step. Demonstrated on fetal ultrasound scan-plane detection, where it reduced false positives, and on multi-organ abdominal CT segmentation. It is a general architecture contribution rather than a clinical product.
records.release_evidence: the source code for the proposed AG models is publicly available
records.dataset_size: two large 3D CT abdominal datasets plus a fetal ultrasound screening set; sizes not stated
records.headline_result: consistent improvement in prediction performance over the base architectures across datasets and training sizes

records.title: Improving preterm newborn identification in low-resource settings with machine learning.
records.exclusion_reason: machine learning identifies preterm newborns from maternal and newborn clinical characteristics in a low-resource setting; early pregnancy ultrasound is the gold standard the model is scored against, not an input, and no images are analyzed

records.title: The utility of CT scan for the diagnostic evaluation of acute abdominal pain.
records.exclusion_reason: Review of CT versus ultrasound strategy for acute abdominal pain/appendicitis across all ages; no AI/ML component.

records.title: White matter connectomes at birth accurately predict cognitive abilities at age 2.
records.model_family: deep learning classifier on white matter connectomes
records.clinical_problem: predicting cognitive ability at age 2 from the brain's wiring at birth
records.patient_population: 75 full-term infants scanned at birth and 37 preterm infants scanned at term-equivalent age
records.model_description: Builds a white matter connectome from diffusion MRI acquired at birth and classifies whether that child will score above or below the median on cognitive testing at two years, then predicts the individual score. Trained on full-term infants and evaluated separately on preterm infants, which is the transfer that matters clinically. Frontal lobe connections and their links to the rest of the brain carried the classification.
records.headline_result: 89.5% accuracy in full-term and 83.8% in preterm infants for the 2-year cognitive group; predicted and actual scores correlated at r = 0.98 and 0.96

records.title: Decision Fusion-Based Fetal Ultrasound Image Plane Classification Using Convolutional Neural Networks.
records.model_family: two fine-tuned convolutional feature extractors - one on the whole image, one on discriminant cropped regions - whose classification decisions are fused
records.clinical_problem: labeling which fetal structure a 2D ultrasound image shows, across 14 structures, so that large retrospective archives can be mined for indicators of abnormal development
records.patient_population: 4074 2-D fetal ultrasound images (3109 training, 965 test)
records.model_description: The diagnosis of the problem is precise: crops confuse structures that look alike, such as kidney and abdomen, while the whole image lacks the local detail to say which structure is where. Fusing decisions from both, without a prior on where to look, is the contribution, and localization falls out of the same machinery. The high mean accuracy alongside much lower precision and recall reflects 14 unbalanced classes. Its stated purpose is retrospective archive mining rather than live scanning.
records.headline_result: mean accuracy 97.05%, precision 76.47%, recall 75.41%, Cohen kappa 0.72; 92% mean accuracy on images without scanner overlays

records.title: Detection of Children/Youth With Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder Through Eye Movement, Psychometric, and Neuroimaging Data.
records.model_family: machine learning classification framework combining multimodal features
records.clinical_problem: developing a low-cost machine-learning-based screening protocol for fetal alcohol spectrum disorder in children/youth
records.patient_population: children/youth with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder and age-matched typically developing controls
records.model_description: Inputs are saccadic eye movement tasks, psychometric tests, and neuroimaging of the corpus callosum; a machine learning framework combines these multimodal measures to classify children/youth with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder, and identifies a reduced low-cost subset (eye movement plus psychometrics) that approaches full-panel performance.
records.headline_result: combination of 4-6 assessments yielded the best FASD-versus-control classification accuracy; a reduced eye-movement-plus-psychometric protocol approached this performance at lower cost
records.study_design: prospective case-control multimodal machine learning screening study

records.title: Objective Detection of Eloquent Axonal Pathways to Minimize Postoperative Deficits in Pediatric Epilepsy Surgery using Diffusion Tractography and Convolutional Neural Networks.
records.model_family: deep CNN on diffusion tractography streamlines with focal and center losses and a soft attention mechanism
records.clinical_problem: identifying eloquent white matter pathways before pediatric epilepsy surgery, so that resection spares motor, language, auditory and visual function
records.patient_population: streamlines from 70 healthy children and 70 children with focal epilepsy, labeled by functional MRI and electrical stimulation mapping
records.model_description: Aimed at the specific inadequacy of the current tools: electrical stimulation mapping is invasive and maps cortex, fMRI needs task cooperation from a child, and neither shows the fibers connecting eloquent areas. The network classifies individual tractography streamlines, with focal and center losses chosen for an extremely unbalanced label distribution and soft attention for interpretability. Ground truth comes from the invasive standard it would reduce.
records.release_evidence: the abstract states the implementation will be released at a GitHub repository
records.headline_result: 73-100% accuracy for objective detection of functionally important pathways, outperforming existing streamline classification models

records.title: Normalization enhances brain network features that predict individual intelligence in children with epilepsy.
records.model_family: machine learning regression algorithm on normalized brain network metrics
records.clinical_problem: predicting individual IQ from resting-state fMRI brain network architecture in children with epilepsy
records.patient_population: 27 patients with epilepsy, ages 8-18 years
records.model_description: Brain network graph metrics (clustering coefficient, transitivity, modularity, path length, global efficiency) are computed from resting-state fMRI in children with epilepsy under two normalization strategies. A machine learning algorithm uses only these normalized metrics to predict each patient's IQ, with normalization substantially improving prediction accuracy over non-normalized metrics.
records.headline_result: Normalization substantially improved subject-level IQ prediction accuracy versus non-normalized network metrics

records.title: Intrinsic Functional Brain Connectivity Predicts Onset of Major Depression Disorder in Adolescence: A Pilot Study.
records.model_family: classifier built on resting-state functional connectivity features
records.clinical_problem: identifying, before any episode occurs, which children at familial risk for major depression will develop it in adolescence
records.patient_population: never-depressed children aged 8-14 with familial risk for major depressive disorder and age-matched controls without familial risk, reassessed by diagnostic interview 3-4 years later
records.model_description: A prognostic rather than diagnostic model, and the design carries the weight: imaging at baseline in children who had never been depressed, diagnosis established 3-4 years later, and the classifier built independently of the group differences the paper also reports. Its comparator is the right one - baseline clinical rating scales - and connectivity beat them. A pilot, with the sample size that word implies.
records.dataset_size: pilot cohort, size not stated in the abstract
records.headline_result: classification of converters versus non-converters from baseline connectivity reached high accuracy, sensitivity and specificity, superior to classification from baseline clinical rating scales

records.title: A radiomics-based nomogram for the preoperative prediction of posthepatectomy liver failure in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma.
records.exclusion_reason: CT radiomics nomogram for post-hepatectomy liver failure in adults with hepatocellular carcinoma

records.title: Fully automated radiological analysis of spinal disorders and deformities: a deep learning approach.
records.journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
records.model_family: fully convolutional network with a differentiable spatial-to-numerical layer
records.clinical_problem: measuring spinal deformity parameters (Cobb angle, kyphosis, lordosis, pelvic incidence) on biplanar radiographs
records.patient_population: 493 patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, adult deformity and spinal stenosis
records.model_description: Takes biplanar spine radiographs and returns the 78 anatomical landmarks (endplate centers, hip joint centers, S1 endplate margins) from which the standard deformity angles are then computed. It is designed to cope with a wide range of conditions and fields of view. The authors are candid that although the predicted spine shape looks convincing and correlates strongly with ground truth, the standard errors on individual angles are large.
records.dataset_size: 493 spines for training, 50 patients for quantitative comparison
records.headline_result: all parameters strongly correlated with ground truth, but standard errors from 2.7 degrees (pelvic tilt) to 11.5 degrees (L1-L5 lordosis)

records.title: Techniques for minimizing sedation in pediatric MRI.

records.clinical_problem: avoiding sedation and general anesthesia for MRI in infants and young children
records.patient_population: infants and young children undergoing MRI
records.model_description: A review of every lever available for getting a diagnostic MRI in a small child awake: environment, child life specialists, feed-and-bundle, distraction, noise reduction, and the technical routes to shorter scans, of which artificial intelligence is one. Useful as the framing document for why faster reconstruction matters in a children's hospital, rather than as a source of model performance figures.

records.title: Fully automatic 3D reconstruction of the placenta and its peripheral vasculature in intrauterine fetal MRI.
records.model_family: 3D Gabor filters and texture features with a support vector machine and uterus edge-based instance selection, plus a curvature-based corner detector for vessels
records.clinical_problem: quantifying placental anatomy and its peripheral vasculature on fetal MRI, which is needed for diagnosis and for planning fetal surgery and which is ambiguous to interpret by eye
records.patient_population: 44 control and pathological cases: singleton and normal or monochorionic twin pregnancies between 25 and 37 weeks
records.model_description: A classical pipeline that beat six deep networks on the same task - 3D U-Net, V-Net, DeepMedic, Holistic3D Net, HighRes3D Net and Dense V-Net were all implemented for comparison and all lost on placenta localization. With 44 cases, engineered features and a support vector machine with careful instance selection still outperform learned ones, which is a useful counterweight to the assumption that a network is always the right tool in this data regime. Segmenting the peripheral vessels as well as the organ is what makes it relevant to fetal surgical planning.
records.headline_result: Dice 0.82 +/- 0.02 for placenta and 0.81 +/- 0.08 for its vasculature, outperforming all six convolutional network baselines on placenta localization

records.title: Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorders in Young Children Based on Resting-State Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging Data Using Convolutional Neural Networks.
records.model_family: convolutional neural networks with transfer learning and classifier combination, both mixture-of-experts and simple Bayes
records.clinical_problem: diagnosing autism spectrum disorder in young children from resting-state functional MRI, before behavioral symptoms are established enough for interview and observation to settle it
records.patient_population: children aged 5 to 10 years from the ABIDE I and ABIDE II datasets
records.model_description: Two constraints are handled at once: small medical datasets and the need to hold the age window narrow. The age restriction to 5-10 years is a deliberate cost - it shrinks an already small dataset - taken because a diagnostic aid is only useful before the clinical diagnosis is obvious. Combining classifiers and transferring features stand in for the data that does not exist. Accuracy in the low-to-mid 70s is representative of what ABIDE supports, and is a reminder of how far this is from clinical use.
records.dataset_size: ABIDE I and ABIDE II subjects aged 5-10
records.headline_result: ABIDE I accuracy 0.7273, sensitivity 0.712, specificity 0.7348; ABIDE II accuracy 0.700, sensitivity 0.582, specificity 0.804
records.study_design: retrospective model development on public datasets

records.title: Deep Learning Method for Automated Classification of Anteroposterior and Posteroanterior Chest Radiographs.
records.clinical_problem: verifying whether a frontal chest radiograph is anteroposterior or posteroanterior, which affects interpretation and which mislabeled metadata routinely gets wrong across facilities
records.patient_population: 112 120 chest radiographs from the NIH ChestX-ray14 database, of which 5941 (5%) are pediatric; a second network was trained on the pediatric subset alone (2885 AP, 3056 PA)
records.model_description: A quality-control task rather than a diagnostic one, and the pediatric interest is in the ablation: training on the 5% pediatric subset alone, a 95% reduction in data, cost almost nothing (AUC 0.997 versus 1.0, difference not significant). That is a concrete data point for the recurring pediatric worry that adult-scale datasets are needed for anything to work. Aimed at curating large datasets for machine learning and at departmental quality assurance.
records.headline_result: AUC 1.0 and accuracy 99.6% for the full-dataset network versus AUC 0.997 and accuracy 98% for the pediatric-only network (difference not significant, p = 0.17)
records.study_design: retrospective model development on a public dataset

records.patient_population: 39 boys, ages 8-12 years, with and without auditory over-responsivity
records.model_description: Diffusion tensor imaging metrics (fractional anisotropy, mean/radial/axial diffusivity) and derived connectome edge-density maps of white matter tracts are input to naive Bayes, random forest, and support vector machine classifiers. The models were trained and compared to classify boys with versus without auditory over-responsivity, with random forest using edge-density metrics performing best.
records.dataset_size: 39 boys, ages 8-12 years (15 with auditory over-responsivity)
records.headline_result: Left superior longitudinal fasciculus FA gave AUC 0.756 for AOR prediction (p = 0.008); random forest with edge-density metrics had the highest classification accuracy among tested models

records.title: Longitudinal Prediction of Infant Diffusion MRI Data via Graph Convolutional Adversarial Networks.
records.model_family: graph convolutional network over spatial and diffusion wave-vector domains, with a multi-scale residual architecture and adversarial learning
records.clinical_problem: missing data in longitudinal infant imaging studies, caused by subject dropout and failed scans, which breaks the developmental trajectories those studies exist to measure
records.patient_population: longitudinal infant brain diffusion MRI
records.model_description: Attacks a problem specific to pediatric longitudinal imaging: infants move, scans fail, families drop out, and a missing timepoint costs a whole trajectory. Building the graph over both space and the diffusion wave-vector domain lets the network use the structure of the acquisition itself, not just the image. Imputing a missing scan is a strong claim that needs careful use downstream, but the alternative - discarding the subject - has its own bias.
records.headline_result: accurate and robust longitudinal prediction of missing infant brain diffusion MRI data

records.headline_result: Improvement of more than 0.1 years in mean absolute error over corresponding spatial-domain approaches; outperforms several state-of-the-art bone-age methods
