records.title: Automated semantic labeling of pediatric musculoskeletal radiographs using deep learning.
records.model_family: five ResNet-18 networks pretrained on ImageNet, one per anatomical region, with 30-fold standard augmentation
records.clinical_problem: knowing which body part a radiograph shows without trusting the metadata, which is what automated hanging protocols and the curation of large training sets both depend on
records.patient_population: 250 pediatric bone radiographs (50 each of shoulder, elbow, hand, pelvis and knee), plus a separate 100-radiograph test set from a single institution
records.model_description: A non-interpretive task, and a reminder of how much of radiology AI's near-term value sits there. The finding worth carrying forward is about data economics: 250 radiographs, augmented thirty-fold with standard transforms, produced perfect classification on two separate test sets. Problems this well-posed do not need large datasets. At 33 radiographs per second it is also fast enough to run over an archive, which is the curation use case the authors name.
records.dataset_size: 250 training radiographs plus a 100-radiograph external test set
records.headline_result: ROC AUC of 1 for all five networks on both test sets, classifying at 33 radiographs per second
records.study_design: retrospective model development with external validation

records.title: Toward Automated 3D Spine Reconstruction from Biplanar Radiographs Using CNN for Statistical Spine Model Fitting.
records.model_family: CNN landmark detection driving a statistical shape model
records.clinical_problem: getting 3D spinal measurements from biplanar radiographs, which currently needs so much manual supervision that it stays out of routine practice
records.patient_population: 68 biplanar radiographs of asymptomatic subjects and adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients
records.model_description: Fits a realistic statistical shape model of the spine to a pair of biplanar radiographs by having networks find the controlling anatomical landmarks, iteratively and coarse-to-fine. Reconstruction takes under a minute against the semi-automated methods it replaces, and 89% of its measurements fell inside the experts' own confidence intervals. The stated aim is dissemination: 3D measurement exists but nobody has time to do it by hand.
records.headline_result: landmark errors 1.6-2.3 mm; absolute error 2.8-4.7 degrees for spinal and 1-2.1 degrees for pelvic parameters; 89% of measurements inside expert confidence intervals
records.study_design: retrospective validation against multi-expert ground truth

records.title: Dilated Dense U-Net for Infant Hippocampus Subfield Segmentation.
records.model_family: fully convolutional network embedding a dilated dense network in a U-Net, with residual connections in the second variant
records.clinical_problem: segmenting hippocampal subfields in infants, where existing methods are built for adults and fail because of poor tissue contrast and structures that change shape rapidly in early development
records.patient_population: infant brain MRI
records.model_description: An architecture argument with a specifically infant motivation: dilated dense blocks give multi-scale context while keeping spatial resolution, which is what the hippocampal subfields need since they are small, adjacent and low-contrast in the infant brain. The comparison is against 3D U-Net on the same data, and the gain of 2-2.5 Dice points is modest but consistent across both variants.
records.headline_result: average Dice improved by 2.1% (DUnet) and 2.5% (ResDUnet) over classic 3D U-net, outperforming other state-of-the-art methods

records.title: A comparison of resting state functional magnetic resonance imaging to invasive electrocortical stimulation for sensorimotor mapping in pediatric patients.

records.model_description: Resting-state fMRI data from pediatric epilepsy patients are analyzed by a machine learning classifier (previously trained and validated in adults) that localizes sensorimotor resting-state networks; results are compared with direct electrocortical stimulation mapping, the clinical gold standard.
records.headline_result: comparable functional localization between resting-state fMRI classifier and electrocortical stimulation mapping (no single summary statistic given)
records.study_design: prospective single-center comparative diagnostic accuracy study

records.title: Automatic evaluation of fetal head biometry from ultrasound images using machine learning.
records.model_family: deep learning pipeline with a plane acceptance check followed by head circumference and biparietal diameter estimation
records.clinical_problem: automating head circumference and biparietal diameter on fetal ultrasound, the biometry used to assign gestational age and flag central nervous system pathology
records.patient_population: fetal ultrasound images: 102 labeled for training, 70 for validation
records.model_description: Biometry with a gatekeeper. The pipeline first decides whether the plane is acceptable and only then measures, which is the right ordering for a measurement that is meaningless off-plane and the part most automated biometry skips. Small dataset, and the reported success rates are plane-level rather than millimetre agreement, so it reads as feasibility.
records.headline_result: 91.43% success for head circumference and 100% for biparietal diameter, with 87.14% accuracy on the plane acceptance check

records.model_description: An anatomically constrained deep learning network iteratively identifies and corrects candidate voxels with topological defects in segmented infant brain MRI to produce topologically accurate cortical surfaces.
records.study_design: retrospective methods development study, validated on simulated and real topological errors

records.title: Deep residual network for off-resonance artifact correction with application to pediatric body MRA with 3D cones.
records.clinical_problem: correcting off-resonance artifacts to enable faster pediatric body MR angiography
records.patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing body MRA
records.model_description: Short-readout (long scan-time, low-artifact) MRA scans are used as reference and augmented with simulated off-resonance to train a residual CNN (Off-ResNet); applied to faster long-readout 3D-cones scans, the network corrects off-resonance blurring, compared against an autofocus method and radiologist scoring of anatomical features.
records.headline_result: long-readout scans corrected with Off-ResNet were noninferior to short-readout reference scans on radiologist scoring (P<.05); superior RMSE/SSIM/PSNR vs. autofocus (P<.01), with 59.3% shorter scan time
records.study_design: prospective single-center technical development and reader-validation study

records.title: Machine Learning Prediction of Liver Stiffness Using Clinical and T2-Weighted MRI Radiomic Data.
records.model_family: support vector machine on clinical plus T2-weighted radiomic features
records.clinical_problem: estimating liver stiffness without MR elastography, which not every center has
records.patient_population: 225 children and young adults (mean age 14.1 years) internally and 84 (mean age 13.7) in an external cohort, with known or suspected liver disease
records.model_description: Classifies liver stiffness above or below 3 kPa from routine T2-weighted images plus clinical data, using elastography as the reference. The point is substitution: if ordinary sequences carry enough signal, centers without elastography could still stratify fibrosis risk. Clinical and radiomic features together beat either alone, and the model held up in an independent external cohort with a modest drop.
records.headline_result: internal AUC 0.84 combining clinical and radiomic features (0.77 clinical, 0.70 radiomic alone); external AUC 0.80 with accuracy 75.0%

records.title: Regression Algorithm of Bone Age Estimation of Knee-joint Based on Principal Component Analysis and Support Vector Machine.
records.model_family: support vector regression (SVR) with PCA dimensionality reduction of HOG/LBP image features
records.clinical_problem: forensic skeletal (bone) age estimation
records.patient_population: adolescents aged 12.0 to <19.0 years (275 male, 225 female), Xinjiang Uygur population, China
records.model_description: The model takes digital radiographs of the knee joint and extracts histogram-of-oriented-gradients (HOG) and local binary pattern (LBP) texture features, reduces their dimensionality with principal component analysis, and regresses skeletal age with a support vector regression model. Separate models were trained and tested for male and female adolescents, intended for forensic bone-age estimation in the age range where hand/wrist growth plates have already fused.
records.dataset_size: 500 subjects (275 male, 225 female) aged 12.0-<19.0 years; 215 male and 180 female used for training, the remainder as an independent test set
records.headline_result: Accuracy within ±0.8/±1.0 year of true age: 80.67%/89.33% (male), 80.19%/90.45% (female); MAE 0.485-0.486 years, RMSE 0.590-0.606 years
records.study_design: retrospective single-center technical development and validation

records.title: Automated data extraction and report analysis in computer-aided radiology audit: practice implications from post-mortem paediatric imaging.
records.model_family: custom automated computational program (DICOM parsing plus rule-based/NLP report analysis)
records.clinical_problem: quality audit of post-mortem MRI protocol adherence and diagnostic image quality
records.patient_population: post-mortem whole-body MRI examinations of fetuses, infants and children at a single pediatric hospital over 5.5 years
records.model_description: A custom computer program batch-processes DICOM files from whole-body post-mortem MRI examinations to extract imaging sequence parameters, and applies natural language processing to authorized radiology reports to extract the stated diagnostic image quality. It automates a departmental audit of imaging protocol adherence (full vs. abbreviated) and diagnostic quality rather than interpreting the images itself.
records.dataset_size: 460 whole-body post-mortem MRI examinations over 5.5 years (approximately 80 GB of DICOM data)
records.headline_result: Automated data-extraction accuracy 96.7% (445/460, 95% CI 94.7-98%); full protocol adherence in 66.3% of cases; 91.9% of studies of diagnostic quality overall
records.study_design: retrospective single-center audit / workflow automation study

records.title: Automatic brain tissue segmentation in fetal MRI using convolutional neural networks.
records.model_family: two sequential CNNs with synthetic intensity-inhomogeneity augmentation
records.clinical_problem: volumetric and morphologic assessment of the fetal brain, which requires tissue-level segmentation
records.patient_population: fetuses undergoing MRI
records.model_description: One network extracts the intracranial volume, a second divides it into seven tissue classes: cerebellum, basal ganglia and thalami, ventricular CSF, white matter, brain stem, cortical gray matter and extracerebral CSF. The trick is in the training: rather than correcting the intensity inhomogeneity that fetal motion causes, artificial gradients are added to clean slices so the network learns to tolerate the artifact, which removes a preprocessing step entirely.
records.headline_result: average Dice rose from 0.77 to 0.88 and mean surface distance fell from 0.78 mm to 0.37 mm when training data included simulated inhomogeneity

records.title: Estimation of the radiation dose in pregnancy: an automated patient-specific model using convolutional neural networks.

records.dataset_size: 32 CT exams augmented to 128 datasets (80%/20% train/test)
records.headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient 0.92-0.98 for internal organs versus manual segmentation; mean uterus absorbed dose 2.9 mGy, organ dose differences -1.55% to 0.28%
records.study_design: retrospective algorithm development and internal validation study

records.title: Using deep-learning techniques for pulmonary-thoracic segmentations and improvement of pneumonia diagnosis in pediatric chest radiographs.
records.model_family: deep learning segmentation of lung and thorax fields, feeding a downstream pneumonia classifier
records.clinical_problem: segmenting the lungs and thorax on children's chest radiographs, and whether doing so improves the harder downstream call of bacterial versus viral pneumonia
records.patient_population: a clinical pediatric chest radiograph set of 1351 patients, with two adult chest radiograph sets used to test generalizability
records.model_description: Segmentation is treated as a means rather than an end, and the paper measures what it buys: cropping to the lung field raised the AUC for bacterial versus viral pneumonia from 0.815 to 0.879, which is a concrete argument for anatomical preprocessing rather than feeding whole radiographs to a classifier. Generalization runs the unusual direction here, from a pediatric-trained model to adult radiographs, and holds up.
records.dataset_size: 1351 pediatric patients plus two adult test sets
records.headline_result: Jaccard 0.910 and Dice 0.948 for lung segmentation; pneumonia classification AUC rose from 0.815 to 0.879 after lung extraction; Jaccard 0.888-0.903 on the two adult sets

records.title: Bone age assessment with various machine learning techniques: A systematic literature review and meta-analysis.
records.clinical_problem: the state of machine learning for bone age assessment
records.patient_population: children and subadults in the 26 studies reviewed, mostly from the United States and Western Europe
records.model_description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 26 bone age studies using machine learning. Its value is in the gaps it names: the field works almost entirely on hand and wrist radiographs and has barely explored radiation-free alternatives such as MRI, few studies address ethnic differences, the samples cluster around the medico-legal age of 18, and socioeconomic influences on skeletal maturation are untouched.

records.title: Automated Ventricular System Segmentation in Paediatric Patients Treated for Hydrocephalus Using Deep Learning Methods.
records.model_family: U-Net trained with one-cycle learning rate policy, transfer learning, generalized Dice loss, mixed precision, self-attention and augmentation
records.clinical_problem: measuring cerebrospinal fluid volume on head CT during treatment of pediatric hydrocephalus, which radiologists do by manual segmentation and which is prone to bias and high intraobserver variability
records.patient_population: paediatric patients treated for hydrocephalus; 80 CT images
records.model_description: A demonstration of how far careful training tricks carry a small dataset: eighty CT scans, a standard U-Net, and a stack of well-chosen optimizations reach near human-level Dice. The clinical case is time and consistency rather than accuracy - the volume is already measurable, just expensively and variably - which is the recurring shape of the argument for segmentation tools in pediatric neurosurgery.
records.headline_result: mean Dice 0.917 (SD 0.0352) on cross-validation and 0.9506 on a separate test set

records.title: Self-supervised learning for medical image analysis using image context restoration.
records.clinical_problem: getting usable models when few images are labelled, demonstrated on fetal ultrasound scan-plane detection
records.patient_population: fetuses imaged with 2D ultrasound; further experiments use abdominal CT and brain tumor MRI
records.model_description: A pretraining recipe rather than a clinical model: patches of an unlabelled image are swapped and the network learns to restore the original, which teaches it semantic features without any annotation. The pretrained weights are then fine-tuned for a downstream task. Demonstrated on fetal ultrasound scan-plane detection, abdominal organ localization on CT and brain tumor segmentation on MRI.
records.headline_result: improved models in all three downstream tasks; magnitudes not stated in the abstract

records.title: Connectomic Profiling Identifies Responders to Vagus Nerve Stimulation.
records.clinical_problem: predicting vagus nerve stimulation response in children with drug-resistant epilepsy from structural and functional connectomic profiling
records.patient_population: 56 children with medically intractable epilepsy from 3 institutions (discovery n=38, validation n=18)
records.model_description: Diffusion tensor imaging identifies white matter microstructural differences between VNS responders and non-responders, which inform beamforming of resting-state magnetoencephalography functional connectivity. These structural and functional connectomic features are combined in a support vector machine trained to predict VNS response and independently validated in a separate cohort, outperforming a classifier built from clinical covariates alone.
records.headline_result: 89.5% accuracy, AUC 0.93 on 10-fold cross-validation; 83.3% accuracy (85.7% sensitivity, 75.0% specificity) in external validation; superior to clinical covariates alone (AUC 0.57, p < 0.008)
records.study_design: retrospective multi-institutional prognostic accuracy study with external validation

records.title: Computed tomography-based predictive nomogram for differentiating primary progressive pulmonary tuberculosis from community-acquired pneumonia in children.
records.model_family: LASSO-selected radiomic signatures from two anatomical regions, combined with a clinical factor in a predictive nomogram
records.clinical_problem: separating primary progressive pulmonary tuberculosis from community-acquired pneumonia in children on chest CT, a distinction that changes treatment entirely and that experienced radiologists get wrong often enough to matter
records.patient_population: 53 children with clinically confirmed pulmonary tuberculosis and 62 with community-acquired pneumonia, split 3:1 into primary (n=86) and validation (n=29) cohorts
records.model_description: Two separate radiomic signatures rather than one, extracted from the consolidation and from the lymph nodes, which mirrors how the two diseases actually differ and lets the model use nodal texture that no visual score captures. Duration of fever is the only clinical variable added. The comparator that gives the result its weight is a senior radiologist reading the same scans, who scored 0.79 against the nomogram's 0.97 - though on 29 validation patients.
records.headline_result: AUC 0.971 (95% CI 0.912-1) versus 0.791 for a senior radiologist's clinical judgment and 0.832 for the clinical factor alone

records.title: The role of task-based neural activation research in understanding cognitive deficits in pediatric epilepsy.
records.exclusion_reason: review of task-based fMRI and cognitive deficits in pediatric epilepsy, no AI/ML component

records.title: Automated age estimation from MRI volumes of the hand.
records.model_family: random forests and deep convolutional neural networks on 3D hand MRI, with several image-input simplifications compared
records.clinical_problem: estimating age in children and adolescents without ionizing radiation, for both clinical and forensic use
records.patient_population: 328 hand MR images of children and adolescents; the best method was then adapted to 2D and applied to a public hand radiograph dataset
records.model_description: The MRI answer to bone age. Three problems with radiographic staging are addressed at once - radiation, the absence of MRI-specific staging systems, and examiner subjectivity - by regressing age directly from 3D volumes and skipping staging entirely. The paper is unusually careful about what is being estimated, separating biological age estimation from chronological age approximation, and it validates by porting the method to 2D radiographs where it matches published automatic methods.
records.headline_result: mean absolute error 0.37 +/- 0.51 years for biological age in subjects 18 or younger
records.study_design: retrospective model development with external dataset validation

records.title: Automated 3D ultrasound image analysis for first trimester assessment of fetal health.
records.model_family: deep learning and image processing pipeline: whole-fetus semantic segmentation, plane orientation estimation, biometry localization and limb detection
records.clinical_problem: assessing fetal health at the first trimester scan - viability, gestational age, early anomaly detection - where the fetus looks nothing like it does in the second trimester and almost no automation exists
records.patient_population: 44 3D ultrasound volumes for development and an independent clinical set of 21 volumes for evaluation
records.model_description: Deliberately broad where the literature is narrow: most first-trimester automation targets one anatomy, and this handles segmentation, plane orientation, biometry and limb detection from a single 3D volume. That matters because the first trimester scan asks several questions at once and the fetus is too small for any of them to be easy. Forty-four development volumes is little, and the claim is calibrated accordingly - approaching, not exceeding, expert assessment.
records.dataset_size: 44 development volumes and 21 independent evaluation volumes
records.headline_result: automated methods approached human expert assessment of a 3D volume on an independent clinical dataset

records.title: A multi-view pyramid network for skull stripping on neonatal T1-weighted MRI.
records.clinical_problem: automatically removing skull/non-brain tissue from neonatal T1-weighted MRI to enable brain structural analysis
records.patient_population: 70 neonates from a local hospital plus 7 infants from the public NeuroBrainS12 dataset
records.model_description: Takes neonatal T1-weighted brain MRI as input and outputs a brain mask (skull-stripped image) using a multi-view pyramid deep-learning network fused across 2D slice views.
records.headline_result: Dice ratio 95.44-97.33%, sensitivity 93.19-97.02%, specificity 97.52-99.68%
records.study_design: retrospective algorithm development and validation study using local and public neonatal MRI data

records.title: Altered Functional Connectivity in Children With Low-Function Autism Spectrum Disorders.
records.exclusion_reason: group comparison of independent-component functional networks in children with autism; descriptive rather than predictive, with no model

records.title: TTTS-GPS: Patient-specific preoperative planning and simulation platform for twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome fetal surgery.
records.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
records.model_family: computer vision and deep learning segmentation and registration of MRI and 3D ultrasound, integrated into a C++/MITK surgical simulation platform
records.clinical_problem: planning minimally invasive fetoscopic laser surgery for twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome, a technically difficult operation with a steep learning curve where untreated cases carry 90% perinatal mortality
records.patient_population: pregnancies with twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome, imaged with MRI and 3D ultrasound
records.model_description: The segmentation is in service of a surgical rehearsal: mother's soft tissue, uterus, umbilical cords, placenta and its vascular tree are segmented and registered automatically, then rendered as an intrauterine environment where the surgeon can simulate the fetoscope view, choose the entry point and practise the laser ablation before the operation. For a procedure this rare and this difficult, rehearsal on the actual patient's anatomy is the intervention. Experienced surgeons rated it highly in a usability study.
records.headline_result: the first twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome fetal surgery planning and simulation platform, rated highly by experienced surgeons in a comprehensive usability study
records.study_design: software platform development with usability study

records.title: Lung ultrasound in infants with bronchiolitis.
records.exclusion_reason: letter arguing that lung ultrasound findings in infants with bronchiolitis are being over-interpreted as pneumonia; commentary, no model

records.title: Deriving external forces via convolutional neural networks for biomedical image segmentation.
records.model_family: convolutional network trained against gradient vector flow to derive an external force field for active contour models
records.clinical_problem: the sensitivity of gradient vector flow - the standard external force in active contour segmentation - to noise and false edges, which limits where snakes can be used
records.patient_population: three clinical applications: fetal head in ultrasound, optic disk in fundus images and fluid in retinal OCT
records.model_description: A hybrid rather than a replacement: the classical active contour machinery is kept, and only the external force - the part that fails on noisy images - is learned, using the classical force as the training reference. Fetal head ultrasound is one of three evaluation tasks and the noisiest of them, which is where the substitution should matter most. The other two applications are ophthalmic and outside this database's scope.
records.headline_result: competitive performance against state-of-the-art algorithms across all three segmentation tasks including fetal head ultrasound

records.title: Application of machine learning to structural connectome to predict symptom reduction in depressed adolescents with cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT).
records.model_family: J48 pruned decision tree classifier over diffusion MRI structural connectome attributes, ten-fold cross-validated
records.clinical_problem: which depressed adolescents will improve with cognitive behavioral therapy - a first-line treatment that many do not respond to, with treatment planning currently unguided by biology
records.patient_population: 30 depressed adolescents treated with three months of cognitive behavioral therapy, with baseline diffusion MRI connectomes and 21 attributes including baseline depression score, age and sex
records.model_description: Treatment selection rather than diagnosis, which is the more useful question and the rarer one in this literature. The deliberate choice of a small pruned decision tree over a black box pays off - the final tree has three attributes and puts right thalamus node strength at the centre, a finding then corroborated by a direct correlation with symptom change. Thirty adolescents, so this is a hypothesis with an accuracy attached rather than a validated predictor.
records.headline_result: 83% accuracy predicting depressive symptom reduction after three months of cognitive behavioral therapy, from a three-attribute tree centred on right thalamus node strength

records.title: Supervised classification approach of biometric measures for automatic fetal defect screening in head ultrasound images.
records.clinical_problem: automatically screening for fetal head abnormalities (microcephaly, dolichocephaly) from ultrasound biometric measures
records.model_description: an SVM classifier takes morphological and biometric features from fetal head ultrasound as input and outputs a classification of normal vs. abnormal (microcephaly/dolichocephaly) cases

records.title: Experience during adolescence shapes brain development: From synapses and networks to normal and pathological behavior.
records.exclusion_reason: symposium review of experience-dependent plasticity in adolescence; no machine-learning model

records.title: Neural Response Patterns During Pavlovian-to-Instrumental Transfer Predict Alcohol Relapse and Young Adult Drinking.

records.title: Multi-task learning for quality assessment of fetal head ultrasound images.
records.model_family: multi-task faster region-based CNN with shared convolutional trunk
records.clinical_problem: deciding whether a fetal head ultrasound image is good enough to measure from, before anyone measures from it
records.patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound
records.model_description: Detects the key anatomical structures of the fetal head, checks whether the image magnification is appropriate, and scores the plane against clinical protocol, all from one network with a shared feature trunk and task-specific heads. It returns a verdict in under half a second, which is fast enough to be useful during the scan rather than after it. Prior clinical rules are folded in to hold down false detections.
records.dataset_size: an institutional dataset; size not stated
records.headline_result: quality assessment of an ultrasound plane in under half a second, comparable with state-of-the-art methods

records.title: Fetal Brain Abnormality Classification from MRI Images of Different Gestational Age.
records.model_family: classical classifiers - diagonal quadratic discriminant analysis, k-nearest neighbour, random forest, naive Bayes and RBF networks - plus bagging and AdaBoost ensembles of them
records.clinical_problem: classifying fetal brain abnormalities on MRI before birth, across a wide span of gestational ages rather than at one fixed age
records.patient_population: fetuses of widespread gestational ages imaged with brain MRI
records.model_description: Pre-deep-learning in method but pointed in framing: most work on early brain abnormality classification had been done on newborns and premature infants, and this pushes the same question back before birth and across gestational ages rather than at a single one. Handcrafted features with a bank of classical classifiers and ensembles compared against their base models; k-nearest neighbour won.
records.headline_result: highest accuracy and AUC around 95% using the k-nearest neighbour classifier

records.title: Diagnosis and classification of pediatric acute appendicitis by artificial intelligence methods: An investigator-independent approach.
records.model_family: machine-learning classifier on a routine biomarker signature
records.clinical_problem: deciding whether a child with abdominal pain has appendicitis, and whether it is complicated
records.patient_population: 590 children and adolescents aged 0-17 with suspected appendicitis at a Berlin hospital (473 histologically confirmed, 117 negative)
records.model_description: Combines the appendiceal diameter measured on ultrasound with the full blood count and C-reactive protein, all of which are obtained routinely anyway, and returns a diagnosis of appendicitis. The framing is investigator-independent: no expert interpretation is needed. Discrimination of appendicitis from no appendicitis is good; separating complicated from uncomplicated inflammation, the decision that would actually change management toward antibiotics, is not.
records.dataset_size: 590 patients, with at most 35% used for discovery and training
records.headline_result: 90% accuracy for appendicitis (93% sensitivity, 67% specificity); only 51% accuracy for identifying complicated inflammation

records.title: Treatment response prediction of rehabilitation program in children with cerebral palsy using radiomics strategy: protocol for a multicenter prospective cohort study in west China.
records.journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
records.clinical_problem: predicting individualized response to rehabilitation treatment in children with cerebral palsy using MRI radiomics combined with clinical data
records.patient_population: 130 children with cerebral palsy, multicenter cohort in west China (planned)
records.model_description: Protocol combining MRI radiomics features with clinical and socioeconomic data as input to predict individualized rehabilitation treatment response in children with cerebral palsy; not yet reporting results.
records.study_design: study protocol for a multicenter prospective cohort study (radiomics-based treatment-response prediction)

records.title: Epilepsy and Autism Spectrum Disorder: An Epidemiological Study in Shanghai, China.

records.title: Vertebral rotation estimation from frontal X-rays using a quasi-automated pedicle detection method.
records.journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
records.model_family: image analysis + machine learning-based pedicle detector
records.clinical_problem: automating measurement of vertebral axial rotation (a scoliosis severity marker) from frontal spine X-rays by automatically locating the pedicles
records.patient_population: 149 healthy and adolescent idiopathic scoliosis subjects; validation cohort of 11 healthy (age 6-33) and 46 AIS (age 6-16) subjects
records.model_description: Input: frontal spine radiographs; output: automatically detected pedicle landmarks used to calculate vertebral axial rotation (Stokes method), combining image analysis, machine learning and minimal manual input.
records.dataset_size: 149 subjects (development); validation set of 11 healthy + 46 AIS subjects
records.headline_result: pedicle localization precision 84%, mean difference 1.2±1.2 mm; VAR signed difference -0.2±3.4°
records.study_design: retrospective method development and validation against manual annotation

records.title: Semi Supervised Learning with Deep Embedded Clustering for Image Classification and Segmentation.
records.journal: IEEE access : practical innovations, open solutions
records.model_family: semi-supervised framework pairing supervised CNN feature learning with deep embedded clustering, implemented on a 3D densely connected fully convolutional network
records.clinical_problem: the cost of expert annotation in medical image segmentation, demonstrated on isointense infant brain MRI tissue segmentation, where the labels are especially expensive because white and gray matter look alike at 6-8 months
records.patient_population: isointense-phase infant brain MRI, alongside MNIST and SVHN benchmark classification tasks
records.model_description: A semi-supervised method with a design property that matters more than its accuracy: it needs few hyperparameters, so it does not require the large labeled validation set that most semi-supervised algorithms quietly assume - which defeats the purpose when labels are the scarce resource. Validated on standard benchmarks and then on the isointense infant segmentation problem, where it beat both supervised-only training and pseudo-labelling.
records.dataset_size: not stated for the infant MRI task
records.headline_result: significant improvement over supervised-only training and over pseudo-labelling for isointense infant brain MRI tissue segmentation; 0.46% error on MNIST with 1000 labels and 4.43% on SVHN with 500

records.title: Development of a Plasma Screening Panel for Pediatric Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease Using Metabolomics.
records.exclusion_reason: plasma metabolomics screening panel for pediatric fatty liver disease; imaging is part of the reference standard, not the model input

records.title: Aleatoric uncertainty estimation with test-time augmentation for medical image segmentation with convolutional neural networks.
records.model_family: test-time augmentation for CNN segmentation uncertainty
records.clinical_problem: knowing when to distrust an automated fetal brain segmentation
records.patient_population: fetuses imaged with MRI; brain tumor MRI is used as a second test case
records.model_description: A way of putting an uncertainty estimate on a segmentation: the same image is transformed several ways at test time and the spread of the resulting segmentations is treated as image-based uncertainty, formalized as Monte Carlo sampling over an image acquisition model. Applied to fetal brain and brain tumor MRI, it flags overconfident wrong predictions better than dropout-based model uncertainty alone.
records.headline_result: better uncertainty estimation than test-time dropout alone, and higher accuracy than single-prediction segmentation

records.clinical_problem: distinguishing children with autism spectrum disorder from typically developing children using resting-state functional connectivity, across multiple imaging sites
records.patient_population: 190 male children ages 6.5-13 (102 with ASD, 88 typically developing) from the ABIDE multi-site public dataset
records.model_description: Input is resting-state fMRI functional connectivity between brain regions; a linear-kernel SVM classifies children as ASD or typically developing, trained on data from some sites and cross-validated on held-out sites.

records.headline_result: mean classification AUC 0.75+/-0.05; best site combination AUC 0.83

records.clinical_problem: predicting future gait impairment in toddlers born very-low-birth-weight preterm from near-term brain white-matter microstructure on diffusion tensor imaging
records.patient_population: 66 VLBW preterm infants imaged near-term; 52/66 completed gait follow-up at 18-22 months

records.headline_result: logistic regression: 93%/79% sensitivity/specificity for gait velocity; up to 100%/100% for single-limb support
records.study_design: prospective cohort study with statistical learning models and leave-one-out cross-validation

records.patient_population: 32 neonates with acute bilirubin encephalopathy, 29 age-matched controls

records.headline_result: Best AUC 0.946 (decision tree)

records.title: Deep Learning for Chest Radiograph Diagnosis in the Emergency Department.

The algorithms detect scoliosis, flag curves of 20 degrees or more, and grade severity, with the aim of triaging who actually needs imaging and of following untreated cases without repeated radiation.
records.headline_result: accuracy superior to human specialists for detecting scoliosis, for detecting curves of 20 degrees or more, and for severity grading

records.patient_population: infant subjects with risk of ASD, around 24 months of age (NDAR)
records.model_description: A dilated-dense U-Net automatically segments the amygdala and hippocampal subfields from infant brain MRI to enable volumetric analysis linked to autism spectrum disorder risk.

records.patient_population: 90 neonates
records.model_description: Spherical convolution, pooling and upsampling operations extend CNNs (U-Net and SegNet architectures) to spherical cortical surface meshes, taking neonatal cortical surface data as input and outputting a parcellation into anatomical regions.
records.headline_result: Outperformed spherical SegNet and a prior patch-wise classification method (no single number reported in abstract)

records.patient_population: 298 pregnant women with suspected placenta accreta spectrum disorders undergoing cesarean delivery (207 training, 91 external validation)

records.study_design: multicentre retrospective radiomics study with external validation

records.title: Age Assessment of Youth and Young Adults Using Magnetic Resonance Imaging of the Knee: A Deep Learning Approach.
records.model_family: two convolutional networks - one selecting the most informative slices of an MRI sequence, one estimating age from them - with GoogLeNet pretrained on ImageNet performing best
records.clinical_problem: age assessment in the range where hand bone age saturates and the growth zones close (14-21 years), for clinical use and for legal age estimation where documents are lacking - without ionizing radiation
records.patient_population: 402 volunteers aged 14-21 years (221 male, 181 female) imaged with knee MRI
records.model_description: Targets the specific age band where hand radiographs stop being informative, using the knee, whose growth plates close later - and does it on MRI, which matters because the legal use of age assessment on undocumented young people cannot ethically justify irradiating them. The result is reported at the threshold that actually gets contested, 18 years, where accuracy was 98.1% for males and 95.0% for females. A first network selecting which slices to use is a sensible answer to sequence-level input.
records.headline_result: mean absolute error 0.793 years for males aged 14-20.5 and 0.988 years for females aged 14-19.5; 98.1% and 95.0% accuracy classifying minors at the 18-year threshold

records.title: Alteration of the anatomical covariance network after corpus callosotomy in pediatric intractable epilepsy.

records.title: ASD-DiagNet: A Hybrid Learning Approach for Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using fMRI Data.
records.model_family: autoencoder jointly trained with a single-layer perceptron classifier
records.clinical_problem: classifying autism spectrum disorder from resting-state fMRI
records.patient_population: 1,035 subjects from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE), across 17 imaging centers
records.model_description: ASD-DiagNet takes resting-state fMRI connectivity features and jointly trains an autoencoder with a single-layer-perceptron classifier to distinguish individuals with autism spectrum disorder from healthy controls. A linear-interpolation data-augmentation strategy generates synthetic training examples, and the method was evaluated on the public ABIDE dataset (1,035 subjects, 17 imaging centers). Code and trained model are released publicly.
records.release_evidence: "The implemented code is available as GPL license on GitHub portal of our lab (https://github.com/pcdslab/ASD-DiagNet)"
records.headline_result: Up to 28% increase in classification accuracy over prior state-of-the-art methods, maximum accuracy 82%, and much faster runtime (40 min vs. 7 h)
records.study_design: retrospective multi-site classification study using a public dataset

records.title: Automatic extraction of the intracranial volume in fetal and neonatal MR scans using convolutional neural networks.
records.model_family: convolutional neural network for intracranial volume segmentation
records.clinical_problem: segmenting the intracranial volume in fetal and neonatal MRI, the preprocessing step that brain tissue segmentation depends on and that is defeated by rapid growth, motion artifacts and inconsistent fields of view
records.patient_population: fetal and neonatal scans spanning 23-45 weeks postmenstrual age, varying field strength, acquisition plane and resolution, and including posthaemorrhagic ventricular dilatation, stroke, asphyxia and Down syndrome
records.model_description: Deliberately trained and tested across the heterogeneity that usually breaks these tools - three axes of acquisition variation, a 22-week age span, and four different pathologies - and the Dice range of 0.98 to 0.99 across all of it is the claim. That robustness is what makes it usable as a generic preprocessing step rather than a study-specific one, which is how the authors position it.
records.headline_result: Dice 0.98 to 0.99 across neonatal and fetal scans regardless of acquisition parameters or patient pathology

records.title: Optimization of Fetal Biometry With 3D Ultrasound and Image Recognition (EPICEA): protocol for a prospective cross-sectional study.
records.clinical_problem: Assessing whether automated 3D ultrasound image-recognition software can reduce variability in fetal biometric measurements (head/abdominal circumference, femur length) used to estimate gestational age and monitor fetal growth
records.patient_population: 225 fetuses, 16-30 weeks of gestation (planned enrollment)
records.model_description: Automated software extracts standard reference planes from 3D ultrasound volumes of the fetal head, abdomen, and femur and computes biometric measurements automatically, to be compared with manual 2D ultrasound measurements for agreement and reproducibility.
records.study_design: prospective cross-sectional study protocol (trial registration NCT03812471)

records.title: Identifying fetal yawns based on temporal dynamics of mouth openings: A preterm neonate model using support vector machines (SVMs).
records.exclusion_reason: The SVM classifier for identifying yawns was developed and tested on video-based behavioral coding of preterm neonates' mouth movements, not on ultrasound images; the intended future application to fetal ultrasound is discussed but not implemented or tested here.

records.title: Performance of deep learning-based algorithm for detection of ileocolic intussusception on abdominal radiographs of young children.
records.model_family: YOLOv3-based detector that localizes the right abdomen and classifies it
records.clinical_problem: screening for ileocolic intussusception on the abdominal radiograph, which is usually the first imaging a young child with suspected intussusception receives and which is insensitive when read by eye
records.patient_population: 681 children aged 5 years or under (242 with intussusception) imaged March 2005 to December 2017 for training, and 75 children (25 with intussusception) from January to August 2018 for validation, with ultrasound as the reference standard
records.model_description: Built around a clinical observation rather than a generic classifier: intussusception lives in the right abdomen, so the detector is trained to find that rectangle first and judge it second. The result is the one worth carrying - the algorithm's sensitivity was 0.76 against the radiologists' 0.46 on the same films, with no loss of specificity. Radiographs miss most intussusceptions when read conventionally, which is why the comparison is so lopsided and why a screening aid here has real value.
records.headline_result: sensitivity 0.76 for the algorithm versus 0.46 for radiologists (p = 0.013), with specificity 0.96 versus 0.92 (p = 0.32)
records.study_design: retrospective model development with temporal validation and reader comparison

records.title: Non-contact physiological monitoring of preterm infants in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit.

records.model_description: BiSeNet, a convolutional network combining a spatial path and a context path via feature fusion, segments the left ventricle and left atrium on pediatric echocardiography images, replacing time-consuming manual sonographer segmentation. It was trained and evaluated on 87 echocardiography videos (2,216 images) from Shenzhen Children's Hospital against sonographers' manual ground truth.
records.dataset_size: 87 echocardiography videos (2,216 images) from Shenzhen Children's Hospital
records.headline_result: Dice index 0.914 (left ventricle), 0.887 (left atrium)

records.title: Ultrasound Image Representation Learning by Modeling Sonographer Visual Attention
records.model_family: convolutional network trained to predict sonographer gaze by visual saliency prediction or gaze-point regression, then transferred to standard plane detection
records.clinical_problem: learning transferable image representations without manual class labels, which are in any case a simplistic approximation of how a sonographer understands an image
records.patient_population: a gaze tracking dataset of sonographers performing routine clinical fetal anomaly screening
records.model_description: Argues that class labels throw away most of what an expert knows, and that where they look is a richer and free signal. The evaluation is careful in a way that matters: besides fine-tuning, the authors train a simple softmax on each layer's activations, which measures the representation itself rather than the transfer hyperparameters - and finds the attention-derived features approach a fully supervised baseline at every layer but the last. The largest fine-tuning gain was on the cardiac planes, which are the hardest.
records.dataset_size: a unique sonographer gaze tracking dataset
records.headline_result: fine-tuning the saliency predictor beat random initialization by 9.6% F1 overall and 15.3% for the cardiac planes, with layer-wise representations approaching a fully supervised baseline

records.title: Visualizing and explaining deep learning predictions for pneumonia detection in pediatric chest radiographs
records.model_family: convolutional networks with activation and prediction visualization tools
records.clinical_problem: pneumonia detection in children's chest radiographs, and the opacity of the models proposed to do it - a bottleneck for screening in the field where poorly interpreted model behaviour would drive decisions
records.patient_population: pediatric chest radiographs
records.model_description: An early argument, made specifically about pediatric chest radiography, that visualization is not an optional extra: the paper's stated purpose is to see what the network activates on and to statistically validate performance against bias, overfitting and generalization error rather than to post a higher number. It also makes the point that pediatric pneumonia is poorly studied relative to adult pneumonia, which is the recurring theme of this whole database.
records.headline_result: demonstration that visualizing and explaining CNN activations for pediatric chest radiograph pneumonia detection helps reduce bias, overfitting and generalization error

records.title: Discriminant Analysis Deep Neural Networks
records.journal: 2019 53rd Annual Conference on Information Sciences and Systems (CISS)
records.model_family: residual networks trained with a Discriminant Analysis Loss Function that minimizes within-class and maximizes between-class variance without eigen-decomposition
records.clinical_problem: pneumonia classification on pediatric chest radiographs, used here as the medical test bed for a new representation-learning objective
records.patient_population: the pediatric pneumonia chest X-ray dataset
records.model_description: A loss-function paper that chose pediatric pneumonia as its medical benchmark. The contribution is computational as much as conceptual - earlier discriminant-analysis losses required eigen-decomposition and matrix inversion, and avoiding both makes the objective usable inside a deep network. Reported to beat the results published with the dataset itself, at 96.63% accuracy with the usual asymmetry between sensitivity (99.2%) and specificity (92.3%).
records.headline_result: 96.63% accuracy with sensitivity 99.23% and specificity 92.30% on the pediatric pneumonia dataset, better than the results published with the dataset

records.journal: 2019 IEEE 16th International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI 2019)

records.patient_population: full-length routine fetal anomaly ultrasound scan videos
records.model_description: The validation is the interesting part: rather than only reporting classification accuracy, the authors apply the model to unlabelled full-length scans and check whether the workflow statistics it derives match those from manually labelled videos - a correlation of 0.95, which is the evidence that the automated description is usable as a measurement instrument. Short- and long-term temporal contributions are ablated, with the multi-stream combination winning.
records.headline_result: top-1 accuracy 0.77 and top-3 accuracy 0.94, with automated workflow statistics on unlabelled scans correlating with manually labelled videos at rho = 0.95 (p = 0.0004)

records.title: Residual Attention Based Network for Hand Bone Age Assessment
records.journal: 2019 IEEE 16th International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI 2019)
records.model_family: Mask R-CNN hand segmentation followed by a residual attention network with hierarchical attention components
records.clinical_problem: bone age assessment from hand radiographs, where whole-image models are distracted by everything in the film that is not hand
records.patient_population: the RSNA pediatric bone age dataset
records.model_description: Two ideas both borrowed from how clinicians work: segment the hand away from X-ray tags and background before anything else, and use hierarchical attention so the network concentrates on the key components of the hand as the Tanner-Whitehouse procedure does. The attention maps double as visual support for the prediction, which is what makes the output arguable rather than opaque.
records.dataset_size: the RSNA pediatric bone age dataset
records.headline_result: superior performance to previous methods on the RSNA pediatric bone age dataset, with attention maps as visual support for each prediction

records.title: Frnet: Flattened Residual Network for Infant MRI Skull Stripping
records.journal: 2019 IEEE 16th International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI 2019)
records.model_family: flattened residual network with a boundary loss for ambiguous low-contrast regions and an artifact simulator for augmentation
records.clinical_problem: skull stripping infant brain MRI, where the brain is small and tissue intensities change rapidly through the early months, so methods built for adults fail
records.patient_population: 343 subjects from newborn to 48 months
records.model_description: Three responses to three specific failures: a simplified architecture for robustness, a boundary loss aimed exactly at the ambiguous brain/non-brain interface that low contrast produces in infants, and an artifact simulator so the model sees poor-quality images during training rather than meeting them first at deployment. Tested across the whole 0-48 month range and reported to beat the state of the art in every age band, which matters because infant methods often work at one age and not another.
records.headline_result: better than state-of-the-art skull stripping in all age groups across a 343-subject dataset spanning newborns to 48-month-olds

records.title: Ensemble Machine Learning for Estimating Fetal Weight at Varying Gestational Age
records.journal: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
records.model_family: ensemble of random forest, XGBoost and LightGBM over cubic-spline-fitted characteristics extracted from ultrasound reports
records.clinical_problem: estimating fetal weight, where ultrasound-based estimation varies between populations, demands strict operating technique from the sonographer and is unavailable in low-resource areas - and where inaccurate estimates cause adverse perinatal outcomes
records.patient_population: 4212 intrapartum recordings
records.model_description: Works on ultrasound-derived biometric characteristics across gestation rather than on images, fitting each with a cubic spline so the model sees a trajectory rather than a snapshot - which is what distinguishes it from the biometry formulas it competes with. The proposed intersection-over-union evaluation acknowledges that fetal weight estimation produces a range rather than a point. Positioned partly as a self-monitoring tool for pregnant women, which is a strong claim on this evidence.
records.headline_result: intersection-over-union of 0.64 with the ultrasound-derived weight range, improving estimation accuracy by 12% and reducing mean relative error by 3% compared with the ultrasound method

records.model_description: Another entry on the standard pediatric pneumonia benchmark, and unusually candid about its own weakness: sensitivity of 0.99 against specificity of 0.86, which the authors name as a limitation rather than burying under the accuracy figure. records.title: Joint Segmentation and Landmark Localization of Fetal Femur in Ultrasound Volumes
records.journal: 2019 IEEE EMBS International Conference on Biomedical & Health Informatics (BHI)
records.model_family: two-branch framework propagating cues bidirectionally between segmentation and landmark localization, with a distance-based loss and an adversarial module enforcing correspondence
records.clinical_problem: segmenting the fetal femur and placing its landmarks in 3D ultrasound volumes, both of which quantitative prenatal assessment needs and both of which are hard given poor image quality, ambiguous boundaries and anatomical variation
records.patient_population: a volumetric ultrasound dataset of fetal femur
records.model_description: Couples two tasks that are usually solved separately and lets each constrain the other - the segmentation tells the landmark branch where the bone is, and the landmarks tell the segmentation where its ends should be. The distance-based loss targets the specific failure mode of landmark detection, false positives elsewhere in the volume, and the adversarial module enforces that the two outputs agree.
records.headline_result: simultaneous segmentation and landmark localization of the fetal femur validated on a volumetric ultrasound dataset, with each task benefiting from the other

records.title: Automated Placenta Segmentation with a Convolutional Neural Network Weighted by Acoustic Shadow Detection
records.journal: 2019 41st Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society (EMBC)
records.model_family: convolutional network containing a layer weighted by automated acoustic shadow detection
records.clinical_problem: placental assessment on routine obstetric ultrasound is usually limited to location and previa, even though many complications originate in abnormal placental development - blocked by technical difficulty and the absence of objective echotexture criteria
records.patient_population: 1364 fetal ultrasound images from 247 patients acquired over 47 months on different machines, by different operators, across a range of gestational ages
records.model_description: The shadow-weighted layer is an artifact-specific piece of engineering: acoustic shadowing is the dominant ultrasound artifact and the network is told where it is, rather than being left to learn around it. The ablation quantifies exactly what that buys - Dice rises from 0.75 to 0.87 on the shadowed subset while barely moving overall, which is the right way to justify a mechanism aimed at a subset of cases. Deliberately heterogeneous acquisition over four years, and framed as a preprocessing step for larger-scale placental analysis.
records.headline_result: Dice 0.92 +/- 0.04 overall, and 0.87 +/- 0.04 versus 0.75 +/- 0.05 on images containing acoustic shadows with and without the shadow detection layer

records.title: Efficient Ultrasound Image Analysis Models with Sonographer Gaze Assisted Distillation
records.model_family: teacher-student knowledge distillation where the teacher is trained with sonographer point-of-gaze alongside the ultrasound video

records.patient_population: ultrasound video with tracked point-of-gaze from expert sonographers, for fetal abdomen, head and femur frame classification
records.model_description: Combines two ideas cleanly: expert gaze as a second form of supervision, and distillation to move what the teacher learned into a model small enough to deploy. The headline ratio is the interesting one - models a thousand times smaller landing within 5% of conventional ones - which is the argument for putting fetal biometry on a phone or a handheld probe rather than a workstation.

records.title: Fully Automatic Pediatric Echocardiography Segmentation Using Deep Convolutional Networks Based on BiSeNet
records.journal: 2019 41st Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society (EMBC)
records.model_family: Bilateral Segmentation Network (BiSeNet) with a spatial path, a context path and a feature fusion module
records.clinical_problem: segmenting the four-chamber view in pediatric echocardiography, which is the preprocessing step for most quantitative cardiac analysis and is currently done by hand by the sonographer
records.patient_population: a self-collected pediatric echocardiography dataset, four-chamber view
records.model_description: One of the few conference papers here on pediatric rather than fetal echocardiography, which is a distinct problem - the heart is larger and faster and the views are the same ones used in adults, so the sparse pediatric literature is more a matter of data access than of difficulty. The two-path architecture separates fine spatial detail from semantic context, and it beat several U-Net variants on left ventricle and left atrium segmentation.
records.headline_result: Dice 0.932 for left ventricle and 0.908 for left atrium, outperforming several U-Net architectures

records.title: Harmonization of Infant Cortical Thickness Using Surface-to-Surface Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Networks
records.model_family: surface-to-surface CycleGAN combining a spherical U-Net with cycle consistency and a correlation coefficient loss
records.clinical_problem: pooling infant neuroimaging across sites, where differences between MRI scanners introduce non-biological variance into cortical thickness that is indistinguishable from real developmental differences
records.patient_population: synthesized and real infant cortical surface data from multiple scanners
records.model_description: Harmonization framed as an image translation problem on the cortical surface rather than in the volume, which is the right domain since cortical thickness is a surface measurement. The design tension is stated exactly: the translation must remove the scanner effect while preserving individual differences, and cycle consistency plus a correlation loss are what stop it from erasing the biology it is meant to protect. Directly relevant to the multi-site infant consortia this field increasingly depends on.
records.headline_result: superior removal of scanner effects while preserving individual differences compared with state-of-the-art harmonization methods, on both synthesized and real infant cortical data

records.title: Agent with Warm Start and Active Termination for Plane Localization in 3D Ultrasound
records.model_family: reinforcement learning agent with a landmark-aware alignment module for warm start and a recurrent network deciding when to stop
records.clinical_problem: locating fetal brain standard planes inside a 3D ultrasound volume, where 3D acquisition removes the operator dependence of finding planes with a 2D probe but leaves a huge search space and wide variation in fetal posture
records.patient_population: an in-house large dataset of 3D fetal brain ultrasound volumes
records.model_description: Two sensible fixes to a reinforcement learning agent in a large search space: give it a warm start from detected landmarks so it does not wander, and let a recurrent network decide when it has arrived rather than stopping after a fixed number of steps. The active termination improves accuracy and speed together, which is unusual. Errors around 3 mm and 9 degrees for the transcerebellar and transthalamic planes.
records.headline_result: 3.4 mm / 9.6 degrees for the transcerebellar plane and 2.7 mm / 9.1 degrees for the transthalamic plane

records.title: TUNA-Net: Task-Oriented UNsupervised Adversarial Network for Disease Recognition in Cross-domain Chest X-rays
records.model_family: task-driven, discriminatively trained cycle-consistent generative adversarial network for unsupervised domain adaptation
records.clinical_problem: recognizing pneumonia on pediatric chest radiographs without labelling a pediatric dataset, by adapting a model trained on labelled adult radiographs
records.patient_population: two public chest X-ray datasets - labelled adult radiographs as the source domain and unlabelled pediatric radiographs as the target
records.model_description: Directly addresses the structural asymmetry of chest radiograph AI: adult labelled data is abundant, pediatric labelled data is not, and the two domains look different enough that a model does not transfer. Translating adult radiographs to look pediatric while preserving disease semantics is a clean statement of the problem, and the loss is built to preserve low-level detail, mid-level features and high-level semantics rather than only fooling a discriminator. Reaching AUC 96.3% without any pediatric labels against 98.1% with them quantifies how much the labels are worth.
records.headline_result: AUC 96.3% for pediatric pneumonia classification without any target-domain labels, against 98.1% for the fully supervised approach

records.title: PRSNet: Part Relation and Selection Network for Bone Age Assessment
records.model_family: part relation module discovering concurrency among anatomical parts from multi-scale context, plus a part selection module ranking their importance, trained end to end

The framing is faithful to the clinical procedure - a radiologist reads the hand as a configuration, not a set of separate bones - and it set the state of the art on the RSNA benchmark by a significant margin.
records.dataset_size: the RSNA 2017 pediatric bone age dataset
records.headline_result: state-of-the-art performance on the public RSNA 2017 Pediatric Bone Age benchmark, outperforming competitive methods by a significant margin

records.title: Structural neuroimaging biomarkers for obsessive-compulsive disorder in the ENIGMA-OCD consortium: medication matters
records.model_family: multivariate classification on standardized cortical and subcortical measures
records.clinical_problem: whether structural MRI can distinguish an individual with obsessive-compulsive disorder from a healthy control, which no diagnostic biomarker currently does
records.patient_population: 2,304 patients and 2,068 controls across 46 datasets, spanning adult and pediatric (<18) samples
records.model_description: A large negative result, and the most useful kind. Across 46 sites, classification of obsessive-compulsive disorder from structural MRI was poor within the pooled sample and fell to chance when models were validated on data from sites they had never seen. Good performance appeared only within medication-defined subgroups, which is a warning that an apparent imaging biomarker can be a treatment marker. Anyone quoting single-site classification accuracies in a developmental disorder should read this first.
records.headline_result: AUC 0.57-0.62 on the pooled sample and no better than chance (0.51-0.54) on completely new sites; above 0.8 only within medication-stratified subgroups

records.patient_population: 80 pregnancies between 18 and 39 weeks: 46 healthy and 34 with fetal growth restriction
records.model_description: Characterizes the placenta rather than the fetus, on the reasoning that placental function is what constrains growth. Shape features (volume, thickness, elongation) are combined with first-order and co-occurrence texture measures from 3D T2-weighted MRI to identify growth-restricted pregnancies and estimate birth weight, in both healthy and affected fetuses.
records.headline_result: 86% accuracy, 77% precision and 86% recall for identifying fetal growth restriction; birth weight error 0.3% in healthy and -2.6% in growth-restricted fetuses

records.title: Application of pattern recognition techniques for classification of pediatric brain tumors by in vivo 3T 1 H-MR spectroscopy-A multi-center study.
records.model_family: linear discriminant analysis, support vector machine and random forest classifiers over TARQUIN-processed metabolite profiles, with borderline SMOTE oversampling
records.clinical_problem: telling medulloblastoma, pilocytic astrocytoma and ependymoma apart non-invasively from proton MR spectroscopy, in a population where biopsy of a posterior fossa mass carries real risk
records.patient_population: 41 children with brain tumors - 17 medulloblastomas, 20 pilocytic astrocytomas and 4 ependymomas - scanned across four different hospitals at 3 T
records.model_description: Spectroscopy rather than image texture, which means the features are named metabolites and the model is chemically interpretable in a way radiomics is not. The question is specifically about the move from 1.5 T to 3 T: the earlier multi-centre work was done at 1.5 T, and this shows the extra spectral resolution translates into better discrimination. Four hospitals, but only 41 children and four ependymomas, so class imbalance is handled by oversampling and the estimate is fragile.
records.headline_result: support vector machine gave the highest balanced accuracy for three-way discrimination, higher than previously reported for a comparable multi-centre 1.5 T dataset

records.title: Please Don't Move-Evaluating Motion Artifact From Peripheral Quantitative Computed Tomography Scans Using Textural Features.

records.patient_population: adolescent peripheral quantitative CT datasets (tibial and radial diaphyses/epiphyses)
records.model_description: A texture-based decision tree classifier takes peripheral quantitative CT image features and classifies scans as motion-affected or acceptable.
records.headline_result: kappa 0.57-0.80 (validation dataset), kappa 0.01-0.39 (independent cross-sectional dataset)
records.study_design: retrospective classifier development and cross-dataset validation study

records.title: Development of a tool to aid the radiologic technologist using augmented reality and computer vision.

records.patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing computed/digital radiography
records.model_description: An augmented-reality device combining a color/depth camera with computer-vision software displays real-time patient positioning, body-part thickness, and motion detection to technologists during pediatric X-ray acquisition, aiming to reduce repeat exposures.

records.title: Network basis of suicidal ideation in depressed adolescents.

records.title: Radiomics in paediatric neuro-oncology: A multicentre study on MRI texture analysis.
records.model_family: support vector machine on 3D texture features
records.clinical_problem: non-invasive diagnosis of childhood brain tumors, which despite advances in MRI has not reached routine practice
records.patient_population: children with brain tumors imaged at multiple UK centres
records.model_description: The question this asks is the one most single-centre radiomics papers do not: does a texture classifier trained at one hospital work at another. It answers it by rigorous pairwise testing between centres, finding AUCs of 76-86% on unseen sites and that similar texture features are enhanced by images from different hospitals. It also examines class imbalance, which is unavoidable when some childhood tumor types are much rarer than others.
records.dataset_size: a multicentre clinical MRI cohort; size not stated
records.headline_result: AUC 76-86% across pairwise cross-centre testing, indicating transferable tumour texture information

records.title: Whole brain white matter connectivity analysis using machine learning: An application to autism.
records.model_family: data-driven fiber clustering with a machine-learning classifier on cluster diffusion features
records.clinical_problem: identifying which white matter connections are altered in autism, and whether that can classify individual children
records.patient_population: 149 children: 70 with autism spectrum disorder and 79 typically developing controls
records.model_description: Clusters whole-brain tractography into anatomically meaningful fiber groups, describes each cluster by its diffusion properties, and uses those as features to classify a child as autistic or not. Because the features are named tracts rather than voxels, the model says which connections carried the decision: corpus callosum, arcuate and uncinate fasciculi, aslant tract, and cerebellar and brainstem connections, with the crossing-fiber tensor most affected.
records.headline_result: 78.33% cross-validated classification accuracy

records.title: Performance of a Deep-Learning Neural Network Model in Assessing Skeletal Maturity on Pediatric Hand Radiographs.
records.clinical_problem: skeletal maturity (bone age) assessment in the workup of endocrine and metabolic disorders
records.patient_population: children undergoing clinical hand radiography at two children's hospitals
records.model_description: Takes a hand radiograph and returns an estimated bone age. Trained on 14,036 clinical hand radiographs and their reports from two children's hospitals, then compared against the mean of the clinical report and three additional reviewers on a 200-examination test set, and against a published automated model on the public Digital Hand Atlas.
records.dataset_size: 14,036 clinical hand radiographs for training and validation; 200-examination and 913-examination test sets
records.headline_result: mean difference from reviewers 0 years; root mean square 0.63 years and mean absolute difference 0.50 years
records.study_design: retrospective two-center diagnostic accuracy with reader comparison

records.title: Spatial Compounding of 3-D Fetal Brain Ultrasound Using Probabilistic Maps.
records.clinical_problem: Reducing shadowing artifact in 3D fetal brain ultrasound to improve visibility of brain structures for monitoring and diagnosis of brain defects
records.patient_population: Phantom and real fetal head ultrasound volumes
records.model_description: An SVM trained on textural features assigns weights (posterior probabilities of brain tissue vs. shadow) used to spatially compound multiple 3D fetal head ultrasound projections into a single clearer volume
records.dataset_size: not stated exactly (phantom + real fetal head volumes)
records.headline_result: Signal-to-noise ratio improved up to 35% and contrast-to-noise ratio up to 135% versus prior compounding methods
records.study_design: retrospective algorithm development and phantom/clinical validation study

records.title: Psychoradiologic Utility of MR Imaging for Diagnosis of Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder: A Radiomics Analysis.
records.model_family: random forest on shape and diffusion radiomic features
records.clinical_problem: diagnosis of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and separation of its inattentive and combined subtypes
records.patient_population: 83 newly diagnosed, never-treated children with ADHD aged 7-14 and 87 age- and sex-matched healthy controls
records.model_description: Takes structural and diffusion MRI, extracts gray-matter shape and white-matter diffusion features, selects the ones with real discriminative power inside cross-validation loops, and classifies a child as having ADHD or not, and then which subtype. Notably, total brain and tissue volumes did not differ between groups, so whatever signal exists is in shape rather than size.
records.headline_result: 73.7% accuracy for ADHD versus control, 80.1% for inattentive versus combined subtype

records.clinical_problem: identifying interhemispheric connectivity abnormalities in drug-naive first-episode adolescent-onset schizophrenia
records.patient_population: 48 drug-naive, first-episode adolescent-onset schizophrenia outpatients and 31 healthy controls
records.model_description: Voxel-mirrored homotopic connectivity values from resting-state fMRI go in; an SVM classifier outputs whether a scan is from an adolescent-onset schizophrenia patient or healthy control.
records.headline_result: sensitivity 100%, specificity 87.09%, accuracy 94.93%
records.study_design: case-control resting-state fMRI study with SVM classification

records.title: Prediction of cognitive and motor development in preterm children using exhaustive feature selection and cross-validation of near-term white matter microstructure.
records.model_family: linear and logistic models with exhaustive feature selection and leave-one-out cross-validation over regional diffusion tensor metrics
records.clinical_problem: predicting cognitive and motor development in very-low-birth-weight preterm children from the near-term MRI they already receive
records.patient_population: 66 very-low-birth-weight preterm neonates imaged at 36.6 +/- 1.8 weeks postmenstrual age, 60 of whom had Bayley-III assessment at 18-22 months
records.model_description: Searches the whole regional diffusion feature space exhaustively rather than testing pre-chosen tracts, and reports the specific three-region sets that come out - which makes the result checkable and the regions themselves a hypothesis for others to test. Separate models for cognitive and motor outcome, and separate treatment of classification (who is impaired) from regression (how much variance is explained); the classification numbers are far stronger than the 30% of score variance explained, and both are reported.
records.headline_result: cognitive impairment predicted at 100% sensitivity and specificity (AUC 1) and motor impairment at 90% sensitivity and 86% specificity (AUC 0.912), with about 30% of continuous score variance explained

records.clinical_problem: predicting the need for postnatal cerebrospinal fluid diversion (hydrocephalus treatment) in fetal ventriculomegaly
records.patient_population: discovery cohort: 25 patients requiring postnatal CSF diversion matched with 25 who did not, from 253 fetal ventriculomegaly patients; replication cohort: 24 patients from a separate institution
records.model_description: Linear measurements, area, volume and morphologic features are extracted from fetal MRI; a machine learning algorithm integrates these multiple features to predict which fetuses with ventriculomegaly will require postnatal CSF diversion, validated in an independent replication cohort.
records.dataset_size: discovery cohort 25+25 matched patients (from 253-patient database); replication cohort 24 patients
records.headline_result: discovery cohort: 82% accuracy, 80% sensitivity, 84% specificity; replication cohort: 91% accuracy, 75% sensitivity, 95% specificity
records.study_design: retrospective case-control study with independent replication cohort

records.title: Subtyping cognitive profiles in Autism Spectrum Disorder using a Functional Random Forest algorithm.
records.model_family: random forest plus community detection on the resulting proximity matrix
records.clinical_problem: whether autism spectrum disorder contains distinct cognitive subtypes with different brain signatures
records.patient_population: 47 children with autism and 58 typically developing children aged 9-13
records.model_description: First classifies a child as autistic or typically developing from seven cognitive tasks, then reuses the forest's internal proximity between subjects to cluster them into subgroups, and finally asks whether those data-driven subgroups differ in resting-state functional connectivity. The clinical interest is in subtyping a heterogeneous diagnosis rather than in the classification accuracy, which is moderate.
records.headline_result: 72.7% classification accuracy (specificity 80.7%, sensitivity 63.1%); three autism and four typically developing subgroups identified
