records.title: Abnormal fronto-striatal activation as a marker of threshold and subthreshold Bulimia Nervosa.
records.model_family: multi-voxel pattern analysis classifier over task fMRI conflict-related activation
records.clinical_problem: whether the fronto-striatal disturbance of bulimia nervosa is present early, when the clinical picture is still subthreshold and the diagnosis is least certain
records.patient_population: two samples of adolescents with bulimia nervosa spectrum symptoms differing in severity, illness duration and age, compared with healthy adolescents, scanned during a Simon task
records.model_description: The design does something most classification studies do not: the classifier trained to separate fully symptomatic patients from healthy adolescents is then applied to the subthreshold group, and it transfers. That cross-severity generalization is a stronger claim than in-sample accuracy, because it says the same circuit disturbance is present before the disorder is, which is what would make it a risk marker rather than a consequence.
records.dataset_size: two adolescent patient samples plus healthy controls, sizes not stated in the abstract
records.headline_result: both threshold and subthreshold bulimia adolescents were accurately discriminated from healthy adolescents, and patterns learned from the severe group generalized to the subthreshold group
records.study_design: retrospective analysis of task fMRI cohorts

records.title: Neural preservation underlies speech improvement from auditory deprivation in young cochlear implant recipients.
records.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
records.model_family: machine-learning classifiers on regional neuroanatomical density and spatial pattern similarity
records.clinical_problem: predicting which deaf children will gain speech perception from a cochlear implant, before the operation
records.patient_population: children implanted before 3.5 years of age, compared against age-matched normally hearing children
records.model_description: Takes presurgical brain MRI from a cochlear implant candidate and predicts how much that individual child's speech perception will improve after implantation. The method first identifies which anatomical networks auditory deprivation has and has not affected; the predictive signal came from the unaffected regions, particularly auditory association and cognitive areas, suggesting what is preserved matters more than what is lost.
records.headline_result: highest classification accuracy, specificity and sensitivity came from brain regions unaffected by auditory deprivation

records.title: MABAL: a Novel Deep-Learning Architecture for Machine-Assisted Bone Age Labeling.
records.model_family: custom convolutional network trained from scratch
records.clinical_problem: bone age assessment, which is tedious and time consuming for the radiologist
records.patient_population: 10,289 skeletal age examinations, 8,909 from one institution's archive and 1,383 from the public Digital Hand Atlas
records.model_description: Argues, and demonstrates, that a network designed and trained from scratch for the specific task can beat transfer learning from natural images, given a large enough institutional dataset. Training is split into four cohorts by sex and age band, which reflects how Greulich and Pyle is applied in practice. Testing uses 20 radiographs per one-year age cohort rather than a random split, so performance is visible across the age range instead of averaged over it.
records.dataset_size: 10,289 training images across four sex and age cohorts
records.headline_result: reported to outperform existing proposed bone age algorithms; figures not stated in the abstract

It was developed on retinal OCT images and then retrained on pediatric chest radiographs to separate normal from pneumonia and bacterial from viral pneumonia. The paper's argument is that a general transfer-learning recipe needs far less labelled data than training from scratch.

records.title: Fully-automated alignment of 3D fetal brain ultrasound to a canonical reference space using multi-task learning.
records.clinical_problem: putting 3D fetal neurosonography volumes into a common reference frame despite arbitrary fetal position
records.patient_population: 140 fetal ultrasound volumes, gestational age 26.0 ± 4.4 weeks
records.model_description: Localizes the fetal brain, segments its structures, and aligns the volume to a reference coordinate system, all from one network with shared features and task-specific outputs. The coordinate system is defined anatomically from the skull boundary, eye sockets and head pose predicted from intracranial structures, which is what makes alignment robust to how the fetus happens to be lying.
records.headline_result: high brain overlap and low eye localization error on co-alignment, independent of gestational age or head size

records.title: VP-Nets : Efficient automatic localization of key brain structures in 3D fetal neurosonography.
records.model_family: three view-based convolutional networks predicting 2D projections of structures onto anatomical views, plus a 3D CNN skull-stripping tool
records.clinical_problem: locating key brain structures in 3D fetal neurosonography, which is used clinically to detect cerebral abnormalities and assess growth but which requires expertise and is tedious even then
records.patient_population: 3D fetal neurosonography volumes
records.model_description: The design imitates how a sonographer works a volume - looking at three orthogonal views rather than reasoning in 3D - and that choice is also what makes it fit in GPU memory at full resolution. The satisfying result is that the model pinpoints structures in 3D despite each stream only ever being supervised in 2D. Compared head to head with random forest and 3D U-Net baselines, and paired with a skull-stripping network so the pipeline takes a raw volume and needs no human step.
records.headline_result: center deviation 1.8 +/- 1.4 mm, size difference 1.9 +/- 1.5 mm and 3D IoU 63.2 +/- 14.7%, consistently outperforming random forest and 3D U-Net baselines

records.title: Combination of rs-fMRI and sMRI Data to Discriminate Autism Spectrum Disorders in Young Children Using Deep Belief Network.
records.model_family: deep belief network on combined functional and structural features
records.clinical_problem: diagnosing autism spectrum disorder in young children, where early diagnosis changes what intervention is possible
records.patient_population: 185 children aged 5-10 from the ABIDE I and II datasets (116 with autism, 69 controls)
records.model_description: Combines resting-state functional MRI with gray and white matter measures over anatomically labelled regions and learns a joint representation with a deep belief network, on the argument that earlier work used only shallow hand-computed features. Deliberately restricted to 5-10 year olds because that is where diagnosis matters. The accuracy is modest and the specificity is poor, which the numbers make plain.
records.headline_result: 65.56% accuracy (sensitivity 84%, specificity 33%, F1 74.76%) by 10-fold cross-validation
records.study_design: technical development on a public dataset

records.title: Distinguishing Adolescents With Conduct Disorder From Typically Developing Youngsters Based on Pattern Classification of Brain Structural MRI.
records.model_family: voxel-based morphometry feeding logistic regression, random forest and support vector machine classifiers, five-fold cross-validated
records.clinical_problem: whether the structural brain alterations reported in conduct disorder are large and consistent enough to identify an individual adolescent, rather than only to differ at group level
records.patient_population: 60 adolescents with conduct disorder and 60 age-matched healthy controls
records.model_description: Asks the right follow-up question to a group-difference literature - can these differences classify a person - and answers it with three classifiers that all land in the same range, which is reassuring against one model being overfitted. Eight regions across frontal, parietal, cingulate, cerebellar, lingual and insular areas carry the signal. Accuracy near 80% in 120 adolescents is a group-level effect strong enough to notice but not a diagnostic test, and the authors call the features potential biomarkers rather than a tool.
records.headline_result: accuracy 77.9-80.4%, sensitivity 75.4-87.5%, specificity 73.3-80.4% and AUC 0.76-0.80 across three classifiers

records.title: A computational framework for the detection of subcortical brain dysmaturation in neonatal MRI using 3D Convolutional Neural Networks.
records.model_family: three-dimensional convolutional neural networks combined with neonatal structural brain segmentation
records.clinical_problem: detecting cerebellar dysplasia - a subtle form of brain dysmaturation - in term infants born with congenital heart disease, where no reliable automated diagnostic tool exists and volume alone does not make the diagnosis
records.patient_population: term infants born with congenital heart disease, neonatal MRI, ten-fold cross-validation
records.model_description: Takes on the two things that usually stop deep learning working on neonatal MRI - small samples and structures that are barely differentiated by signal intensity - by pairing the network with an explicit structural segmentation. The class activation maps then do real scientific work rather than serving as a plausibility check: they localize the discriminating signal to the superior cerebellar surface, posterior lobe and midline vermis, which the authors connect to genetic mechanisms and neurodevelopmental outcome. Code released under the BSD licence.
records.release_evidence: the code developed for this project is open source, published under the BSD License and designed to be generalizable
records.headline_result: classification accuracy 0.985 +/- 0.024 for subtle cerebellar dysplasia in congenital heart disease under ten-fold cross-validation

records.title: Early prediction of cognitive deficits in very preterm infants using functional connectome data in an artificial neural network framework.

records.model_description: Learns a compressed representation of the functional connectome without labels, using a large public dataset, then uses that representation to predict 2-year cognitive outcome in a small preterm cohort. The transfer step is the point: neonatal cohorts are too small to train a deep model directly. Frontal lobe and somatosensory regions contributed most. The authors present it explicitly as proof of concept given the sample size.
records.dataset_size: 884 subjects for unsupervised pretraining; 28 very preterm infants for prediction
records.headline_result: 70.6% accuracy and AUC 0.76 for cognitive deficit at 2 years corrected age

records.title: Interactive Medical Image Segmentation Using Deep Learning With Image-Specific Fine Tuning.
records.model_family: CNN with image-specific fine tuning inside a bounding-box and scribble pipeline
records.clinical_problem: outlining fetal organs on MRI when only some organ classes were annotated for training
records.patient_population: fetuses imaged with MRI; a second application uses brain tumor MRI
records.model_description: The radiologist draws a bounding box, and optionally scribbles, and the network segments the structure inside it, fine-tuning itself on that specific image before producing the final contour. Because it adapts per image, it can outline organ classes that were never annotated during training. Demonstrated on fetal MRI organs and on brain tumor MRI.
records.headline_result: more robust than state-of-the-art CNNs on unseen object classes, with fewer user interactions and less user time than traditional interactive segmentation

records.title: Use of Machine Learning to Determine Deviance in Neuroanatomical Maturity Associated With Future Psychosis in Youths at Clinically High Risk.
records.model_family: supervised machine-learning brain-age regression on T1-weighted MRI
records.clinical_problem: identifying which clinically high-risk adolescents will convert to psychosis
records.patient_population: 953 healthy children aged 3-21 for model development; 275 clinically high-risk individuals (39 of whom developed psychosis) and 109 controls aged 12-21 for application
records.model_description: A model trained on structural MRI of healthy children to predict chronological age; the gap between that predicted age and the child's real age is then read as a measure of deviant neuroanatomical maturation. Applied to clinically high-risk adolescents, a larger gap was associated with higher risk of developing psychosis, but only in the younger part of the range.
records.dataset_size: 953 healthy children for training; 384 subjects for external validation and application
records.headline_result: clinically high-risk individuals showed a mean 0.64-year gap between predicted and chronological age versus controls (P = .008); greater deviation was associated with psychosis risk (P = .01)

records.title: Automatic Estimation of Fetal Abdominal Circumference From Ultrasound Images.
records.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
records.model_family: convolutional network classifying anatomical landmarks, followed by a Hough transform to fit the circumference
records.clinical_problem: automating abdominal circumference measurement, the hardest of the standard fetal biometry parameters because the abdomen has low and non-uniform contrast against its surroundings and an irregular outline
records.patient_population: clinical ultrasound data from 56 pregnant women, with two experts providing acceptance judgments
records.model_description: Built around how the sonographer decides rather than around end-to-end regression: the network is trained to recognize the three landmarks that define an acceptable abdominal plane - stomach bubble, amniotic fluid and umbilical vein - and only then does a Hough transform fit the circle. That keeps the training requirement small and the failures interpretable. The paper names its failure modes plainly, which is unusual: an oversized fetus, absent amniotic fluid, or a distorted abdominal outline.
records.headline_result: agreement of 0.809 and 0.771 with two experts, against 0.905 agreement between the two experts themselves; stable even on images degraded by shadowing
records.study_design: retrospective model development with expert acceptance check

records.title: 3-D Reconstruction in Canonical Co-Ordinate Space From Arbitrarily Oriented 2-D Images.
records.model_family: CNN regression predicting rigid transformations to a learned canonical atlas
records.clinical_problem: initializing slice-to-volume registration for fetal MRI, where heavy in-utero motion breaks optimization-based methods
records.patient_population: fetuses at around 20 weeks gestation, including heavily moving cases, plus simulated data
records.model_description: Predicts where an arbitrarily oriented 2D slice belongs in a canonical 3D atlas space from intensity alone, with no initialization. Conventional registration has a narrow capture range and needs a good starting estimate, which a heavily moving fetus does not provide; this removes that dependency and slots into a full reconstruction and motion compensation pipeline. It runs fast enough for real-time use.
records.dataset_size: simulated MRI plus real fetal MRI data
records.headline_result: average spatial prediction error 7 mm on simulated data, with qualitatively improved reconstructions for heavily moving fetuses at around 20 weeks

records.title: Diagnostic model for attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder based on interregional morphological connectivity.

records.clinical_problem: diagnosing ADHD in children from structural imaging, where previous models used regional features and reached limited accuracy
records.patient_population: children with ADHD and controls
records.model_description: Changes the feature rather than the classifier: instead of the volume or thickness of each region taken separately, it constructs an individual's interregional morphological connectivity - how regions covary in shape within one brain - and shows that this significantly outperforms regional features on the same data. The identified altered connections involved insula, caudal anterior cingulate, frontal pole and postcentral cortex, and correlated with clinical symptoms, which is the check that keeps the features interpretable rather than merely discriminative.
records.headline_result: total accuracy 74.65% with sensitivity 75% and specificity 74.29%, significantly better than a model built on regional features

records.title: Detection of Traumatic Pediatric Elbow Joint Effusion Using a Deep Convolutional Neural Network.
records.model_family: deep convolutional neural networks of varying depth and architecture, some ImageNet-pretrained and some randomly initialized

records.patient_population: 882 children presenting to the emergency department with upper extremity trauma, 901 lateral elbow radiographs
records.model_description: A direct test of whether a small pediatric dataset is enough. Fewer than 700 training radiographs, transfer learning from ImageNet, and a hyperparameter search on 115 validation images produced a classifier that reads elbow effusion at roughly 91 percent sensitivity and specificity. The clinical framing matters more than the numbers: effusion is the finding that tells the emergency physician to treat a child as fractured when no fracture line is visible.
records.headline_result: test-set AUC 0.943, sensitivity 0.909, specificity 0.906

records.title: Characterization of coronary artery pathological formations from OCT imaging using deep learning.

records.patient_population: 33 retrospective pullbacks of intracoronary cross-sectional OCT images from pediatric patients with Kawasaki disease
records.model_description: An unusual corner of pediatric imaging AI: intravascular OCT in the coronary arteries of children with Kawasaki disease, where the pathological formations differ from adult atherosclerosis and no reader has seen many of them. Rather than train from scratch on 33 cases, the authors take deep features from three ImageNet-pretrained networks and vote - the standard small-data recipe, applied to a disease that will never have a large dataset.
records.headline_result: accuracy, sensitivity and specificity up to 0.99 +/- 0.01 per tissue class with the majority voting scheme

records.title: Visual assessment versus computer-assisted gray scale analysis in the ultrasound evaluation of neonatal respiratory status.
records.model_family: computer-assisted gray scale analysis with textural features and machine learning, compared against a standardized visual score
records.clinical_problem: grading neonatal respiratory status from lung ultrasound at the cot side, against oxygenation as the reference, so that point-of-care ultrasound can substitute for blood gas sampling in the NICU
records.patient_population: 75 neonates admitted to the NICU for respiratory distress, with a 600-frame ultrasound dataset; oxygenation ratio and alveolar-arterial gradient as reference standards
records.model_description: The comparison is against a trained human reading the same frames, and the humans win - visual scoring correlated better with both oxygenation indices than the texture analysis did, with near-perfect interobserver agreement. That is a useful negative for a literature full of claims in the other direction, and the authors read it correctly, presenting computer-assisted analysis as a route to point-of-care diagnostics rather than as an improvement on the expert eye. Region-of-interest size mattered to the texture result.
records.headline_result: visual scoring correlated with oxygenation at r = -0.55 and 0.59 (kappa 0.91 between observers) versus r = -0.35 to -0.42 and 0.46 to 0.58 for gray scale texture analysis

records.journal: Machine learning in medical imaging. MLMI (Workshop)
records.model_family: multi-channel convolutional neural networks with a patch-level data-expanding strategy, inspired by deep multi-instance learning
records.clinical_problem: finding imaging biomarkers that identify infants at risk of autism, since diagnosis currently rests on behavioral observation at three or four years and intervention efforts miss the critical window before age two
records.patient_population: infants in the National Database for Autism Research (NDAR)
records.model_description: The clinical argument is the strongest part: autism is diagnosed behaviourally at three or four, the developmental window for intervention closes around two, and imaging is the only thing available before symptoms. Patch-level expansion is how a network gets trained on the handful of infant scans that exist - each brain becomes many training examples. A workshop paper reporting improvement over comparison methods rather than a deployable accuracy.
records.headline_result: significant improvement over comparison methods for early diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder from infant MRI

records.title: Machine-learning analysis outperforms conventional statistical models and CT classification systems in predicting 6-month outcomes in pediatric patients sustaining traumatic brain injury.
records.clinical_problem: predicting six-month outcome after pediatric traumatic brain injury, where adult CT grading systems are the only tools available
records.patient_population: 565 children under 18 who sustained traumatic brain injury and had a head CT within 24 hours
records.model_description: Predicts whether a child will have a favorable Glasgow Outcome Scale score six months after traumatic brain injury, from the admission head CT and clinical record. The comparison is the point: the established adult CT grading systems (Helsinki, Rotterdam, Marshall) were first evaluated on this pediatric cohort and found only moderately predictive, and the pediatric-specific network substantially outperformed all three.
records.headline_result: AUC 0.946 ± 0.042 versus 0.781-0.838 for the Helsinki, Rotterdam and Marshall CT scores

records.title: Automatic segmentation of OCT retinal boundaries using recurrent neural networks and graph search.
records.exclusion_reason: retinal optical coherence tomography layer segmentation; ophthalmic imaging is outside radiology as scoped for this database

records.title: AUTOMATIC RENAL SEGMENTATION IN DCE-MRI USING CONVOLUTIONAL NEURAL NETWORKS.
records.journal: Proceedings. IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging
records.model_family: cascade of two 3D convolutional neural networks using spatial and temporal information, one for localization and one for segmentation
records.clinical_problem: segmenting renal parenchyma on dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI in children, the step that stands between the acquisition and any quantitative measure of kidney function
records.patient_population: pediatric patients with normal kidneys and kidneys with varying degrees of hydronephrosis
records.model_description: Uses the contrast time course as an input rather than a nuisance, which is what distinguishes this from segmenting a static volume - the kidney is defined as much by how it enhances as by where it is. Performance is reported separately for normal and hydronephrotic kidneys, and the gap between 91.4 and 83.6 Dice is the honest measure of how much a dilated collecting system costs the model. Seconds per case, which is what makes routine functional analysis practical.
records.headline_result: mean Dice 91.4 for normal and 83.6 for abnormal pediatric kidneys, with runtime in the order of seconds

records.title: Automatic classification of pediatric pneumonia based on lung ultrasound pattern recognition.
records.model_family: neural network on brightness-distribution feature vectors
records.clinical_problem: diagnosing childhood pneumonia where there is no radiologist and no radiography, using lung ultrasound
records.patient_population: 21 children under 5 in Lima, Peru (15 with clinically and radiographically confirmed pneumonia, 6 without lung disease)
records.model_description: Strips out skin, fat and muscle from a lung ultrasound frame, divides the remaining image into rectangular segments, and classifies the brightness pattern of each as consolidated or normal lung. The motivation is explicitly resource-constrained: lung ultrasound detects pneumonia well but needs a trained interpreter, and this removes that requirement. The cohort is very small, which the accuracy figures should be read against.
records.dataset_size: 60 lung ultrasound frames from 21 children; 3,055 feature vectors
records.headline_result: 90.9% sensitivity and 100% specificity for pneumonia infiltrates

records.title: A Review of Denoising Medical Images Using Machine Learning  Approaches.
records.exclusion_reason: general review of ML image-denoising methods across radiology; not focused on pediatrics

records.title: Imbalance of Functional Connectivity and Temporal Entropy in Resting-State Networks in Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Machine Learning Approach.
records.clinical_problem: Distinguishing individuals with autism spectrum disorder from controls using patterns of brain network connectivity and signal irregularity on resting-state fMRI
records.patient_population: Individuals with ASD and controls from the ABIDE cohort (ages not stated in abstract)
records.model_description: Input: resting-state fMRI functional connectivity and wavelet-based temporal entropy across 264 brain regions; output: model distinguishing ASD from control individuals and associated with symptom severity
records.headline_result: RSN entropy model significantly distinguished ASD from controls (p=0.01)
records.study_design: retrospective cross-sectional analysis of a public neuroimaging cohort

records.title: A Label-fusion-aided Convolutional Neural Network for Isointense Infant Brain Tissue Segmentation.
records.journal: Proceedings. IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging
records.model_family: fully convolutional neural network (FCNN) with label-fusion guidance
records.clinical_problem: segmenting brain tissue on infant MRI during the low-contrast isointense stage
records.patient_population: infants aged 6-8 months (isointense stage), iSEG MICCAI Grand Challenge dataset
records.model_description: A fully convolutional neural network is applied region-by-region, guided by a traditional registration-based segmentation, to segment T1- and T2-weighted infant brain MRI into white matter, gray matter and cerebrospinal fluid.
records.headline_result: Outperformed traditional joint label fusion and FCNN-only methods on Dice coefficient
records.study_design: retrospective algorithm development and benchmark comparison

records.title: Multimodal Data and Machine Learning for Detecting Specific Biomarkers in Pediatric Epilepsy Patients With Generalized Tonic-Clonic Seizures.
records.clinical_problem: identifying brain changes associated with generalized tonic-clonic seizure epilepsy in children
records.patient_population: 14 children with generalized tonic-clonic seizure epilepsy and 30 age- and gender-matched healthy controls
records.model_description: Takes gray matter volume and fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (fALFF) values from multimodal brain MRI as input and outputs an SVM classification distinguishing epileptic from healthy children.
records.headline_result: SVM accuracy 83.72% (fALFF, right thalamus) and 74.42% (gray matter volume, right thalamus), both P<0.002
records.study_design: retrospective case-control MRI study with machine-learning classification

records.title: Deep Learning Based Attenuation Correction of PET/MRI in Pediatric Brain Tumor Patients: Evaluation in a Clinical Setting.
records.model_family: deep learning for MR-derived attenuation correction
records.clinical_problem: quantitatively accurate FET-PET/MRI in children without a CT for attenuation correction, and without a second sedation
records.patient_population: 79 pediatric brain tumor examinations, 36 with active tumor volume above 1 mL analyzed
records.model_description: Generates the attenuation map that PET reconstruction needs directly from MRI, so a child having simultaneous FET-PET/MRI does not need a CT and does not need a second sedation for a sequential scan. Compared against a CT-derived reference and against a non-learned MR-based method on the clinical metrics that actually drive decisions, tumor-to-background activity ratios.
records.headline_result: the only method with all patients inside predefined clinical limits; tumor-to-background difference from CT-based reference -0.1% (95% CI -0.8 to 0.5) versus 5.9% for Dixon-based correction

records.title: DeepSSM: A Deep Learning Framework for Statistical Shape Modeling from Raw Images.
records.journal: Shape in medical imaging : International Workshop, ShapeMI 2018, held in conjunction with MICCAI 2018, Granada, Spain, September 20, 2018 : proceedings. ShapeMI (Workshop) (2018 : Granada, Spain)
records.model_family: convolutional neural network that localizes the structure, establishes correspondences and regresses PCA loadings in a point distribution model, trained with a shape-statistics data augmentation scheme
records.clinical_problem: building statistical shape models straight from raw images, replacing a registration-segmentation-correspondence pipeline that needs parameter tuning, manual delineation and quality control at every step
records.patient_population: three applications, the first of which is pediatric cranial CT for characterizing metopic craniosynostosis; the others are adult femur CT and left atrium MRI
records.model_description: A MICCAI-workshop method paper whose lead application is pediatric: metopic craniosynostosis is a shape diagnosis, and statistical shape modeling is how shape is quantified, but the conventional pipeline is too hand-operated to run at scale. The augmentation trick is the enabling piece - 40-50 processed scans with known shape parameters are resampled into thousands of plausible training images, which is how a deep network gets trained on a surgical cohort's worth of data.
records.dataset_size: 40-50 processed CT/MRI scans per application, augmented into thousands of training images
records.headline_result: accurate low-dimensional shape representations produced directly from unseen 3D images with essentially no parameter tuning or user assistance

records.title: A metabolomics-based approach for non-invasive screening of fetal central nervous system anomalies.
records.journal: Metabolomics : Official journal of the Metabolomic Society

records.title: Automatic Lacunae Localization in Placental Ultrasound Images via Layer Aggregation.
records.journal: Medical image computing and computer-assisted intervention : MICCAI ... International Conference on Medical Image Computing and Computer-Assisted Intervention
records.model_family: deep learning (iterative deep aggregation / layer aggregation CNN)
records.clinical_problem: localizing placental lacunae to screen for abnormally invasive placenta on ultrasound
records.patient_population: 23 abnormally invasive placenta and 11 non-AIP participants (3,440 images)
records.model_description: A layer-aggregation network takes 2D placental ultrasound images with weak dot annotations and outputs localized placental lacunae confidence maps to aid diagnosis of abnormally invasive placenta.
records.dataset_size: 3,440 images, 9,618 labelled placental lacunae from 23 AIP and 11 non-AIP participants
records.headline_result: mean average precision (mAP) 35.7%

records.title: Learning Generalizable Recurrent Neural Networks from Small Task-fMRI Datasets.
records.journal: Medical image computing and computer-assisted intervention : MICCAI ... International Conference on Medical Image Computing and Computer-Assisted Intervention
records.clinical_problem: predicting autism spectrum disorder treatment outcome and classifying autistic versus typically developing children from task fMRI
records.patient_population: children with autism spectrum disorder (N=21 for treatment-outcome prediction; N=40 for ASD vs. typical classification)
records.model_description: Task-based fMRI data from small pediatric cohorts are used to train recurrent neural networks, aided by ROI-based resampling data augmentation, inclusion of non-imaging variables for subject-specific initialization, and selection of the most generalizable model across multiple training runs. The resulting RNNs predict treatment outcome for children with autism spectrum disorder and classify autistic versus typically developing children from task-fMRI scans.
records.dataset_size: 21 children (treatment outcome); 40 children (ASD vs. typical classification)
records.study_design: technical development, retrospective small-cohort classification study

records.title: Deep Learning for Fast and Spatially-Constrained Tissue Quantification from Highly-Undersampled Data in Magnetic Resonance Fingerprinting (MRF).
records.journal: Machine learning in medical imaging. MLMI (Workshop)

records.title: SonoEyeNet: Standardized Fetal Ultrasound Plane Detection Informed by Eye Tracking.
records.journal: Proceedings. IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging
records.clinical_problem: Can automated detection of the standard fetal abdominal circumference plane in ultrasound be improved by incorporating information about where experienced sonographers actually look?
records.patient_population: fetal ultrasound video clips with sonographer eye-movement data
records.model_description: SonoEyeNet is a CNN that takes fetal ultrasound video frames plus a visual heatmap derived from sonographers' recorded eye movements as input, to detect the standard abdominal circumference imaging plane.
records.headline_result: With eye-fixation information: precision 96.5%, recall 99.0%, F1 97.8% (vs. 73.6%/74.1%/73.8% without eye fixation)
records.study_design: retrospective algorithm development and internal testing

records.title: Multi-task SonoEyeNet: Detection of Fetal Standardized Planes Assisted by Generated Sonographer Attention Maps.
records.journal: Medical image computing and computer-assisted intervention : MICCAI ... International Conference on Medical Image Computing and Computer-Assisted Intervention
records.model_family: multi-task convolutional network with a generator and discriminator trained adversarially against sonographer gaze maps
records.clinical_problem: detecting the standardized abdominal circumference plane in fetal ultrasound video
records.patient_population: fetal ultrasound video frames with sonographer gaze tracking data
records.model_description: Solves the practical objection to gaze-informed models: the previous version needed eye tracking at inference, which no clinic has. Here the discriminator trains the generator to reproduce sonographer attention, so gaze is needed only during training and the deployed model works from the image alone - with plane detection performance intact.
records.headline_result: precision 96.8, recall 96.2 and F1 96.5 for standardized abdominal circumference plane detection, without needing gaze tracking at inference

records.title: Automatic Detection of the Inner Ears in Head CT Images Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks.
records.journal: Proceedings of SPIE--the International Society for Optical Engineering
records.clinical_problem: automatically classifying head CT volumes by whether they contain one, two, or no ears, to automate a cochlear implant image-guided programming pipeline used in adult and pediatric patients
records.patient_population: over 2,000 CT volumes from 153 patients (adult and pediatric cochlear implant populations)
records.model_description: a deep CNN takes a head CT volume as input and outputs a classification of ear content (two ears, one ear, or none) to automate an image-processing pipeline for cochlear implant programming
records.headline_result: overall classification accuracy 95.97%

records.title: Radiation-free quantification of head malformations in craniosynostosis patients from 3D photography.
records.journal: Proceedings of SPIE--the International Society for Optical Engineering
records.clinical_problem: quantifying cranial malformations in craniosynostosis patients using radiation-free 3D photography instead of CT
records.patient_population: 17 craniosynostosis patients compared with a normative population
records.model_description: a landmark-based registration method takes a 3D photograph of the head as input and outputs a quantified cranial malformation score relative to a normative statistical shape atlas built from healthy 3D photographs
records.headline_result: malformation 2.68 +/- 0.75 mm (craniosynostosis) vs. 1.70 +/- 0.41 mm (normative), p<0.001

records.title: Quantifying the Association between White Matter Integrity Changes and Subconcussive Head Impact Exposure from a Single Season of Youth and High School Football using 3D Convolutional Neural Networks.
records.journal: Proceedings of SPIE--the International Society for Optical Engineering
records.clinical_problem: quantifying association between cumulative subconcussive head impact exposure and white matter integrity changes in youth and high-school football players
records.patient_population: youth and high school football players, ages 9-18, imaged pre- and post-season
records.model_description: a 3D CNN takes the change in fractional anisotropy DTI maps (pre- to post-season) as input and outputs a classification of players into high vs. low cumulative head-impact-exposure groups
records.headline_result: ROC AUC 85.71%, F1 score 83.33%
records.study_design: prospective single-season cohort study with 3D CNN classification

records.title: Single Season Changes in Resting State Network Power and the Connectivity between Regions: Distinguish Head Impact Exposure Level in High School and Youth Football Players.
records.journal: Proceedings of SPIE--the International Society for Optical Engineering

records.title: Visualization and Interpretation of Convolutional Neural Network Predictions in Detecting Pneumonia in Pediatric Chest Radiographs.
records.model_family: customized VGG16 with visualization of class-relevant regions
records.clinical_problem: pneumonia detection in children, and separating bacterial from viral pneumonia
records.patient_population: children undergoing chest radiography for suspected pneumonia
records.model_description: Classifies a pediatric chest radiograph as normal or pneumonia and then as bacterial or viral, and, unusually for this literature, spends most of its effort on showing where the model looked. It introduces a way of localizing the region that drives predictions across all images of a class rather than one image at a time, on the argument that an unexplained black box is unusable for screening decisions.
records.headline_result: 96.2% accuracy detecting pneumonia and 93.6% distinguishing bacterial from viral

records.title: PREDICTION OF PIVOTAL RESPONSE TREATMENT OUTCOME WITH TASK FMRI USING RANDOM FOREST AND VARIABLE SELECTION.
records.journal: Proceedings. IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging
records.model_family: random forest with two-step (shadow + stepwise) feature selection on GLM-derived fMRI features
records.clinical_problem: predicting response to pivotal response treatment (a behavioral intervention) in autism spectrum disorder
records.patient_population: young children with autism spectrum disorder undergoing task-based fMRI (n=20)
records.model_description: Task-based fMRI comparing two conditions is analyzed voxel-by-voxel with a general linear model to obtain t-statistics; a two-step feature-selection process (a random-forest-based 'shadow' method followed by stepwise selection) picks the most informative voxels. A random-forest regression model then predicts treatment outcome for pivotal response treatment in young children with autism, evaluated with leave-one-out cross-validation.
records.headline_result: the proposed pipeline generated the highest accuracy compared with other standard regression methods (exact accuracy value not given)

records.title: Fast Multiple Landmark Localisation Using a Patch-based Iterative Network.
records.journal: Medical image computing and computer-assisted intervention : MICCAI ... International Conference on Medical Image Computing and Computer-Assisted Intervention
records.model_family: convolutional network learning the spatial relationship between an image patch and landmark positions, applied iteratively, with multitask regression and classification and PCA over landmark configurations
records.clinical_problem: locating anatomical landmarks in 3D fetal screening ultrasound volumes, from which standard scan planes can then be derived automatically
records.patient_population: 72 3D ultrasound images from fetal screening examinations
records.model_description: The iterative patch design is what makes it fast: instead of evaluating every location in a volume, the network is handed a patch, told which way to move, and repeats until it converges - so inference touches a small fraction of the data. Modelling the ten landmarks jointly through PCA imposes the anatomical constraint that they cannot move independently. The endpoint that matters clinically is that the derived standard planes look like the ones a sonographer would have chosen.
records.headline_result: average landmark localisation error 5.59 mm with 0.44 s to predict 10 landmarks per volume

records.title: Random forest and Self Organizing Maps application for analysis of pediatric fracture healing time of the lower limb
records.model_family: random forest (feature ranking) and self-organizing maps (SOM)
records.clinical_problem: prediction of fracture healing time in pediatric long-bone fractures
records.patient_population: children aged 0-12 years with lower-limb long-bone fractures at a pediatric orthopedic unit
records.model_description: The model takes features derived from radiographs of pediatric lower-limb long-bone fractures (fracture type, angulation, percentage of bone contact area) together with age, gender, and bone type as input. Random forest ranks which variables most influence fracture healing time, and self-organizing maps then analyze the relationship between the top-ranked variables and healing time. It is intended to help predict expected fracture healing duration in children.
records.headline_result: age and fracture contact-area percentage were identified as the most important variables explaining fracture healing time

records.title: Multiagent-consensus-MapReduce-based attribute reduction using co-evolutionary quantum PSO for big data applications

records.title: Occult spastic diplegic cerebral palsy recognition using efficient machine learning for big data and structural connectivity abnormalities analysis
records.journal: Journal of Medical Imaging and Health Informatics
records.model_family: k-nearest neighbor (k-NN) classifier on structural connectivity network features
records.clinical_problem: identification of occult spastic diplegic cerebral palsy (brain injury not visible on conventional MRI)
records.patient_population: children with occult spastic diplegic cerebral palsy compared with age- and sex-matched healthy children
records.model_description: The model uses structural brain connectivity networks derived from MRI as input. A k-nearest-neighbor classifier is trained to recognize children with 'occult' spastic diplegic cerebral palsy (no visible lesion on conventional MRI) from large datasets, and permutation testing compares network topology (global efficiency, clustering coefficient, path length) between the occult SDCP and healthy control groups. It is intended to identify subtle structural connectivity abnormalities invisible to conventional MRI reading.
records.headline_result: k-NN provided effective classification results; global efficiency was significantly lower in the occult SDCP group than in controls (p<0.001)
records.study_design: retrospective case-control diagnostic accuracy / network analysis

records.title: Computerized detection of spina bifida using SVM with Zernike moments of fetal skulls in ultrasound screening
records.model_family: support vector machine using Zernike moment shape features
records.clinical_problem: detection of spina bifida (neural tube defect) on prenatal ultrasound screening
records.patient_population: fetuses undergoing ultrasound screening for neural tube defects
records.model_description: The model takes ultrasound images of the fetal skull as input. It extracts Zernike moment shape features from the skull region and classifies them with a support vector machine to detect shape markers of spina bifida. Oversampling/undersampling techniques address the rarity of positive cases, and the system is intended as computer-aided decision support to help avoid false negatives.
records.headline_result: average F-measure 0.6276 and GMRP 0.6306 on non-sampled test data; accuracy 94% and specificity 98% under the best sampling configuration (400% borderline-SMOTE followed by 50% random undersampling)

records.title: Determination of cognitive variation from brain mri analysis
records.journal: Indian Journal of Public Health Research and Development

records.title: Bone age assessment model based on multi-dimensional feature fusion using deep learning
records.journal: Academic Journal of Second Military Medical University
records.model_family: deep convolutional neural network feature extraction combined with clinical/demographic data
records.clinical_problem: bone age assessment
records.patient_population: children undergoing left-hand radiography for bone age assessment
records.model_description: The model takes left-hand radiographs as input. A deep convolutional neural network automatically extracts 17 key regional bone-age features from the hand and wrist joint, which are combined with demographic data (sex, population statistics) to estimate bone age. It is intended to improve on traditional manual radiographic bone-age reading.
records.headline_result: mean absolute error of 0.455 years, better than traditional methods and end-to-end deep learning alone

records.title: Placental maturity grading via hybrid descriptors and fisher vector
records.model_family: hybrid CNN (19-layer, transfer learning) + hand-crafted texture features, Fisher vector encoding, SVM classifier
records.clinical_problem: placental maturity grading to assess fetal growth and maternal health
records.patient_population: pregnant women undergoing obstetric ultrasound (placental imaging)
records.model_description: The model takes B-mode and color Doppler energy ultrasound images of the placenta as input. It combines convolutional features from a deep CNN (with transfer learning) with hand-crafted texture features, encodes them with a Fisher vector, and classifies placental maturity grade using a support vector machine. It is intended to automate placental maturity grading, which is otherwise a subjective manual assessment.
records.headline_result: accuracy 94.15% with hybrid descriptors (19-layer network), 3.01% higher than the hand-crafted-feature model and 7.35% higher than the CNN-only feature model

records.title: Notes to current ways of development in computed tomography imaging techniques*
records.exclusion_reason: general review of CT scanning technique developments; low-dose pediatric imaging and deep learning are mentioned only as brief separate bullet points, with no specific pediatric AI model developed or evaluated

records.title: Real-time automatic fetal brain extraction in fetal MRI by deep learning
records.journal: 2018 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI 2018)
records.model_family: deep fully convolutional network based on 2D U-net with auto-context, compared against a voxelwise FCN and a SIFT / random forest / conditional random field method
records.clinical_problem: extracting the fetal brain from 2D fetal MRI slices in real time, the first step of every fetal neuroimage analysis and one made hard by arbitrary fetal orientation, surrounding maternal organs and intermittent motion
records.patient_population: 250 stacks of training images with manual brain masks; 17 normal and 18 extremely challenging test stacks with extreme motion, noise or severely abnormal brain shape
records.model_description: The evaluation design is what makes this credible: a separate test set of deliberately extreme cases, where Dice fell from 96.5% to 78.8% - a gap most papers would not report. Running in about a second per stack is the enabling property, since it puts brain extraction inside the acquisition loop, where it can drive real-time motion tracking and detection rather than only offline reconstruction.
records.headline_result: average Dice 96.52% on normal and 78.83% on extremely challenging fetal brain stacks, at about 1 second run time, outperforming both comparison methods

records.clinical_problem: paediatric bone age assessment with deep convolutional neural networks

records.title: Brain Tumor Type Classification via Capsule Networks
records.journal: 2018 25th IEEE International Conference on Image Processing (ICIP)
records.exclusion_reason: capsule network classification of brain tumor type on MRI; brain tumors are described as common in children and adults but the abstract does not state the ages of the imaged patients, so a pediatric population cannot be established from the record

records.title: Isointense infant brain segmentation with a hyper-dense connected convolutional neural network
records.journal: 2018 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI 2018)
records.model_family: hyper-densely connected 3D convolutional network with two separate paths for T1 and T2 and direct connections between layers of the same and different paths
records.clinical_problem: neonatal brain tissue segmentation, where poor image quality and low white/gray matter contrast defeat the multi-atlas label fusion strategies that had dominated - which are slow and sensitive to registration error
records.patient_population: the MICCAI iSEG grand challenge on 6-month infant brain MRI segmentation
records.model_description: The architectural idea is cross-path dense connectivity: every layer can see every earlier layer in both the T1 and T2 streams, so the network learns how the two contrasts relate at every depth rather than fusing them once. That is well matched to the isointense problem, where neither modality alone separates the tissues but their combination does. Ranked first or second on most metrics among 21 teams on the iSEG challenge.
records.headline_result: ranked first or second on most metrics among 21 teams in the MICCAI iSEG 6-month infant brain segmentation challenge

records.title: Similarity based classification of ADHD using singular value decomposition
records.journal: Proceedings of the 15th ACM International Conference on Computing Frontiers
records.model_family: Eros similarity between multivariate time series with a k-nearest-neighbour classifier, plus a model selection scheme that picks k from training data
records.clinical_problem: discriminating children with ADHD from healthy children on functional and structural MRI, in a disorder whose cause is unknown and where data mining is being used to find discriminating patterns
records.patient_population: children in the ADHD-200 Consortium competition datasets
records.model_description: Treats each subject's fMRI as a multivariate time series and compares subjects by a time-series similarity measure rather than by extracted connectivity features - a different framing from almost everything else on ADHD-200. Choosing k from the training data rather than by tuning on the test set is the discipline that makes the reported 20-point improvement over the competition's best results worth taking seriously, though it applies to two datasets rather than all of them.
records.headline_result: about 20% better than the best results reported in the ADHD-200 competition on two datasets

records.title: Classification of Bacterial and Viral Childhood Pneumonia Using Deep Learning in Chest Radiography
records.journal: Proceedings of the 3rd International Conference on Multimedia and Image Processing
records.model_family: fully convolutional network lung segmentation followed by a deep CNN classifier, with DCNN and manual features fused and classified by a support vector machine
records.clinical_problem: separating bacterial from viral pneumonia on children's chest radiographs, the distinction that decides whether a child is given antibiotics
records.patient_population: 4513 pediatric patients aged 1 to 9 years from Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Center, 2003-2017; lung segmentation trained on the adult JSRT (241 images) and Montgomery County (138 images) datasets
records.model_description: Two design choices worth noting. Segmentation is trained on adult public datasets and applied to pediatric radiographs, which is a deliberate use of the data that exists for a task where anatomy transfers. And learned features are fused with handcrafted ones before an SVM rather than either alone, with the comparison between them reported. The accuracy of around 0.80 on the bacterial-versus-viral call is a realistic figure for a distinction that radiologists also find hard.
records.dataset_size: 4513 pediatric patients; 379 adult radiographs for segmentation training
records.headline_result: accuracy 0.8048 +/- 0.0202 and sensitivity 0.7755 +/- 0.0296 with transfer-learned deep features, AUC 0.6937-0.8234

records.title: InfiNet: Fully convolutional networks for infant brain MRI segmentation
records.journal: 2018 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI 2018)
records.model_family: fully convolutional network with double encoder arms for T1 and T2 feeding a joint decoder that upsamples using pooled indices from each encoder block, trained on Generalized Dice Loss
records.clinical_problem: voxel-wise segmentation of infant brain MRI at the isointense stage
records.patient_population: isointense-stage infant brain MRI
records.model_description: Emphasizes parameter efficiency and practicality rather than raw accuracy: reusing max-pooling indices for learning-free upsampling keeps the decoder small, and the Generalized Dice Loss is chosen for the high class imbalance that infant tissue segmentation presents. Whole-volume segmentation in under 50 seconds, with competitive performance against several state-of-the-art multi-modal architectures.
records.headline_result: whole-volume infant brain segmentation in under 50 seconds with performance competitive against multiple state-of-the-art deep architectures and their multi-modal variants

records.title: Deep learning with ultrasound physics for fetal skull segmentation
records.journal: 2018 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI 2018)
records.model_family: two-stage convolutional network where the second stage receives physics-derived angle-of-incidence and shadow-casting maps computed from the first stage's partial segmentation
records.clinical_problem: segmenting the fetal skull in 3D ultrasound so that cranial deformation can be assessed, where 2D biometry is limited by inter- and intra-observer variability and operator dependence
records.patient_population: 66 cases of 3D fetal ultrasound
records.model_description: The most elegant idea in this batch: the parts of the skull missing from an ultrasound volume are missing for a physical reason - the beam struck at a grazing angle, or bone cast a shadow - so the network is given an angle-of-incidence map and a shadow map computed from its own first-pass segmentation and asked to complete what the physics says should be there. The clinical payoff is reported rather than implied: 3D-based cranial deformation assessment reached 100% specificity against 50% for traditional 2D biometrics.
records.headline_result: average Dice 0.83 +/- 0.06 for skull segmentation, with cranial deformation assessment reaching 100% specificity versus 50% for traditional 2D biometrics

records.title: Fully convolutional structured LSTM networks for joint 4D medical image segmentation
records.journal: 2018 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI 2018)
records.model_family: fully convolutional networks for the spatial model integrated end-to-end with LSTM units for the temporal model
records.clinical_problem: consistent joint segmentation of a longitudinal image series, which is what reveals developmental trajectories and monitors disease progression - and which fails when appearance changes substantially between timepoints
records.patient_population: longitudinal pediatric MRI
records.model_description: Aimed squarely at the pediatric case: traditional 4D segmentation builds a template or assumes the timepoints can be co-registered, which is exactly what a developing brain violates, since appearance changes between scans. Treating time as a sequence to be modelled by an LSTM rather than as a registration problem is the reframing, and the application shown is longitudinal pediatric MRI.
records.headline_result: the first deep learning framework integrating fully convolutional networks and LSTM end to end for joint 4D segmentation, demonstrated on longitudinal pediatric MRI

records.title: SonoEyeNet: Standardized fetal ultrasound plane detection informed by eye tracking
records.journal: 2018 IEEE 15th International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI 2018)

records.clinical_problem: detecting the standardized abdominal circumference plane in fetal ultrasound video
records.patient_population: fetal ultrasound video clips with eye movement data collected from experienced sonographers
records.model_description: The size of the gain is the finding: adding human visual fixation information lifted F1 from 73.8% to 97.8%, which says the model without it was largely failing and that where an expert looks carries most of the discriminating information. That also explains why the follow-up work went to such lengths to remove the eye tracker from inference - the signal is essential and the hardware is not deployable.
records.headline_result: precision 96.5%, recall 99.0% and F1 97.8% with eye fixation information, against 73.6%, 74.1% and 73.8% without it

records.title: Standard Plane Detection in 3D Fetal Ultrasound Using an Iterative Transformation Network
records.model_family: convolutional network regressing the transformation from the current plane toward the standard plane, applied iteratively, with auxiliary classification outputs as confidence measures
records.clinical_problem: finding the standard scan planes in a 3D fetal brain ultrasound volume, which 3D acquisition makes easy to capture and hard to navigate - manual identification is laborious and needs expert knowledge of fetal anatomy
records.patient_population: 72 ultrasound volumes of the fetal brain
records.model_description: Reframes plane finding as a navigation problem: rather than classifying every candidate plane, the network is asked which way to move the current one, and iterates until it converges. Adding a classification head as a confidence measure on the regressed transformation is what stops it drifting. Under half a second per plane, with errors around 4 mm and 13 degrees on the transventricular and transcerebellar planes.
records.headline_result: 3.83 mm / 12.7 degrees error for the transventricular plane and 3.80 mm / 12.6 degrees for the transcerebellar plane, at 0.46 s per plane

records.title: Intrinsic Connectivity Network-Based Classification and Detection of Psychotic Symptoms in Youth With 22q11.2 Deletions.
records.model_family: classifiers trained on intrinsic connectivity network features in one cohort and tested in an independent cohort
records.clinical_problem: identifying which young people with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome - one of the largest known genetic risk factors for psychosis - are on a psychosis-risk trajectory
records.patient_population: two independent cohorts: UCLA (33 with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome and 33 matched controls) and Syracuse (28 and 28)
records.model_description: The design is what gives it weight: classifiers trained at UCLA were tested at Syracuse, and three of twelve network-derived classifiers replicated. More importantly, four networks predicted psychosis-risk status within the deletion syndrome group in both cohorts - a within-diagnosis stratification that replicated across sites, which is rare in psychiatric imaging. 22q11.2 deletion syndrome is a defined genetic population, so this is closer to a stratification biomarker than a diagnostic classifier.
records.headline_result: the anterior cingulate/precuneus, default mode and posterior default mode classifiers distinguished 22q11.2 deletion syndrome from controls in the replication cohort, and four networks predicted psychosis-risk status within the syndrome in both cohorts
records.study_design: retrospective two-cohort model development and replication

records.title: Multi-modal, Multi-measure, and Multi-class Discrimination of ADHD with Hierarchical Feature Extraction and Extreme Learning Machine Using Structural and Functional Brain MRI.

records.dataset_size: selected subjects from the public ADHD-200 dataset

records.model_description: The clinical case for this is unusually clear: task-based functional mapping requires a cooperative patient, and many children are not, whether through age, cognitive deficit or the need for sedation. A trained classifier identifies resting-state networks in the individual child, and the maps are loaded straight into the surgical navigation system. Six of the twenty children were sedated and it still worked, which is the point.
records.headline_result: resting-state network maps produced for all 20 patients and uploaded to clinical navigation systems, including in six sedated children

records.title: Presurgical thalamocortical connectivity is associated with response to vagus nerve stimulation in children with intractable epilepsy.

records.model_description: Whole-brain resting-state fMRI connectivity to thalamic regions of interest is measured before vagus nerve stimulation implantation in children with drug-resistant epilepsy. Enhanced thalamic connectivity to the anterior cingulate cortex and left insula was associated with greater treatment benefit.
records.headline_result: 86% accuracy on 10-fold cross-validation; 88% accuracy in an independent external validation cohort of 8 children
records.study_design: retrospective diagnostic/prognostic accuracy study with external validation

records.title: Predicting Slice-to-Volume Transformation in Presence of Arbitrary Subject Motion
records.model_family: convolutional neural network regressing the rotation and translation of an arbitrary 2D slice into a learned canonical atlas coordinate system
records.clinical_problem: the limited capture range of intensity-based 2D/3D registration, which needs a good initialization - precisely what is unavailable when a fetus has moved unpredictably between slices
records.patient_population: simulated MRI brain data with extreme random motion, plus fetal MRI within a full reconstruction and motion compensation pipeline
records.model_description: Solves the initialization problem rather than the registration problem, which is the correct target: conventional methods work well once close and fail entirely when far, and a learned regression to atlas coordinates puts them close. Milliseconds per slice makes it usable inside an acquisition. The demonstration that matters is on very young fetuses, where the motion is worst and previous reconstruction pipelines simply failed.
records.headline_result: average prediction error 7 mm on simulated data with extreme motion, and convincing reconstruction of images of very young fetuses where previous methods fail

records.title: Context-Sensitive Super-Resolution for Fast Fetal Magnetic Resonance Imaging
records.model_family: residual convolutional network for context-sensitive upsampling that learns organ-specific appearance
records.clinical_problem: the trade-off in fetal MRI between fast low-resolution acquisition, which the fetus's motion demands, and the detail that diagnosis requires
records.patient_population: 145 fetal scans
records.model_description: Argues against the spatially independent upsampling that was standard - it treats every part of the image the same and so is error prone - and learns instead what particular organs should look like at high resolution. The evaluation goes one step further than image quality: the super-resolved slices are fed into brain volume reconstruction on motion-corrupted data, where the gain is larger (1.73 dB) than on upsampling alone (1.25 dB), showing the benefit compounds through the pipeline.
records.headline_result: PSNR increased by 1.25 dB over baseline upsampling on under-sampled fetal data, and by 1.73 dB when used for brain volume reconstruction from motion-corrupted captured data

records.title: Toward automatic diagnosis of hip dysplasia from 2D ultrasound
records.journal: 2017 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI 2017)

records.title: Cascaded Fully Convolutional Networks for automatic prenatal ultrasound image segmentation

records.title: Temporal HeartNet: Towards Human-Level Automatic Analysis of Fetal Cardiac Screening Video
records.model_family: multi-task convolutional network with an anchor mechanism and IoU loss, made recurrent so regional convolutional features are computed over sequential frames
records.clinical_problem: describing what a fetal cardiac screening video actually contains - whether the heart is visible, which viewing plane, and where and how it is oriented - which is what would let a system guide interpretation frame by frame
records.patient_population: a real-world clinical dataset of fetal cardiac screening ultrasound video
records.model_description: Predicts four quantities jointly - visibility, plane, location and orientation - which is closer to what a sonographer knows at each moment than any single classification would be. The recurrent design means each frame's prediction is conditioned on the whole video, so a moment of poor visibility is interpreted in context rather than in isolation. Performance on par with expert annotations on real clinical screening video.
records.headline_result: frame-level joint prediction of fetal heart visibility, viewing plane, location and orientation on par with expert annotations

records.title: Quantitative Ultrasound for Measuring Obstructive Severity in Children with Hydronephrosis.
records.model_family: quantitative image analysis producing 131 morphological parameters, with machine learning used to fit safety thresholds
records.clinical_problem: deciding which children with hydronephrosis actually need a diuretic nuclear renogram, using the ultrasound they have already had
records.patient_population: 50 consecutive children with hydronephrosis of varying severity who had both 2D sonography and diuretic MAG3 renography
records.model_description: A triage model rather than a diagnostic one, and the design reflects that: thresholds are fitted at 100 percent sensitivity, so the model is only allowed to rule out. What it buys is concrete and measurable in avoided studies - up to 62 percent of children spared a diuretic renogram, which for this population means avoided radiopharmaceutical, catheterization and sedation. It also beats the two scoring systems urologists actually use, the Society for Fetal Urology grade and the hydronephrosis index.
records.headline_result: at 100% sensitivity, specificity 94%, 70% and 74% for the three washout thresholds (AUC 0.98, 0.94, 0.94), significantly better than SFU grade and the hydronephrosis index; up to 62% of diuretic renograms avoidable

records.title: Pediatric laminopathies: Whole-body magnetic resonance imaging fingerprint and comparison with Sepn1 myopathy.
records.model_family: random forests over semiquantitative signal abnormality and atrophy scores across 109 muscles
records.clinical_problem: distinguishing pediatric LMNA-related dystrophy from SEPN1-related myopathy, two congenital myopathies whose clinical overlap makes the genetic workup expensive and slow
records.patient_population: 8 children with LMNA-related dystrophy and 9 with SEPN1-related myopathy, whole-body MRI with 109 muscles scored each
records.model_description: A clean use of machine learning at very small n: with 17 children and 109 scored muscles per child, the data are wide rather than long, and random forests are used to find which muscles carry the discrimination rather than to build a classifier for deployment. The output is a named pattern - an atrophied semimembranosus as the single most informative feature - which is the form a radiologist can actually use at the workstation. Whole-body MRI muscle pattern reading is exactly the kind of expertise that lives in a few centres.
records.headline_result: a selective whole-body MRI pattern for pediatric LMNA-related dystrophy, distinguishable from SEPN1-related myopathy, with atrophied semimembranosus the most relevant discriminating feature

records.title: Automated Outcome Classification of Computed Tomography Imaging Reports for Pediatric Traumatic Brain Injury.
records.journal: Academic emergency medicine : official journal of the Society for Academic Emergency Medicine
records.model_family: hybrid system pairing the MedLEE natural language processing engine with statistical machine learning classifiers
records.clinical_problem: turning free-text head CT reports into structured traumatic brain injury outcomes, which is otherwise done by trained human abstractors and is the rate-limiting step in large trauma studies
records.patient_population: 2121 CT reports from the PECARN pediatric traumatic brain injury study, manually coded by trained abstractors, split evenly for training and testing
records.model_description: Report mining rather than image analysis, and an unusually careful instance of it: MedLEE supplies negation, certainty and temporal modifiers so that a mentioned-but-absent finding is not counted, findings are coded against the NINDS common data elements so the output is comparable across studies, and past, future and indication mentions are filtered out. The paper is explicitly a generalization test of a method that had worked for a simple outcome (orbital fracture), applied to a complex one.
records.headline_result: validation of automated outcome classification for pediatric traumatic brain injury from free-text head CT reports, extending a hybrid NLP and machine learning system from a simple to a complex outcome
records.study_design: secondary analysis of a multicenter study

records.title: Disrupted white matter connectivity underlying developmental dyslexia: A machine learning approach.

records.patient_population: 28 school-aged children with developmental dyslexia and 33 age-matched controls
records.model_description: Takes structural and diffusion MRI, reduces each white-matter region to five measures (volume, fractional anisotropy, mean, axial and radial diffusivity), and classifies a child as dyslexic or not. The features that carried the classification extended well beyond the classical reading network into limbic and motor tracts, which is the paper's substantive claim.

records.title: Atypical Structural Connectome Organization and Cognitive Impairment in Young Survivors of Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia.
records.model_family: random forest classifier on structural (diffusion MRI) connectome and demographic features
records.clinical_problem: predicting cognitive impairment in survivors of pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia from brain structural connectivity
records.patient_population: 31 survivors of pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ages 5-19) treated with chemotherapy only, compared with 39 matched healthy controls
records.model_description: Diffusion tensor imaging was used to build whole-brain structural connectomes, analyzed with graph-theoretical measures (small-worldness, clustering coefficient) in young survivors of acute lymphoblastic leukemia versus healthy controls. A random forest model combining connectome and demographic variables was then trained to automatically classify survivors as having cognitive impairment or not.
records.dataset_size: 31 ALL survivors (ages 5-19) and 39 matched healthy controls
records.headline_result: Random forest classification accuracy 0.89 (p < 0.0001) for cognitive impairment status
records.study_design: case-control diagnostic imaging study with random forest classification

records.title: Three-dimensional morphology study of surgical adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patient from encoded geometric models.
records.journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
records.clinical_problem: classifying three-dimensional spinal deformity in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis, which the two-dimensional Lenke system does not capture
records.patient_population: 663 adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients across 915 visits, reviewed by the Scoliosis Research Society 3D Classification Committee
records.model_description: Compresses each patient's 3D spine reconstruction into a learned code and clusters those codes with no assumptions about how many groups there should be or what defines them. Eleven groups emerged, discriminated mainly by curve location, kyphosis and lordosis, and subgroups appeared within existing Lenke types. This is data-driven taxonomy rather than diagnosis, aimed at replacing a classification the field agrees is inadequate.
records.headline_result: eleven clusters identified with curve location, kyphosis and lordosis as the discriminating factors, revealing subgroups within existing Lenke types

records.title: A neural network-based 2D/3D image registration quality evaluator for pediatric patient setup in external beam radiotherapy.

records.patient_population: Six pediatric patients with brain tumors receiving proton therapy

records.headline_result: Sensitivity 0.865-0.964 and specificity 0.797-0.990 for detecting registration error >1mm; final acceptance ratio 92.4%

records.title: Ultrasound-based gestational-age estimation in late pregnancy.
records.journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
records.model_family: genetic algorithm searching polynomial regression equations
records.clinical_problem: estimating gestational age in women who first present late in pregnancy with unknown menstrual dates
records.patient_population: 4,229 women with certain menstrual dates from eight geographically defined urban populations in the INTERGROWTH-21st Fetal Growth Longitudinal Study
records.model_description: Takes routine fetal biometry from a single late ultrasound and returns an estimated gestational age. An automated search over more than 64,000 candidate polynomial equations picked head circumference and femur length as the best pair. The clinical value is in antenatal care where first-trimester dating was never done; the honest limitation, stated by the authors, is that accuracy degrades to worse than two weeks in the third trimester.
records.release_evidence: the prediction equations are published in full in the abstract
records.headline_result: gestational age uncertainty of 6-7 days at 14 weeks, 12-14 days at 26 weeks, and more than 14 days in the third trimester

records.title: Deep Learning Guided Partitioned Shape Model for Anterior Visual Pathway Segmentation.
records.model_family: partitioned statistical shape and appearance model steered by conditional-space deep learning features across multiple MRI sequences
records.clinical_problem: segmenting the optic nerves, chiasm and tracts on MRI - thin, long, structurally variable and poorly contrasted against neighbours - including when they are distorted by low-grade glioma
records.patient_population: MRI sequences from 165 pediatric subjects, evaluated leave-one-out
records.model_description: Built for a structure that defeats generic segmentation and for a population where it matters most - optic pathway glioma is a childhood tumor, and treatment decisions turn on how the pathway is involved. The design pairs a statistical shape model, which enforces that the result still looks like a visual pathway, with learned features that carry it through the low-contrast optic tracts and pathological regions where intensity alone gives out. Partitioning the model regionally is what allows local deformation without losing global plausibility.
records.headline_result: mean Dice 0.779 for the whole anterior visual pathway and 0.791 for the optic nerve, significantly better than state-of-the-art methods and as robust as manual segmentation

records.title: Accurate Learning with Few Atlases (ALFA): an algorithm for MRI neonatal brain extraction and comparison with 11 publicly available methods.
records.model_family: sparsity-based atlas selection combined with machine-learning label fusion, for multi-modal input
records.clinical_problem: brain extraction from neonatal MRI - the first step of nearly every neuroimaging pipeline - where methods built and validated on adults have never been shown to hold
records.patient_population: multi-modal brain MRI of 50 newborns
records.model_description: The comparison is unusually thorough: eleven publicly available brain extraction methods run on the same 50 newborns, which establishes not just that ALFA works but how badly the adult-derived alternatives do on neonates. The atlas selection strategy is the contribution - a handful of atlases spread evenly through the data space rather than many similar ones - and because it learns from partially labelled data it scales to large cohorts.
records.headline_result: outperformed all eleven compared publicly available brain extraction methods across modalities on 50 newborns

records.title: Automatic Segmentation of MR Brain Images With a Convolutional Neural Network.
records.model_family: convolutional neural network (multi-scale patch and kernel sizes)

records.patient_population: preterm infants scanned at 30 and 40 weeks postmenstrual age, alongside aging adults (~70y) and young adults (~23y) used as comparison cohorts
records.model_description: The model takes a single anatomical MR brain image as input and outputs a multi-class tissue segmentation. It is a convolutional neural network that combines multiple patch sizes and convolution kernel sizes to capture multi-scale voxel information, learning discriminative features from training data rather than relying on hand-crafted ones. It was evaluated across five separate cohorts spanning preterm infants and adults of different ages.
records.dataset_size: five datasets covering preterm infant MRI (30 and 40 weeks PMA, coronal and axial) and adult/young-adult MRI cohorts; exact per-group counts not stated
records.headline_result: Average Dice coefficients of 0.87, 0.82, 0.84, 0.86, and 0.91 across the five segmented datasets
