records.title: Network-based classification of ADHD patients using discriminative subnetwork selection and graph kernel PCA.
records.journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
records.model_family: support vector machine with graph kernel PCA feature extraction
records.clinical_problem: ADHD diagnosis from resting-state fMRI brain networks
records.patient_population: children and adolescents with ADHD (118) versus normal controls (98) from the ADHD-200 dataset
records.model_description: Resting-state fMRI-derived whole-brain connectivity networks are searched for discriminative subnetworks that differ between ADHD and control groups. A graph kernel principal component analysis extracts features from these subnetworks, and a support vector machine classifies each subject as ADHD or normal control. The method was trained and tested on the ADHD-200 dataset (118 ADHD, 98 controls).

records.title: Surface-Based fMRI-Driven Diffusion Tractography in the Presence of Significant Brain Pathology: A Study Linking Structure and Function in Cerebral Palsy.
records.model_family: surface-mesh fMRI-seeded diffusion tractography pipeline with a machine-learning track classifier
records.clinical_problem: running diffusion tractography in brains with major pathology, where automated cortical parcellation fails, manual region drawing is slow and error-prone, and the usual structure-function assumptions break down after cortical reorganisation
records.patient_population: 31 children with unilateral cerebral palsy
records.model_description: Aimed at exactly the situation pediatric neuroimaging keeps running into: the brain is too abnormal for atlas-based methods and too numerous for hand-drawn regions. Seeding from the child's own functional activation sidesteps the atlas, surface meshes tighten the seed, and a learned track classifier removes the irrelevant pathways that fMRI smoothing drags in. The head-to-head against the standard voxelwise approach is decisive on the metric that matters for a clinical pipeline - how many children could be processed at all.
records.headline_result: processed 87% of participants versus 65% for the voxelwise approach, with 15 of 20 diffusion-clinical correlations significant (R2 0.43-0.73) versus 2 for voxelwise

records.title: Multiclass Classification for the Differential Diagnosis on the ADHD Subtypes Using Recursive Feature Elimination and Hierarchical Extreme Learning Machine: Structural MRI Study.

records.model_description: Computes five surface-based MRI measures at every cortical vertex and classifies each vertex as lesional or not, with accuracy judged against the region that was actually resected. The result that matters is on the MRI-negative cases: in patients whose scans radiologists had read as normal, it found the histologically confirmed lesion in 14 of 24. Separating thick from thin cortex and sulcal from gyral regions into distinct classifiers was what made this work.
records.headline_result: lesion detected in 6 of 7 MRI-positive patients and in 14 of 24 (58%) MRI-negative patients

records.title: Spectral clustering based parcellation of FETAL brain MRI
records.journal: 2015 IEEE 12th International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI)
records.model_family: unsupervised spectral clustering of the cortical surface into K regions using only intrinsic geometry
records.clinical_problem: parcellating the fetal cerebral cortex into homogeneous regions, which neuroimaging studies depend on and which is hard before birth because the anatomical landmarks used in older brains are weak or absent
records.patient_population: fetal brain MRI acquired in utero across varying gestational ages and degrees of folding
records.model_description: Being unsupervised is the whole point here rather than a convenience: supervised parcellation needs landmarks defined on an adult or infant brain, and the early fetal cortex does not have them, so relying only on the intrinsic geometry of the surface sidesteps a circular dependency. Reproducibility across fetuses of different gestational age and folding magnitude is the appropriate evidence for a parcellation with no ground truth.
records.headline_result: convincing parcellation reproducibility of the cortical surface across fetuses of varying gestational age and folding magnitude, using only intrinsic geometric properties

records.title: Using regional homogeneity from functional MRI for diagnosis of ASD among males
records.journal: 2015 International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN)
records.model_family: regional homogeneity features over 116 AAL atlas regions, reduced by chi-square feature selection, classified by a metacognitive radial basis function network

records.headline_result: classification performance improved by up to 10% by analyzing adolescents and adults separately, using fewer than 200 selected features

records.title: Automatic brain extraction in fetal MRI using multi-atlas-based segmentation
records.journal: Proceedings of SPIE, the International Society for Optical Engineering/Proceedings of SPIE
records.model_family: multiple atlas fusion segmentation, compared against single-atlas strategies

The third result is the one that matters for the pipeline: better brain segmentation propagated into better high-resolution reconstruction, so the preprocessing step is not just a convenience but a determinant of final image quality.
records.dataset_size: a large fetal MRI dataset, size not stated
records.headline_result: multiple atlas fusion significantly more accurate than single-atlas segmentation, with Dice above 0.90 and improved reconstruction quality

records.title: Lung boundary detection in pediatric chest x-rays
records.journal: Proceedings of SPIE, the International Society for Optical Engineering/Proceedings of SPIE
records.model_family: model-based lung boundary detection with age-specific lung shape models, inside the US National Library of Medicine chest radiograph screening system
records.clinical_problem: extending an adult-trained chest radiograph screening system for tuberculosis to children, in the low- and middle-income settings where over 95% of tuberculosis deaths occur
records.patient_population: pediatric chest radiographs across developmental stages, compared against adult lung shape
records.model_description: Confronts a problem the field mostly ignores by assumption: the lung is a different shape in a child than in an adult, and a model-based segmenter built on adult anatomy fails accordingly. The contribution is to quantify how lung shape changes from infancy to adulthood and to propose data-driven age groupings for separate models - 0-23 months, 2-10 years and 11-18 years - which is the kind of explicitly developmental thinking pediatric imaging AI needs and rarely gets. From the NLM's screening system, aimed at resource-limited tuberculosis screening.
records.headline_result: quantification of lung shape change from infancy to adulthood, supporting pediatric age groupings of 0-23 months, 2-10 years and 11-18 years for separate lung models

records.clinical_problem: tissue segmentation of the neonatal brain, where incomplete myelination makes contrast variable and inhomogeneous and where subcortical midbrain structures are routinely misclassified for lack of contrast
records.patient_population: neonatal brain MRI, with diffusion tensor imaging added
records.model_description: Two ideas that predate the deep learning wave but address the same failures. Building a sharp subject-specific atlas from a population of manually segmented cases, rather than segmenting against a blurred population average, sharply cut the outright failure rate. And adding diffusion information recovers white matter that structural MRI simply cannot show at this age because it is not yet myelinated - a physical rather than algorithmic limitation, and the corpus callosum and internal capsule are where it pays off. The cost is an extra sequence, which the authors state plainly.
records.headline_result: much lower failure rate and considerably improved segmentation compared with a population-average atlas, with diffusion information improving white matter segmentation especially in the corpus callosum and internal capsule

records.clinical_problem: Semi-automated segmentation of fetal ultrasound images to improve estimated fetal weight via standard biometric measurements.
records.patient_population: 215 fetuses; 103 used for weight estimation within 3 days of delivery
records.model_description: A semi-automated segmentation system measures biparietal diameter, head circumference, abdominal circumference, and femur length from fetal ultrasound images, feeding these into regression, artificial neural network, and support vector regression models to estimate fetal weight.
records.headline_result: Mean absolute percentage error reduced from 6.71% (manual) to 4.66% (computerized)

records.title: Automated Bone Age Assessment of Older Children using the Radius.
records.journal: Proceedings of SPIE--the International Society for Optical Engineering
records.model_name: Digital Hand Atlas Bone Age CAD
records.model_family: computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) algorithm using hand/wrist and radius region-of-interest features
records.body_region: hand and wrist (extended with the radius)
records.clinical_problem: skeletal maturity (bone age) assessment, including detection of growth pathologies related to endocrine and nutritional disease
records.patient_population: children 0-18 years of age undergoing hand radiography, drawn from a collection of 1,400 normal hand x-rays; focus on older children (16/14-19 years) where phalangeal and carpal features are fully developed
records.model_description: A computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) system estimates skeletal bone age from hand radiographs using features from the phalanges and carpal bones, extended in this work to include the radius as an additional region of interest for older children whose phalangeal and carpal growth plates have already matured. The output is an estimated bone age used as an index of skeletal development for detecting growth pathologies.
records.dataset_size: 1,400 normal hand radiographs of children aged 0-18 years (Digital Hand Atlas)
records.study_design: retrospective technical development (algorithm extension) and preliminary evaluation

records.title: Bone age estimation based on phalanx information with fuzzy constrain of carpals.
records.model_family: back-propagation / radial basis function / support vector machine neural networks with fuzzy logic
records.clinical_problem: skeletal bone age assessment
records.patient_population: children from infancy through adolescence undergoing hand radiography for bone age assessment
records.model_description: The system automatically segments phalanx and carpal regions on hand radiographs and extracts geometric and morphological features. Back-propagation, radial basis function, and support vector machine neural networks classify phalanx bone age, combined with a fuzzy assessment based on the normalized carpal bone area ratio, to extend automated bone age assessment to younger children where carpal features are more informative than phalanx features alone.
records.study_design: technical development and retrospective algorithm validation

records.title: Automatic bone age assessment for young children from newborn to 7-year-old using carpal bones.
records.journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
records.model_family: knowledge-based automatic segmentation with fuzzy classification (computer-aided diagnosis)
records.clinical_problem: bone age assessment in young children
records.patient_population: children from newborn to 7 years old, hand radiographs from a digital hand atlas
records.model_description: Building on an existing phalanx-based CAD bone-age system that worked well only from age 7 onward, this method automatically segments carpal bone boundaries on hand radiographs, extracts morphological features, and applies fuzzy classification to estimate bone age. It was evaluated on about 205 cases from a digital hand atlas against chronological age and two radiologists' readings.
records.dataset_size: about 205 cases from a digital hand atlas
records.study_design: retrospective technical development and validation against radiologist readings

records.title: Multivariate examination of brain abnormality using both structural and functional MRI.
records.clinical_problem: detecting brain abnormalities associated with prenatal cocaine exposure in adolescents from structural and functional MRI
records.patient_population: 49 adolescents (24 normal, 25 prenatally cocaine-exposed teenagers)
records.model_description: Regional statistical features extracted from structural and functional MRI are combined via a hybrid feature-selection method with a nonlinear support vector machine to classify each adolescent as normal or prenatally cocaine-exposed.
records.study_design: case-control study with multivariate pattern classification, leave-one-out cross-validation

records.title: Computerized geometric features of carpal bone for bone age estimation.
records.model_family: neural network (back-propagation NN, radial basis function NN)
records.clinical_problem: Estimating skeletal bone age in children from hand radiographs
records.patient_population: 465 boys and 444 girls, hand X-ray films
records.model_description: Geometric shape, area, and sequence features are extracted from carpal bones on hand radiographs and classified by neural network classifiers (linear, nearest-neighbor, back-propagation NN, radial basis function NN) to estimate bone age.
